What the Register of Deeds does for a seller

This is the office that records the deed passing title to your buyer. It also holds the lasting county-wide index of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and easements. Staff do recording only. They may not practice law under state law, which rules out legal forms and explanations of what a document does. Your closing attorney handles that.

Graham is the seat and Burlington the largest community. Properties in Burlington, Mebane, Elon, Haw River and the rest of the county's thirteen townships all go through this one office. The county has 83,187 housing units (July 2025), and with 186,177 residents the office stays busy with conveyances.

The front counter is open from 8:00 to 5:00 on weekdays, but the last submission for recording is 4:30. That cutoff dates from August 2013, when the county adopted G.S. 153A-94(b). The phone menu has separate options for recording help, for earlier recorded documents, and for vital records.

Recording fees

Recording a deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page beyond. A deed of trust starts from a longer base, and its figure was reset effective October 1, 2016.

Recording and copy fees at the Alamance County Register of Deeds
Filing or copyCost
Deed$26 for pages 1 to 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for pages 1 to 35, then $4 per page
Multiple documents in one filing$10 added to the recording fee
Non-standard document$25 added to the recording fee
Plat$21
Certified copy$5 for the first page, $2 per added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

Vital records such as marriage licenses and certified birth, death and marriage certificates are paid in cash or by money order only. Before you go, ask which payment types the office accepts for recording.

North Carolina excise tax on a deed

Each conveyance is taxed by the state at $1.00 per $500 of value, with a fraction of $500 counted whole. Under G.S. 105-228.30, the transferor pays the register of deeds before recording. For a parcel in more than one county, payment goes where most of the value lies.

Proceeds go from the register to the county finance officer. The county general fund keeps half, and the rest goes to the state once refunds and the county's collection allowance are taken out. The same statute covers timber deeds.

You will not see this tax on the county fee schedule, because it is a state levy separate from the recording charge. Your settlement attorney reads the consideration off the deed and collects the tax with the fee. Ask to see the figure on your settlement statement before closing day.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alamance County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deed formatting rules

Paper deeds must satisfy G.S. 161-14(b), and the office repeats the rules on its recording page. A deed that falls short still gets recorded, for an extra $25.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches above the first page text, with half an inch minimum elsewhere on page one and on all edges of later pages.
  • Black print on white paper, with nine point as the smallest legible font. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Printing on one side only.
  • The instrument's title at the top of page one, under the margin.

Plats follow a separate rule: mylar only, cut to 18 by 24 inches. Enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope sized for the recorded document.

After the deed is recorded

Staff stamp each instrument with the day and hour it arrived and record in arrival order. The statute allows up to 30 days to finish indexing. Keep the book and page number the county assigns, since that is how you will refer to the document later.

One step surprises some sellers because it comes first. Deeds recorded since May 2, 2011 (timber deeds and releases excepted) pass through the county Tax Department for a delinquent tax certification. Overdue county tax stalls recording until it is paid, so ask for a payoff early.

Electronic recording has been available since November 2015 for everything but plats, so your attorney can submit through a vendor. After recording, Land Records at the Tax Department revises the owner name and mailing address. Straight sales move quicker than splits. Call with your book and page number if nothing changes after several weeks.

Other county offices in a house sale

Three other offices usually touch a sale, and each keeps a different slice of the record.

  • Tax Department, Land Records: at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, phone (336) 228-1312. It owns the parcel's owner name, mailing address and tax map, and staff want the book and page number of any recorded deed when you call about a change.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds estate filings and court orders, which establish who owns a house after a death or a court proceeding. When title runs through an estate, the clerk files the estate papers and this office records the deeds the heirs or the court sign.
  • North Carolina Secretary of State: holds business filings. A merger, name change or dissolution alters how a company-owned parcel is listed.

Names on the county record follow the recorded deed letter for letter. A misspelling on the deed itself needs a corrected document recorded here, and a lawyer can prepare it. A marriage or court-ordered name change does not alter the owner name unless a new document is recorded.

Tax bills are mailed in July and due September 1, so changing a mailing address before July keeps the bill from going astray after you sell.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alamance County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to search or copy land records

Search recorded deeds by name through the office's online search, and go to the office itself for certified copies. Online records are unofficial, and the paper records in the office are the official ones.

  • Certified copies: $5 for page one, $2 for each page after it.
  • Plain copies: $0.25 a page.
  • Owner, mailing address and legal description: the Tax Department's property record search.
  • Tax maps are drawn for assessment and are not surveys. Hire a surveyor and use the recorded plat for any boundary question.

Paying off a mortgage? Have the lender record the release, since cancellation of a deed of trust is itself a recorded instrument.

Getting ready to record your sale

Work backward from the 4:30 cutoff. Ask your closing attorney whether the deed will go by electronic recording or on paper. If it is paper, check the margins, font size and one-sided printing against the formatting list above. Confirm that the tax certification has cleared, and that the excise tax and recording fee are collected at closing. Afterward, keep the book and page number, and update your mailing address with Land Records so a bill does not go to the wrong place.

Frequently asked questions

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alamance County?

Documents must come in by 4:30 p.m. The doors stay open until 5:00, yet the recording cutoff comes half an hour earlier under G.S. 153A-94(b).

Who pays North Carolina's deed excise tax?

The transferor pays it before recording. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 per $500 of value, rounding any part of $500 up.

What does it cost to record a deed here?

A deed costs $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. Documents that miss the formatting rules carry a $25 surcharge.

Is electronic recording offered in Alamance County?

Yes, for every document except plats, since November 2015. Closing attorneys normally submit through a recording vendor.

Why did my deed have to go to the Tax Department first?

Deeds recorded after May 2, 2011, other than timber deeds and releases, need delinquent tax certification from the county Tax Department before recording. Unpaid county tax must be cleared first.

Where Alleghany County records a deed

Take any deed for Alleghany County land to the Register of Deeds, 348 South Main Street, Sparta, NC 28675, or call 336-372-4342. People work in the office until 5:00 p.m., yet the 4:30 p.m. mark is the last chance to submit a document.

Register and tax office share the Sparta administration building, a convenience because no deed gets recorded here without a paper from the tax side. The register is a recording office, and staff explain county requirements and nothing more. Drafting and legal advice belong to your closing attorney. To look up an owner by street address, call the E-911 and Mapping office at 336-372-7920 instead of the register.

The county has 11,479 residents and 8,035 housing units against 5,177 households, which suggests many second homes and seasonal cabins. With an older population, many sales are heirs selling a parent's house, and an estate deed has to meet the same recording rules.

What the Sparta office checks on a deed

The county's checklist asks for a notarized signature, a named drafter, the buyer's address, a tax certification, and payment of excise tax and fees.

  • A notary must properly acknowledge the grantor's signature.
  • Page one of a deed or deed of trust written in North Carolina names whoever drafted it.
  • Page one also carries the grantee's address, so the tax office knows where to mail bills.
  • The tax administrator's certification is attached before the deed is recorded.
  • At recording, the grantor pays the real estate excise tax.
  • No document is accepted until recording fees are paid.

Staff look at layout too. The paper should be legal or letter size, with a wide blank band at the top of page one, dark ink of at least 10 points, printing on one side only, and the instrument title near the top. Pen works for blanks and corrections. Miss these and the deed is still recorded, but a $25.00 surcharge joins the usual charges.

The tax certification

Every deed travels with a tax certification form, and without it recording stops. The tax office issues the form at 336-372-8291.

G.S. 105-361(a) is the basis. On request, the tax collector must supply a written certificate of the current and prior-year taxes, penalties, interest and costs that sit as a lien on the parcel. All taxes on the parcel must be paid in full before its deed can be recorded, and your request must name the person under whom the land was listed in each year. Ask early, because an open bill can hold up recording.

Plan for every county charge on the parcel, including the solid waste fee and fire district tax, to be cleared at the closing table. Decide with your closing attorney who will request the certificate.

What recording a deed costs

Plan on $26.00 to record a standard deed of up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each page past that. The seller's excise tax is a separate charge.

Alleghany County recording charges (G.S. 161-10)
FilingCost
Deed or similar general instrument$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; each later page adds $4.00
Excise tax (grantor pays)$2.00 on every $1,000 of price
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra
Mortgage satisfaction or cancellationFree
Plain copy, in person$.05 per page
Certified copy$5.00 for the first page, $2.00 each after

State law, G.S. 105-228.30, expresses the same tax as one dollar per $500 or part of $500 and places it on the seller. Mortgage-type documents have a higher base fee, which the lender's closing agent takes care of.

Property tax rates and the next revaluation

For fiscal year 2026-27 the county rate is 0.597 per $100 of value. Residential property also pays a $108 solid waste fee and a fire district rate that varies with the house's location. Reappraisal comes at least once in eight years: the last one took effect in 2021, and the next begins January 1, 2027. Notices will be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and the revaluation update covers about 14,736 parcels. Values moved by different amounts in different areas, so do not assume your neighbor's change matches yours. Owners can contest a value before the county appeal board.

Fire district rates, per $100 of value:

  • Cherry Lane: .04
  • Laurel Springs: .07
  • Sparta: .03
  • Glade Creek: .07
  • Piney Creek: .06

Early-payment discount and exemptions

Pay the current year's taxes during August and you get a 2 percent discount. Wait past January 5 and 2 percent interest is added on January 6, followed by 0.75 percent at the start of each later month.

Property and improvements must be listed by January 31. The county tax office also handles the exclusions and exemptions the state offers: religious, educational, charitable, elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and farm present use value. For the age-65 or disabled exclusion, 2026 income may not exceed $38,800. A disabled veteran can exclude the first $45,000 of value with no age or income test.

File with the county assessor; the state accepts forms through June 1. If you sell a house that carries one of these programs, tell the buyer's attorney, since the circuit breaker deferral can bring back up to three years of deferred tax when the property is transferred.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alleghany County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If the deed needs to go out the same day

Closings do not always land early in the day. Since the register stops taking documents at 4:30 p.m., ask your closing attorney whether the deed will be delivered that afternoon or the next business day. Have the tax certification in hand before the signing so nothing is waiting on the tax side. If a bill turns up unpaid at the last minute, it has to be cleared first, and the clock may run out before the cutoff.

How to prepare before closing

Begin with the tax certification, then the deed details, then the money. Following this order keeps recording on schedule.

  • Call the tax office at 336-372-8291 for the certification form and the amount owed on the parcel.
  • Check that the deed names the drafter and gives the buyer's mailing address on page one.
  • Arrange for the excise tax and recording fee to be paid at closing, before the 4:30 p.m. recording cutoff.
  • Ask the Clerk of Court at 336-372-3900 how to look up judgments or mechanics liens that could attach to the land.
  • Afterward, order a certified copy of the recorded deed if the buyer's lender wants one.

Houses needing repairs, carrying liens or facing inherited title questions can still sell as-is. Recording follows one process for every house, and only the payoff amounts change.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Alleghany County Register of Deeds stop accepting documents?

The cutoff is 4:30 p.m. every day, though the building stays open until 5:00 p.m. The office is at 348 South Main Street in Sparta, phone 336-372-4342.

Is a tax certification required for an Alleghany deed?

Yes. A tax certification form must accompany all deeds. Get it from the Alleghany County Tax Office at 336-372-8291, and expect any unpaid property tax on the parcel to be settled first.

Who owes the deed stamp tax on an Alleghany sale?

The seller, as grantor. The county prints $2.00 per $1,000 of price, paid at recording, which equals the one dollar per $500 in state law.

What does a copy of a recorded Alleghany deed cost?

An in-person plain copy is $.05 a page, and mail requests work too. Certified copies are $5.00 for the opening page and $2.00 for every further page.

When does the next Alleghany County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027. Notices of new values are due to be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and owners can contest a value before the county appeal board.

Getting a deed into the Avery County records

You can bring a deed to the Avery County registry, mail it, or send it by electronic recording. Monday through Friday the counter has staff from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., though the final filing of the day must be in by 4:15.

Every land record for the county lives in this office, and the public search website displays index entries and images of documents. The staff record documents and stop there. State law keeps them from practicing law, which means no legal forms, no drafting coaching and no opinions on how a filed paper affects title. Your closing attorney covers all of that.

Tax maps serve valuation and nothing more. A parcel's legal description is the one in the recorded deed, and when a map line and the deed conflict, the deed wins.

What recording costs in Avery County

The office charges $26.00 to record a general instrument of up to 15 pages and $64.00 for a deed of trust of up to 35 pages. Pages beyond that cost $4.00 each. Excise tax is billed apart from these.

Fees charged by the Avery County registry (G.S. 161-10)
Filing or serviceCharge
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages; each added page $4.00
Deed of trust$64.00 for the first 35 pages; each added page $4.00
Plat$21.00 a page, on 18 by 24 inch sheets only
Excise tax (paid by seller)$1 for each $500 of price
Mortgage satisfaction or cancellationFree
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, then $2.00 a page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Watch for two small extras. Naming more than 20 distinct parties for indexing adds $2.00 per name beyond the twentieth. A later instrument that points back to more than one earlier recorded instrument costs $25.00 for every extra reference.

Who pays the excise tax when a house sells?

Sellers pay this one. G.S. 105-228.30 places the tax on the transferor, who settles with the registry before recording.

State law sets $1 for each $500 of price, rounding a leftover portion up to a full $500. County government and the state divide the proceeds. Because it tracks the contract price, you can work out the amount as soon as a contract is signed, and it belongs on the settlement statement.

  • Seller: the excise tax, and the release of the old mortgage, which usually costs nothing to record.
  • Buyer: recording fees for the new deed and the lender's deed of trust.
  • Either side: the nonstandard document charge, if the paperwork misses the format rules.

Contracts can shift these costs, so read the settlement statement before signing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Avery County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why recording matters for ownership

G.S. 47-18 says a transfer reaches lien creditors and later purchasers only once it is registered in the land's home county. Whoever records first generally ranks first.

That is why a closing here finishes with a recording rather than a signature alone. A deed that never leaves a drawer puts the buyer at risk. The same office holds the paperwork that clears your side, like the satisfaction of an earlier deed of trust. You should end up with both a payoff letter and a recorded cancellation in the index.

File the recorded copy and its recording stamp with your closing papers. Together they show the date your transfer took effect, which can matter later if anyone questions it.

Avery County housing in brief

Avery County sits high in the northwestern mountains, and its seat, Newland, stands at 3,589 feet. Population is 18,110, yet there are 14,597 housing units for 6,791 households, a sign of many vacation homes. Median owner-occupied value is $265,800, and 83.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Snow averages 58 inches a winter, so check any house left empty through the cold months before it is shown.

Seven towns sit inside the county: Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Crossnore, Elk Park, Newland, Seven Devils and Sugar Mountain. Tax records divide the land into eight townships (Altamont, Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Cranberry, Linville, Roaring Creek, Toe River and Wilson's Creek) and ten fire districts. When you ask the tax office for a payoff, give the township or town along with the parcel details so the right rates are applied.

How taxes reach a closing

The tax office sends the real and personal property bills, and its work divides into assessment and collections. The 2025 county rate is 0.335 plus a 0.065 fire rate, a total of 0.40. Ask the tax office how those figures apply to a bill.

Today's values come from the revaluation effective January 1, 2022, and notices went out that March. Bills are due September 1, with interest starting after January 5. The listing period runs through January, and taxpayers carry the duty to list even if no form arrives.

For payoff figures, call 828-733-8214 for assessment or 828-733-8228 for collections, then pass the numbers to the title attorney.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Avery County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens on closing day

Your closing attorney gathers the signed deed, the excise tax and the recording fees, then files it. Before that, the seller signs in front of a notary, the lender is paid off, and any earlier deed of trust is released. After recording, the register's index shows the new deed, and the old mortgage should show as cancelled. A few weeks on, check for yourself by searching the online index by name, and confirm both entries appear. If something is missing, the attorney's office can chase it, and the register's staff can tell you whether a document was received and when.

Checks before recording day

Go through this list a few days early, because a rejected filing late in the day can push the recording to the next morning.

  • An attorney drafts the deed, a notary witnesses the signature, and the preparer's name appears on it.
  • Print on white paper in a legible font with a clear top margin so the nonstandard charge is avoided.
  • Bring a plat only on 18 by 24 inch sheets, if a subdivision map is part of the transaction.
  • Plan to reach the register before the 4:15 p.m. recording cutoff, and leave time for any fix the clerk flags.
  • Look up the property in the online index. Recorded easements, and old deeds of trust that still read as open, will show there and are better found before closing day than during it.

An inherited house or one that needs repairs follows the same recording steps. A quick as-is sale goes through the same register, and the excise tax still follows the contract price.

Frequently asked questions

When can I record in Avery County?

Doors are open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but it stops accepting filings at 4:15 p.m. It takes counter, mail and electronic submissions.

What will Avery County charge me to record my deed?

Plan on $26.00 for a general instrument through page 15, then $4.00 for each added page. The excise tax of $1 per $500 comes on top, and nonstandard paper adds $25.00.

Is there a fee to record the release of a mortgage in Avery County?

No. Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust is free on the register's fee schedule, matching the statewide fee statute.

Can the Avery County register of deeds give legal advice about my deed?

No. Staff are not allowed to practice law, so no forms, no filling-in help and no explanation of what a paper does. Ask an attorney instead.

Who gives me a tax payoff figure in Avery County?

The Avery County tax office. Dial 828-733-8214 for assessment or 828-733-8228 for collections, and ask for this year's balance and any earlier balance on the parcel.

Reaching the Beaufort County registry

The office is at 112 W 2nd Street, Washington, NC 27889, with mail going to P.O. Box 514. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., filings stop at 4:45 p.m., and the phone is 252-946-2323.

The registry handles deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats, assumed business names, UCC statements, military discharges and vital records, and it administers notary oaths. Index, historical index and map searches run through beaufortcountyrod.com.

Under G.S. 84-4 and 84-5, staff cannot help prepare legal papers. Arrive with a finished deed from your lawyer.

What a Beaufort deed must show

State standards and local steps both apply.

  • Letter or legal paper, printed on one side in legible type of 9 points or larger on white stock.
  • Three blank inches at the head of page one, and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • The kind of instrument written at the top of the first page.
  • A preparer's name on every deed and deed of trust.
  • On a deed, the buyer's address plus a note on whether the seller lived there as a primary residence.
  • A sign-off from Land Records on deeds and certain maps before filing.

Paper that misses the format rules can still be filed for a $25.00 nonstandard fee, and the register may waive that fee when only the type size is short and the text is legible. Surveys and plats, along with Torrens documents, cannot be filed electronically, so they go in on paper.

Why a deed goes through Land Records first

The county ties its mapping and tax listing to recorded deeds, so Land Records looks at a deed before the register files it. That office is at 220 N. Market Street in Washington, phone 252-946-6591.

Land Records manages the county's parcel mapping and GIS databases, applies recorded documents such as wills and deeds when it administers tax listings, and helps the public and professionals with record reviews. Drop the deed there early, since approval comes before recording.

The register's downloads also include a resolution on tax certification for deeds. Ask the register or the tax collector whether a certificate is needed for your closing, because the rule is set locally.

Excise tax is a separate line. The seller pays a dollar per $500 of price at the registry, and the county retains half. For anything out of the ordinary, request the office's current schedule.

Fraud alert for owners

The registry emails you, at no charge, when a recorded document matches a name you enroll. Each email address can list five names, and only filings made after signup count.

The reason is simple: the office must record any document that is properly executed and presented with payment, and it cannot know whether a signature is forged. Nothing can be removed from the official records after recording, even if a document is proven fraudulent. An owner who suspects fraud should call the sheriff's office at 252-946-7111 and speak to an attorney, because the register has no power to reverse a filing.

The name you enroll can be your own or a relative's, which suits owners of land they rarely visit.

Beaufort County for a seller

Beaufort is a coastal plain county built around the Pamlico River, with Washington, the county seat, where the Tar and Pamlico rivers meet. Seven municipalities lie within it: Aurora, Bath, Belhaven, Chocowinity, Pantego, Washington and Washington Park. Population is 44,670, and the county has 25,204 housing units with 69.5 percent of homes owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $192,700.

Waterfront and inland parcels do not move together. Property on or near the water has historically changed in value much faster than inland land, so the type of parcel matters more than the county average when you price a house.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Beaufort County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How taxes interact with a sale

Bills are issued as of July 1 and fall due September 1. If payment is not in by January 5, interest and enforced collection start. For real estate, the owner on January 1 is the listing taxpayer and stays responsible until the past due date, whatever the buyer and seller agree at closing.

That is a trap for sellers. If you close after the bills go out, one may still arrive in your mail. Send it on to the buyer or return it to the collector. Escrow lenders are not automatic either: the owner must tell the lender the amount and confirm with the collector that payment arrived.

The 2025 revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and a six-year cycle follows. Value appeals may be filed from January each year, up to the adjournment of the county review board, typically in mid-April. County, fire and EMS district rates are set with the county budget, while town officials set municipal rates. Vehicles are taxed through the NCDMV at tag renewal, not on the real estate bill. The tax collector offers payment plans with a 20 percent down payment, set up in person between January 6 and June 30.

Getting ready to file your deed

Work through the order of the visit. First, have your lawyer finish the deed with the preparer's name, the buyer's address and the residence note. Second, take it to Land Records at 220 N. Market Street for sign-off, and ask whether a tax certificate is needed. Third, bring the deed and the fees to the registry before 4:45 p.m. Fourth, pay the excise tax, since the seller owes it at the registry. Afterward, make sure the tax bill reaches the right person, and consider signing up for the fraud alert on your name.

After recording, you can confirm the deed through the index search at beaufortcountyrod.com. If you need proof for a lender or an attorney, a certified copy costs $5.00 for the first sheet and $2.00 for each more. Keep the recorded copy with your closing papers. If the release of your old deed of trust has not shown up in the index, ask the lender, since that release records at no fee.

Frequently asked questions

When is the last filing time in Beaufort County?

Filing closes at 4:45 p.m., fifteen minutes before the 5 p.m. weekday close. The office is at 112 W 2nd Street in Washington and can be reached at 252-946-2323.

Does a deed need Land Records approval in Beaufort County?

Yes. Deeds and some maps must be approved by the Beaufort County Land Records office before recording. Land Records is at 220 N. Market Street, phone 252-946-6591.

Can I record a plat electronically in Beaufort County?

No. Survey maps and plats, along with Torrens documents, are not accepted electronically. Those are the only document types excluded from electronic recording.

Who pays the tax bill after a Beaufort sale?

The January 1 owner stays responsible until the past due date, regardless of what the buyer and seller arranged at closing. Send any notice to the buyer or back to the collector.

Can Beaufort County warn me about filings in my name?

Yes. The register runs a free fraud alert email service. You can enroll five names per email address and receive a notice when a matching document is recorded, but only for documents recorded after signup.

Office address, hours and contact

Deeds are recorded in Windsor, in the courthouse at King and Dundee streets. The register's office is on the first floor. Visitors use 108 Dundee Street, and mail goes to PO Box 340, Windsor, NC 27983.

The office is open from 8:30 to 5:00, but recording stops at 4:30. A deed that arrives at a quarter to five waits until the next morning. Electronic recording is accepted, so closing attorneys can file without driving to Windsor. Holidays and bad weather may close the doors, so call ahead if timing is tight.

Bertie County Register of Deeds contact and filing details
DetailBertie County answer
Street address108 Dundee Street, Windsor
Mailing addressPO Box 340, Windsor, NC 27983
Phone and fax(252) 794-5309 and (252) 794-5374

Why recording a deed matters

Bertie's register is the custodian for deeds, trust deeds, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, maps and military records. The office is elected every second year and works under Chapter 161 of the General Statutes.

A buyer's priority depends on filing. G.S. 47-18 says a deed nobody has recorded loses to lien creditors and to purchasers who paid value, and the date of registration sets the order. Until the deed reaches the courthouse, a rival claim can get ahead of the buyer.

  • Records are filed by name, so the office cannot look up an owner from a street address.
  • For an address search, call the tax assessor's mapping line at (252) 794-5311.
  • Anyone may request a copy of a recorded paper in person, by letter or by phone. Military discharge forms are the exception, since access is limited.

Recording fees

Charges track the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, which the county fee page reproduces. Expect $26.00 for an ordinary document up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 a page beyond. Deeds of trust and mortgages are priced at $64.00 up to 35 pages, again plus $4.00 a page beyond.

  • Extra instrument inside the same document: $10.00
  • Paper that fails the format rules: $25.00 added to the filing fee
  • Mortgage satisfaction: free

Pay the fee before filing; the statute makes that schedule the only filing charge. If your document has an odd page count, phone (252) 794-5309 before you send it.

Excise tax the seller pays at recording

The state's excise tax falls on the seller. The rate is $1.00 per $500 of price or value, and any remainder under $500 is rounded up. The register takes the money first, then files the deed.

The county general fund keeps half of the receipts and the Department of Revenue gets the other half. When land straddles two counties, the county with the larger share of the value gets the tax. Your closing attorney figures the amount from the contract price and normally deducts it at settlement.

Bertie County recording rules

A resolution adopted in April 1991 under G.S. 161-30 took effect June 1, 1991. The register may not take any map or instrument affecting real property unless two items appear on its face: a name and address for returning the document, and the grantee's permanent mailing address.

Format rules apply as well. Filers should use letter or legal size paper, black print on white, type no smaller than 9 point, printed on one side, with a blank 3 inch strip across the top of page one. Paper that does not fit is still accepted if the $25.00 non-standard fee is paid, and the register can waive it when the font is a bit small but readable.

Run a quick check before mailing anything to Windsor: signature and notary stamp in place, both addresses on page one, fee and transfer tax in hand.

Old land records and inherited tracts

Bertie Precinct became a county in 1722, when it separated from Chowan County, and the register's land and grant records start that same year. The original county was large. It took in what are now Tyrrell, Edgecombe, Northampton and Hertford counties, and by 1780 it had been divided into roughly its present shape.

If you are selling an inherited farm tract, this can matter. A chain of title that begins in colonial grants may run through Bertie books even when the land now lies in a neighboring county, so a title search can reach back much farther than the online window. The online index starts in 1977 and also supports a search by book number from Book 600. Call the office about anything older.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bertie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other services at the Windsor counter

The register's staff also issue marriage licenses, swear in notaries, and sell birth and death certificates, so the counter can be busy. A marriage license applicant must arrive before 4:00 p.m., an hour ahead of the recording cutoff. Notary oaths need no appointment, and a new notary may bring the green transmittal letter from the Secretary of State.

Two items at the counter are cash only: the $60.00 marriage license and the $24.00 statewide birth certificate service for people born anywhere in North Carolina from 1971 onward. When you call, ask how the office wants payment for a recording.

Changing names on a deed

To change a name, have an attorney prepare a new deed. Sign it in front of a notary, then deliver it with the fee. That is the register's own answer.

A land contract works differently. Chapter 47H gives the seller five business days to record the contract or a short memorandum of it. The purchaser has until midnight of the third business day after signing to back out.

Paid-off loans can leave a loose end. Get a satisfaction from the lender and record it. There is no fee, and it removes a snag from the title check before a sale.

How the register fits into a sale

Your closing attorney or title agent searches the records, files the new deed and any lender's deed of trust, and pays the transfer tax out of the settlement. Most sellers never set foot in the office.

Property taxes are the one title item that lives elsewhere. Unpaid bills are a lien and are cleared with the tax collector, as covered in our Bertie County property tax guide. Gaps from older paperwork, such as a mortgage never released or an estate never opened, get fixed by recording the missing document before closing.

One courthouse serves the whole county, so a parcel in any of the eight towns is recorded at the same counter. Whoever buys, the new deed still ends up in the Windsor books.

Frequently asked questions

What number reaches the Bertie County Register of Deeds?

Call (252) 794-5309, or send a fax to (252) 794-5374. The office is at 108 Dundee Street in Windsor.

What is the last time to record a deed in Bertie County?

Recording closes at 4:30 p.m., thirty minutes before the office does. Electronic recordings are accepted too.

How much does it cost to record a standard Bertie County deed?

Through 15 pages the charge is $26.00, then $4.00 for each extra page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through 35 pages.

Who pays the excise tax on a Bertie County sale?

The seller pays $1.00 per $500 of value to the register before the deed is recorded.

How do I find the owner of a Bertie County street address?

Call the tax assessor's mapping office at (252) 794-5311. The register indexes by name, so an address alone will not work there.

What the Brunswick County Register of Deeds handles

Land records for the whole county are kept here. Deeds, deeds of trust, easements, maps, releases and satisfactions pass through the office, as do marriage licenses, certified copies and oaths. Voters choose the register for a four-year term. The staff can file what you bring but cannot advise you or draft the paper.

Other filings include restrictions and covenants, assumed names, UCC statements and powers of attorney, on top of the steady flow of deeds from coastal home sales. A seller reaches this counter in person, by mail or through a title firm. Until the buyer's deed is on the record, the sale is not protected against outside claims.

Location and hours

Find the office in Building I at 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422. The phone is 910-253-2690, with 877-625-9310 as the toll-free alternate, and mail is addressed to PO Box 87 in Bolivia. Services run on separate schedules.

  • Land and vital records: opens 8:30 am, closes 5 pm, weekdays.

  • Passports: by appointment, 8:30 am until 3:30 pm.

You can hand a document over at the counter, post it to the box, or ship it by courier to the Courthouse Drive street address. The county holiday calendar applies to the recording desk.

What the county requires before recording a deed

The clerks work from a short county checklist. They accept only an original, or a certified copy bearing the original signature.

  • A check to BCROD for the recording fee, with a stamped return envelope.
  • Page one shows who prepared the deed and where to reach them.
  • Seller and buyer both appear on the face of the deed, each with an address.
  • Signatures and a notary seal that reads clearly.
  • The delinquent tax certification step the county lists for all deeds.
  • Excise tax, which the county words as $2 for every $1,000 of sales price.

Layout counts too. The county quotes G.S. 161-14(b), which calls for letter or legal paper, a three-inch blank band on page one, half-inch margins on the rest, black ink on white in 9 points or larger, and printing on one side only. A deed that misses these limits is still taken, with $25 added.

Plats have their own price. A freestanding plat on film or mylar must be 18 by 24 inches and approved by the county review officer; the state schedule charges $21.00 per sheet.

Who pays the excise tax?

It falls on the seller. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor pays the register before the deed is recorded: one dollar for each $500 of value, with a leftover fraction counted as a full $500. County government keeps half of every collection and passes the other half to the state.

Unpaid property tax is its own obstacle. The county makes tax certification a condition of recording, and a deed filed electronically has to say the closing attorney will pay any delinquent taxes to the county tax collector when funds go out. If you owe taxes, get a payoff figure from the collector early, and ask your attorney to show the excise line on the settlement statement.

Electronic recording

Lenders and other businesses may e-record through Internet Technologies, Inc. (Inttek) in the normal weekday recording hours, while private owners usually file on paper.

  • Sending ACH funds into escrow adds 2.5% of the escrowed amount.

  • A map can be e-recorded if it shows an existing parcel.

A deed recorded this way has to begin with a prepared-by statement naming a North Carolina attorney, plus the delinquent tax wording, and every e-filing carries the submitter statement tied to the county's submitter agreement. Ask your closing firm which route it takes. Many deeds reach the office the day they are signed through e-filing.

How to search deeds and get copies

Online records start with September 1939 filings. Enter just one detail, whether a buyer's name, a date range, a document type or a book and page, and every result can be downloaded as a PDF.

Index books for 1932 to 1953 are scanned as legacy indexes: find the name alphabetically, then key the book and page into the search page. A certified copy can be ordered by mailing a written request and payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or through the search site.

A redaction form lets anyone ask the office to blank out a Social Security, bank or card number on an image posted online. There is also a free fraud alert that notifies you whenever a document is recorded under your name, handy for owners of vacant or inherited houses.

Why recording matters when you sell

Recording decides who stands first among competing claims. G.S. 47-18 gives an unregistered conveyance no weight against lien creditors or paying buyers, and priority follows the time of registration.

So the buyer's attorney holds the money until the deed and new loan papers are filed. On your side, an old mortgage should show a recorded satisfaction. The lender files it, the county charges nothing, and a quick search of your own deed confirms it is there.

Inherited houses, liens and unpaid taxes slow the process, so raise them with the closing attorney early. A cash buyer's offer still needs the same deed, the same tax certification and the same excise payment.

A seller's checklist for closing day

Have the closing attorney confirm three things on the deed itself: both parties named with addresses, a notary seal that reads clearly, and the preparer's name on page one. Confirm the tax certification is done, the excise payment is on the settlement statement, and the recording fee check is made out to BCROD. If the deed will be e-recorded, check that the prepared-by statement and delinquent tax wording are in place.

The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value conveyed, a figure the county also words as $2 per $1,000, and the seller pays it up front.

Only businesses and lenders can, through Inttek. Vendor fees run 6% plus $0.50 for cards or 2.5% for ACH escrow, in addition to normal recording fees.

Office location and hours

The office is at 205 College Street, Asheville, NC 28801, with weekday service from 8 am until 5 pm. Recording and real estate staff take calls at 828-250-4302, vital records at 828-250-4300 and the help desk at 828-250-4303. Spanish speakers can use 828-250-4307.

A holiday closing calendar is posted on the office's web page, so check it before planning a same-day recording around Thanksgiving or the December holidays. The county website is buncombenc.gov, and older buncombecounty.org links forward there.

Records go back to the 1700s. Anyone who prefers paper can use the public record search room at the same address during office hours.

What documents Buncombe County records

The office keeps the paper trail for Buncombe land: conveyances, deeds of trust and their cancellations, plats, assumed business names, UCC filings, separation agreements, road maintenance agreements and powers of attorney. All of it is open to public inspection.

Staff act as record keepers. They will not draft or change papers, although forms for satisfactions and assumed names are on hand, and anyone needing a deed drawn up is sent to an attorney. Filings must be originals with live signatures and a notary's acknowledgment.

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust
  • Satisfactions and cancellations after payoff
  • Plats and miscellaneous maps
  • Assumed names and UCC filings
  • Powers of attorney and related papers

Deed formatting rules

Start with paper size, which must be letter or legal. Leave a three-inch blank strip at the top of page one, half an inch on its other edges, and half an inch on every edge of later pages.

  • Black ink, white paper, a legible font of 9 points or bigger.
  • Printing on a single side of each sheet.
  • A title for the instrument written near the top of page one.
  • No highlighter over important information.
  • Color or grayscale images count as non-standard.

Off-standard deeds are accepted at an added $25. A color scan alone triggers it, so have the final deed printed on plain white paper.

Filing and copy costs

Filing fees follow one statewide schedule, while copy rates come from the county.

Typical recording and copy charges at the College Street office
ServiceAmount

To order by mail, enclose the Real Estate Records Request Form and a check or money order made out to Register of Deeds. Adding a stamped return envelope speeds things up.

What to bring to College Street

If you are carrying the deed in yourself instead of using a title firm, bring the original with live signatures and the notary's acknowledgment, a check or money order for the recording fee, and the excise tax payment. Count the pages first, because $26.00 covers a general instrument only up to page 15, and a deed of trust covers up to page 35 at $64.00.

Check that the deed is printed on plain white letter or legal paper with the three-inch blank strip on page one. If you want proof of what was recorded, order a certified copy afterward, either at the counter or by mail with the request form. Call 828-250-4302 if you are unsure about any step, though staff cannot give legal advice.

Who pays the deed tax

The seller pays the register before the deed is filed. The charge is one dollar on each $500 of price, counting a partial $500 as a whole one.

Buncombe keeps half in its general fund and passes the rest to the state monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Review the excise tax line on the settlement statement, because it follows the price on the deed.

A parcel that straddles two counties pays in the one holding the larger share of its value.

Filing online

Electronic filing is open to firms. Lenders, law offices, attorneys and surveyors submit through an authorized eRecording provider.

After choosing a provider, the company completes a Submitter Memorandum of Understanding. For a seller this explains how a title firm can have a deed recorded quickly. Individual owners can carry originals to College Street or mail them.

Filed documents can be found in the online records search, which comes with a video tutorial. Results cover deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney and assumed names, and can be printed.

Online tools for land records

On its Real Estate Recording page, the county pairs an Online Records Search with a lookup tutorial. Nearby sit a Parcel Ownership Dashboard, a Cemetery Finder and a Farm Finder. The index runs from conveyances to assumed names, and the oldest entries date to the 1700s.

Use them before listing to verify how title is vested, spot an old easement or catch a deed of trust that was never cleared. If one shows up, contact the lender, who is the one to file the cancellation.

How the 2026 reappraisal delay affects a sale

Buncombe's 2026 tax bills use the 2021 schedule of values because of a state law passed in July 2026, and the new reappraisal takes effect January 1, 2027. The county levy on those bills is 61.54 cents for each $100 of valuation.

The bill due around your closing rests on the older values. You can view bills at tax.buncombenc.gov, and the Tax Assessment office takes questions at 828-250-4920. Our Buncombe property tax guide covers appeals, relief programs and rates.

Renters and investors selling in Buncombe

About a third of homes in the county are rented, so some sellers are investors with tenants in place. A lease leaves the register's work unchanged, but your closing attorney should hear about it early so the deed, the tenant's rights and the closing date line up.

Checks before your deed is recorded

Three checks matter: the deed's layout, the excise line and any property tax still owed. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance has force against lien creditors and buyers only after registration, so recording time sets priority.

An autumn closing can overlap a bill that has been issued but not paid, since bills normally come due September 1 and carry a grace period into early January. Collections answers at 828-250-4910.

Read your own deed in the online search before accepting an offer, including the legal description and easements. If a mortgage was paid off long ago, confirm a satisfaction was recorded, and ask the lender to file one when it was not.

Frequently asked questions

What hours does the Buncombe register keep?

It serves the public weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm, at 205 College Street. Holiday closings follow the county calendar posted on the office's web page.

Will the Buncombe register help draft my deed?

No. Its role is to record and preserve documents, not to write or revise them. Forms for satisfactions and assumed names are available, and deed drafting goes to an attorney.

How much is a certified copy of a Buncombe deed?

Page one of a certified copy is $5 and each later page is $2. Plain copies cost $0.25 a page. Mail orders should enclose payment made out to Register of Deeds.

How much is the Buncombe County deed tax?

The rate is $1.00 on each $500 of price, with any remainder counted as a full $500 unit. The seller settles it before recording, and the county retains half.

What if my Buncombe County deed is not on standard paper?

The deed is recorded, with a $25 non-standard fee on top. Standard means letter or legal paper, black ink, at least 9 point type and the required margins.

What happens at the register after a sale closes

Your signed deed goes into the permanent public record of Burke County land ownership, and until it is filed the buyer's title can be beaten by someone else's paperwork. Staff file deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, powers of attorney and assumed names, and they also issue vital records, marriage licenses and notary commissions.

Timing of the filing decides who wins a dispute. G.S. 47-18 says a transfer cannot be enforced against lien holders or later paying buyers until it is registered in the county of the land, and the earlier filing time wins. An unfiled Burke County deed in a closing folder gives the buyer no protection at all.

Wills and estates sit elsewhere. Estate and court-action questions go to the Clerk of Court.

Office location and hours

Take the deed to the Morganton office on South Green Street, which opens at 8 each weekday morning, closes at 5 in the afternoon and shuts on observed county holidays. Postal packages go to Post Office Box 936 in Morganton, ZIP 28680, and callers reach staff at 828-764-9340. Confirm the door number by phone before you send a courier.

Voters choose the Register of Deeds every second year (G.S. 161-1). Staff cannot advise on wording, so your closing attorney will draft the deed and deliver it.

  • Hand delivery in Morganton on weekdays
  • Courier or postal delivery of originals
  • Electronic filing by an approved submitter
  • Searching real estate records through the county website

Burke County recording fees

For a deed, expect $26 covering the first 15 pages and $4 for every page past that. For a mortgage or deed of trust, the charge is $64 covering 35 pages plus the same $4 per extra sheet. These follow G.S. 161-10, so they match what every North Carolina register charges.

Selected charges, Burke County Register of Deeds fee schedule FY 24-25
Document or serviceCharge

Deeds of trust or mortgages$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page

The nonstandard surcharge hits papers that ignore the state's layout rules, so ask whoever drafts the deed to follow G.S. 161-14 on margins and type size. Cancelling a paid-off mortgage costs nothing, which is handy when a seller is clearing an old loan.

Who pays the state stamp tax

Sellers carry this cost, and the register wants payment first. The levy comes from G.S. 105-228.30: a dollar for every $500 of value, with any leftover fraction rounded up, owed by the transferor. The county fee schedule restates the rate as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 charged up to $500.

Half the money remains in Burke County's general fund, while the remainder travels to Raleigh in monthly remittances. Since the amount tracks the price in the deed, it grows with the sale. Get the stamp figure from your closing attorney's settlement statement rather than guessing.

Tax office sign-off before filing

The register will not take a deed conveying real property until the tax collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. The Delinquent Tax Certification form cites G.S. 161-31, a law letting commissioners impose that rule, and the printed form was revised on April 22, 2026.

Gather these details before closing day, because the form asks for all of them:

  • GIS PIN or REID number of each parcel changing hands
  • Names of the grantor and grantee, plus the grantee's mailing address
  • The owner shown in tax records, and the street address of the property
  • The price paid and how many acres are being sold
  • Whether a single-wide or double-wide home is part of the sale
  • Whether the land sits in the Present Use Value program, and whether the buyer will keep it there
  • Any personal property that goes with the sale, from motor vehicles to boats and farm equipment

Tax staff complete a ten-year grid of owners, deferred amounts and taxes due. Call the tax administration office at 828-764-9430 or write to collections@burkenc.org. Correcting a mistake in a recorded deed means drafting a new one, carrying it through the tax office and then filing it again.

Electronic filing

The register takes electronic documents through Simplifile and Corporation Service Company. The closing firm opens a submitter account, sends the package from its own desk and receives the recorded copy digitally right after filing.

If you sign from another state, that route can cut days off the gap between signing and public ownership. Ask the attorney whether the firm files through one of these platforms and whether the tax certification is already done.

Selling in Burke County and the 2027 revaluation

Burke County is heading into a countywide revaluation for 2027. Commissioners hold a hearing on the proposed schedule of values and the present use schedule for that project, with both documents open at the tax office and on the county site.

The county has 88,655 residents and 41,669 housing units, with homeowners living in about 74.5% of homes. The typical owner's home value is $185,400, median rent is $884 a month and median household income is $58,592.

Nearly one in four Burke residents (23.2%) is past 65, which makes the state's elderly and disabled homestead exclusion relevant locally. For 2026 the income cap for that program is $38,800.

Before you hand over the deed

Work through this list with your closing attorney. Confirm the tax certification is finished and the collector has signed off. Check that the deed follows the layout rules, so the $25.00 nonstandard fee does not apply. Make sure the settlement statement shows the stamp tax and the recording fee. If an old mortgage was paid off, have the satisfaction recorded, which costs nothing. Then ask whether the firm will file in person at Morganton, by courier, or electronically, and when the recorded copy will come back.

If you are carrying the paperwork yourself, remember that staff cannot advise on wording and the office closes at 5 each weekday. Call 828-764-9340 first if you are unsure which fee applies to your document.

Frequently asked questions

What will it cost to file a deed with the Burke County register?

Roughly $26 for a deed up to 15 pages, then $4 for each more. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages. The seller's stamp tax is billed apart from those fees.

Do I have to clear the Burke County tax office before filing a deed?

For a deed moving real property, yes. The delinquent tax certification form, tied to G.S. 161-31, bars the register from accepting it until the tax collector certifies no delinquent taxes. Send the form with the PIN or REID number and sale facts.

Does the Burke County register handle probate and wills?

No. Estate and court questions go to the Clerk of Court at 828-433-3200, and the register's office stays on land and vital records.

Who covers the excise tax when a Burke County house sells?

The seller. State law makes the transferor pay the register before recording, at a dollar for each $500 of value. The settlement statement shows the exact amount.

Can I look up Burke County property records from home?

Yes, real estate records are viewable online. For gaps the index leaves open, call 828-764-9340 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays.

What the Cabarrus County register files and keeps

This is the office that records your deed, your buyer's deed of trust and every release or assignment tied to the property, and keeps them as public record. The register is the legal custodian for recording, indexing, storing and preserving land documents, birth, death and marriage records, veteran discharges, notary records, subdivision maps and condominium plans.

Counter staff only record. State law bars them from practicing law, so expect no blank forms, no coaching on how to fill one in, and no opinion on what a signed instrument means for you. Drafting normally falls to your closing attorney.

Once recorded, every page is open to public viewing. Do not put a Social Security number or bank account number on anything you submit.

Why recording time matters to a seller

The clock stamp decides priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance protects the buyer against lien creditors and later purchasers for value only once it is registered in the county where the land lies, and the order of registration sets who comes first. Since the counter stops taking filings at 4:30, ask your attorney when the package is due to arrive.

Two habits save trouble. Confirm that the payoff of your old mortgage has been released, because a satisfaction of a deed of trust carries no recording fee under state law, but it still has to be filed. Have the attorney confirm that each owner named on the deed has signed and that the property description copies your earlier deed.

Filing hours and accepted payment

The filing window is weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and recording fees are paid by cash or check only. Credit cards are not accepted for recording fees, which catches out sellers who expect to settle every charge by card at the counter.

After you bring or mail in a document, the office follows a fixed routine:

  • Staff check that the document can be recorded and work out the correct fee
  • It is stamped with the date and time, then given a document number, book and page
  • It is indexed in the computer system
  • Each day the documents are imaged, and a copy goes to the NC Department of Archives for backup
  • The processed document is returned to the proper party by the next day

That one-day return helps if a buyer's lender is waiting on proof of recording.

Recording fees

A deed, release or other general instrument costs $26 for 15 pages with $4 added per further page. A mortgage or deed of trust costs $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. Both sit inside the uniform statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10.

Cabarrus County recording fees
DocumentFee
Deeds, trustee deeds, releases, assignments, powers of attorney$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Plats (mylar, 18 x 24 inches only)$21 per sheet
Subsequent instrument citing more than one original$10 for each added reference
Nonstandard document$25 on top of the recording fee

The $25 nonstandard fee applies when paper size, margins, ink or type fall short of G.S. 161-14. The checklist asks for letter or legal paper, a blank band three inches deep at the top of page one, black ink on one side only and type no smaller than 10 point. The fee does not apply to a document whose notary acknowledgement predates July 1, 2002.

Excise tax on a deed

The stamp is $2 for each $1,000 of purchase price, added to the recording charge and divided equally between Cabarrus County and the state. The statute behind it is G.S. 105-228.30, which puts the cost on the person transferring title and prices it per $500 of value.

Since the register takes only cash or check for recording fees, plan how the seller's side will be funded at the closing table. Most sellers have the closing attorney deduct the stamp from proceeds, so ask for the figure early and confirm who will deliver the payment to the office.

Searching Cabarrus County records online

The register runs an online records search for property data, and the office's remote site holds indexes and document images from 1792 to the present, plus all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps.

The county partners with Logan Systems to redact Social Security and driver's license numbers from the internet copy, beginning with records from 1935. For older documents, the office has a Public Records Redaction Request form. The register files only fixture-related UCC statements, and everything else in that category goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

If a title search for your sale turns up an old lien or easement, the index is where a closing attorney will trace it.

Other services at the counter

The office handles a few side tasks that often come up around a sale or an estate. It files military discharges at no charge when you bring the original or a military copy with a raised seal, and only the person the statute allows may record or obtain a copy. Discharges that have been on file for 80 years or longer are public, while newer ones carry restricted access.

It also swears in new notaries, collecting a $10 oath fee, with no appointment needed once the Secretary of State's notice arrives. Copies of birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage license applications are available through the county's records pages, which helps heirs who need certificates to settle an inherited house.

Selling in Cabarrus County

Cabarrus is a fast-growing Piedmont county northeast of Charlotte, with Concord as the county seat. The population is 249,725, up 10.6% from the April 2020 base, with 100,316 housing units and an owner-occupied rate of 71.2%. The median owner-occupied home is worth $354,800 and median gross rent is $1,414.

Plan your closing around the 4:30 recording cutoff, and have your attorney confirm the fee, the stamp tax and the payment method before the package goes in.

If you are bringing a deed yourself, check the page count against the fee table, make sure the paper meets the format checklist, and carry a check or cash, since cards are not taken. A deed that is ready and correctly formatted usually comes back the next day with its document number, book and page, which your buyer's lender may ask to see.

Frequently asked questions

What does it cost to file a deed with the Cabarrus County office?

Fifteen pages run $26, and each page beyond that adds $4. On top of that come the excise stamp, which the county lists at $2 per $1,000 of price, and a $25 surcharge if the paper or print misses the state format rules.

Will the Cabarrus County office take a card for recording fees?

No. Recording fees must be paid by cash or check, and credit cards are not accepted. Your closing attorney can usually handle the payment from the seller's proceeds.

What hours does Cabarrus County accept documents for recording?

Weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Finished documents are sent back to the proper party by the following day.

Can the Cabarrus County staff tell me what my deed should say?

No. The office acts as a recording office only, and North Carolina law prohibits staff from practicing law. They cannot supply legal forms, instruct you on completing them, or explain legal effects, so see an attorney.

How far back do Cabarrus County online records go?

The register's remote site has indexes and images from 1792 to the present, along with all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps. Redaction of personal numbers online begins with 1935 records, and older ones need a redaction request form.

Where Caldwell County records a deed

Deed records are kept in Lenoir at the Register of Deeds office, 905 West Avenue NW. Staff work the counter Monday through Friday, eight to five, and county holidays are days off.

The office has held real estate records since 1841, the year the county was formed. Filings here cover deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney and maps. Marriage licenses and birth and death records come from the same office. It does not hold wills; those belong with the Clerk of Court.

The record shows no change of owner until the buyer's deed is filed at this counter. If two claims compete, the one recorded first wins in this state, so file right after signing. The recording priority statute has the exact wording.

Filing charges

A standard deed of up to 15 pages is $26.00 to file, and extra pages are $4.00 apiece. Loan documents are priced higher: $64.00 for a deed of trust of up to 35 pages. One statewide schedule, G.S. 161-10, covers every county, so Lenoir sets none of these amounts itself.

The fee schedule is the whole fee and is collected before the document is filed. Phone ahead to find out which payment types the counter accepts.

Stamp tax on a sale

The seller does. As grantor you pay it when the deed is lodged, and G.S. 105-228.30 assigns the duty to the transferor, to be paid to the register before filing.

  • It attaches to any instrument that conveys an interest in land.
  • Part goes to the county and part to the state.
  • The closing agent usually deducts the stamp amount from the seller's proceeds.
  • For a gift deed with no price, ask the office how it handles the stamp.

A cash sale follows the same rule. The sale price sets the amount, so agree on it with the closing attorney first.

What must a deed carry before the office files it?

Three conditions apply. Every deed must show the grantee's current mailing address. Any deed or deed of trust drawn in North Carolina must name its drafter on page one. To get the original back by mail, include a stamped envelope with your address on it.

The office scans each document when it is presented and hands it back or mails it out, so there is no waiting period for a return. The state adopted recording standards in 2002 for page layout, and the office links to them. Check them before printing, since a paper that misses the layout rules can be recorded only with the extra nonstandard fee.

Staff cannot fill in your forms or search title. You can write your own deed, but an attorney is recommended. A name can only be added to or removed from a deed by recording a new deed.

Searching land records before you sell

The register of deeds site has a free online search. Each real estate index back to the county's founding is posted there, and scanned documents go back to the early 1900s.

Look for the vesting deed, any loan still open, and any easement or road maintenance agreement on the parcel. Check for a road maintenance agreement if your driveway is shared. If your copy is gone, the office can issue a sealed certified one.

  • Spot any loan never released, then request a payoff letter.
  • Confirm that every named co-owner will sign.
  • Look for recorded agreements that run with the land.

Everything on file is public except certified vital records and recent military discharges.

How the tax bill affects a closing

If county tax is unpaid it attaches to the parcel as a lien, and the closing is where that lien gets cleared. The Tax Office shares the Lenoir address and weekday hours, and its phone is 828-757-1340. Letters to that office go to PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645.

Bills arrive in July, with a 2% early-pay discount that month and 1% in August. The due date is September 1, and the interest-free window shuts on January 5. The interest schedule in G.S. 105-360 charges 2% beginning January 6, then three-fourths of a percent each month after.

The county went through a general reappraisal for 2025, so ask the Tax Office for your parcel's current value. The same office bills the rescue readiness charge, 14 fire districts and three municipalities: Sawmills, Rhodhiss and the Village of Cedar Rock. That means one bill may carry several lines, and each line needs a payoff figure at closing. Card payments by phone go to 1-844-866-6645. The office also keeps a foreclosure list and an online listing portal for business and personal property.

What a seller should bring and do

Open the online index before closing and find your vesting deed. Check how each owner's name is spelled. Confirm that any old loan shows as released, and ask for a payoff letter if one does not. Your closing attorney drafts the deed, which must name the drafter on page one and show the buyer's mailing address.

The stamp tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing. The recording charge must be paid before the office files a thing. Enclose a prepaid, pre-addressed envelope if the original should come back by mail. After recording, the buyer appears as the owner. A cash buyer brings no new deed of trust, so usually only the deed is filed. Certified copies of the recorded deed can be ordered afterward.

If the home was inherited, wills are not kept here, so get estate paperwork from the Clerk of Court first and then record the deed that moves title. Staff cannot search title or fill in forms for you, so have your attorney or closing agent handle both. The marriage license counter closes half an hour before the rest of the office, which matters only if you are making a second errand of it.

A short order of events helps: find the vesting deed, confirm no loan is left unreleased, agree the price so the stamp amount is known, have the deed drafted, sign, and record the same day if you can. Every step before recording is yours or your attorney's, and recording is what makes the sale official in the public index.

Caldwell County housing snapshot

The July 2025 population estimate is 81,105, in 38,057 housing units. Owners live in 73.5% of units, and the middle owned home value is $192,200 for 2020-2024. Median gross rent is $744.

A senior or disabled owner on a modest income can ask the Tax Office about the state exclusion. For 2026 the income ceiling is $38,800.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a lawyer to file a deed with the Caldwell County register?

No, you can write your own deed, though an attorney is urged since staff cannot advise or search title. Whoever writes it, the deed needs the grantee's mailing address and a drafter named on page one.

What are the hours of the Caldwell County Register of Deeds?

You can reach the counter at 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir from eight until five, Monday to Friday. New marriage license applications stop half an hour earlier.

Is the stamp tax on a Caldwell County sale my cost as the seller?

Yes. Yes. The tax is $1.00 on each $500.00 of the price, and the statute puts it on the transferor.

Does the Caldwell County register of deeds keep wills?

No. Wills are filed with the Clerk of Court. For an inherited house, take estate questions to the clerk and deed history questions here.

How far back do Caldwell County land records go?

Back to 1841, when the county was formed. Every real estate index is searchable online, and scanned images begin in the early 1900s.
