The Register of Deeds takes deeds for recording at the County Administrative Building, 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort. The public can inspect records there on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

This office is the legal custodian of every land record and land transaction in the county, and each one is indexed and imaged into the permanent file. Only military discharges are closed to the public. An online database lets you view and print land records from home, which is the quickest way to find your vesting deed before listing.

Older paperwork works differently. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, and a cancelled deed of trust is stamped on the card itself. If an old loan was released but the online image does not show it, call the office instead of assuming the lien is still open.

Recording fees

The county keeps a single fee list, and its real estate lines follow the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. The office takes cash, credit or debit card, money orders and cashier's checks for recording.

Recording fees
Document or serviceFee
General instruments other than deeds of trust and mortgages$26 covers 15 pages, then $4 a page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 covers 35 pages, then $4 a page
Plats$21 per sheet
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee
Document containing multiple instrumentsAdditional $10
Nonstandard documentsAdditional $25
Certified copies$5 for page one, $2 per page after
Uncertified copies$0.25
Excise tax$2 per $1000.00 of sales price

An assignment that carries extra index references adds $10 for each one. Military discharges are recorded free. Ask the office to confirm the amounts before you write a check.

Avoiding the nonstandard document fee

Follow the county's recording standards. A paper that falls short will still be recorded, though the office charges $25 more than the usual fee.

  • Page size: letter or legal.
  • First page: leave 3 inches blank across the top.
  • Remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages: a 1/4 inch blank margin on the standards page.
  • Print: black on white, in a legible font, with 10 points as the smallest size treated as legible.
  • Pages: one-sided only.
  • Title: name the kind of instrument at the head of page one.

Side margins are the one point to check. The fee page says the minimum went back to one-half inch under Session Law 2019-117, while the standards page shows 1/4 inch, so ask the office which one it applies before you print the deed. Pen is acceptable for blanks and corrections, and the office may treat slightly small type as legible and skip the fee.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Carteret County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays the stamp tax when a Carteret County house sells?

The seller does. The transferor pays the register before recording, as G.S. 105-228.30 directs.

The statutory rate is $1.00 per $500.00, rounding any remainder up to a whole unit. The county fee list shows the same thing as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price. On a settlement statement it appears on the seller's side, since the closing agent usually withholds it from your proceeds.

Filing matters as much as the tax. Until a transfer is registered in the county where the land lies, G.S. 47-18 leaves it ineffective against lien creditors and paying purchasers. A buyer who skips recording leaves the door open to later claims.

What to pull from the records before listing

Gather four things from the online database or the Beaufort counter: your vesting deed, each deed of trust on the parcel with its release if one exists, any plat for the lot, and recorded easements. Plats are $21 a sheet on the fee list, and map copies are $1.00 or $2.00 depending on size.

  • The vesting deed shows exactly how title is held, including any co-owners who must sign.
  • A recorded satisfaction shows an old loan was released, and filing one costs nothing.
  • A plat or map shows the lot lines before a buyer's survey does.
  • Uncertified copies are $0.25 a page, so printing the record for your own file is cheap.

A recorded release is the proof a title company looks for. Paid-off loan with no release on file? Have the lender record one now, before the buyer's title search turns up the gap.

Property taxes and your closing

Taxes still open on the parcel come out of the closing. Phone the Tax Administration Office at 252-728-8485 early to get the amount. That office is in the same Beaufort building, so you can do both errands in one visit.

The two offices do different jobs. The register files the deed and takes in the stamp tax. The tax office bills the annual tax, answers value questions and tracks relief claims. Due dates, interest, appeals and collection are laid out in the Carteret County property tax guide.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Carteret County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other records, and inherited houses

The office also holds birth, death and marriage records for events within the county, and it issues certified copies. Certified death certificates and marriage license copies cost $10 each. Not everyone is eligible for a certified copy, so check before you go.

An heir selling a parent's house would normally collect the death certificate, the vesting deed and certified copies of recorded papers touching the land. Certified copies of recorded papers run $5 for page one, then $2 a page. With an estate involved, the Carteret County Clerk of Superior Court can say what the estate file needs.

This is a recording office. It gives no legal advice, supplies no legal forms and will not explain the legal effect of an instrument, so use an attorney for drafting.

A usual sequence for a seller: pull the vesting deed, confirm any old loan shows a release, have an attorney draft the deed to the layout standards, pay the stamp tax out of proceeds at closing, and record the deed promptly so the buyer's ownership is on the public index. Staff will not review the deed's legal effect, so any question about wording goes to your attorney before signing, not to the counter afterward.

Owners who live elsewhere can mail documents to the Beaufort address above and check the record remotely through the online database.

Carteret County housing at a glance

Population reached 70,469 on July 1, 2025, a 4.1% rise over 2020, spread across 54,293 housing units. The median owned home was worth $333,300 for 2020-2024, and owners occupy 74.7% of units.

With that many units, the recorded history on an older parcel can be long. Read the chain of deeds and any aperture card notes before a buyer's title company does.

Frequently asked questions

Will Carteret County charge me to file a release after I pay off my mortgage?

No. Releases of paid-off loans are recorded free under the statute.

What does a standard Carteret County deed cost to file?

A standard deed is $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page added. A deed that breaks the layout standards adds $25, and a document that bundles several instruments adds $10.

How can I pay for recording at the Carteret County register of deeds?

Cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check all work. Mail can be sent to 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516.

Can I view Carteret County deeds online?

Yes, through the Register of Deeds Online Database, where land records can be viewed and printed. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, so call the office about cancellation details for those older records.

What is the Carteret County transfer tax rate?

The seller pays $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price before filing. That equals the state's $1.00 per $500.00.

What the Catawba County Register of Deeds records

The office records and keeps deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, powers of attorney, plats, easements, rights of way, assumed names and similar land documents. Birth and death records, marriage licenses and notary oaths are handled here too. The land records start in 1842, when the county was carved out of Lincoln County. Lincoln County keeps anything older.

Come between eight and five on a weekday, holidays excepted, to record a document or look at filed records. The phone number is (828) 465-1573. Indexes and images go online once a document is recorded, though they have not been verified. Recorded documents are scanned within one business day.

Voters elect the register. Staff are barred from preparing documents or answering legal questions, which means an attorney should draft the deed. Wills and divorces belong to the clerk of superior court at (828) 695-6100.

How to record a deed

A paper filer delivers the signed, acknowledged deed with payment. An electronic filer goes through one of two eRecording companies: Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The filer completes a memorandum of understanding with the company before the first submission. For 2023 the county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents, a 74 percent average.

Paper filers should check a short list before the trip:

  • A deed cannot be accepted without the buyer's present mailing address on it.
  • A map or real estate instrument must name and address whoever receives it after recording.
  • Anything you want mailed back requires a stamped, addressed envelope big enough to hold it.
  • The instrument must meet the state's recording standards, and the office uses Times New Roman as its standard font.
  • A cover sheet may be required for some documents, so ask first if you are unsure.

Timing matters because of G.S. 47-18. A conveyance gives no protection against lien creditors or later buyers who paid value until it is registered where the land lies, and priority goes by the time of registration. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will reach the register.

Fees and excise tax

Recording fees are set by state statute, and the county adds a few surcharges. The excise tax is separate, and the seller pays it.

Catawba County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
General instruments, a deed among them$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, then $4.00 per added page
Loan security instruments (mortgage, deed of trust)$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, then $4.00 per added page
Subdivision plat$21.00 for every sheet
Paper that fails the state's format standards$25.00 extra
Assignment citing several deeds of trust$10 each after the first one cited
Instrument naming over 20 parties$2 for every extra party indexed
Photocopy of a recorded deed$.25 a page
Photocopy of a recorded plat$2.00 flat
Conveyance excise tax$1.00 per $500 of value, rounded up by fraction

Stated another way, the tax is $2.00 per $1,000 of price. The seller owes it, and a transfer for no payment needs no stamp. Satisfactions of deeds of trust record free. The counter takes cash, a business check, or a debit or credit card.

The county general fund keeps half of the excise tax, and the other half, less refunds and an allowance, goes to the state.

Looking up a property by address

The register's records describe land by legal description, not by street address, so an address search belongs with Tax Mapping. Three county numbers cover most seller questions:

  • Register of Deeds, (828) 465-1573, for recording, copies and the index.
  • Tax Mapping, (828) 465-8420, for matching an address to a parcel.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, (828) 695-6100, for wills and divorce records.

Mapping staff or the online real estate maps will do the address lookup. The GIS map is not a legal or binding map. Then take the parcel details to the Register of Deeds online deed search to read the chain of title.

The office cannot correct a missing item, error or misspelling on an original recorded document under G.S. 132-3, so expect to need an attorney for a correction. If a deed is lost, the office can issue a certified copy bearing its seal, which carries the same weight as the original.

The recording of a deed, more than the paper itself, is the main evidence of ownership. A seller who inherited or bought long ago should look for the vesting deed in the index before listing.

How recording ties to selling a house

With financing, a sale can produce three recordings: the deed to the buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, and a satisfaction of your old loan, which is free to record. Options, contracts to convey and leases over three years also need registration to bind later purchasers.

Chapter 47H governs contract-for-deed sales of one to four family homes in which the seller holds title through five or more payments. Within five business days the seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it, and the buyer can cancel through the third business day. A seller who used that structure should check the index for the memorandum.

On closing day the sequence is simple. The closing attorney confirms the buyer's mailing address, checks that the deed meets the recording standards and the excise tax is deducted from your proceeds. The deed then goes in by paper or through Simplifile or CSC, and it is scanned within one business day. After that the index shows the new owner, and the old loan's satisfaction, once recorded, clears your side of the chain. If something looks wrong on a recorded document, call the office first, then your attorney, since the register cannot correct the original.

Property tax runs alongside recording. What the parcel owes is stated by the tax office rather than the register, and a deferred circuit breaker balance comes due on transfer.

Catawba County at a glance

The county measures 413 square miles in the Blue Ridge foothills. The 2025 estimate is 170,172 people and 77,827 housing units. For 2020-2024 the median value of an owned home is $241,600, and 72.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

A seller who lives out of town can handle most of this by phone and mail, since the online indexes and the eRecording companies avoid a trip to the counter.

An old tract's chain of title can run back past 1842, and records before that year are held in Lincoln County.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Catawba County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8 to 5, holidays excepted. The phone is (828) 465-1573. Ask for the office's current street address when you call. eRecording is also available.

What are the charges for filing a deed with Catawba County?

The fee table above lists each charge. Page count drives the base fee, a $25.00 surcharge applies if the format rules are missed, and the seller separately owes the conveyance excise tax. Call (828) 465-1573 to confirm a total before you send a check.

Can Catawba County record a deed electronically?

Yes. All document types can be eRecorded through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The submitter completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider first.

Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Catawba County?

No. State law bars the office from preparing legal documents or giving legal advice, so you need an attorney to draft or correct a deed. Staff can show you the indexes, and certified copies of recorded deeds are $.25 per page.

Who pays the deed excise tax in Catawba County?

The seller, as grantor, pays the register before the deed is accepted. It is $1.00 per $500 of consideration, and a partial $500 counts as a whole one. Where nothing was exchanged, no stamp applies.

Office location and hours

The office occupies the Courthouse Annex at 12 East Street, Pittsboro, in the ground-level wing facing the traffic circle where the historic Superior Courthouse stands. Parking is behind the annex, reached from Chatham Street (also US 15/501 South) just past the circle. From the lot, walk to the wide stairwell opening in the middle of the building, skip the stairs, and take the passage on the left to the end of the building nearest the BP station.

Send letters to P.O. Box 756, Pittsboro, NC 27312, and use the East Street address for courier deliveries. The main number is 919-542-8235.

Three different clocks apply here. Miss a cutoff and the package waits for the next business day.

  • Front counter: weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Paper documents: last accepted at 4:30 p.m.
  • Electronic submissions: taken between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

State holidays are closed days. Remaining 2026 closings are Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, and December 24, 25 and 28.

Recording fees

Recording a deed starts at $26.00 and covers 15 pages; each page after that adds $4.00. The $2 verification fee is built into that figure. Deeds of trust run $64 for the first 35 pages and also add $4 a page beyond that. Payment is due up front, before filing.

These match the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, which also tacks on $25.00 for a nonstandard document. Chatham lists a uniform commercial code filing at $38.00 for one or two pages.

Filing a deed electronically

Electronic filing runs through two vendors, Simplifile and CSC. The office takes those submissions Monday to Friday until 4:00 p.m., and it now e-records plats as well. Title companies and attorneys file this way as a matter of routine, so sellers rarely hand-carry anything.

CSC takes questions at erecording@cscglobal.com or 1-866-652-0111. A paper filing needs the original documents. The office stores records. It does not write documents or repair errors, so staff cannot draft or correct a deed for you.

Searching is a separate service. You can search recorded deeds at chathamncrod.org. The office also sends an e-mail alert whenever something is filed under a name you pick, a useful safeguard against deed fraud.

Formatting rules that can cost you $25

The layout in G.S. 161-14(b) applies to everything filed after July 1, 2002. A noncompliant document is still recorded, though the office first collects the $25.00 nonstandard fee, so clean formatting saves money. The requirements:

  • Standard letter or legal paper.
  • Page one needs an empty three-inch strip across the top, and every other edge needs a quarter inch of clear margin.
  • Dark ink on white paper, printed on one side, in type of at least 9 points.
  • The instrument type, such as warranty deed, printed just below that empty strip.
  • A prepared-by line on page one of each deed or deed of trust, outside the margin zones.
  • Where the original should be mailed back, written on page one of each paper filing.

Pen works for filling blanks on printed forms and for corrections.

Steps from signed deed to recorded deed

Sellers rarely handle this themselves, yet the sequence is worth knowing.

  1. An attorney prepares the deed with a prepared-by line and a return-to address on page one.
  2. The closing office checks the layout so the $25.00 nonstandard fee does not apply.
  3. Excise tax is deducted from the seller's proceeds and sent with the recording fee.
  4. The package goes in electronically before 4:00 p.m., or on paper before 4:30 p.m.
  5. Staff stamp the filing time. That time sets your place in line ahead of or behind any other filing on the property.

Late arrivals are not lost. They are stamped the following business day, so plan the closing hour accordingly.

Deed excise tax and recording priority

The state charges $1.00 for every $500 of price, rounded up, under G.S. 105-228.30. The seller owes it before the deed is recorded. Half stays with the county general fund, and the state revenue department gets the other half. Your closing attorney takes it out of your proceeds and forwards it with the recording package, so you will see it itemized on the settlement statement.

Filing order matters too. Under G.S. 47-18, a transfer offers no protection against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on file with the register of deeds where the land lies, and priority follows the time stamp. A buyer's lender wants the deed logged ahead of anything else filed against the house.

The county counts 38,294 housing units, and median home value for 2020 to 2024 was $446,200. At those prices the excise tax is a sizable closing cost here, so plan for it before you list.

Birth, death and marriage records

The office also keeps births, deaths and marriages for the county and files notary oaths and assumed-name records. Marriage licenses and notary oaths require an appointment, made by calling 919-542-8235 as well.

Certified copies of birth and death records are $10.00 each, and a marriage license is $60.00. These records come up in sales more often than people expect. If you inherited the house, the title company will probably want a certified death certificate. A marriage or divorce may also change who has to sign. Order certified copies early. Only people eligible under state law can receive them.

Before your deed is recorded

Pay off the property tax, collect your paperwork, and leave recording to the closing office. Property is revalued every four years in Chatham, and the county rate held at 60 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-27, so the tax on your settlement statement may not match the bill you remember. For tax offices, appeals and relief programs, see our Chatham County property tax guide

If a mortgage is still open, get a payoff figure from the lender. Recording the cancellation costs nothing. Plat questions, old easements and missing signatures on inherited land should come up early, because the register of deeds cannot repair defects. Before listing, ask a North Carolina attorney how to clear any defect.

Selling for cash removes the lender's schedule, yet the deed still goes through this counter and these fees.

Frequently asked questions

What number reaches the Pittsboro recording desk?

Dial 919-542-8235. Staff can answer questions about filing a package. The office is at 12 East Street, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 756.

What is the latest I can bring a paper deed to the Chatham counter?

Half past four on business days. Electronic filings cut off earlier, at four, and state holidays mean no recording at all.

What is the fee for an ordinary deed?

Budget $26.00 for a deed of up to fifteen pages, with $4.00 more for every added page. The excise tax the seller pays is a separate charge.

What if my deed ignores the layout rules?

The office will accept it and add $25.00 for a nonstandard document under G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Fix the top band and print dark on white before you submit.

Which electronic vendors does Chatham work with?

Simplifile and CSC. Both feed the register of deeds on weekdays up to 4:00 p.m., and plats can go in electronically too.

Office and market snapshot

Prices are moderate, so a seller's stamp tax stays small relative to typical equity.

Recording fees

Recording costs $26 for a deed of up to fifteen pages. A deed of trust costs $64 for up to thirty-five. Past those limits, each added page is $4.

Fees posted at the Murphy counter

Plats filed after October 1991 must be clear mylar, sized 18 by 24, 21 by 30 or 24 by 36 inches. The recording amounts track the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, and a cancellation of a deed of trust is recorded without charge.

Deed stamps

The local stamp is $2 for each $1,000 of the price, equal to the statutory $1.00 per $500. By G.S. 105-228.30 the seller owes it, and it must reach the register ahead of filing. One half stays in the county's general fund, and Raleigh receives the rest.

Points a seller should know:

  • The stamp shows up among the seller's charges at closing.
  • Each $500 of price is taxed, and a partial $500 rounds up.
  • Under G.S. 47-18, an option, a contract to convey or a lease over three years binds later purchasers and lien creditors only after registration in the land's county.

Looking up tax and deed information

The county's interactive tax viewer displays tax amounts from 2008 forward. It refreshes each morning at 6 a.m., so a payment appears the next day. It was compiled for county use from recorded deeds and plats, so verify anything important against the public record.

When a value, parcel record or deed looks wrong, call the Cherokee County Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296. The recorded original is kept in Murphy, and certified copies of it are available there.

Tax relief that changes when you sell

Three groups of owners can ask the county assessor for relief: seniors, disabled owners and owners with a disabled-veteran designation. For 2026, a senior or disabled owner earning $38,800 or less may exclude the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value. The disabled veteran exclusion covers the first $45,000 and has no age or income limit. File form AV-9 by June 1 before the tax year. The statutes are G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C.

Already getting one of these benefits? Ask the Appraisal Office how a sale affects it before you sign a contract.

How a deed gets from closing table to the record

Your attorney normally runs this sequence. The deed is drafted and signed by every owner on title. The seller's stamp tax is figured from the purchase price and held back from the proceeds. The recording fee is added, and the package reaches the Murphy office before 4:30 p.m. After recording, the register keeps the original, and the new owner can order a certified copy at $5 for page one and $2 for each page after.

If you transfer property without a closing attorney, bring the signed original, payment for the fee and stamps, and a return address. Staff will not fix drafting errors, so settle any wording questions before you arrive. Aim to arrive well before the 4:30 p.m. cutoff.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cherokee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Birth, death and marriage records

Vital records live at this counter too, and some come up during a home sale. Heirs may need a death certificate, a marriage record can affect who signs, and notaries book by appointment.

  • Certified birth, death and marriage certificates: $10 each, with requests directed through the county's vital records portal.
  • Marriage license: $60.
  • Notary appointment: $10 each.
  • Copies of any record: $0.10 apiece.

If heirs need a certified certificate, order it early so the title company has it when the file is reviewed.

Questions to settle before closing day

A short call to the right office can save a delay. Ring the register at 828-837-2613 to check the fee for your page count and ask about any plat. Phone the Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296 if the parcel record does not look right or if you receive tax relief. Then have your attorney tell you the stamp amount that will print on the settlement statement.

Doing this a week ahead leaves time to correct a missing owner, an old lien or a plat problem. The register records what you hand over and does not review it for mistakes.

Selling for cash instead

Paying cash does not move the deed around the recorder. It still goes through the Murphy counter, the stamp still applies, and any deed of trust on your side still needs a payoff and a recorded release. What a cash sale removes is the buyer's appraisal and underwriting wait, which is often where inherited or repair-heavy houses stall. You still choose the closing attorney, the deed still has to match your vesting deed, and the Murphy office still files it at the same price per page.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting ready to record

Deal with the tax bill, the loan payoff and title questions before the attorney files. Property tax comes due September 1, and interest starts January 6, as set by G.S. 105-360. Because the lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, closing usually pays the current bill out of the proceeds.

Four steps keep a sale moving.

  • Identify every owner in the chain of title, including heirs on an inherited house.
  • Where lot lines are unclear, a surveyor can advise on plats, which are a separate $21 filing.
  • Request a payoff letter from each lender. Recording the release is free.
  • Dig out your vesting deed so the new deed repeats its legal description exactly.

Staff record documents but never write them, so a North Carolina attorney should prepare the deed. When repairs, liens or squabbling heirs have stalled a sale, a cash purchase avoids a lender's timetable. Our North Carolina page explains that route.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Cherokee County register's office?

75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, Murphy, NC 28906. Call 828-837-2613, and bring land records in by 4:30 p.m.

What does recording a Cherokee County deed cost?

A deed up to 15 pages is $26, then $4 a page. Deeds of trust are $64 up to 35 pages, and a plat filing is $21.

How are Cherokee County deed stamps figured?

At $2 for each $1,000 of price, the same rate the state writes as $1.00 per $500. The seller pays it when the deed goes on record.

Who answers questions about a Cherokee County tax value?

The Cherokee County Appraisal Office, at 828-835-3296, handles questions about parcel data and values.

Is there a charge for deed copies?

Yes. Plain copies are ten cents a page. A certified document is $5 for page one and $2 per page afterward, and vital record certificates are $10 each.

Chowan County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Chowan County, NC Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Chowan County, NC Register of Deeds sale

Selling in Chowan County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Chowan County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Chowan County?
We buy Chowan County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Office location and contact

Find the Register of Deeds inside the Chowan County courthouse, 101 S. Broad Street, Edenton. The mailing box is PO Box 487, Edenton, NC 27932. Call (252) 482-2619 or fax (252) 482-3062. Counter hours: eight to five, Monday through Friday.

Its mission statement names it the keeper of vital records and real estate recordings. Its real estate archive reaches back to the 1600s, marriage licenses are dated as early as 1868, and birth and death records start in 1913. That depth means a title search here can run through very old deeds.

The county has about 14,082 residents and 7,312 housing units. Median home value for 2020 to 2024 came to $235,800, with 70.5% of units lived in by their owners. Only 48 building permits were issued in 2025, so nearly every deed filed here moves an existing house or a parcel of land.

Checklist before a deed is recorded

Chowan adds a local land transfer tax, a parcel number approval and a stop at the tax office to the usual recording steps. Run down this list first.

Pre-recording checklist, Edenton office
RequirementWhat the office expects
Notary acknowledgmentSignature, seal and expiration date of the notary all filled in
Grantee addressPermanent mailing address printed on the deed itself
DrafterName of whoever drafted a deed or deed of trust, shown on page one
Recording feesPaid under the county fee list
Land transfer tax1% of the sale price, citing S.L. 1985-881
Excise tax$2.00 per $1,000 or fraction of it, based on the sales price
Parcel numberApproved by the Land Records/GIS Department for any document with a legal description
Tax officeDeed presented with an affidavit of consideration before recording

Every document needs a date and a legal description too. A deed with an attached survey, and any other survey, must be reviewed and signed by the county's review officer before it is recorded.

County land transfer tax and state excise tax

Sellers here owe two taxes. Edenton collects a 1% land transfer tax on the sale price (S.L. 1985-881) in addition to the state excise tax. In the statute, G.S. 105-228.30, the excise tax reads $1.00 per $500, and the county's list restates it as $2.00 per $1,000. Whoever transfers the property pays before the deed goes on record.

Both charges rise with the price, so skip guessing from memory. Ask the register or your closing attorney for today's numbers and for how your contract splits them. Neither tax can be put off until after recording. Read each tax line on your net sheet before you accept it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Chowan County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Stops before the register of deeds

Two other offices handle a deed before the register does. Land Records/GIS approves a parcel identification number for any real estate document carrying a legal description, plats included, and its review officer signs surveys. Find it in the same courthouse at 101 S. Broad Street, or call (252) 482-7157.

The Tax Office is the second stop, and many sellers overlook it. The register will not record a deed until it has been shown there with an affidavit of consideration. The tax office is at 305 W. Freemason Street, Edenton, phone (252) 482-8486, mailing address PO Box 1030.

  1. An attorney prepares the deed, listing the drafter, the buyer's mailing address and the legal description.
  2. Land Records/GIS approves the parcel number and reviews any attached survey.
  3. Take the deed and the affidavit of consideration to the tax office.
  4. Pay the recording fee, excise tax and transfer tax at the register, and the deed is recorded.

A closing attorney normally runs all four. Without one, for instance when deeding a house to a relative, you carry out each step yourself.

E-recording and fees

Electronic recording in Edenton is limited to satisfactions, the papers that release a paid-off mortgage or deed of trust. Lenders and title companies send those online. Deeds, deeds of trust and plats, including the deed that sells your house, are delivered in person or mailed with the right fee.

Certified copies can be bought online by card for pickup or mail, and checkout adds a small processing fee. Staff will not help you complete documents or search title, since state law prohibits them from practicing law without a license.

The statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10 puts a general instrument at $26.00 through 15 pages and a deed of trust at $64.00 through 35, plus $4.00 per page beyond. Chowan's posted fee list controls, so phone ahead before writing a check.

What to bring to the counter

Recording without an attorney takes preparation. Carry the signed, notarized original with the drafter named on page one, a permanent mailing address for the buyer, a full legal description and a parcel number that Land Records/GIS has already approved. Add the affidavit of consideration from the tax office and money for the recording fee and both taxes.

Leave one item out and you probably make a second trip, since deeds cannot be e-recorded here. Staff can explain the fees but cannot repair a drafting mistake.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chowan County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property tax relief and a sale

Three state programs lower or defer tax for qualifying owners. You claim each one from the county assessor, not the Department of Revenue.

  • Senior and disabled owners may exclude whichever is greater, $25,000 or half the appraised value of a primary home, if 2026 income is $38,800 or less.
  • Owners with a disabled-veteran designation, and their unmarried surviving spouses, get $45,000 of appraised value excluded, with no age or income limit on the state form.
  • A circuit breaker limits the bill to a share of income and defers the rest as a lien that comes due on a sale or at the owner's death.

The deferral is what shows up at closing: tax deferred for up to three earlier years is payable once a disqualifying event, such as a sale, happens. See G.S. 105-277.1B, for the rules; the AV-9 application goes to the county tax office.

Recording priority and tax bills

An unregistered deed offers little protection. Under G.S. 47-18, it affects purchasers and lien creditors only once registered where the land lies, and generally the earlier registration prevails. Both sides therefore want the deed filed the day of closing.

Property tax is the other thing to watch. Bills fall due September 1 and accrue interest after January 5 under G.S. 105-360, and the lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date. Call the Tax Office, (252) 482-8486, for what you owe today, when the next revaluation is, and which relief programs apply to the house.

If you inherited a Chowan house, have fallen behind on payments or want to skip repairs, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale route. A cash buyer does not shortcut the process. The checklist, the tax office visit and the transfer tax still apply, so leave time before closing.

Frequently asked questions

What number do I call for Chowan deed questions?

Call (252) 482-2619. The courthouse office at 101 S. Broad Street, Edenton, serves the public weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00.

Does Chowan County e-record deeds?

No. The office e-records satisfactions only, so a deed must be mailed or delivered to Edenton with the correct fee.

What taxes apply when a Chowan deed is recorded?

A land transfer tax of 1% of the sale price and an excise tax of $2.00 per $1,000 or fraction. Both must be paid before recording.

Do I have to visit the tax office before recording in Chowan County?

Yes. Every deed goes to the Chowan County Tax Office with an affidavit of consideration first. The office is at 305 W. Freemason Street, Edenton.

Can Chowan County staff help me write or fix my deed?

No. They cannot help complete documents or do a title search, since that would be unauthorized practice of law. Use a North Carolina attorney.

Clay County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Clay County?
We buy Clay County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where Clay County deeds are filed

The Register of Deeds is at 261 Courthouse Drive, Suite 2, in Hayesville, or call 828-389-0087. Its website is deeds.claync.us. Your deed to the buyer joins the permanent land record at this office, where the buyer's lender or title attorney can verify it.

Recordable items include deeds, loan documents, cancellations, plats, assumed business names and powers of attorney. The same staff issue marriage licenses, keep vital records and military discharges, and commission notaries.

Staff will not give legal advice, hand out forms, coach drafting, or explain what a recorded paper does to your rights. See a lawyer first.

Clay is a small market of about 12,239 residents and 7,868 housing units. Owner-occupants hold 81.2% of occupied homes, valued at a median $278,400 in the 2020 to 2024 period.

Page layout rules

Break the county's layout rules and your deed costs more to file. The real estate records page has the full list.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, printed black on white and blank on the reverse.
  • Page one needs an empty three-inch top margin; keep a quarter inch clear on its other edges and on all edges of later pages.
  • Nothing under 9-point type. Ink is fine for blanks and corrections.
  • The title of the document, for example Deed, stated just beneath the empty band on page one.
  • The signer's signature, plus a notary's seal and acknowledgment.
  • On deeds and loan documents, a "Prepared By" line naming the drafter, the grantee's mailing address, and the excise tax noted on the deed.

Nonconforming paper is still recorded, after the clerk adds a $25.00 non-standard document fee (G.S. 161-10(a)(19)). Correct the margins beforehand and you skip it.

Recording charges

One statewide schedule sets the charges, so Clay matches every other county. Payment is due when you file, so have the office add up your packet before you visit.

What a Clay County seller pays at the Hayesville counter
Document or chargeAmount
Warranty or other deed$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; each page after that adds $4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 covers pages 1 to 35; each page after that adds $4.00
Payoff cancellation of a loan lienFree
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Non-standard document add-on$25.00
Deed excise tax, statute wording$1.00 per $500.00 of price or value, rounding up
Deed excise tax, Clay County wording$2.00 per 1000

Both excise lines describe a single rate in different words.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clay County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays the excise tax

It falls on the seller, as grantor, and the register holds the deed until it is paid.

Half is kept in Clay County's general fund. The state receives the other half each month, less refunds and the county's allowance. You will find it under seller charges on the settlement statement, because the attorney subtracts it from your proceeds.

Why filing order matters

G.S. 47-18 says a deed does not protect a buyer from lien creditors or competing purchasers until it is registered in the land's county. Whoever registers first ranks first. Options, contracts to convey, leases longer than three years and rights of first refusal or first offer follow the same rule. A buyer holding an option on Clay County land will want to record it at this office.

Seller financing follows its own chapter. When a one to four family home is sold on a contract for deed, the seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day.

Property values and tax bills

New real property values took effect in 2026. The tax office appeals page says reappraisals run every eight years. The usual sequence is the same each time: review your value notice, ask for an informal review, file a written or in-person appeal if you disagree, then possibly appear before the board. Ask the tax office, not the register, how a new value will change your next bill.

The collector also bills Town of Hayesville taxes. The online payment portal lists a 2.25 percent service fee on credit cards, a $4.95 flat debit fee and a $2.00 electronic check fee.

Bills fall due September 1. A payment made after January 5 picks up interest, 2 percent at first and then three-fourths of a percent for each month starting in February (G.S. 105-360). Make sure whoever runs your closing confirms the bill was paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Clay County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps for a seller

Selling cleanly in Clay County means doing a few things in order. First confirm that the deed on file matches how you hold title and that no paid-off loan is missing its recorded cancellation. Next, a lawyer drafts the deed with a Prepared By line, the buyer's mailing address and the excise tax notation. The signed, notarized deed then goes to Suite 2 with the fee, and the register holds it until the excise tax is paid.

After recording, the time of registration fixes your buyer's priority. Consider keeping a certified copy for your files. Certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page, so a short deed is inexpensive to document. If anything about the recording looks wrong later, the office can pull the record for you.

Selling an inherited house

If you inherited a Clay County house, the paper trail back to the owner who died begins at the superior court clerk's office, well before the register's counter. Inherited property makes up a real share of local sales.

A small estate can be settled by affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1 when personal property, after liens, totals $20,000 or less and 30 days have gone by; a lone surviving spouse can go to $30,000 after any spousal allowance. The affidavit is filed with the clerk in the decedent's home county and has to describe every parcel of land the person held. The state repealed its estate tax, so there is none for deaths since January 1, 2013.

When the clerk's paperwork is in order, the signed deed goes to Suite 2 and is recorded at the table's rates.

Watching for a fraudulent filing

From the register's website you can reach online land records and a county fraud-alert service. Sign up, and a notice goes out whenever something new is filed under your name.

Look before you list. Two things can stall a closing: a filing you never signed, and a loan you repaid long ago that nobody cancelled. Satisfactions cost nothing to record, so have the lender file one at payoff. If a house needs fast action, our North Carolina page explains a cash sale option.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where are Clay County deeds filed?

In Suite 2 at 261 Courthouse Drive, Hayesville, NC 28904, phone 828-389-0087. The deed should follow the office's published margin, type and notary rules.

Will the Hayesville office help me draft a deed?

No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft, complete or explain a deed. Hire a lawyer for the drafting.

What if my deed breaks the layout rules?

It is still filed, after a $25.00 non-standard document fee. Fix the margins, type size and notations first to skip the fee.

Is the deed tax my cost as the seller?

Yes. It is paid before filing, at $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or value, counting any part of $500.00 as a full unit.

How often does Clay County reappraise?

Every eight years. New values took effect in 2026, and the tax office can explain what your value means for your bill.

Selling in Cleveland County?

Visiting or contacting the Shelby office

The Register of Deeds is in Room 151 of the county administration building, 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby, NC 28150. It is open weekdays from eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and the land records line is 704-484-4834. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1210, Shelby, NC 28151, and email to rod.info@clevelandcountync.gov, as the office's frequently asked questions page lists.

Everything on file is public except military discharge records. Passports, marriage licenses (by appointment) and certified vital records go through the same counter, so expect a mixed crowd.

Owners live in most Cleveland County homes: about 70.9 percent of occupied homes, with a median value of $200,000 for 2020 to 2024. The county has roughly 103,325 residents.

What the office records and how to submit

The office records the paperwork that moves or secures a house. It accepts paper, overnight courier and electronic submissions. The land record recordings page lists the documents it files.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust
  • Easements and powers of attorney
  • Satisfactions of paid loans
  • Plats, accepted by e-recording since 2019
  • Assumed business name certificates
  • Notary oaths, by appointment only

Electronic filers use Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Send an original by courier with a prepaid return envelope and the recorded document comes back in it, and there is no extra charge to schedule a FedEx pickup. Wills are not recorded here; they go to the Clerk of Court.

Filing fees and copy charges

A filing costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each page after that. Mortgage-type documents get a longer first block under the state fee statute: 35 pages for $64.00.

  • Copies of deeds in person: $.25 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for every page after it.
  • Assumed business name certificate: $26.00 to record, plus a $15.00 vendor convenience fee if filed online, for $41.00 through the online portal.
  • Transfer tax on a sale: $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price.

To put a new name on a title, have a new deed drawn up by an attorney. Staff record deeds but do not draft them.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cleveland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays the transfer tax

The seller does, and the register collects it before filing. The state statute sets it at $1.00 per $500.00 of consideration or value, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $500.00, which equals the office's per-thousand wording.

Half of the money stays in the county general fund. The other half, minus refunds and the county's allowance, moves on to the state. At a closing the attorney usually deducts it from your proceeds, so you see a deduction on the settlement statement instead of a bill at the counter.

Searching Cleveland County land records online

Verified online records start in 1995. Older material sits in an unverified index and in scanned index books. The available land records page gives the ranges.

Online coverage of Cleveland County land records
Record setDates covered
Searchable real property index01/03/1995 to present
New unverified searchable index01/01/1945 to 12/31/1994
Searchable plat index (starts with Plat Book 19)05/16/1995 to present
Viewable images of index books1841 to 1944

Entries from 1979 to 1985 can be searched only by name and year, so open the document to see the exact recording date. Images from before 1960 need the book and page number, and a book such as 15-A is typed as 15A with no dash. Anything not online can be viewed at the office, which also offers escrow accounts for faxed or emailed copies for a fee.

Beware the $86.00 deed notice

Some residents receive a solicitation that looks like a bill. The register of deeds warns people not to pay it. The mailer asks for $86.00 for a "Property Assessment Profile" that includes a copy of your deed.

The same documents cost 25 cents per page from the Cleveland County Mapping Office and the Register of Deeds. Report the notice to the Consumer Protection Division of the N.C. Department of Justice at 919-716-6000. The office also runs a fraud detection notification service. After you sign up, check your spam folder for the confirmation email and confirm it.

If a relative is selling or has inherited a house in the county, pass this warning along.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cleveland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Plats and parcel maps

The register of deeds keeps recorded plats only. Every other map comes from the Cleveland County Mapping Office at 704-484-4849, which also answers parcel questions by street address.

If you plan to divide a lot, call the register before filing. The office points e-recording filers to it for the review officer and administrator signatures that plats need.

Inherited houses and seller-financed sales

Two situations call for extra paperwork before the register can act. After a death, G.S. 28A-25-1 lets an heir, creditor or public administrator use an affidavit in place of a full estate once 30 days have gone by and personal property net of liens is $20,000 or less. The affidavit goes to the court clerk and describes every tract of real property the decedent owned.

A seller who finances a one to four family home through a contract for deed must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days under Chapter 47H. The buyer has until midnight on the third business day to cancel. Both tasks end at the Shelby counter. If a house is stuck in probate or needs repairs before a sale, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale route.

After the deed is filed

Tax Administration shares the building at 311 East Marion Street and answers at 704-484-4843. Bring questions about the bill on the parcel you just sold to that office.

Bills are due each September 1 and carry interest from January 6 (G.S. 105-360), so make sure your settlement agent knows what has been paid. Recording is a separate step, and G.S. 47-18 ranks instruments by who registers first where the parcel sits. The deed belongs at the Shelby counter the day you close.

If you file yourself rather than through an attorney, send the original with payment for the $26.00 first block of pages and the transfer tax. A prepaid return envelope brings the recorded deed back to you. Call 704-484-4834 first if you are unsure what your document needs, since staff can explain fees but cannot draft or correct it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When can I visit the Cleveland County deed office?

Weekdays from eight to five, in Room 151 at 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby. Call 704-484-4834 about land records.

Does the Shelby office accept electronic filings?

Yes. It e-records through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and has taken plats electronically since 2019. Overnight courier recordings are also accepted at the Shelby address.

What is the price of filing a deed in Shelby?

$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for each added page. A sale also carries transfer tax, which the office puts at $2.00 per thousand dollars of the price.

Are wills filed with the Cleveland County deed office?

No. Wills go to the Clerk of Court. Deeds, easements, plats, loan documents and payoff satisfactions go to the register.

What do I do with an $86.00 deed notice that looks like a bill?

Do not pay it. The register says the property profile is available for 25 cents a page, and it asks you to report the mailer to the Consumer Protection Division at the N.C. Department of Justice.

Columbus County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Columbus County, NC Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Columbus County, NC Register of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Columbus County, NC Register of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Office location and cutoff times

Columbus County deeds go to Suite B at 125 Washington Street, Whiteville. Mail goes to PO Box 1086, Whiteville, 28472. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and shuts for county holidays.

New recordings are taken until 4:45 p.m. each day, a quarter hour ahead of closing time. Marriage license applications end at 4:30 p.m.

Sellers reach this office last. Both your deed to the buyer and the buyer's lender's deed of trust are filed in Whiteville, typically by the closing attorney or title office. Keep the cutoff in mind when you read a closing calendar.

Recording fees

Ordinary deeds start at $26.00 for fifteen pages and add $4.00 per extra page. Columbus follows the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10.

Columbus County recording fees
DocumentFee
Deed of trust$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, plus $4.00 per added page
Deeds, easements and most other instruments$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, plus $4.00 per added page
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge
  • Seller pays nothing to record a release of a paid-off mortgage. Certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each page after, and a UCC filing for two pages is $38.00.
  • Copies made at the counter or ordered by mail cost 25 cents a page, and online viewing of deeds is free.
  • A notary oath taken at the office carries a $10 fee, payable by cash or local check.

Deed excise tax

Whoever sells pays the excise tax, and it is collected at the counter ahead of filing. The rate in G.S. 105-228.30 is $1 per $500 of price or value, with any part of $500 rounded up. The county FAQ gives the same rate as $2 per thousand dollars of purchase price. One half stays in the county, and the state revenue department gets the other.

The amount rises with the price and appears as its own settlement line. Register staff cannot quote it without the deed in front of them, so get the number from your closing attorney before signing day.

To change the name on title, record a new deed at the usual $26.00 rate. The office advises hiring an attorney to draft it and warns that excise tax can apply.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Columbus County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording and searching records online

Electronic recording covers every document type but plats. The register's website lists the approved vendors on its e-recording page. A closing package filed that way can make the 4:45 p.m. cutoff with nobody driving to Whiteville.

The online index works by name, so each search begins with a person or company rather than a house number, and staff cannot say who owns a given street address. If you need to find an owner by address, the county tax office is the place; its land records and mapping staff can help.

  • Enter the owner's name, then open the recorded deed.
  • Compare the legal description in the deed against your tax bill.
  • Scan the deed of trust section for a mortgage that never got a satisfaction.
  • Questions about mechanics liens and judgments belong with the Clerk of Court at the courthouse, not the register.

Why the recording date matters

When two claims compete for one piece of land, the recording date settles it. Registration is what counts under G.S. 47-18. Until a deed, option, long lease or right of first refusal is registered in the land's county, its holder has no shield against lien creditors or paying buyers, and the first to register ranks highest. A signed deed alone does not finish a sale, because until the register stamps a recording time on it, a later claim could still move ahead.

Owner financing is a special case under Chapter 47H, which covers a home for one to four families sold in five or more payments while the seller retains title. The seller must file the contract or a memorandum within five business days, and the buyer can cancel for three business days. Study the whole chapter first.

Farm notice on land records

A parcel near active farming picks up a warning in the land records under Session Law 2018-113. The triggers are a qualifying poultry, swine or dairy farm, or a voluntary agricultural district, within one-half mile, or any other qualifying farm within 600 feet.

Your buyer's title search may flag the parcel. Nobody can sue over a researcher's failure to report the notice, and brokers and appraisers are not liable for omitting it. It informs; it does not restrict the sale. About 54 people live per square mile on the county's 938.12 square miles of land, which makes farm neighbors common. Buyers will ask about it, so have an answer ready.

Preparing your own filing

If you file the deed without a closing attorney, check the basics before you drive to Whiteville. Count your pages so you can bring the exact fee, which is paid when you file. Know the excise tax figure beforehand, because staff cannot calculate it without the deed. Get there before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff, and let an attorney draft the document, as the office advises.

Once recorded, the deed can be viewed online at no charge, or you can ask for a certified copy at the counter.

A seller's timeline in Whiteville

Think of the recording step as the last domino. Once the buyer's funds are cleared and everyone has signed, the closing attorney sends the deed and the lender's deed of trust to Suite B, either by hand or through an e-recording vendor. If the package misses the 4:45 p.m. window, nothing is wrong with the sale; it simply sits until the next business morning, and a competing claim that gets registered first would outrank yours.

A seller who is out of town should confirm that the deed was recorded and not just signed. A quick look at the name-based online index will show it.

Local market in brief

Columbus is rural, with about 50,487 residents and 23,724 housing units. Owner-occupants live in 71.1% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $146,000. Just 55 building permits were issued in 2025, so almost every deed moves an older house. Weigh your asking price against that median.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What the county tax bill means for closing

Taxes come due September 1. The tax office accepts mail (PO Box 1468, Whiteville), phone, drop box, counter and online payment at columbus.webtaxpay.com.

No penalty applies until early January. Then comes a 2% charge for January 6 to the end of that month, followed by three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of a month beginning February 1 (G.S. 105-360). The tax lien on real property attaches as of the listing date, so an unpaid bill stays with the parcel when it sells.

Before you close, ask the tax office for the amount owed and pass that payoff figure to whoever prepares your settlement statement. The assessor handles homestead relief for seniors and disabled owners on Form AV-9 and can supply current forms. If back taxes or repairs make an ordinary sale hard, a cash sale is another route; see our North Carolina page.

Frequently asked questions

Who files the deed after a Columbus County sale?

The register's office in Whiteville. Your closing attorney or title office normally submits the package, at the counter or through an e-recording vendor, before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff.

What does the register charge for a deed here?

A flat $26.00 covers fifteen pages, and each added page is $4.00. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for 35 pages.

Who owes the deed excise tax on a Columbus County sale?

The seller. The register collects at the counter before filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value, which the county FAQ words as $2 per thousand dollars.

Can the Register of Deeds look up who owns a certain address?

No. The retrieval system is name based, so a search needs a person or company name. Use the county tax office for address-based parcel records.

Where do I ask about liens and judgments on a Columbus County property?

Ask the Clerk of Court at the courthouse. Also check recorded deeds of trust for any unreleased mortgage.

Where Craven County deeds are recorded

Land documents here go to 226 Pollock Street, New Bern, ZIP 28560. Reach the office at 252-636-6617. State law makes the register one of three county-wide elected offices.

On the land side the office handles deeds, deeds of trust, plats, maps and every other instrument touching real property. Staff also keep vital records and military discharges and issue marriage licenses and assumed business names. Records go back more than three centuries, so an old family tract can be traced at the same office that records a current sale.

What matters most to a seller is the cutoff. Recording stops at 4:30 p.m., and notaries are not sworn in after that hour either. A late funding would be filed the next business day, so ask your closing office how it plans for that.

Recording fees

Fifteen pages of an ordinary deed run $26, then $4 a page. A deed of trust runs $64 for 35 pages and $4 for every page beyond.

Craven County land record charges
Document or serviceFee
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
All other instruments, first 15 pages$26
Each page past the first 15 (or past 35 for a deed of trust)$4
Satisfaction of a deed of trustNo fee
Several recordings combined in one document, indexed separately$10
Non-standard document$25
Plat$21 per page
Excise tax$1 for each $500 of consideration, rounded up

Copies, vital records and marriage licenses can be paid for with cash, check or card; call about any other payment type. A $3.50 convenience fee applies to online vital-record orders through the county's vendor, but not to a real estate recording.

Who pays the deed excise tax

This one is the seller's. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay the register ahead of filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value.

  • A leftover fraction of $500 is treated as a whole $500.
  • Half the money stays in the county's general fund; half goes to the state.
  • It follows the deed's stated consideration or value and is listed among the seller's charges on the settlement statement.

Your closing attorney will work out the exact dollars. The result can differ from a quick estimate from the price when the price is not the full value of what changes hands.

Recording electronically and searching records

Three tools sit on the Real Estate page of the register's site: an e-recording partner page, a public records search and a UCC filings page. The sidebar also carries a Recordation Notification link, whose coverage the office can explain.

Lenders and closing offices that send many documents are the natural users of e-recording, and with an attorney handling your closing you will rarely file anything yourself. Mailed UCC filings need a check made out to Register of Deeds at the Pollock Street address.

  • Find your vesting deed through the online search and compare its legal description with what you plan to convey.
  • Before listing, scan for any deed of trust lacking a satisfaction.
  • If the house was inherited, ask what the office keeps under the wills and divorce decrees pages in its menu.

What registration does to your title

Registration sets priority. G.S. 47-18 denies protection to an unregistered deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal against lien creditors and purchasers for value, with competing claims ranked by registration time.

Sellers should ask for proof of recording once the funds move. The release of an old mortgage works the same way. Recording a satisfaction is free, so verify that a paid-off loan no longer appears as open on the index.

Chapter 47H, on contracts for deed, adds its own recording duty. The seller must file the contract or a memorandum inside five business days, the buyer may cancel during three business days, and forfeiture needs written notice with at least 30 days to cure. Read that chapter first if you plan to finance a buyer.

Checklist before the deed is filed

Look over the register's index and fee schedule before closing; problems found now are cheaper than problems found after funding.

  • See that the index lists your vesting deed under the name you are selling in, with a legal description that agrees with the survey or tax record.
  • Match every deed of trust with a satisfaction. Because satisfactions cost nothing to record, a payoff lender has no fee reason to hold one back.
  • Count the deed's pages: $4 more per page after 15, or after 35 for a deed of trust.
  • Ask whether the instrument is non-standard, which carries a $25 fee, or whether several recordings are bundled in one document, which adds $10 for separate indexing.
  • Get the current-year payoff from Tax Collection so no bill stays open after the title changes hands.

Your closing attorney sees the whole title picture and should have the last word, but these items give you questions to ask.

If you file the deed yourself

Few Craven County sellers ever carry a deed to the counter, but some transfers happen without a closing office. If yours does, bring the signed original, the fee for its page count and the excise tax. Get there before 4:30 p.m. for same-day recording; anything later is recorded the next business day.

Review the layout first, since a non-standard document costs $25 extra and bundled recordings add $10 for separate indexing. Afterward, search the online records to confirm the deed is indexed under the right names, and file the recording details with your closing papers.

Flood insurance and tax items

Planning moved the county's Community Rating System class from 8 to 7, lifting the flood insurance premium discount for owners in unincorporated areas from 10% to 15%. A buyer's insurance agent can say what applies at a specific address.

Tax bills are separate from the register. Payment is due September 1, and interest holds off until after January 5. Ask the Tax Collection Division, 252-636-6605, for a payoff figure ahead of closing so the bill is cleared by the time the deed goes on record.

If a home faces tax foreclosure, the county's foreclosure page lists properties for sale and gives the tax collection email for questions. Listed properties are not owned by the county, and owners are pointed to a state homeowner assistance site for delinquent tax help. If you would rather skip repairs and delays, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale.

Local market in brief

Craven County is mid-sized and growing: roughly 105,025 residents now against 100,720 at the 2020 count, living in 50,334 housing units. The median owner-occupied value was $231,600 for 2020 to 2024, with 68.4% of homes owner-held, and 553 building permits were issued in 2025. Eight towns, Bridgeton through Vanceboro, lie within its borders, so a town levy may apply to your parcel; the tax office can tell you.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Craven County deed get filed?

In New Bern, at the register's Pollock Street office. Recording ends at 4:30 p.m., so ask your closing office how a later deed is handled.

What is the price of recording a Craven deed?

$26 for fifteen pages plus $4 per extra page. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages.

Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost anything in Craven County?

No. A satisfaction of deed of trust is recorded at no charge.

Who covers excise tax on a Craven sale?

The seller. It goes to the register ahead of filing at $1 per $500 of consideration, with a partial $500 counted in full.

Can I look up Craven deeds from home?

Yes. The register links an online public records search, and its Real Estate page covers e-recording partners.

Where to find the Cumberland County Register of Deeds

The office is in Room 114 of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse, 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville. The land records line is 910-678-7775. Office hours and the yearly holiday schedule are posted at ccrod.org.

Land records reach back to 1754, which the office gives as the county's official start. The same counter handles notary oaths and vital records, and retired service members can file discharge papers (DD-214) free of charge.

Why filing time on a deed matters

A buyer in this state has no protection from rival claimants until the deed is on the public record at the courthouse. If two papers conflict, the one registered first generally prevails, which is why the recorded time stamp is worth checking.

These habits keep the paperwork clean:

  • Have each signature notarized before anything is carried to Dick Street.
  • Pair the deed with a payment covering the excise tax and the filing fee.
  • Ask the closing attorney what date and time the filing was stamped.
  • Save the book and page reference from the recorded copy.

Counter clerks cannot draft a deed or advise on its wording. That is attorney work.

Recording fees

The schedule on the office website dates from October 1, 2016. Filing an ordinary deed begins at $26.00 and a mortgage filing begins at $64.00. Other charges follow.

Recording fees at the Cumberland County office
Document or serviceFee
Deed or other instrument, first 15 pages$26.00, then $4.00 for each additional page
Mortgage or deed of trust, first 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 for each additional page
Second instrument inside one document$10.00
Document in a non-standard format$25.00 added to the recording fee
SatisfactionsNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each page after
Plat or map recording$21.00 per page
DD-214 recordingNo fee

Pay by check or money order to the office. A document recorded a second time is charged as if new.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cumberland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deed excise tax

The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and a partial thousand is rounded up. The statute states the same rate as $1.00 per $500. It goes in with the filing fee and is written on page one of the deed.

The seller, whom the law calls the transferor, is the one who owes it, and the clerk collects before recording. Half goes to the county and half to the state. If the contract price is not a round number, your closing attorney can work out the amount.

What a deed needs before it is accepted

Page one has to name the preparer and carry a return address. The recording requirements page lists:

  • The draftsman line, usually written "Prepared by" or "Drawn by."
  • A return address block, also on page one.
  • The excise tax or revenue amount on the front of the deed.
  • Paper size, margins, type size and page count within state recording standards.
  • Signatures notarized before filing.

Satisfactions and UCC filings do not have to follow the formatting rules. A deed with the wrong layout is still taken, but $25.00 is added.

Property Notification alerts

Enrollment is free, and an email arrives whenever a recorded document carries your name. The office pitches it as a guard against deed fraud. See a filing you never approved? Phone a real estate attorney.

To enroll, go to ccrod.org, pick Records Search, choose New Property Notification and follow the screens. An alert shows the matched name, the date, the book and page, and a link to the document. The alerts are no guarantee against fraud, but they help if you own a vacant or inherited Fayetteville property.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cumberland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deed records and the property tax listing

On January 1, Tax Administration looks to documents indexed here and in the Clerk of Court's estates division to decide who the listing owner is. The county keeps a permanent listing, so owners report only what changed, such as a deck, an in-ground pool or a remodel. Forms are due back by January 31.

Send them to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or drop them at Room 530 of the courthouse. Bills are due September 1. Interest of two percent starts January 6, with three-quarters of a percent more each month from February 1. For a sale partway through the year, ask Tax Administration who is billed.

An owner rated permanently and totally disabled through military service can apply at the assessor's office for a state exclusion of $45,000 in appraised value.

Housing in the county

Cumberland County has 338,473 people, 146,623 housing units and 652.56 square miles of land. Owners occupy 55.0 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental market. Typical owner-occupied value is $199,200, typical gross rent is $1,222 a month and typical household income is $61,291. Individual streets vary.

If you are comparing sale options, remember that a typical sale here involves four recording-related pieces: the deed itself, the excise tax, the filing fee, and a satisfaction for any loan you pay off. Only the satisfaction is free, and the DD-214 recording is free for service members as well. Ask your attorney to list all four on the settlement statement so nothing is missed at closing. Questions about the amounts can go to the land records line at 910-678-7775.

What a seller should check before signing

Start with the loan. A satisfaction for a paid-off mortgage is recorded free, so a cleared loan should leave that document in the record. When payments have lapsed, the lender goes through a power-of-sale hearing before the clerk of superior court, and after the sale is reported anyone can file an upset bid within ten days, at least five percent over the price and $750.00 or more higher.

Then look at title: the last recorded deed, any liens, and whether a deed of trust is still open. If the house passed through an estate, the clerk's estates division has records worth reviewing. Your attorney usually runs this search, and your job is to hand over the old closing papers and any loan statements you have.

After closing, the executed deed is delivered here along with the tax and fee, and the stamped original returns to the address on page one. Selling for cash skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting, yet recording costs still apply. File the book and page numbers with your sale papers.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the excise tax on a Cumberland County home sale?

The seller. The statute calls that person the transferor, and the tax is collected at the counter before the deed is recorded. The county's page shows $2.00 per $1,000 of price, and the statute shows $1.00 per $500.

What does it cost to record a deed in Cumberland County?

Deeds begin at $26.00 for fifteen pages, plus $4.00 for each page beyond that. A mortgage begins at $64.00 for thirty-five pages. Satisfactions are free.

Can Register of Deeds staff draft my deed?

No. State law bars them from legal advice and from writing deeds. Get it drafted, signed and notarized first, and take wording questions to an attorney.

What is the Property Notification service?

A free email alert for when a document under your name is filed in Fayetteville. Enroll at ccrod.org under Records Search. The office calls it an early warning, not a fraud guarantee.

Where does a real property listing form go?

Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or hand it in at Room 530 of the courthouse. January 31 is the due date, so changes count that year.

Currituck County Register of Deeds: location and hours

The office is at 153 Courthouse Road, Suite 600, Currituck, NC 27929. It is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Deeds and other property and business papers are recorded, indexed and kept here. Marriage licenses and certified vital records come from the same counter, and any recorded paper can be copied for a fee.

Two transfer taxes on a Currituck sale

Two taxes apply when real estate changes hands in Currituck. The state's excise stamp tax runs $1.00 per $500.00 of price. The county adds its own land transfer tax at $1.00 per $100.00, rounding up for any fraction.

State law puts the excise tax on the seller, paid at the counter ahead of recording. Who pays the county tax is a question for the office and your closing attorney. Both amounts follow your price, so ask for exact numbers early and look for them on the settlement statement.

Recording fees

Fifteen pages of a general instrument cost $26.00, and thirty-five pages of a mortgage or deed of trust cost $64.00. Everything else:

What the Currituck office charges
Document or serviceFee
Instruments in general, pages 1 to 15$26.00, with $4.00 per page after that
Deed of trust or mortgage, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Each extra instrument in a single document$10.00
Satisfaction of a deed of trust or mortgage$0.00 for the first reference, $25.00 for each added reference on the same instrument
Plats, maps and condominium unit ownership filings$21.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Uncertified copy at the office$.25 per page
