Mailed copies are $1.00 a page, and your request needs a stamped return envelope.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Currituck County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Formatting a document for recording

Format is set by state rules (G.S. 161-14). Ignore them and the paper still gets recorded, at a $25.00 surcharge for non-standard documents. What the notices page asks for:

  • Letter size (8 1/2 by 11) or legal size (8 1/2 by 14) paper.
  • A three-inch top margin on the first page and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black type on white paper, 10 point or larger.
  • Print on one side of the page only.
  • A title line naming the kind of instrument, placed first.

Blanks and corrections may be filled in with a pen. Keep Social Security, driver license and bank account numbers off the page unless the law demands them. When one is already in a recorded image, a written request gets it taken off the online copy, and there is no charge.

Farm proximity notice

Under G.S. 106-741, a county's land records must carry a notice for tracts near a qualifying farm, such as a poultry, swine or dairy operation within half a mile. Currituck keeps a file of parcels that may sit within half a mile of farm use property. That file was last updated in February 2019.

Selling inland acreage? Buyers and their title searchers may run into the notice. The statute says a searcher's failure to report a nearby farm creates no legal claim. For your own parcel, staff can point you to the current file.

2026 property tax rates

The countywide 2026 rate is .60 per $100 of valuation, down from .62 for 2025. It applies equally to land, buildings, mobile homes, boats, vehicles and business personal property. Special districts add to it:

  • Carova Beach Road Service District: .02, shown as .62 combined.
  • Corolla Fire Protection Service District: .08, shown as .68 combined.
  • Knotts Island Fire Protection Service District: .09, shown as .69 combined.
  • Moyock Watershed Service District: .01, shown as .61 combined.
  • Ocean Sands North/Crown Point Stormwater: .255, with listed combinations for properties also in the water and sewer or fire districts.

Solid waste fees for 2026 are $500.00 per dwelling unit on the southern Currituck beaches and $274.00 per dwelling unit on the mainland and northern beaches. A 6 percent occupancy tax applies if the house has been a vacation rental. The tax office can tell you which districts cover your parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Currituck County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a recording moves through the office

Before you go, line up the pieces: a deed drafted by an attorney, signatures notarized, the first page showing the title line and the preparer, and payment for the filing fee and excise tax. The office checks the format, collects the money and records the paper. Anything that misses the format rules is still taken, with the extra $25.00.

Afterward you can ask for a certified copy at $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each page after. For your own files, an uncertified copy at the office is $.25 a page. Keep the recorded book and page reference with your closing papers.

Mail is an option for copies, though it costs more and slows things down. Send the request with a stamped return envelope and allow time for the round trip. If a deadline is close, such as a buyer's lender wanting a certified copy, go in person during weekday hours.

Before you close a Currituck sale

Confirm the recorded owner, whether any deed of trust is still open, and which special districts tax the parcel. The land records show recorded deeds and deeds of trust. A paid-off loan gets a satisfaction, and the first reference is free.

Both transfer taxes are collected when the deed is presented, so the closing attorney should list them on the settlement statement. Ask the tax office what is owed on the current bill. Statewide, bills are due September 1 and interest starts January 6, which means a sale in fall or winter has to settle any open balance.

Behind on the mortgage? Foreclosure here follows the state's clerk-hearing process, with a ten-day upset bid period once the sale is reported. A cash buyer may close quickly enough to pay off the loan from the proceeds, and cash skips the lender's appraisal. The deed, both taxes and the filing fee are still due at recording, so plan for them.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Currituck Register of Deeds hours?

The office is open weekdays from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM at 153 Courthouse Road. Holidays change the schedule, so confirm before you drive over.

Is there a county land transfer tax in Currituck?

Yes. Beyond the state's $1.00 per $500.00 excise stamp tax, the county charges $1 per $100 of price, counting any fraction.

What does recording a deed of trust cost in Currituck County?

$64.00 covers a deed of trust or mortgage of up to thirty-five pages. Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust is $0.00 for the first reference.

Will the Register of Deeds search my title?

No. Clerks do not give legal advice, draft documents or search title. They will show you how to browse the records. For a sale, an attorney or title company does the search.

What is the Currituck property tax rate for 2026?

The countywide rate is .60 per $100 of valuation. Special districts add more, for example .08 for Corolla Fire and .09 for Knotts Island Fire. The county tax page lists them all.

Office address, phone and recording cutoff

You will find the office at 110 West Center Street in Lexington, NC 27292. The mailing address is P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. Call 336-242-2150, or fax 336-238-2318. The building is open weekdays 8am to 5pm and closed on county holidays, but the counter stops taking recordings at 4:30pm sharp. That cutoff has applied since August 1, 2020.

The office handles real estate records, vital records, military service records and the notary oath. Counter visits get same-day recording and same-day return of vital records, and a public computer lab and self-serve kiosks are there for legal searches.

The county counts about 180,182 residents and 79,412 housing units. Three in four occupied homes are owner-occupied (74.4 percent), at a median value of $219,100. About 92.2 percent of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so few houses change hands in a typical year.

Searching the land records

Real estate searches run through the county's deeds search site, with records indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything older, contact staff directly.

  • To find a paid-off mortgage, search the document type Release.
  • Judgments are looked up through the Clerk of Courts office instead.
  • Attorneys are encouraged to use an e-record system or submit by mail.
  • Color-coded plats do not upload properly and will not be recorded.

The office also posts answers to common questions: whether an instrument must be notarized, whether you can prepare your own deed, and whether you must be present to record.

Tax certificate required for deeds

The counter turns away any real property deed that lacks a certificate from the Tax Administrator showing no overdue tax on the parcel. The rule has applied since March 1, 2019 and rests on G.S. 161-31.

A closing run by an attorney gets around the certificate. The deed instead carries a printed line stating that a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any overdue tax will be paid to the collector from the sale money. Without an attorney, ask the Tax Department for a certificate through its online form. It can take up to two business days. If you are selling on your own, file the request well before closing, since an unpaid earlier bill will stop the deed at the window.

Why recording protects buyer and seller

G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from a deed, an option or a long lease until it is registered in the county, and whoever registers first ranks first.

So whether you sell in Lexington, Thomasville, Denton or a rural township, treat recording as the last step of the sale, not an afterthought. Ask your closing attorney for the recorded book and page, plus proof that the earlier deed of trust was released.

Who owes the tax bill when a house sells

Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 is billed for the year, and selling later in the year does not clear that owner of the bill. Closings usually split the bill by date, so read the settlement statement to see whether the buyer's portion was credited.

To be safe, ask that the collector be paid straight from closing funds. The collector answers at 336-242-2180 and also issues the certificates the Register of Deeds asks for. A certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, so clearing the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

Other records the office handles

Besides deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a stamped return envelope. If you inherited a house and are selling it, you will likely need death certificates for the estate file. Order several at once.

What to bring on recording day

Arrive before 4:30pm with the signed, notarized deed, the tax certificate or the attorney's printed line on the deed, and payment for the excise tax and the filing fee. A deed of trust or other instrument that runs past the page allowance picks up $4.00 for each added page, so count pages before you go. Card payments add a 3% convenience fee or $1 minimum, which makes a check the cheaper choice for a large amount.

The counter gives same-day recording, so you should leave with confirmation. If an attorney is handling the sale, they typically file for you, and you only need the book and page afterward. Save that reference with your closing papers, because a later buyer's title search will start from it. Questions about timing or a rejected document can go to the office at 336-242-2150 before you make the trip.

Checklist before the deed goes in

A sensible order for a seller handling the details:

  • Look up the parcel's tax bill for any delinquency.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Check that the deed names its preparer and gives a return address.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Obtain the loan payoff figure and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

A loan in default goes to a power-of-sale hearing before the clerk of superior court, and an upset bid can be filed for ten days after the sale is reported. Request the lender's payoff statement in writing right away. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the certificate, excise tax and filing fee still apply.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?

4:30pm sharp, though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The cutoff has applied since August 1, 2020.

Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?

Since March 1, 2019, a real property deed is accepted only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?

Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, call the office at 336-242-2150.

Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?

The seller does, at the counter, before filing. The rate is one dollar for each $500 of price or part of $500.

Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?

Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a stamped return envelope is needed for return.

Duplin County Register of Deeds office

Take your deed to 118 Duplin Street in Kenansville. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. Call 910-296-2108 with questions, send a fax to 910-296-2344, or mail documents to Box 970, Kenansville, NC 28349.

The same staff also take care of:

  • Deeds of trust and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed business names and military records.
  • Maps and plats.
  • Notary commissions and marriage licenses.
  • Certified copies of vital records.

Real property records, vital records and maps can be searched online at duplinrod.com.

What recording protects

Until a deed sits in the public record, its holder has little protection from outsiders. G.S. 47-18 says a deed, contract to convey, option, lease over three years or first-refusal right loses to lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered in the county where the land is.

If two documents conflict, the one registered first wins. A signed deed left unfiled exposes the buyer, so find out from your closing attorney when it will be filed.

Ownership data for tax purposes lives with Land Records in the tax department. Call that office after closing to learn when the new owner appears on the account.

Recording fees

Every county uses one statewide fee schedule, G.S. 161-10, and the money is due when you hand in the paper.

What filing costs at the Duplin County office
DocumentFee
Deed or other ordinary instrumentBase $26.00 (15 pages), plus $4.00 each extra page
Deed of trust, mortgageBase $64.00 (35 pages), plus $4.00 each extra page

Two extras come from that statute too: $25.00 on a nonstandard document and $10.00 for each additional instrument in a filing. Pages decide the total, so count them before you mail.

Deed stamp tax

Grantors owe this tax. At one dollar per five hundred dollars of consideration (partial amounts round up), it is collected at the counter before the deed is recorded.

  • The county general fund receives half.
  • The other half is forwarded to the state after the county withholds a 2% collection allowance.
  • A tract spread over several counties pays where most of its value lies.

Your closing attorney can calculate the stamp for your sale price. Without payment, the deed is not accepted.

Coordinating with the tax office

Two separate buildings, two separate jobs: the register records the deed, and the Tax Department at 117 Beasley Street handles the bill. Reach Collections at 910-296-2112 and assessing at 910-296-2110.

The bill is due September 1 and interest begins January 6, which means an autumn or winter closing comes with an open bill. The tax office refers delinquent accounts to the county attorney. Foreclosure sales are held at the courthouse steps in Kenansville, and the high bidder puts down 20%.

Get a payoff from Collections before closing. Should the parcel lie in Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw, the county collects that town's levy too, and the payoff should include it. The recommended 2026-27 budget sets the county rate at 58 cents per $100, plus fire district rates. Values were last reset January 1, 2025, and the next reset is January 1, 2030.

Steps to get a deed recorded

No document is filed until payment is made, so the order below matters.

  1. Request a payoff from Collections so the year's tax and any back balance are settled at closing.
  2. Have the deed prepared and signed.
  3. Pay the deed stamp and add the page-based fee from the table.
  4. Bring the document to 118 Duplin Street or mail it to Box 970.
  5. When a lender later wants a certified copy, the per-page charge in the table applies.

Selling an inherited house? Decide who may sign for the estate before anything is drafted. The register files paper without ruling on that, so see an attorney and the court clerk first. Cash sales skip the lender's appraisal and underwriting, though recording steps and costs are unchanged.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Duplin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Owner-financed sales

Yes, they are recorded here, and Chapter 47H adds rules. It covers written agreements for one-to-four family dwellings or manufactured homes priced at $5,000 or more, where the seller keeps title and there are five or more payments after the down payment.

  • Paper, signatures and an acknowledgment are all required.
  • The buyer may rescind up to midnight ending the third business day after execution or delivery.
  • The contract, or a short memorandum of it, must be recorded by the seller within five business days.
  • Forfeiture starts with a written default notice that allows at least 30 days to cure.

A seller who forgets to record loses the protection described above, so put it on the closing checklist.

What to bring when you file

You need the signed, acknowledged deed plus two payments: the page-based fee and the deed stamp. Count pages beforehand. The $26.00 base fee stops at page 15, and the $64.00 deed of trust fee stops at page 35. Every extra page costs $4.00, and a nonstandard layout adds $25.00.

When mailing to Box 970, put everything in one envelope so the clerk can record without calling you back. Not sure whether a second instrument in the same filing triggers the $10.00 charge? Phone 910-296-2108 and ask. Records you want copied later can be ordered from the same counter, so keep the book and page of your recording on file with your closing papers.

Selling with taxes owed

Taxes you owe do not vanish when the house sells. They follow the parcel, which is why a closing attorney usually pays them off the top of your proceeds. Delinquent Duplin accounts are referred to the county attorney, and an inherited house with back taxes could already be in line for that. Check with Collections at 910-296-2112 before listing.

Cash buyers sometimes close fast enough to clear the balance before a foreclosure sale date is set. The deed is then recorded, the seller pays the stamp, and the tax account should show the new owner once Land Records catches up.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Housing in Duplin County

Duplin County is home to about 51,571 people in 24,235 housing units, 70.3% of them owner-occupied. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $137,400, rent is $865 and household income is $55,148. New building permits totaled 127 in 2025. In-town house or farm acreage, the paperwork goes through that one Kenansville office.

What are the Register of Deeds hours in Duplin County?

The office keeps weekday hours, 8 am to 5 pm, at 118 Duplin Street. Questions go to 910-296-2108.

What will I pay to record a Duplin County deed?

State law sets the fee. A short deed begins at $26.00 and a deed of trust at $64.00, and pages beyond the included count are $4.00 apiece.

Who owes the excise tax on a Duplin County home sale?

The seller. It is paid at the register's counter before recording and works out to one dollar per five hundred dollars of value.

Can I look up Duplin County land records online?

Yes. The register's website, duplinrod.com, has real property records, vital records and maps.

Does recording a deed settle my property tax?

It does not. Tax is billed and collected by the Tax Department and falls due each September 1, so ask Collections for a payoff at 910-296-2112 ahead of closing.

Durham County deed counter: location and hours

The deed counter is on the second floor of Durham County Administration Building II, at 201 East Main Street in Durham, NC 27701. It takes filings Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:45pm, holidays excluded. The phone number is 919-560-0480.

Plenty of sellers never visit. Their law firm or title agent files the signed deed and receives it back stamped. Since the document itself is what protects you, learn the office's rules before you sign.

Durham County had about 347,240 residents in mid 2025 and 164,222 housing units. Owners occupy 55.5% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $389,400. The transfer tax follows price, so a pricier home produces a bigger tax line at closing. Request an itemized estimate from the settlement agent early, and weigh each offer by what you net.

Recording an ordinary deed of 15 pages or fewer is $26.00, with $4 added per extra page. A mortgage is priced on its own line, and a release of one is free of charge.

Every North Carolina county charges the same scale, set by G.S. 161-10, and you pay at the counter.

Deed transfer tax

The state levies $1 on every $500 of price or value, and a remainder below $500 is treated as a whole unit. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the seller pays it to the register before the deed is filed.

Half the money stays with Durham County's general fund. The other half is remitted to the state each month. You will see the amount on your settlement statement, next to the contract price.

  • The seller carries this cost, so count it when you compare offers.
  • Paying off a deed of trust at closing adds no filing charge for the release.
  • The statute measures the tax on consideration or value, so the deed's stated price matters.

Electronic recording

A deed can be recorded over the internet through four approved vendors. A deed that arrives before 4:45 pm is processed and sent back the same business day. An individual who wants an account contacts a vendor directly.

  • Simplifile
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • CSC, the Corporation Service Company

Title agents often hold accounts already, which lets a Durham closing finish in one day. If you sign outside a closing, you can bring the original to the counter in person.

Format rules for a printed deed

The county's recording standards repeat G.S. 161-14(b). A document that breaks a rule is still filed after the $25.00 surcharge. Use white letter or legal paper, print on a single side, and put the instrument type at the top of page one. Reserve three inches of blank space above the text on page one, keep half inch margins everywhere else, and set type at 9 points or larger. Plats are 18 by 24. Pen may fill blanks and make corrections.

When tiny print is the only flaw, the registrar can waive the surcharge if the page is legible.

Why filing protects a seller and buyer

Recording decides who ranks first. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered deed loses to a lien creditor or a buyer who paid value, and when two papers compete the earlier registration time wins.

The office indexes what it is handed and cannot repair a recorded paper. Misspelled names, defective legal descriptions and wrong parcel numbers are beyond its power to fix. Report an indexing slip by email and you receive an Administrative Notice linked to the original entry. So proofread first.

A Recording Notification Service will email you when a document is recorded in your name, which helps guard a vacant house against property fraud.

Property tax and your sale

Property tax is a different office's job. Durham County Tax Administration, 3rd Floor of the same building (919-560-0300), runs it. Real property was last reappraised effective January 1, 2025.

Bills go to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and one that reaches the wrong person should be handed to the new owner. Before closing, ask the tax collector what is owed so the settlement agent can pay it.

Searching recorded documents before you sell

An Online Public Records Search covers recorded real estate and business documents. Search your own parcel before listing, and the chain of deeds, deeds of trust and releases appears, so you can see whether an old mortgage was released.

This helps most with inherited houses and loans paid off long ago. Filing a satisfaction costs nothing, and certified copies run $5.00 for page one plus $2 for each more.

Land records are only part of the job. The office also takes assumed business names, corporate and partnership certificates, military records, notary oaths, plats and vital records. Marriage licenses cost $60.00 and certified birth or death copies cost $10.00.

Closing steps and a cash sale

Most sales follow one path: your settlement agent drafts the deed, you sign, and the agent files it in person or electronically along with the tax and fee. Read the first page for the instrument name and every spelling before you sign, because the office will not correct mistakes afterward.

Selling for cash removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting steps, yet you still owe the transfer tax and recording fee. Have the stamped deed returned and file it with your closing papers.

If you are paying off a mortgage at closing, the lender records a release, and the filing costs nothing. Later, search your own parcel online to confirm the release appears. It is worth doing a few weeks after closing, since a missing release can surface when the buyer sells or refinances. Staff at 919-560-0480 can tell you whether a document has been received.

If an e-recording is rejected, the vendor or title agent sorts it out, and a deed in on time before 4:45 pm still returns the same business day once accepted. Plan the signing early in the week so a rejected format does not push your closing past a weekend.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the Durham County excise tax at a sale?

The seller pays, handing it to the register of deeds before filing. The rate is $1 per $500 of price, counting any leftover fraction. Durham County keeps half and the state receives half.

Does Durham County charge to file a mortgage payoff?

No. The fee schedule shows no fee for a satisfaction, so releasing a deed of trust at closing costs nothing at the register of deeds.

What if my deed is printed in tiny type?

The office can still file it. Missing a layout rule triggers a $25.00 nonstandard surcharge, though the registrar may skip it when the only flaw is print under 9 points and the page reads clearly.

Can a homeowner e-record a deed alone in Durham County?

Usually through a vendor. The county names Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, ePN and CSC, and each sets up its own account. A submission received by 4:45 pm comes back the same business day.

How do I correct a misspelled name on a Durham County deed?

Staff cannot change it, because documents are recorded and indexed as presented. Your closing attorney can advise how to correct the deed. Email the office only about an indexing error, and it replies with an Administrative Notice.

Contacting the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds

Land records sit here beside births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notary files and maps. The office phone is (252) 641-7924, and that is the number to use for counter hours and the street address. Tarboro is the county seat.

Once you sign a deed to sell an Edgecombe County house, it is filed in this office, normally by your closing attorney. What follows explains the charges and the local habits that can hold up a recording.

Recording fees

A deed is recorded as a general document: $26.00 buys the first 15 pages, and every extra page adds $4.00. The excise tax is a separate $1.00 for each $500.00.

Edgecombe County register of deeds fees
ServiceFee
General instruments (not deeds of trust or mortgages)$26.00 first 15 pages; $4.00 per page past 15
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages; $4.00 per page past 35
Excise tax$1.00 per $500.00
Nonstandard document$25.00 plus the recording fee
Plat$21.00
Certified copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 per later page
Plain copy$.10 a page
Map copy$.50 at 11 x 17, $1.00 at 18 x 24
Satisfaction of a mortgageNo fee

Staff process filings and requests the same day they arrive. People filing by post should put a stamped return envelope, addressed to themselves, in with the papers.

The tax certification requirement

Under a county resolution, no deed is recorded until the Tax Collector has certified it, unless there is a workaround. The workaround is a line on the deed saying that a North Carolina attorney drew it up and that the closing attorney will send any overdue taxes to the tax collector out of the sale money.

Your attorney can put that line in. Anyone who writes a deed without an attorney must visit the Tax Collector and request the certification first.

  • Attorney route: the preparer statement satisfies the resolution, and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  • Do it yourself route: obtain the certification before bringing the deed to the register.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Edgecombe County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can a deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. Simplifile is the vendor on the county's E-Recording page, which also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. A firm or title agent holding an account can transmit a deed with no courier.

If you have no account, your closing attorney can file it for you. Paper filings follow the state filing standards, which the Real Estate page posts as a PDF beside an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

What must never appear in a recorded document

Leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver's license, state ID, passport, bank account, credit card and debit card numbers, plus PINs and passwords. G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) allows a number like that only if a law or court order requires it or if just the last four digits are shown.

Filed documents join the official county records, so read yours before signing and ask the preparer to strip anything sensitive.

Farm and timber land

The recording date counts as the transfer date for Present Use Value. To keep farm or forest land in the program, the buyer files a new application within 60 days of that date.

Deferred taxes, even from years before your sale, pass to the new owner. When land drops out of the program, the current year and three earlier years are due with interest. If you own land like this, call the Tax Assessor about its status before you list or entertain an offer.

  • Farm use needs 10 cultivated acres, and forest use needs 20 forested acres plus a management plan.
  • Farm income must average $1000 a year across the last three years.
  • A sale to an owner who cannot qualify can take the land out of the program.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Edgecombe County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Vital record copies

A certified birth, death or marriage certificate is $10 a copy. You can order online through Permitium/AIS, which tacks on a $3.35 convenience fee and card fees, or mail in an application. Birth and death files start in October 1913, and marriage files start in 1867.

Heirs selling an inherited house usually need a certified death certificate for the estate paperwork. Order it early so it is in hand when the buyer's attorney asks.

How property taxes connect to the deed

Real estate, personal property and vehicle tax for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns all flow through the Tax Collector. That office writes the statements of taxes due that attorneys and agents ask for, so have your closing attorney request one ahead of the closing date.

Call (252) 641-7810 about taxes paid or owed, and the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855 about a value. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers rates, listing and appeals.

Rocky Mount and Tarboro homes: which county office?

The land decides the county. A house in Tarboro belongs in the Edgecombe County office, and so does anything on the Edgecombe side of Rocky Mount. Because Rocky Mount straddles Nash and Edgecombe counties and is the largest municipality here, find out which side your parcel is on before the deed goes out.

A single parcel that crosses the line pays its excise tax to whichever county holds the larger share of the value. A parcel in one of the small towns, such as Princeville, Pinetops, Whitakers, Speed, Leggett, Conetoe, Macclesfield or Sharpsburg, still needs its county confirmed.

Before the signing appointment, have your attorney verify the parcel number and county. Same day processing helps only if the paper lands at the right office.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for a seller

  1. Ask the Tax Collector for a statement of what is owed on the parcel.
  2. Let the attorney draft the deed with either the preparer statement or a certification in hand.
  3. Settle the excise tax at filing. You owe it as seller, and the register takes it with the deed.
  4. Send the deed in electronically if your attorney or title agent has an account.
  5. Expect any mortgage payoff to produce a satisfaction that costs nothing to record.

Plan on a short wait only if everything arrives together. Bring or send the signed deed, the payment for recording and the excise tax, and the tax certification or preparer statement. A missing piece sends the packet back, and mailed packets lose days in the post. Phone (252) 641-7924 if you are unsure what your attorney has already handled.

Selling for cash removes the lender's paperwork. The deed, the excise tax and the tax certification stay exactly the same.

Local housing context

The county counts 49,121 residents (July 2025 estimate) and 23,604 housing units. Owners occupy 60.8% of homes, and the median value is $125,100. Page charges are the same for a modest house as for an expensive one. Only the excise tax rises with the price, so it is usually the largest recording cost.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a fee to record a mortgage release in Edgecombe County?

No. The office records a satisfaction for free, so a mortgage release at closing costs nothing to file.

What is the Edgecombe County excise tax rate?

It is $1.00 per $500.00. As the seller you pay it to the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

Does Edgecombe County record a deed that lacks a tax certification?

Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. Otherwise the Tax Collector must certify it. The statement must say a North Carolina attorney prepared the deed and the closing attorney will pay delinquent taxes from proceeds.

How do I get a certified birth or death certificate in Edgecombe County?

Either order through Permitium/AIS or mail in the application. A copy is $10, and ordering online also costs a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

Does the Edgecombe County register accept electronic filing?

Yes, through Simplifile, with CSC eRecording Solutions as another option. Your attorney or title agent normally does the submitting.

Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Forsyth County, NC Register of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Forsyth County, NC Register of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Forsyth County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Forsyth County?

Land documents filed in Forsyth County

The registry is the county's permanent file of land title papers: deeds, deeds of trust and mortgages, satisfactions, plats, leases, notices of foreclosure and a few other filings. It also takes assumed business names, rights of way, covenant agreements, UCC filings, affidavits, powers of attorney, separation and prenuptial agreements and living wills.

Wills, divorces and estates belong to the Clerk of Court instead. An heir selling an inherited Forsyth County house files the estate papers with the clerk first, then brings the deed to the register once authority is in place.

How to file a deed

Carry in the signed original, or route it through an approved electronic vendor, on a business day during office hours.

  • At the counter: the paper comes back to you once it is recorded.
  • By mail: send the exact fee as a business check, cashier's check or money order made out to the Forsyth County Register of Deeds, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. Do not mail cash.
  • Electronic: the sender signs a submitter agreement with an authorized e-recording provider and completes a memorandum of understanding. The county lists CSC, EDL, EPN, IGS and Simplifile as vendors, and files must arrive by 4:30 p.m.

A buyer is protected only once the deed is on the registry. Until then, G.S. 47-18 leaves the transfer exposed to lien creditors and later purchasers, and the time of registration decides who ranks first. The office only records. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice.

Recording fees

The charge depends on the kind of instrument and its page count.

Real estate recording fees, Forsyth County Register of Deeds
Filing typeFee
Routine document$26 through page 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 through page 35, then $4 per page
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25
SatisfactionNo fee
Several instruments sent as one$10 for each, on top of recording
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 for later pages
Plain copy$.25 a page

An added $2.00 applies per party beyond 20, counting attachments and exhibits. G.S. 161-10 sets these amounts and calls them complete and exclusive. At the counter the office takes business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards. Cards carry a 3 percent charge with a $1.00 floor and cannot be used by phone. Personal checks and e-checks are turned away.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Forsyth County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays the excise tax?

The seller, called the transferor in the statute, hands over the excise tax before the deed is recorded.

The charge under G.S. 105-228.30 is one dollar per $500 block of price or value, with a partial block rounded up. The county general fund keeps one half. The state half goes each month to the Department of Revenue, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. Land lying in two counties is taxed where the larger value sits.

Annual property tax is separate. It is billed to the January 1 owner, and the county suggests clearing it at closing, so a settlement statement can show both items.

Layout rules for a filing

A paper that misses the standard is charged an extra $25 as a non-standard document under G.S. 161-10.

  • Letter or legal size paper, typed or printed in black on white, one side only.
  • Leave three inches blank at the top of page one, keep side margins at half an inch or more, and use type of 9 points or larger.
  • The name of the instrument placed directly beneath that blank space.
  • Ink signatures in the acknowledgment, or else a certified copy of the signed original.
  • A grantee's current mailing address on a deed, and the drafter's name on the front of a North Carolina deed of trust.

The layout rules come from G.S. 161-14. Compare your draft to this list before it travels to the courthouse, since fixing a margin costs less than the surcharge.

Clearing an old mortgage from the record

The lender or noteholder cancels a mortgage by recording a satisfaction, and the office charges nothing to record one.

A deed of trust or mortgage is a security instrument that is canceled once the debt is paid. A deed is title and is never canceled. Cancellation is the job of the owner or noteholder in the county where the instrument was recorded. Forms that can do it include a satisfaction of security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction and an affidavit of satisfaction.

Do not assume the lender has acted. Payoff papers and satisfactions are not mailed to the borrower automatically after the loan is paid in full. Call the register of deeds to check that the loan is marked satisfied before you list the house.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Forsyth County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax maps and deed lookups

Parcel maps from the tax office show lot lines, but the deed holds the legal description you should rely on. Dimensions on tax maps are calculated for tax purposes only, and the acreage on a tax record may not match the deeded or platted acreage.

To find legal lot dimensions, open the Deeds tab on the parcel's property detail page or use the register of deeds lookup. Do this before a sale when a fence, a split lot or an old boundary dispute is in play.

Other services and fees

Besides land records, the office charges for notary work and vital records, and it waives fees for some military papers.

  • Notary public: $10, and notarial acts are $5 for each signature, except when performed with an act that already carries a fee.
  • Comparing a copy for certification: $5.
  • Recording a military discharge and getting a copy: no fee, and the Thank a Veteran photo ID is also free.
  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10; marriage license: $60.

Heirs who need a certified death certificate pay $10 for it. Call the office to confirm which of these documents can be issued the same day.

What a seller should bring

A clean filing needs four things: the signed original deed, the exact fee in an accepted form of payment, the excise tax and a return envelope if you mail it. Check the deed against the layout list above, and confirm the grantee's mailing address is on it.

If a mortgage is being paid off at closing, ask the lender or your attorney who will record the satisfaction, since it costs nothing but still has to be filed. A cash sale skips the lender, so there may be no satisfaction at all if the house was owned free and clear.

Finally, ask your closing attorney to send the deed electronically before 4:30 p.m. when timing matters. Recording time decides priority, and a deed sent late in the day waits for the next business day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

County context

The county has 159,925 households (2020 to 2024), and 2,875 building permits were issued in 2025. Median gross rent is $1,098. A busy market means a steady flow of deeds, so allow for counter and e-filing volume.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Forsyth County office charge for filing a document?

It depends on the instrument. A routine document is $26 through page 15, then $4 per page, and a satisfaction of a deed of trust is free. G.S. 161-10 backs the county's fee sheet.

Will the Forsyth County office accept my personal check?

No. Personal checks, counter checks and e-checks are turned away. Business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards work.

What is the cutoff for an e-filed deed in Forsyth County?

E-filed items need to land by 4:30 p.m. on a business day. Counter and mail filings follow the regular weekday hours.

Who covers the excise tax on a Forsyth County sale?

The seller pays it to the register of deeds first. The rate is one dollar per $500 block of value, and a partial block is rounded up.

Can staff at the Forsyth County registry help draft my deed?

No. The office records papers only, and state law keeps staff from giving legal advice or showing how to draft an instrument, so see an attorney.

Franklin County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Franklin County, NC Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Franklin County, NC Register of Deeds sale

Selling in Franklin County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Franklin County?
We buy Franklin County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where the Franklin County Register of Deeds is

Go to 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard, Louisburg, NC 27549. The office moved there during construction at the county courthouse. For mail use P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549. Call 919-496-3500 or fax 919-496-1457. You can pay by credit card.

This is the office that holds the deed you received, the deed of trust on it and any plat or power of attorney tied to the parcel. Because the office relocated recently, call before you drive over with a document, and mail or e-record when you can.

Records the office keeps

One counter serves both land records and vital records, and a home sale depends mostly on the land side.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust, which move title and secure a loan.
  • Powers of attorney, assumed names, maps and similar papers tied to real property.
  • Military discharge records.
  • Birth and death certificates back to 1913 for events in Franklin County, and marriage certificates back to 1869, with a bond book that carries marriage information from 1779.

Staff can print birth and death certificates for any North Carolina event from the state system. Certified or regular copies of vital records can also be ordered online through a county vendor. Someone selling an inherited house often leaves with a death certificate and the old deed from a single visit.

Tax certification before recording

A deed moving real property is turned away unless the Tax Collector first certifies that no delinquent ad valorem or other administered tax is a lien on it. The county has applied this rule since April 1, 2015.

The Collections Department stamps deeds free of charge on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, excluding county holidays. There are three ways to get it done.

  • Walk the deed in to Collections before recording.
  • Mail it to the Franklin County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, Attention: Tax Certification.
  • Use eRecording, which forwards deeds to the tax office on its own.

Electronic recordings that need the stamp must reach the tax department by 4:30 pm, so a closing that wraps up late should send its package early.

A seller with back taxes hits the snag here. The deed sits until the balance is cleared, or until the closing agent pays it from your proceeds.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can I record a Franklin County deed electronically?

Yes. Title companies, banks, attorneys and private individuals can file electronically, and the office takes every document type except UCC filings.

The county authorizes CSC eRecording Solutions (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and the ePN eRecording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Filing this way is faster and cuts postage and courier costs, and it leads to fewer rejected documents and better security. The closing attorney usually picks the provider, so you will rarely arrange it yourself. Do ask what day the recording will happen.

Fees at the counter

Your closing pays two things here: a recording fee that grows with page count, and a tax that follows the sale price.

A general instrument is $26 for pages one through 15 and $4 for each additional page. A deed of trust is $64 for the first 35 pages. The release of a paid-off loan is recorded free. Certified copies start at $5, and a paper in the wrong format adds $25.

The deed tax is a dollar per $500 of price or value, with any remainder counted as a full $500. The seller pays it at the register of deeds window before recording, and the money is split between the county and state revenue. Look at your settlement statement for the final figure.

Who handles each step of a sale

Four parties handle separate pieces of a Franklin County sale.

Franklin County offices and the part each plays in a sale
OfficeRole in the saleContact
Register of DeedsRecords the deed and deed of trust, keeps land records and collects the recording fees919-496-3500
Collections Department (Tax Collector)Collects property tax and certifies there is no delinquent tax before a deed is recorded919-496-2172
Tax AdministrationSets values and handles real estate value appealsCounty Tax Office, through the Value Appeals page
eRecording providerSends the signed documents to the Register of Deeds electronicallyCSC, Simplifile or ePN
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Franklin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax bills and the seller

Each September 1 is the due date for real estate tax, and 2026 bills go delinquent on January 6, 2027. Bills go out by mail in late July or early August. Pay before September 1 and you may get a discount.

If you sell after the bill has arrived, the county says to give it to the buyer unless you intend to pay it. The tax office stays out of private deals among buyers, sellers and attorneys. Since the tax is a lien, though, buyers usually insist on settling it at closing. Escrow does not change who gets the mailing, so confirm with your lender in the second week of September that it paid. Franklin County also bills a Solid Waste Availability Fee for each electrical connection. Commissioners set the amount yearly, and living there only part of the year does not excuse it.

Disputing an assessed value

The form for the Board of Equalization and Review can be filed from January 1 until the board adjourns, normally in May. A notice of changed value gives you a separate 30-day window.

Staff review the file before anything else, and unresolved cases go to the board, which sends its decision by mail. Franklin County revalued as of January 1, 2024, so bring evidence from that date. A larger bill, a fixed income or a market drop after January 1, 2024 does not count. What does count: lower values on comparable properties, comparable sales before that date, fire or storm damage still unrepaired, a denied septic permit and documented cleanup costs. You carry the burden of proof. If affordability is the real concern, ask the tax office about relief programs.

A simple order for your closing day

Start with the Collections stamp, since nothing else can be recorded without it. Next, have the attorney confirm the fee amount and the excise tax so the check or card payment matches. Then pick the delivery route: walk it in, mail it or send it through eRecording. If you are mailing, allow extra days, and if you are sending electronically, remember the 4:30 pm cutoff for anything needing the stamp.

After recording, keep the recorded copy with your sale papers. A buyer's lender will expect the deed to be on the registry before funds are released. Selling for cash does not change this order of steps.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Why recording order matters

The time a paper is registered sets its rank. G.S. 47-18 says a deed, an option, a lease running longer than three years and similar interests have no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until registered in the county where the land lies.

This is why closings are planned around recording cutoffs, and why an old unrecorded deed can stall a new sale. When an inherited Franklin County house has the late relative as the owner of record, look at the index before you list it and ask your closing attorney which papers must be recorded first.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Franklin County Register of Deeds in the courthouse?

No, not at present. The office sits at 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard in Louisburg while the courthouse is under construction. Mail goes to P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549, and the phone is 919-496-3500.

Do I need a tax certification stamp to record a deed in Franklin County?

Yes, whenever a deed transfers real property. The Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent lien exists, at no cost, weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. With eRecording the deed is forwarded to the tax office automatically.

What does Franklin County charge to record?

Expect $26 for a general instrument through page 15 and $64 for a deed of trust through page 35, with $4 for each page beyond those. Phone the office before you mail a long document.

Can a title company record electronically in Franklin County?

Yes, for every document type but UCC filings. CSC, Simplifile and the ePN network are the routes, and the company or attorney normally submits.

Who pays the North Carolina deed excise tax?

Where the Gaston County Register of Deeds is

You will find the office on the courthouse's first floor, 325 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Way, Gastonia, NC 28052. Older deeds, letters and directions may show the former street name, 325 N. Marietta Street, for the same building.

Write to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053, or phone 704-862-7681. Doors are open from 8:30 am to 5 pm. The 4:45 pm cutoff for real estate recordings falls before the office closes, so a late-afternoon closing in Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly or Cherryville should go in early. Using the records or taking a notary oath needs no appointment.

Online records search

A new vendor now powers the records search, and the previous system is gone. All of its records moved to the new one, so any saved link to the old site should be replaced.

The public search finds deeds, deeds of trust and other property records. A few older records never went online, and the staff will help with those if you stop in or call. Uncertified copies can be pulled online. For a certified copy, use the Certified Copy Request Portal, call 704-862-7681, email rod@gastongov.com or go to the office. If you need a prior deed to prove how your family took title, you will usually want a certified copy for the closing attorney.

Other services at the office

Beyond deeds, staff index plats, maps, mortgages and other personal property papers. The same counter issues marriage licenses, holds birth and death certificates and handles passport applications.

Paper records are kept in vaults, and digital copies sit on secure servers in the courthouse.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Gaston County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Copies and counter payments

Plain copies run $0.25 a page. Certified copies start at $5 for page one, and each added page is $2.

Ways to pay Register of Deeds fees:

  • Cash.
  • Business check or money order payable to the Gaston County Register of Deeds.
  • Debit or credit card.

Employees can show you the books and help with the computers. State law keeps them from title research, and they will not run a lien check. If you lose a deed, buy a copy in person or write to the P.O. Box for one. A name change on a deed requires a brand new deed, so see an attorney, because the office stocks no legal forms for deeds or powers of attorney.

Recording fees for a closing package

The uniform fee schedule follows G.S. 161-10.

  • General instruments: $26 covers pages one to 15, then $4 per page.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: $64 covers pages one to 35, then the same $4 per page.
  • Satisfactions of a paid-off loan: free.
  • Plats: $21 for each sheet.
  • Additional instruments bundled in one document: $10 apiece.

The transfer tax comes on top. G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at one dollar for every $500 of price, rounding a remainder up to the next $500, and the seller pays when the deed is presented.

Timing your closing around the cutoff

The 4:45 pm recording cutoff is the date that matters most to a seller. A deed that arrives after it waits for the next business day, and during that gap an earlier filing by someone else can take priority. Ask your closing attorney or title agent to send the package well before the cutoff, and avoid scheduling signatures for the last hour of the day.

Have these ready when the package goes in: the signed deed, the fee payment, the transfer tax paid by you as seller, and the satisfaction for any loan being paid off. Payoff paperwork is recorded free, but it still needs to be filed. If you sell for cash, there may be no lender documents at all, and the package is shorter, though the deed and tax are the same.

Before you list, pull your own deed from the public search and read the legal description. If a name is misspelled or a prior owner never recorded a deed, tell your attorney right away, since fixing the chain takes longer than any other step. Ask for a certified copy only if the closing attorney requests one, because plain copies cost far less per page.

Questions about the county's land records can go to rod@gastongov.com, which is also the address for certified copy requests, so keep your parcel details handy when you write.

Protection from deed and lien fraud

A free alert service runs through the county's land records software provider. Enter a name and an email address, and a message arrives whenever a recording is filed under that name.

Alerts cannot stop fraud. They only let you notice a suspicious filing fast, which is valuable when the house is empty, rented or inherited and the mail piles up. People preparing documents for recording may not include Social Security, bank account or card numbers unless the law requires one. A number that slips through can be taken off the online image if you ask in writing under G.S. 132-1.10(g). That request is free, but the filing itself stays public.

How values and appeals tie to a sale

A four-year reappraisal cycle applies here. January 1, 2023 is the latest value date, and 2027 is next, with an informal review ahead of any Board of Equalization and Review hearing.

Appeals can be filed beginning January 1 and ending when the board adjourns, usually the last week of April, or 30 days after a Notice of Value Change when that comes later. Reach the Tax Office at 128 West Main Avenue in Gastonia or 704-866-3158. The Register of Deeds does not collect property tax. That bill stays with the parcel until paid, and buyers expect it cleared at closing. Our Gaston County property tax guide covers rates, relief programs and payment options in detail.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Why recording order matters

The first paper registered usually ranks first. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance or a lease of more than three years has no effect on lien creditors or paying buyers until it is on record in the county where the land lies.

Before the buyer's deed is filed, make sure the earlier deeds in the chain, any estate documents and the release of a paid-off loan are all indexed. Recording a release costs nothing. Your closing attorney can search the index and send in the satisfaction of your old mortgage before the sale.

What an heir should record before selling

Estate paperwork comes first, because a deed signed by someone not yet holding title will not clear. When a small estate has no will, G.S. 28A-25-1 allows a small estate affidavit, filed where the decedent lived.

It covers up to $20,000 in personal property after liens, and the affidavit names every tract of land the decedent owned. Whichever route your family uses, the document giving you authority to sell ends up in the Gastonia index, so leave time before closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the mailing address for Gaston County recordings?

Address the envelope to Gaston County Register of Deeds, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. If you ship overnight, use an express envelope and enclose a prepaid return envelope.

How late in the day can a Gaston County deed be filed?

4:45 pm for real estate recordings. The office stays open until 5 pm, but marriage applications stop at 4:30 pm.

How much are copies at the Gaston County office?

A black and white copy is $0.25 a page. A certified copy is $5 for the first page and $2 for every page after it.

Is the Gaston County records search online?

Yes, through a public search, and nothing was lost in the switch to the new vendor. A few older records are not digitized, so phone 704-862-7681 if you cannot find one.

Is the Gaston County deed tax the buyer's or the seller's?

You do, as the seller, at one dollar for each $500 of price when the deed is handed in. Your settlement statement shows the exact figure.

Contacting the Graham County Register of Deeds

The office is at 12 North Main Street, Robbinsville, NC 28771. Mail goes to PO Box 406, Robbinsville, NC 28771. The phone is (828) 479-7971 and the fax is (828) 479-6902.

The counter is staffed weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30, with a break at noon. Browsing records needs no appointment. The office may run flex hours or close some days for unforeseen reasons, and on those days recordings are accepted in the Tax Office. Phone ahead if your closing depends on a counter visit.

Fees are payable by cash or check and nothing else. The Tax Office and the assessor work from 196 Knight Street in Robbinsville, and the assessor's phone is (828) 479-7963. A single trip can handle the deed and any tax questions that surface.

What the office records

The office records legal documents, deeds, plats and certified documents. It also handles notary oaths, marriages, births and deaths. Records are kept under the North Carolina General Statutes and are open to the public.

For a house sale, the items that matter are your vesting deed, any deed of trust and the plat for your lot. Ask whether a plat for your parcel is on file before you list. A missing or dated boundary description can slow a closing.

The county is divided into three townships, Cheoah, Stecoah and Yellow Creek, and carries municipal codes for Robbinsville, Fontana and Santeetlah. Your deed and tax bill may refer to one of these.

Recording fees

Graham publishes a fee sheet of its own, citing G.S. 161, and its real estate lines track the state schedule.

Graham County fee sheet, real estate lines
Recording itemFee
Standard land record instrument$26 through page 15, then $4 per added page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 through page 35, then $4 per added page
Satisfaction of a loanNone
State excise tax on conveyances$2 per thousand
Second instrument inside one document$10 each
Nonstandard format$25 extra
Plat$21 per sheet
Copies$5 certified first page, $2 each added; $0.25 plain

That sheet carries an October 1, 2011 date, and the deed of trust tier was amended October 1, 2016. A quick call to the office will tell you whether the numbers changed before you write a check.

Deed tax at closing

The state's conveyance tax shows on Graham's sheet as $2 per thousand of price, the same rate as one dollar per $500 in G.S. 105-228.30.

As the seller you hand it over at the counter right before the deed goes on record. County and state split the receipts. Look for it as a separate line on your settlement statement, and ask your closing attorney how it will read on the deed.

Property tax due dates and penalties

Tax notices mail on July 1 with a September 1 due date. Nothing accrues until after January 5.

  • Interest of 2% begins January 6, then 0.75% a month until paid.
  • A second real estate notice goes out each February.
  • Delinquent taxes are published in the Graham Star every April, and advertising fees are added to each listed bill.
  • Enforced collection can start any time after January 5: wage garnishment, bank attachment, a state debt setoff against income tax returns and lottery winnings, levy on rents and foreclosure.

A delinquent bill will not match the printed figure, so ask the collector for the exact payoff first. The tax office has a foreclosure line at (828) 479-7962.

How to pay your Graham County tax bill

Payment works at the counter, over the phone or online. Accepted forms are cash, credit card, money order and checks payable to Graham County. After hours, use the locked drop box at the building's side entrance.

The county does not set or collect the card charge. The processor takes 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum. Partial payments and prepayments go through if the parcel or account number is noted on the check. When a lender escrows your taxes, the bill still lands with you, so forward a copy to the servicer. Bounced checks cost $25.00 or 10 percent, whichever is more.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Graham County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other items the tax office bills

Land and buildings are only part of what this office handles. It also values the following and takes exclusion applications.

  • Motor vehicles, boats, jet skis and houseboats.
  • Elderly, present-use value, religious and educational exclusions.
  • January listings of personal property and business personal property, improvements, business listing extensions and value appeals.

Motor vehicle tax is a separate bill payable to the NCDMV office at 74 S. Main Street in Robbinsville, phone (828) 479-4896. A houseboat sticker costs $5.00 and requires a copy of the pump out permit when you pay. Own a boat or houseboat? Clear those bills before closing so a buyer does not inherit them.

Exclusions and reappraisal

Elderly, disabled and veteran exclusion forms come from the assessor or the collector. Either way they go back to the assessor by June 1.

Graham has a 2027 Schedule of Values built on market values as of January 1, 2027, and a separate present-use schedule for farm and forest land. Two exclusions matter most for a homeowner. G.S. 105-277.1 removes $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger, for an owner 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled. G.S. 105-277.1C removes $45,000 for a disabled veteran, with no age or income test. Personal property listing runs January 1 through January 31. Call the assessor at (828) 479-7963 with questions.

What happens if property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid tax stays attached to the parcel from the listing date onward. G.S. 105-374 lets the county bring a foreclosure action, patterned on mortgage foreclosure, in the county where the property is located.

Notice goes to the owner of record, a spouse and other lienholders. The land is auctioned on the courthouse steps, and the commissioner may demand up to 20 percent down. Anyone wanting to raise the bid or file an exception has 10 days after the sale report. An owner can still redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs. Behind on the bill? Phone the collector early, because newspaper advertising fees get added to each listed account.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Before you record a deed

Pay the tax bill, make sure each old loan has a recorded satisfaction, and let your closing attorney review the chain of title.

Under G.S. 47-18, whichever document is registered first in the land's county generally wins over later ones. Satisfactions cost nothing to record here. Did the deed holder die? Finish the estate paperwork first, since the buyer's lender wants proof of signing authority in the index before it funds.

A workable order: get a written balance from the collector, gather your payoff letters, have the satisfactions recorded, then hand the attorney your vesting deed and any plat. A cash buyer skips a lender's title review, but the recorded chain still has to be clean.

Frequently asked questions

Can I pay Graham County recording fees by card?

No, recording fees take cash or a check only. Cards work for property tax at the tax office, with a processor fee added.

What if the Graham County office is closed when I need to record?

Phone (828) 479-7971 before you go. During flex hours or a closure, the Tax Office takes recordings. Bring cash or a check for the fees.

What are the recording charges in Graham County?

Expect $26 for a land record instrument through page 15 and $64 for a deed of trust through page 35, then $4 per extra page. Satisfactions are free.

When are Graham County property taxes due?

Notices mail July 1, and payment is due September 1. Interest of 2% begins January 6.

Is the Graham County transfer tax the same as the statewide rate?

Yes. The sheet shows $2 per thousand, equal to $1 for each $500 of price, and the seller pays it ahead of recording.

Where to file and who to call

Walk into the courthouse at 101 Main Street in Oxford (NC 27565) or phone 919-693-6314. Mail can go to P.O. Box 427.

The counter opens weekdays at 8:30 AM and closes at 5 PM. Anything ordered online after 4 PM is handled the following business day. Ring ahead for a sale and ask what staff will want to see for your instrument, since they do not draft or repair documents.

The register is an elected countywide officer, serving a two-year term under G.S. 161-1.

What the office files

Land records make up the bulk of the work, including deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names and powers of attorney. Every item is recorded, indexed and scanned, and the deed books go back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Think of it as a recording counter rather than a legal clinic. Because state law bars the office from practicing law, staff cannot give you legal forms, walk you through completing one, or interpret a recorded document. Take those questions to a North Carolina attorney.

Fees when a deed is filed

Most sales involve two charges. The recording fee is set by G.S. 161-10 and does not vary by county. The excise tax is the seller's.

Granville County recording charges
DocumentRecording fee
General instrument$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, plus $4.00 per page after
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, plus $4.00 per page after
Cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge
Excise tax, paid by seller$1.00 per $500 of value, remainder rounded up

Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor owes the tax, payable ahead of recording, and half goes to the county. For a tract that crosses county lines, the county with the largest share of value collects. The amount is computed from the price written in the deed, so compare the deed to your real contract before you sign.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Granville County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why record a deed promptly

Leave a deed unrecorded and it loses to later buyers and lien creditors. Priority goes to the first instrument registered, by clock time, in the land's county (G.S. 47-18).

Leases longer than three years, options and rights of first refusal follow the same rule. If you are carrying the financing yourself, Chapter 47H applies: the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed should be recorded inside five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day.

Property fraud alerts

The office offers a free alert tool called PropertyCheck. Owners can sign up for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The fraud in question works like this: a forger transfers title to a different name and records the papers while the true owner knows nothing. An alert cannot stop a filing. What it gives you is time to phone 919-693-6314 and reach a lawyer fast.

Vital records at the Oxford counter

Certified birth, marriage and death certificates cost $10.00 apiece, and plain copies cost $1.00. Orders placed online carry a $4 service and card fee that is not refundable. The system holds records from 1913 forward, and each request must include a copy of valid photo ID.

Newlyweds should wait 10 days after the ceremony before ordering a certified marriage copy. To collect a record in person, bring valid state-issued photo ID. Collecting for someone else is restricted to these people.

  • The person named on the record.
  • A spouse, brother or sister, parent or step-parent, grandparent, or child, step-child or grandchild.
  • A funeral director, for a death certificate only, with proof of license.
  • An authorized agent, attorney or legal representative, who may be asked for proof.

Online requests are served in order received, refunds are not offered, and updates on an order come by email.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Granville County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to check in the records before closing

Begin by searching your own parcel in the online records. With documents viewable online and copies available on request, you can pull your vesting deed and old loan papers from home.

  • The deed that put the property in your name, with matching spelling and legal description.
  • Any deed of trust that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Plats or easements that affect the parcel.
  • Assumed-name filings, if a business ran from the house.

Fixing problems before you list beats fixing them under a closing deadline. When a recorded instrument looks wrong, ring 919-693-6314 to learn how it can be corrected, and hire an attorney for anything requiring legal drafting.

The recording counter and the tax office

Two offices, one subject. The recording counter moves title. Granville County Tax Administration (919-693-4181) sets values and bills the tax. A balance owed becomes a lien on your parcel dating to the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), so plan to clear it before the new deed goes on record.

A 1.5% discount applies to current taxes paid from July 1 through August 15, with the bill due September 1. Closing in that window? Ask the tax office what paying promptly would save. Whether the land is in Oxford, Butner, Creedmoor, Stem or Stovall, the deed is filed at the one Oxford courthouse counter.

Housing in the county

Granville County has 25,685 housing units and 22,474 households, averaging 2.52 residents each. Building permits in 2025 numbered 257, and the midpoint monthly cost for owners with a mortgage is $1,546. Recording charges come from state law, so they stay the same whatever those numbers do. Local market figures matter for pricing, not for what the Oxford counter charges to file.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for a typical seller

A sensible order of work for a seller: look up your parcel online and request a written tax balance; collect payoff letters and confirm old loans were cancelled of record; have your attorney draft the deed, since register staff cannot; pay the excise tax at closing so the deed can be filed in Oxford; and keep copies of the recorded deed and your tax receipt.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork and appraisal. It does not skip the recording or the tax, and the buyer's attorney will still search the same records you searched. If something surfaces, such as an old uncancelled deed of trust, fixing it early keeps the closing date from slipping.

Frequently asked questions

What will a standard deed cost to file?

Under G.S. 161-10, recording is $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per additional page. The seller also pays excise tax at $1.00 per $500 of value.

When can I come in?

Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. If your deed is out of the ordinary, ring 919-693-6314 before you drive over.

Can staff prepare my deed for me?

No. North Carolina law keeps recording staff from practicing law, so they cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

Is a loan payoff cancellation free to record?

Yes. Under the state fee schedule, recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage costs nothing.

How far back do Granville deeds go?

Deeds are available back to 1746, while vital records ordered online start in 1913.

Greene ties recording to its tax records. Each deed must carry the Deed Information form, signed off by the Greene County Tax Office, before the register will take it.

  • Who is giving and who is receiving the property, with addresses.
  • The street address and legal description, plus buildings if the deed splits a parcel.
  • Any personal property that moves with the land, such as a mobile home.
  • Whether deferred tax value is involved, and how the two parties are related if so.
  • Unpaid prior-year tax and the current-year figure, filled in by the tax office.

The tax office also marks the document as a transfer, a split or a merge and assigns the parcel number. The back of the form has instructions for deeds where delinquent taxes exist. If you owe back tax on the parcel, phone the tax office at 252-747-3615 before you head to the courthouse.

E-recording

Almost every deed can be filed electronically. Only maps and highway rights-of-way are excluded, so a closing attorney can file from a distance.

The tax form works differently online. For electronic filings, the tax office approves Deed Information sheets inside the e-recording platform, and filers should not deliver anything to the tax office by hand or mail. Paper filers get the signature first and then bring the packet to Snow Hill.

Index searches cover 1875 to the present on a site run by Courthouse Computer Systems. The office moved to that system in December 2025, and staff take questions at 252-747-3620.

Recording fees

Charges come from G.S. 161-10 and are the same statewide. A general instrument is $26.00 for its first 15 pages, and a deed of trust is $64.00 for its first 35. Every page past those points adds $4.00.

Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust is free, and plats run $21.00 a sheet. Other items are priced separately by the county: a certified birth, death or marriage copy is $10.00 in cash, and a marriage license is $60, cash only.

Who pays the excise tax?

The seller does. The state charges $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, counting a partial $500 as whole (G.S. 105-228.30). The transferor pays the register of deeds before the deed is filed.

The money is split between the county general fund and the state. The tax follows the amount stated in the deed, so compare that figure to your sale contract. A deed bounced for a missing tax form or a wrong amount is not effective against later buyers and lien creditors until it is properly registered (G.S. 47-18).

Greene County tax rates and fees

The county's 2026 rate is $0.7835 per $100 of value, with town and fire district charges stacked on top. The tax office is at 229 Kingold Boulevard, Suite B, Snow Hill (PO Box 482), phone 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

Greene County 2026 rates and fees
Jurisdiction or feeRate or amount
County rate$0.7835
Town of Hookerton$0.465
Town of Snow Hill$0.340 (sticker fee $5.00)
Town of Walstonburg$0.500 (sticker fee $2.00)
