Solid waste fee, city$65.00

Eleven fire districts are listed, from Arba at $0.0700 to Fort Run at $0.1220, and a Middle Swamp service district shows $0.0910. If you hold mobile homes, boats, aircraft or unlicensed vehicles on January 1, list them during January. A late listing draws a ten percent penalty.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Greene County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Vital records and licenses

Vital records and licenses take up much of the counter. A certified birth, death or marriage copy costs $10.00 in cash when you ask in person with a photo ID issued by the DMV.

  • By mail: send the signed application, a copy of your state photo ID, a $10.00 money order payable to the Greene County Register of Deeds (personal checks are refused) and a stamped return envelope to PO Box 86, Snow Hill, NC 28580.
  • Marriage license: each applicant 18 or older needs a certified birth certificate, a state photo ID or a passport for non-residents, a Social Security card, and a divorce decree or a spouse's death certificate if previously married. The fee is $60, cash only, and licenses are issued between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
  • Licenses go back to the county that issued them, wherever the wedding takes place.

The office also runs a Thank-A-Vet program, takes assumed business name filings and links to a tool for protection from property and mortgage fraud.

Deferred tax on the deed form

Item six on the form asks whether deferred value is involved and, if so, how the grantor is related to the grantee. Item seven lists deferred taxes due by year. The form warns that deferred taxes have not been calculated unless that section is filled in.

The tax office completes the prior-year and current-year lines. If your parcel carries deferred value, ask the office to calculate the amount before the deed is signed, because an uncalculated figure is treated as unknown. Do not leave that question for the closing table.

The form also asks for Social Security numbers, but disclosure is voluntary under federal law and N.C.G.S. 105-309 for tax administration.

Greene County housing

Greene County has 20,700 residents, up 1.2% from the 2020 estimates base, and 8,070 housing units. About 66.5% of homes are owner-occupied. The middle value of an owner's home is $117,400, and middle gross rent is $853. Building permits numbered 59 in 2025. Treat these as county averages, since one farmhouse or town lot can sit far from them.

Getting ready to sell

Begin at the tax office. Ask for the current and prior-year balance and whether any deferred value attaches to the parcel, then have the Deed Information form signed. Next, make sure your attorney has the payoff letters and a fresh look at your vesting deed. At closing, the seller's excise tax is paid and the deed is recorded, usually electronically. A cash sale skips a lender's review, but the tax form and the excise tax still apply.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records Greene County deeds?

The Register of Deeds in the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill. It opens 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays except holidays and takes e-recordings for everything but maps and highway rights-of-way.

Does the Greene County tax office sign off on deeds?

Yes. Every deed needs a tax form signed by the Tax Office. E-filers get that approval through the electronic platform.

How is the deed excise tax figured here?

At $1.00 per $500 of the consideration or value, with any remainder counted as a full $500. The seller pays the register of deeds before recording.

What number do I call for the register of deeds?

252-747-3620. The tax office has its own line, 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

How old are the online Greene County indexes?

Online index searches cover 1875 through the present. The office began using a new records system in December 2025.

Mail can be addressed to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. General questions can go to guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov. One set of land records covers a Jamestown farmhouse, a Summerfield lot and a downtown Greensboro condo alike.

Filing a deed

Deliver a properly formatted deed with the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office puts it on record. Electronic submission works too, because Guilford accepts every real estate document sent through its approved e-recording vendors.

E-recording returns the book and page data plus a stamped image within minutes, and the system rejects a document immediately if it misses the state's recording standards. Paper filings must also show where to send the original after recording. A standard document needs:

  • Letter or legal size paper, one-sided, black type on white stock.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and a quarter inch of margin elsewhere.
  • Type no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument's title printed as a heading on the first sheet.
  • Pen entries for blanks and corrections are acceptable.

A document that fails any item draws the non-standard surcharge on top of the regular fee, so check the layout before you send it.

Recording fees

Recording begins at $26 for a general instrument through page 15 and $64 for a mortgage or deed of trust through page 35. After those limits, every page costs another $4. The state sets those base amounts, while the county table covers the smaller charges.

Guilford County recording and copy fees
Recording itemFee

Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for pages 1 to 35, then $4 per page
Non-standard document$25 added to the recording fee

A plain copy of a real estate record costs 5 cents a page at the counter and $1 by mail. Only these statutory fees may be charged, and they are collected up front.

Some extras can appear around a sale. Taking a notary oath is $10, and authenticating a notary is $1 per notary per page. A map copy is 50 cents, and certified plats are $5 per copy. UCC filings run $38, or $45 above two pages plus $2 for each page past ten. Guilford takes only fixture-related UCC filings, and every other UCC filing goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

Who pays the deed excise tax?

The person giving up title pays it, turning it over to the register before the deed is recorded. The statutory rate is $1 per $500 of price, with any leftover fraction rounded up to a full $500. Deeds since August 1, 1991 are listed at $2 per thousand, which comes out the same.

One half of the revenue stays in the county's general fund. The remainder goes to the state revenue department each month. Your closing statement shows the tax as its own line, apart from the recording fee. Two older rate bands, $1 per thousand for 1968 through July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968, matter only when you read an old deed. For your own sale, get the exact figure from the closing attorney.

Recording a payoff

A loan stays visible against the title until someone records a satisfaction. North Carolina gives an unrecorded deed, option or long lease no priority over lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and ranks competing claims by when they were registered.

There are three recordable forms of satisfaction, none of which costs anything to file:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and acknowledged before a notary.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit by a North Carolina attorney serving as satisfaction agent, for use when a lender never provides one.

The office no longer takes the original deed of trust and note as proof of payment. If an old lender's loan still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears it, and your attorney or the lender can arrange that.

Protecting yourself from forged deeds

Enroll in the Property Fraud Alert. It emails you when a document appears under a name variation you registered. The register must record a deed that meets the legal form once fees and taxes are paid, and the office does not test whether a signature is real.

Vacant or distressed homes, older owners and low-income owners are frequent targets. Warning signs include a transfer you never signed, tax bills that stop arriving, and a default notice on a home with no mortgage. If you find a bad deed, assemble the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney and the register. The register cannot pull a recorded document from the index, so ask an attorney how to challenge it.

It also helps to check credentials, read contracts and consider a title search and title insurance.

Can a recorded deed be corrected?

Only indexing mistakes can be fixed by the office. G.S. 132-1.10 bars it from changing a recorded instrument, so a misspelled name, a faulty legal description or a wrong loan amount in the document itself needs a corrective instrument prepared by your attorney.

An Indexing Correction Request form handles cases where the index differs from the document. Call 336-641-7556 or use the office email with questions. The corrective instrument is recorded at the usual fees. The recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

Before you sell

Pull your vesting deed and check each name's spelling against your ID. Make sure every old loan has a recorded satisfaction. Ask your attorney if a plat or easement touches the lot. On closing day the seller's excise tax is paid and the deed is recorded, usually electronically. A cash sale skips a lender's review, but the recording and the tax stay the same. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.

Guilford housing context

Guilford has 246,403 housing units. About 59.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle owned home is worth $259,900, and median gross rent is $1,163. Builders drew 2,876 permits in 2025.

Frequently asked questions

Which phone number reaches Guilford's register of deeds?

336-641-7556, for the Greensboro office at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Staff are available on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

What does a Guilford deed filing cost?

Expect $26 for an instrument of up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past that, plus a $25 surcharge when the document is non-standard. The seller also pays the excise tax before recording.

Is e-recording available through the Guilford register?

Yes. The office takes all electronically submitted real estate documents via approved vendors, sends back the recording details and a stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state standards.

Does the Guilford register verify a deed's authenticity?

No. A deed that meets the format rules is recorded once fees and taxes are paid. Owners can sign up for the free Property Fraud Alert and report forgeries to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

Do satisfactions of a mortgage carry a Guilford recording fee?

No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are filed free of charge. The office does not accept the original deed of trust and note in their place.

What the Halifax County recording office does

The office takes in, indexes and safeguards land records. It also handles plats, UCC filings, vital records and assorted miscellaneous documents. The elected register serves a 4-year term and leads a team of one assistant and four deputies.

Business runs from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. An online Register of Deeds Index Search is linked from the county site. The county budget for 2026-27 sets aside $516,743 for the office.

How far back the records go

Paper indexes reach to 1732, which is older than the county itself. Online, the index search offers three layers:

  • Indexes and images of recorded real property documents from 1976 forward.
  • Historical real estate indexes for 1934 through 1975.
  • Survey maps dating from 1818.

Other record sets start at different points. Marriage records begin in 1825, and birth and death records begin in October 1913. Anything on a parcel that predates 1976 means working from the historical or hard-copy indexes.

Tax Collector sign-off before recording

Under a commissioners' rule that took effect January 1, 2016, the register will not accept a deed conveying real property unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent ad valorem tax, or other tax the collector must collect, encumbers the parcel.

Staff need time to research each parcel, so the collector stops taking deeds at 4:30 in the afternoon. The collector's office is Tax Administration, 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, phone 252-583-2121. Do this step before you go to the register, since a deed without the certification is turned away. Bring the deed itself, the parcel description and a phone number where the collector can reach your attorney if a question comes up. Recording fees

The 2026-27 fee schedule lists $26 for an instrument up to 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust or mortgage up to 35 pages, adding $4 for each page past those limits. State law fixes the same base amounts.

The schedule also lists $10 for each added index reference on an assignment, $2 per party past 20 distinct parties, and 25 cents a page for photocopies and scanned images. State law treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, collected at filing.

The deed stamp tax

Halifax lists the excise stamp tax at $1.00 per $500 of consideration, with any remainder counted as another $500. State law matches that figure and places the duty on the party giving up title, who must pay before the deed is recorded.

Revenue is split in two. The county general fund keeps one portion, and the state revenue department receives the rest monthly after refunds and an allowance. The 2026-27 county budget shows $353,500 for the Register of Deeds among other taxes and licenses. A parcel split across county lines pays in the county holding the larger share. Ask your closing attorney for the exact amount before settlement.

Recording rules for contracts for deed

Registration is what gives a deed, option or long lease its force against lien creditors and later paying purchasers, and the order of registration sets priority among competing claims.

Seller financing falls under Chapter 47H when the buyer will make at least five payments besides the down payment, the seller keeps title, and the property is a principal dwelling of one to four families or a manufactured home with a price of $5,000 or more. Three features stand out:

  • The agreement must be written, signed and acknowledged.
  • The seller records it, or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed, within five business days.
  • The buyer may cancel through midnight of the third business day, and a default notice must allow a cure date at least 30 days out.

Ask an attorney to draft any land contract and to confirm that it was recorded.

  • Certified copy of a birth certificate or a death certificate: $10 each.
  • Notary public oath administered: $10, and $5 to verify a commission.
  • Military service record: no charge.

The same schedule prices a certified plat copy at $5 for the first page and lists right-of-way plans at $21 for the first page and $5 for each added page.

Tax foreclosure sales and the land records

A tax foreclosure auction ends with a deed, which the register records. The county publishes each sale notice on its Tax Foreclosures page, and bidding happens in the courthouse lobby at Halifax. A bid stays open to a higher one for 10 days, and the property goes as is.

Buyers take subject to taxes, assessments and liens held by parties who were not named defendants, so a title examination before bidding is wise. If your own house faces a tax sale, selling before the auction keeps the price in your hands, and the register will record your deed once the tax certification is on file.

Halifax County housing

The county has 25,078 homes and apartments and 20,383 households. Owners hold 62.9% of occupied homes, a middle-priced owned home is valued at $106,200, and rent sits at a median of $813. Seniors make up 25.2% of the population. Only 75 permits for new building were issued in 2025.

Getting a deed ready

A practical order for a seller: pay or confirm the tax balance, get the collector's certification, gather payoff letters and confirm old loans have recorded satisfactions, then have your attorney finalize the deed. The excise stamp tax is paid at recording. A cash sale skips a lender's paperwork, but the certification and the stamp tax stay. Allow extra days if a municipal balance shows on the parcel, because the collector has to research it before the deed can be accepted. Keep copies of the certification and the recorded deed with your closing papers.

Frequently asked questions

When can I visit the Halifax County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from half past eight to five, with holidays closed. The tax certification a deed needs is handled at the Tax Collector's office, which closes its deed window a half hour before the register's counter.

How much will a Halifax County filing run?

The 2026-27 schedule shows $26 for up to 15 pages plus $4 for every added page, and $25 more for a non-standard form. The seller also owes the excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.

What can make the Halifax County register reject a deed?

A missing certification from the Tax Collector is one reason. A county rule effective January 1, 2016 bars the register from accepting a deed until delinquent taxes are cleared and certified, so visit Tax Administration first.

How old are the land records the Halifax County register holds?

Paper indexes go back to 1732. Online search covers recorded documents from 1976 forward, historical indexes for 1934 through 1975, and survey maps from 1818.

Is recording a satisfaction of a mortgage free in Halifax County?

Yes. The fee schedule shows no charge for satisfactions, consistent with state law. A deed of trust itself starts at $64 for its first 35 pages.

Office location and what it records

Title searches are off limits to staff. For a chain of title, you or the buyer must hire an attorney or a title company. The index is organized by name, so if all you have is a street address, find the owner in the county GIS viewer first.

Recording fees

The office's posted fee list carries a July 1, 2026 date and tracks G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at $26.00 and a loan instrument at $64.00. Pages beyond the included count cost $4.00 each.

Deed tax on a sale

The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of price, the same as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500. That rate has been in force since August 1, 1991, replacing a 50-cent rate that began in 1968.

When a deed counts as recorded

Recording happens when staff keys the deed into the system. Walk-ins have no set cutoff, but anything that cannot be keyed by 5:00 p.m. waits for the next business day. Electronic submissions stop at 4:45 p.m.

Order of registration sets priority between competing claims. G.S. 47-18 denies any conveyance, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal effect against lien creditors and paying buyers until the instrument is registered in the county where the land lies.

  • E-recording works for every document type, maps and plats included.
  • Maps are accepted only at 24x36 or 18x24 inches.

Before you sign a deed

Make sure the deed matches the record owner's name exactly. Names cannot be added or dropped on a deed already recorded, which means fixing an error takes a brand-new deed. The office advises hiring an attorney unless legal drafting is familiar to you.

  • Look through the grantor index for open deeds of trust, then ask every lender for a payoff figure.

A separation agreement shows up at this office only if someone recorded it. If you are separating, find out whether one exists and whether it mentions the house.

How do I get copies of records?

You can walk in, mail a request to Suite 200, or search online. Plain copies are $0.25 each.

Searches work best with the exact spelling on the instrument, so try the seller's name, a spouse's name and any former trust or company name. On older chains, remember the 1892 and 1894 fires. A closing attorney may have to start from later instruments.

The office also records assumed business names, at $26.00 on paper or $41.00 filed online, along with UCC fixture filings. Neither affects a house sale unless the property secures a business loan.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Harnett County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Finding a plat or map

In the online record search, use the Advanced tab and enter a map book and page. Maps kept in a plat cabinet follow a different pattern. Type PC# and the cabinet letter in the book field, then put the slide number and its letter in the page field with no space or dash.

For example, Plat Cabinet C, Slide 123-B is entered as PC#C in the book field and 123B in the page field. The office also keeps an index to plats for browsing by hand.

Boundary questions are common on older houses. Ordering a new survey early, if the one on file looks stale, heads off a delay once the buyer's attorney starts asking. A plat recorded here costs $21.00 per page.

Who records the deed after a tax foreclosure sale?

The winning bidder does. After the court confirms a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale, the bidder receives a commissioner's deed. The county's foreclosure page makes recording it with the register the bidder's job, to be done promptly.

Those properties sell as is. Neither the county nor the commissioner gives a warranty, and no sale depends on financing or marketable title. An owner in that spot can redeem before confirmation, or sell to a buyer able to close first, with a deed recorded at this office in the ordinary way.

A seller's checklist for the register's office

Taking things in order keeps closing simple. First, pull the grantor index under your name and list every open deed of trust. Second, request payoff letters from each lender. Third, have the attorney draft the deed with the owner names spelled as they appear in the record. Fourth, confirm the tax balance with the Tax Department upstairs in Suite 101.

On closing day the attorney sends the deed for recording, and the seller's deed tax is settled before it goes in. Aim to submit before the 4:45 p.m. electronic cutoff, so the deed is registered that day and holds its place in line.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Housing numbers for Harnett County

For 2020-2024 the county had 49,845 households averaging 2.73 persons. Median gross rent runs $1,112, while mortgaged owners pay a median $1,594 monthly. Roughly 86.8% of residents aged one and over stayed put the year before, and workers average 32.8 minutes of travel to work, which buyers weigh against price.

Frequently asked questions

What does it cost to record a Harnett deed?

Expect $26.00 for a deed up to 15 pages, with $4.00 more per extra page. A mortgage runs $64.00 up to 35 pages. The schedule is dated July 1, 2026.

Who pays the deed excise tax in Harnett County?

It falls on the seller and is paid to the register ahead of recording, at $1.00 per $500 of price or value.

Will the register of deeds check my title?

No, state law bars staff from title work. Use an attorney or title company, or search the name-indexed records yourself, with the GIS viewer to match a name to an address.

How late in the day can a deed be recorded?

Paper filings must be keyed by 5:00 p.m., so a long document should arrive earlier. E-recordings close at 4:45 p.m. Later items are recorded the following business day.

Does it cost anything to record a mortgage satisfaction?

No. Satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust are free on the schedule. Lenders normally file the release after payoff.

Henderson County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Henderson County, NC Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Office hours and location

The Register of Deeds is inside the Henderson County Courthouse, 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. It records documents Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The main phone is 828-697-4901.

Staff run a recording counter. They check that a document meets the North Carolina Real Estate Recording Standards, but they cannot give legal advice, so ask your closing attorney what a deed should say. You can pay by check, cash, money order or card. Card payments carry a vendor fee that goes to the vendor.

The Tax Department's Land Records section works from the same courthouse. It builds the county's official index of tax listings from recorded deeds and Clerk of Court files, so a deed that reaches the register soon appears in the parcel data used for billing.

What the office keeps

Land transactions in the county are archived here. The office lists these holdings:

  • Land transfers, easements, rights of way and surveys
  • Deeds of trust, mortgages and UCC filings
  • Separation agreements
  • Assumed business name (DBA) filings
  • Notary public oaths
  • Vital records, with certified copies at $10.00 and photocopies at $.25
  • Military records, recorded and certified for the veteran at no charge

Marriage licenses are by appointment only, between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM on weekdays. Call instead of emailing. Assumed business name forms must be printed on one side of the paper only. Front-and-back printing fails the recording requirements and adds a non-standard document fee to the recording fees.

Searching deeds and plats online

The online deed index runs from 1979 to the present and is hosted by a records vendor. You accept a disclaimer first. The site works best on a desktop or laptop with Chrome or Edge, cookies on and pop-up blocking off for the site.

To pull a plat, open the Register of Deeds system and choose View Images. Pick Plat as the book type, enter the recording year or Cabinet A, B or C as the book, and give the plat number as the page. Leading zeros are not needed. The county's guide lists slide ranges by year, such as 2024 at slides 15330 to 16020 and 2025 at slides 16021 to 16768, with 2026 starting at slide 16769. Older plats from 1988 forward follow the same numbering, and three early cabinets hold the oldest slides.

The online images carry no guarantee of accuracy. The official records stay in the courthouse office, so confirm anything important at the counter.

A privacy notice on the search page cites G.S. 132-1.8(g). Leave Social Security, driver license, bank account and card numbers off any document you file unless the law requires them. You can ask the register in writing to remove such a number from an online image, and there is no fee for that request.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Henderson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

State law sets the amounts, so Henderson County follows G.S. 161-10. Ask the office about any local charge for services outside recording.

Recording fees that apply in Henderson County
DocumentFee
General instrument$26.00 for 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee

Deed stamp tax when you sell

The seller pays it, as the transferor named in the statute. The rate is $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or fraction of it, and the register collects it first.

Look for the line on your settlement statement before closing day. The rule is in G.S. 105-228.30.

What the 2027 reappraisal means for a seller

Values reset on January 1, 2027. Henderson reappraises real property every four years, well ahead of the eight-year minimum in G.S. 105-286, and the last reappraisal took effect in 2023.

Values follow market prices from recent qualified sales, and a mass appraisal groups similar properties together. It weighs location, construction type, age, replacement cost and zoning. A building still under construction on January 1 is valued by its percentage of completion. Land enrolled in the Present-Use Value Program for agriculture, horticulture or forestry can carry an assessed value below market.

The Tax Department counts about 71,500 parcels, and property taxes are an estimated 50 percent of the county operating budget in fiscal year 2027. The Board of Commissioners sets the rate and the Assessor sets values. The Tax Department has divisions for real property, personal property, exemptions and deferment, land records and collections. Programs cover elderly or disabled owners, disabled veteran owners, nonprofits, commercial farms and wildlife management. See the county reappraisal page.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henderson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Henderson County housing market

The county had 122,375 people in July 2025, 5.2 percent above the April 2020 base. It has 61,173 housing units, and builders pulled 1,093 permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 75.0 percent of homes, valued at a median $351,400. Monthly owner costs are $1,608 with a mortgage and $482 without. Gross rent is near $1,187, and household income is $68,187. Adults past 65 are 29.1 percent of residents, so the property tax exclusions for older and disabled owners are worth a question to the Tax Department.

Preparing a deed for recording

A short checklist keeps the document from being flagged or delayed at the counter.

  • Print on one side of letter or legal paper in black ink, using at least 10 point type.
  • State the instrument type across the head of page one and leave a three inch blank margin there.
  • Redact Social Security and account numbers unless the law requires them.
  • Put the drafter's name and the parcel number on page one.
  • Have your attorney file the satisfaction of any paid-off deed of trust.

If the deed fails the formatting standards, the register records it anyway after collecting an added nonstandard document fee. Staff can also issue a certified copy of anything the office recorded.

Bring the signed original, the parcel number, and a card or check for the fees. If you are not sure the formatting passes, call 828-697-4901 before you travel to the courthouse, since the counter closes at 5:00 PM and a document that needs fixing could miss the day.

A typical sale runs in this order. The attorney drafts the deed, you sign, the closing attorney delivers it to the counter, and the seller's stamp tax is collected before recording. Any paid-off deed of trust gets a satisfaction, which is free to record. Once recorded, the deed shows up in the county's land records and then in the parcel data the Tax Department uses for billing.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an appointment to record a deed?

Appointments are listed only for marriage licenses, which run 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM and are booked by phone. Recording is open during the regular weekday hours, and the office answers questions at 828-697-4901.

How far back does the online deed index go?

It covers 1979 to the present. For older plats, choose Plat as the book type and enter a year or Cabinet A, B or C. The county's plat guide gives the slide ranges.

Does Henderson County reappraise every year?

No. Real property is reappraised every four years, last in 2023, with the next effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one at least every eight years.

Can I pay by card at the Register of Deeds?

Yes. Cards are accepted along with checks, cash and money orders. The vendor that processes the card adds a fee, and the county does not charge it.

What does a certified vital record cost?

A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate is $10.00 with proper ID and an acceptable relationship to the person named. Photocopies are $.25.

Office location and hours

You will find the office on the courthouse's third floor, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, Winton. Call 252-358-7850. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, minus county holidays and closings.

Staff keep real estate documents going back as far as 1862, and land deeds in the area date to 1710. Its shelves include deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge and notary records, and vital records for local births, deaths and marriages. The index is by name, so a lawyer tracing an old farm tract works backward through owners.

Recording fees

Fees can change, as the posted schedule itself cautions, so phone ahead before mailing a check. Mailed returns need a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Real estate fees, Hertford County Register of Deeds
Document or servicePosted charge
Deeds and general instruments$26.00, first 15 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00, first 35 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price

Plat copies run $3.00 a page. Fax or online copy requests are $1.00 for the first page and $.25 for every later one.

Formatting rules and the nonstandard fee

Paper standards come from G.S. 161-14. Miss them and the office records the document anyway, adding the $25.00 fee.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

A drafter rule comes from Session Law 2011-351: whoever prepared a deed or deed of trust, person or law firm, is named on page one. Each deed also needs the tax parcel pin. For delinquent taxes the office wants one of two things, a tax department stamp showing none or wording that sends the closing attorney to pay back taxes out of proceeds. E-filed deeds must use the wording.

Can a deed be e-recorded?

Yes, for everything but maps. Corporation Service Company and Simplifile are the named submitters, and the recorded copy returns electronically right after recording.

Your closing attorney picks the route, so a seller normally has nothing to submit personally.

Paper filers should enclose a check made out to the Register of Deeds with a working phone number written on it. Maps, which cannot be e-recorded, have to go in on paper.

What the office cannot do for a seller

Sellers often call the register for help it cannot give. Knowing the limits saves a trip.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A recorded deed of trust is your clue that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot alter a recorded deed. Fixing one takes a new deed, and the office suggests an attorney.
  • An owner cannot be named from a street address, because the index runs by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be.

Who pays the deed excise tax?

Sellers carry it. G.S. 105-228.30 assigns the burden to the transferor, at the $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price shown on the fee schedule.

A conveyance binds later purchasers and lien creditors only after registration under G.S. 47-18, so record soon after signing. Read both rules at G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

Other services at the Winton counter

Vital records and a few other items come through this counter, which helps if you also need paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each with government photo ID, released only to close relatives or an authorized agent.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00, no appointment needed once the Secretary of State sends notice.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

Home values in Hertford County

Population is about 19,015 as of mid 2025, spread over 9,873 housing units. A median owned home is $119,200, and 67.4 percent of homes are lived in by owners. With values this modest, flat charges like recording fees take a bigger bite out of a small sale, so get the closing attorney's cost list before pricing.

The 2027 revaluation and deeds recorded now

The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Recording steps stay the same for deeds filed before or after that date. Only the assessed value on the parcel changes.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector sit at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. Ask the collector about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A seller's path through the office

Before closing, ask your attorney to confirm the deed will name you exactly as the record owner. A mistake means a new deed, since the office cannot change one already recorded. Check that page one names the preparer and carries the tax parcel pin, and that the deed includes the sentence directing back taxes to be paid from closing proceeds. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff so no delinquent tax holds up the deed.

On closing day the seller's excise tax of $2.00 per $1000.00 is collected with the recording. Any paid-off deed of trust is cancelled at no fee. Recording is what protects the buyer against later purchasers and lien creditors, so ask the attorney to send the deed promptly. An e-recorded copy comes back electronically. A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, which means one fewer instrument to record and one less satisfaction to chase.

If something goes wrong after closing, such as a misspelled name or a missing page, call the office at 252-358-7850 right away. Staff can tell you what was recorded, but the fix is a new deed prepared by an attorney. For questions about where a parcel sits, Land Records Mapping at 252-358-7809 is the right call, and for estate or divorce papers tied to the sale, the Clerk of Superior Court at 252-358-7100 holds them.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?

The schedule lists $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. Call 252-358-7850 to check for changes.

What is the excise tax on a deed?

The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, and the seller pays it.

What happens if my deed is formatted wrong?

It is recorded anyway, with a $25.00 non-standard fee added. Check the paper, type and page one rules above before you file.

Can staff search my title or find a lien?

No. State law keeps register staff from searching titles, and the office cannot confirm whether a lien exists. An attorney or title professional can read the recorded instruments.

Can I get a copy of my recorded deed?

Yes, at the counter or on the county sites, though older indexes and images may be missing online. Certified copies are priced per page.

Where to record a deed

Deeds can be filed at either of two Iredell sites, in Statesville or Mooresville. The counters stay open Monday through Friday, eight to five.

  • Statesville site: 211 Constitution Ln, Statesville, NC 28677, telephone 704-872-7468
  • Mooresville site: 610 E Center Ave, Mooresville, NC 28115, telephone 704-663-4533
  • Shared fax line: 704-878-5426

Staff at these counters also issue certified birth and death certificates, marriage licenses and military discharge copies, and give notary oaths. Almost every record is open to anyone. Military discharges are the lone exception.

A seller typically never visits. The closing attorney carries in the signed deed along with the buyer's loan paperwork, and a later call to either site confirms both made the record and in what order.

Why recording matters in a sale

Until a deed is recorded, the transfer carries no weight with outsiders. Clerks index the deed and the lender's security instrument by party name, and the filing time decides who is first in line.

North Carolina's recording statute withholds a conveyance's force from lien creditors and paying buyers until it is registered in the county of the land, and then ranks claims by registration time. So a closing is not done at the signing table, and attorneys hold funds until recording is confirmed.

Drafting help and title opinions are off the menu for staff, as are title searches. Changing the names on a deed means a fresh one, drafted, notarized and recorded, which is why most owners hire a lawyer.

Judgments live with the Clerk of Court, 704-832-6600. One lasts ten years, may be renewed for ten more, and attaches to land you own now or acquire later. Have your attorney check for entries against you ahead of signing a sale contract.

Filing fees

For an ordinary instrument the fee is $26.00 through page fifteen and $4.00 per page beyond. A loan security document starts at $64.00 for thirty-five pages. Both follow G.S. 161-10, which applies in all one hundred counties alike.

Filing fees in Iredell County
Filing typeCharge

No other charges stack on top of this schedule, and payment is due when you file.

Already-recorded documents are copied at county prices. Deeds are $.25 a page and a printed recorded map is $1.00, with an added charge for mail, so phone before sending a request.

Who pays the deed transfer tax?

Whoever transfers the property owes this tax, and the Register collects it before the deed is placed on record. The charge is $1.00 per $500 of price, rounding any leftover fraction up to a full $500.

The excise tax statute sends half the receipts to the Iredell general fund and the rest to the state revenue department.

It is figured on the price or value of the interest changing hands. Since the duty falls on the seller, find this line on your settlement statement and ask your attorney how the contract treats it. A cash offer does not change it, because the tax follows the deed, not the buyer.

Looking up land records online

A link on the county Register page opens a search of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and powers of attorney. Records stretch from December 1788 to today and are indexed by party name, as state law requires.

The Land Records page offers a search guide, indexing rules and a separate guide for property recorded before 1964. The online portal may show incomplete results during a software change and is not an official record, so for a sale request a certified copy from the office instead of printing from the screen.

  • Find an owner: use the tax office GIS maps, or call 704-878-3020 for help with them.
  • Proof a mortgage is paid: your lender files a certificate of satisfaction, and staff can mail or email you a copy.
  • Replace a lost deed: give names and a purchase year, and a copy costs $.25 per page.

A deed passes ownership, usually seller to buyer. A deed of trust is a three-way tie between borrower, lender and a neutral trustee that secures a loan. A lender's title policy protects the lender, while an owner's policy is optional and protects you against defects a title search missed. The office recommends carrying both.

Property tax and the Register of Deeds

You do not pay property tax at this office. Tax Administration in Statesville bills and collects it, while the Register only records instruments. The two meet at a sale, because a buyer's attorney expects the tax account to be current.

On request the collector will accept a payoff at the closing table, or a prepayment at last year's rate before the new bill is out. The county charges .50 per $100 for 2026, per its rates page, and towns like Statesville and Mooresville add their own.

January 1 fixes ownership for tax purposes. Close later in the year and the bill is still yours unless the contract shifts it, so check the proration line on the settlement statement.

A seller's steps at the Register's office

Take these steps so recording goes without a hitch.

  1. Engage a North Carolina attorney to draft the deed, because staff will not.
  2. Sign in front of a notary, and the attorney takes the notarized deed to Statesville or Mooresville.
  3. Pay the transfer tax and filing fee at the time of filing.
  4. Ask for word that the deed and any loan paperwork made the record, and note the filing order.
  5. Keep the lender's certificate of satisfaction for any loan you paid off.

To see what is on record before listing, search your name in the online index, then ask the office for a certified copy of anything that matters.

A few contacts help along the way. For parcel maps and finding an owner, call 704-878-3020. For judgments, call the Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600. For anything about recording, the Statesville site is 704-872-7468 and the Mooresville site is 704-663-4533. Keep the closing attorney in the loop on all of them, since the attorney controls when the deed is sent.

Iredell County housing numbers

Mid-2025 population stood at 211,798, with roughly 93,711 housing units. Owners fill 71.9 percent of occupied units (2020-2024) and the typical owned house is $321,400. The midpoint household earns $81,419, rent at the midpoint is $1,252 monthly, and 1,835 building permits were issued in 2025.

Frequently asked questions

Which office should I use to record a deed?

Either one. The Statesville site at 211 Constitution Ln and the Mooresville site at 610 E Center Ave both accept recordings on weekdays between eight and five.

What does it cost to file a deed in Iredell County?

A routine instrument is $26.00 up to fifteen pages, and every extra page adds $4.00. Deeds of trust start at $64.00 for thirty-five pages, then add the same $4.00 per extra page.

Who bears the excise tax on a sale?

The seller pays it before the deed is filed, at a dollar per $500 of value. Your contract and closing statement show how it is handled.

Can county staff prepare my deed?

No. State law bars them from drafting deeds. Hire a North Carolina attorney, then bring the signed, notarized deed in for filing.

Where do I check for a judgment against my property?

The Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600 holds them, and the Register does not. A judgment lasts ten years and may be extended for ten more.

Where the office is and what it keeps

The Jackson County Register works from Room 108 at 401 Grindstaff Cove Road in Sylva, NC 28779. Walk-in recording and e-recording share one weekday window, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at half past four. Recording questions go to 828-586-7530.

The archives cover real estate transactions, Jackson County births and deaths, and marriage licenses issued locally. The office also records DD214 military discharge forms and issues certified copies to the discharged service member free of charge.

  • Records portal: deeds.jacksonnc.org
  • E-recording: the department page links an e-recording guide
  • Plat questions: Land Records and Mapping at 828-586-7539, or the Planning Department at 828-631-2261

Tax Administration shares the 401 Grindstaff Cove Road address, so one visit can cover both recording and the tax certification described below.

Deed format requirements

Anything filed after July 1, 2002 has to satisfy G.S. 161-14(b). A document that misses the rules draws a $25 non-standard fee on top of the usual recording charge.

  • Letter paper (8.5 by 11) or legal paper (8.5 by 14), with the original handed in
  • A three-inch blank band at the head of page one, and half an inch along its other edges and on every edge of later pages
  • Black ink on white stock, typeface of at least 10 points
  • Print on a single side
  • The name of the instrument printed beneath the top margin

Staff draft nothing, supply no forms and alter nothing on a submitted paper. If a legal description has an error, the drafter must correct it.

Land records reviews each deed too. Expect to provide an individual's or law firm's name and address as preparer on the first page, the names and addresses of the grantors and grantees, either a metes and bounds description or a plat cabinet and slide reference, the grantor's back deed references, and a statement on whether any grantor lives on the parcel as a primary residence. A deed that divides a parcel must cite a recorded survey or bear approval from the Planning Department.

Recording charges

Ordinary instruments run $26 for the opening fifteen pages with $4 for each page past that, and a deed of trust is $64 for its opening thirty-five pages. These amounts agree with G.S. 161-10.

Jackson County Register of Deeds charges
Item filed or requestedAmount
Deed, assignment, release or power of attorney, pages 1 to 15$26
Each page beyond the first set$4
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
SatisfactionNo charge
Plat, each page$21
Certified plat copy$5
Uncertified plat copy$2
UCC filing of two pages$38
UCC filing of three to ten pages$45
Document outside the format rules$25 added

A UCC termination is $38, and pages after the tenth add $2 apiece.

Payment method matters. Attorney or law firm checks, cashier's checks and money orders are taken. Personal checks are refused.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jackson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deed excise tax and the tax certification

The county prints the tax as $2 against every $1,000 of sales price, collected when a deed that conveys an interest is filed. That matches the statute's wording of $1 on each $500.

The excise tax statute makes the seller pay the register ahead of filing. Half of the money stays with the county's general fund and half goes to the state. A parcel that straddles county lines is taxed by whichever county holds the larger value.

Jackson adds a tax check that surprises some sellers. Since March 7, 2011, every deed goes to the Tax Collector's Office for a certification that no delinquent property taxes are owed, and the collector asks for the Parcel Identification Number to speed things up. If back taxes might exist on your parcel, ask for a payoff before the day of closing so the certification does not hold up recording.

Property tax dates and a sale

Tax Administration, at the same Sylva address, bills real and personal property for the county and also collects for Dillsboro, Forest Hills, Highlands and Webster. Sylva sends its own bill and keeps its own collections.

Bills are due September 1, and January 5, 2027 is the final day to pay this cycle without interest. Starting January 6, unpaid balances pick up 2 percent, then 0.75 percent more each month. Relief program applications close June 1, and the formal appeal period for real property runs in the spring after a reappraisal notice.

Useful numbers for a seller: Tax Collections at 828-586-7550, Real Property at 828-586-7549, and Exemptions, Present-Use Value and Property Tax Relief at 828-586-7542. The county's land borders the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, so a parcel missing from county records may sit on tribal land, which the tribe maps through its own viewer. A tax lien reaches a parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so ask the collector to confirm any open balance in writing.

Plat rules

A plat sheet is accepted at 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches, with a border of at least half an inch on every side. Staff look for the surveyor's original seal and wet-ink signature plus the statements G.S. 47-30 requires.

Plats sent electronically face the same requirements as those carried in, and whoever submits is responsible for collecting signatures first. Plats filed in the office must be reproducible, black on white paper or Mylar.

Some plats go to Land Records or the Planning Department for review before they are filed. If your lot came from a recent split, ask the surveyor whether the plat is already on file, since the deed has to cite it. The charge is $21 per page.

Jackson County housing numbers

The county had 45,039 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 4.4 percent since April 2020, across 491.11 square miles and 28,707 housing units. Homeowners hold 60.8 percent of occupied homes (2020-2024), and the typical owner-held house is worth $284,700. Middle monthly rent is $904, and median household income is $55,815.

Confirm which town's rate applies to your parcel, since municipal bills are handled differently in Sylva than in the other towns. Cullowhee has its own community planning council on the county meeting calendar.

A seller's checklist for the Sylva office

Start by getting the Parcel Identification Number, because the Tax Collector's Office wants it for the delinquent-tax certification. Ask Tax Collections at 828-586-7550 whether any balance is open. Have your closing attorney prepare a deed that meets the format rules, including the preparer's name on page one, a full legal description and the back deed reference.

On closing day the attorney's firm check, not a personal check, pays the recording fee and the excise tax. The deed goes to the Tax Collector's Office for certification and then to the Register for recording. If you paid off a loan, the satisfaction is recorded at no charge. A cash buyer skips the lender's deed of trust, so there is less to record, but the tax certification and the excise tax still apply.

Frequently asked questions

Which office accepts a deed for filing?

The Register of Deeds in Room 108 at 401 Grindstaff Cove Road, Sylva. Walk-in and electronic recording share one weekday window that closes at 4:30 p.m.

What is the fee to file a deed in Jackson County?

Fifteen pages cost $26 and each added page costs $4, while a deed of trust starts at $64 for thirty-five pages. Paper outside the format rules adds $25.

Are personal checks accepted at the recording desk?

No. Attorney or law firm checks, cashier's checks and money orders are the accepted payment types.

Does a Jackson County deed need a tax clearance?

Yes. Each deed goes to the Tax Collector's Office to certify there are no delinquent property taxes, so bring the parcel number.

How is excise tax figured on a deed?

The county posts it as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price. The seller pays ahead of recording.

Where to record a Johnston County deed

The Register of Deeds is on the ground floor of the Smithfield courthouse, Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, near the 2nd and Market Street corner of Courthouse Square. Call 919-989-5160 for land records.

The office is open weekdays except county holidays, and the real estate counter takes walk-ins without an appointment until 4:45 p.m. Vital records have their own line, 919-989-5161. An heir who needs a death certificate for an estate sale should use that number.

In North Carolina, priority follows the time a document is registered in the county where the land sits. A signed deed that never gets recorded leaves the buyer exposed to a later purchaser or a lien creditor. The usual plan is to record on the day the buyer funds.

Recording fees

A plain deed costs a flat $26.00 through page 15, and each extra page adds $4.00. A deed of trust or mortgage has a longer base, $64.00 through page 35.

Johnston County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
Deed, easement or similar instrument$26.00 up to page 15, extra pages at $4.00 each
Home loan security instrument (deed of trust or mortgage)$64.00 up to page 35, extra pages at $4.00 each
Release of a security instrumentNone
Document that breaks the formatting rules$25.00
Plat map$21.00 a page
Fax, local call10 cents a page

If you mail a package and are owed a refund of $1.00 or less, none is sent. Anything larger comes back as a check from county finance.

The transfer stamp

The excise stamp is $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration, which the office also writes as $1.00 per $500. The seller pays it. State law puts the burden on the transferor, and it is due at the register's counter before the deed is recorded.

Half the money goes to the county general fund and half to the Department of Revenue. The stamp is a separate line from the per-page fee, and the closing company normally puts both in the seller column of the settlement statement.

Because the rate applies to each $500 or part of $500, ask the office or your closing attorney for the exact stamp on your contract price before closing day.

Can a Johnston County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. Johnston County was among the first in North Carolina to e-record every document type, and among the first anywhere to e-record plat maps. Most of what the office receives now comes in electronically.

The approved submitters are:

  • CSC eRecording
  • EPN
  • Indecomm
  • NTC
  • Simplifile

After recording, the document goes back to the submitter within seconds for review. Title companies and closing attorneys usually have an account with one of these services, so a seller rarely logs in. If you close without a lawyer, ask whoever handles your closing which service they use and when the file can go out.

The county also runs an online search. You can look up a grantor or grantee name, a reception number, a date range or a subdivision, and a find-related function pulls up documents that share a legal description.

What raises a recording bill

Three things add to the total, and each has its own line on the schedule.

  • Length. Every page past 15 on a deed adds $4.00.
  • Bundled instruments. A document containing two or more instruments with different legal effect adds $10.00 for each extra one.
  • Format. A paper that fails the state recording standards draws another $25.00.

Payoff paperwork is the cheap part. A satisfaction, trustee's satisfaction or affidavit of satisfaction carries no charge, so clearing an old loan costs nothing at the register. If your lender has not released its lien, ask it to send the satisfaction for recording right after payoff.

Before the deed goes to the register

Have the deed signed, notarized and complete before it leaves the closing table. The register records instruments and does not draft or repair them.

Run through this list before the signing appointment ends:

  • Match the grantor names to the way title is held today.
  • Copy the parcel description from your own deed.
  • Work out the stamp amount the seller will pay.
  • Ask your lender to record a satisfaction of the old deed of trust.
  • Ask the Johnston County tax office about any unpaid bill, since the property tax lien attaches to a parcel on the January 1 listing date.

The office also offers a free fraud alert, which you join through the county website. Owners who rent out a house or leave it empty during a sale may want it, since the office reports property fraud cases on the rise.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Johnston County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited homes and liens

Estate paperwork belongs to the clerk of court, and the register only records the deeds that follow. Smaller estates have a shortcut: once 30 days have gone by since the death, an heir, creditor or public administrator can file an affidavit if personal property net of liens does not exceed $20,000.

The register keeps the lien index but removes nothing by itself. A mortgage or deed of trust leaves the record only when a satisfaction is recorded. Tax liens work differently. They attach to the parcel on its January 1 listing date, and collection is a court foreclosure.

A house with liens, back taxes, tenants or repair needs can still sell for cash without a listing or showings. The deed goes to this same register and carries the same recording fee and stamp as any other sale.

Closing day, step by step

A smooth recording depends on what happens before the deed reaches Suite 209. Most sales follow the same order.

  1. The closing attorney or title company reviews the deed for the right grantor names and parcel description.
  2. You sign in front of a notary, and the buyer funds the purchase.
  3. The seller's excise stamp is collected as part of the settlement figures.
  4. The file is sent to the register through one of the approved e-recording services, or carried to the counter before 4:45 p.m.
  5. The office records the deed, and the submitter receives the recorded copy back within seconds.
  6. Your old lender records its satisfaction, which costs nothing, and you keep a copy for your files.

If you are selling without an attorney, ask your title company who will handle recording and when. A deed that misses the afternoon cutoff waits until the next business day, and priority follows the time of registration, so timing counts.

Johnston County market context

Johnston County sits east of Raleigh and has grown fast, with a population of 256,448 and about 99,408 housing units. A typical owned home is worth $305,600, and 76.1 percent of households are owner-occupied. Builders pulled 3,002 permits in 2025, so new houses compete with resales and buyers of older homes often ask for repairs or credits.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What phone number reaches the Johnston County Register of Deeds?

Dial 919-989-5160 for land records, or 919-989-5161 for vital records and marriage licenses. The office is in Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, Smithfield.

How much does a standard Johnston County deed cost to record?

A plain deed runs $26.00 up to page 15, with $4.00 added for each later page. Loan paperwork is priced higher, $64.00 up to page 35. The stamp is a separate charge.

Is there a charge for recording a satisfaction in Johnston County?

No. Satisfactions of a security instrument, trustee's satisfactions, notices, certificates and affidavits of satisfaction are recorded at no charge.

Is e-recording available for Johnston County deeds?

Yes, through an approved submitter. CSC eRecording, EPN, Indecomm, NTC and Simplifile are on the list, and your closing company normally sends the file for you.

Whose job is it to pay the transfer stamp in Johnston County?

The seller pays it at the register's counter while the deed is still unrecorded. The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration.

Selling in Jones County? Get a Cash Offer

Selling in Jones County?

Office location and hours

The Jones County Register of Deeds is at 101 Market Street in Trenton. The mailing address is PO Box 189, Trenton, NC 28585, and the phone is 252-448-2551. Monday through Thursday the counter is staffed from morning into late afternoon, and recording stops at 4:30. Fridays are short: open from 8 a.m. to noon, with an 11:30 cutoff for recording.

That short Friday matters for a closing. A deed that reaches the counter after 11:30 on a Friday sits until Monday, so sellers here usually schedule signing early in the week.

Besides land transactions, the office keeps births, deaths, marriages, service discharges, notaries, assumed names and maps. Its land indexes go back to the late 1700s, and records from before 1978 are searched through their own page on the county site.

Recording fees

Trenton charges $26.00 to record a deed of up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 per additional sheet. Loan paperwork gets a longer allowance: $64.00 covers 35 pages.

Jones County real estate recording charges
What you are recording or requestingAmount
Loan security (deed of trust)$64.00 to page 35, $4.00 per page past that
Deeds and other instruments$26.00 to page 15, $4.00 per page past that
Combined instruments in one filing$10.00
Release of a deed of trust by satisfactionFree of charge
Document out of format$25.00
Plat sheet$21.00 each
Certified real estate copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 each page after
Plain copy25 cents

The excise stamp is $2.00 for each $1,000 of purchase price, or $1.00 per $500 of consideration. The seller pays it at the counter.

Tax office approval comes first

Before the register will record anything, the deed and a filled-in Tax Certification Form must be shown to the Tax Office and approved. The form is also called the Tax Data Sheet or Tax Collection Form, and the register's site links to it.

Two more local rules apply:

  • Jones County ordinance wants the tax parcel ID number printed on page one of each deed.
  • A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for real property that is subject to delinquent taxes.

In practice an unpaid Jones County tax bill can stop a deed at the counter. A seller with back taxes should pay them at or before closing, and the closing agent can settle the bill so the deed is accepted the same day.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jones County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording standards for a deed

Anything on paper filed after July 1, 2002 has to follow the layout rules of G.S. 161-14(b), and the register posts them online. A document that misses the mark is charged $25.00 extra, added to the normal recording fee.

  • Paper size of 8 1/2 by 11 or by 14.
  • A blank 3 inch band at the top of page one, half an inch of margin on its other edges, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Black or dark ink on white stock, type no smaller than 10 points.
  • Text on a single side of each sheet.
  • The instrument type printed right under the top margin, with the preparer identified on page one.

Small print under 10 point that still scans clearly may get the nonstandard fee waived. Maps and plats follow separate rules: they must be 18 by 24 inches, with one mylar and one paper copy, and a Jones County review officer approves the map before it is recorded.

Liens and satisfactions

To clear an old mortgage, the lender records a satisfaction, and the Trenton office charges nothing for that. There are two kinds: a Satisfaction of Security Instrument signed by the secured creditor, and a Trustee's Satisfaction signed by a trustee or substitute trustee.

Wills never go to the register. They are filed with the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, so an heir selling an inherited house should head there first.

Under state law a tax lien reaches the parcel on its January 1 listing date, carrying penalties, interest and costs. If it stays unpaid, the county enforces it by filing a foreclosure action in court. Before you sign a sales contract, ask the Jones County tax office for a current payoff figure.

Property tax before you sell

The bill is due September 1. On January 6 it becomes delinquent and 2 percent interest applies for January, followed by 3/4 percent every month. If you mail your check, the U.S. Postal postmark sets the date. A postage meter date does not count.

Property was last revalued January 1, 2022, with January 1, 2030 set for the next one. Market changes between those dates are not counted. If you disagree with an assessment, call 252-448-2546 to set up an informal appeal before March 1. Later appeals may need a formal hearing before the county review board.

Visit the tax office at 418 Hwy 58 N in Trenton. The counter shuts at five o'clock Monday through Thursday and at midday on Friday. Partial payments are taken at the Tax Collections Office, and a payment plan is available only if no enforced collection action has begun. Agricultural and forest tracts can qualify for use value taxation, with a new application going to the assessor during the regular January listing period.

Jones County housing market

With 9,575 residents and 4,804 housing units across 471.37 square miles, Jones County is among the more thinly settled places in the state. Owned homes have a typical value of $130,300, and 79.4 percent are lived in by their owners. About 26.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, which means estates and older sellers are common. With just 46 building permits in 2025, a seller mostly faces other resales, and a house needing repairs can linger on the market.

Does a cash sale change the recording steps?

A cash buyer's deed follows the same path as any other. It is approved by the tax office, shows the parcel number on page one, has its stamp paid by the seller, and gets to the register before the weekday or Friday cutoff.

The difference is pace and condition, and a quick closing can matter to an heir or an out-of-town owner. A cash deal skips the lender appraisal, and the house is bought in its current state. That can help an owner who has liens, a vacant house, tenants or an estate to wind up. Overdue taxes must still be cleared at closing so the register will take the deed.

Trenton is small, and a rejected deed can cost you a trip and a day. Before you head to the closing table:

  1. Have the tax office approve the Tax Certification Form.
  2. Confirm the parcel ID number is on page one.
  3. Pay any delinquent taxes so the register will accept the deed.
  4. Arrive before 4:30 on Monday through Thursday, or before 11:30 on Friday.
  5. Bring a payoff letter if an old deed of trust needs a satisfaction recorded.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Jones County Register of Deeds hours?

Walk in Monday to Thursday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., though anything to be recorded must arrive by 4:30 p.m. On Fridays the office closes at noon and takes recordings until 11:30 a.m. Call 252-448-2551.

Can Jones County record a deed if property taxes are unpaid?

No. A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for property subject to delinquent taxes. Pay the bill first, then present the deed.

What must page one of a Jones County deed show?

The tax parcel ID number, which a county ordinance demands, along with the instrument type and the name of whoever prepared it. Leave a 3 inch blank top margin and 1/2 inch on the sides.

Does Jones County bill for recording a loan release?

No. A satisfaction of a deed of trust is free, whether it is the creditor's signed form or the trustee's.

Where are wills recorded in Jones County?

At the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, phone 252-448-6220, not at the Register of Deeds. The register records the deeds that follow.

Contact and hours

The Lee County Register of Deeds answers at 919-718-4585. You will find it on South Horner Boulevard in Sanford, open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning to 5:00. Since January 1, 2017, the daily recording cutoff for every document has been 4:30.

The office exists to maintain, protect and provide access to every recorded transaction and the county's vital records. For a seller, the real estate side is what counts: it records properly notarized instruments, mostly concerning land in Lee County, and keeps the index that title examiners search.

Marriage licenses are by appointment only. If you need vital records for an estate sale, you can order certified copies online through the link on the county's Register of Deeds page.

Recording fees

Sanford's base price for a deed is $26.00 and covers 15 pages. Sheets after that run $4.00 each. Mortgages and deeds of trust start at $64.00 and cover 35 pages. The printed schedule cites G.S. 161-10, the statewide fee statute.

An additional subsequent instrument index reference is $25.00 each.

Excise tax on the sale

The schedule prints the state excise tax on real estate conveyances as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 up to $500. Under the statute the seller owes one dollar for each $500 of value, rounding any leftover amount up to a full unit, and pays at the register before recording.

The sheet also explains where the money goes. One half stays with the county, and the other half, less a 2 percent handling fee, goes to the state. That split is the county's bookkeeping and does not change what the seller owes.

Your closing attorney's settlement statement should show the excise line in the seller column, right beside recording. If the figure seems off for your contract price, phone the register.

Documents with no recording charge

Cancellations are free, which covers releasing an old deed of trust. A military discharge is also free to file, along with one certified copy of it.

Everything else follows the page-based fees. These are the items that usually come up when a Lee County house is sold:

  • The seller's deed to the buyer, priced by its length.
  • The buyer's deed of trust, if there is a loan, charged at the higher base.
  • A cancellation of the seller's old loan, recorded for no fee.
  • A plat, if a lot is being split, at $21.00 a sheet.

A cash sale has no new loan to record, so the register's bill is usually just the deed fee and the excise stamp, plus any copies you ask for.

Can I be alerted when something is recorded against my property?

Yes. The register offers a free property notification service. You register a name, and an email arrives whenever a document under that name is filed in the Lee County office. Sign-up runs through a state-wide notification website linked from the county page.

This suits owners who live away from a house, hold an inherited property, or rent a home out. A filing under your name that you did not expect is a red flag for fraud, and the email lets you call the office quickly.

You can also search deeds through the Sanford and Lee County deeds online portal that the county links. Use it to confirm that a deed from your closing has appeared and to read the book and page of earlier deeds.

Copies and other records

The register issues certified copies of recorded instruments for $5.00 on the opening page plus $2.00 per page after it. A comparing copy for certification costs $5.00. These help when a lender or buyer's attorney asks for a stamped copy of an older deed, easement or plat.

Estate sales often need vital records too. Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records are $10.00 each in the schedule, and certified vital records can be ordered online through a link on the county page.

Other items on the schedule that can touch a sale:

  • A certificate for removal of graves, $12.00 for page one then $3.00 a page after that, which may come up when rural land with an old family plot is conveyed.
  • Right-of-way plans, $21.00 up front and $5.00 for every one after.
  • A UCC search for filings made before July 1, 2001, $38.00 per name plus $1.00 per copy.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property tax bills

Property tax is handled apart from the register. The Lee County Tax Office, 106 Hillcrest Drive in Sanford, lists and appraises real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles, and it collects both current and delinquent taxes. It is open weekdays from eight to five.

Three direct lines cover the main needs:

  • Collections: 919-718-4662
  • Listings: 919-718-4661
  • Appraisals: 919-718-4660

The department's page offers a comparable sales tool called Comper, which sellers can use to see recorded sales near their address. On the bill itself, the due date is September 1 and no interest accrues before January 6. After that date 2 percent is added, then 3/4 percent a month from February 1.

What to bring to the Sanford office

A short trip to South Horner Boulevard goes better with the right papers in hand. Bring the signed and notarized deed, payment for the page fee and the seller's excise tax, and a clear idea of how many pages the deed runs. If a cancellation of an old loan is part of the closing, confirm with your lender who will send it, because the register records it without charge but cannot chase the lender for you.

Out-of-town sellers can skip the trip. The closing attorney or title company normally presents everything on your behalf, and the free notification service tells you once the filing under your name appears in the Lee County records.

Lee County housing market

Lee County has 70,258 residents, up 11.0 percent from 2020, and 28,511 housing units in a compact 255.06 square miles. A typical owned home is worth $240,200, and owners live in 67.3 percent of homes. The rest are rentals at a median $1,017. Builders took out 674 permits in 2025, so new homes are part of the supply, and a resale usually competes with them on price and move-in readiness.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling quickly and as is

Selling for cash to a direct buyer means no listing and no repair list, yet the paperwork still lands at this office. You sign the deed, the closing agent brings it in ahead of the 4:30 p.m. cutoff, and your excise tax is paid first.

Pull together your own deed, a payoff statement if a loan remains, and the latest tax bill before accepting an offer. Should a lien appear on the title, have the lender record its cancellation so the next owner gets a clear record.

On closing day the usual flow in Sanford is short. The attorney checks the deed, you sign before a notary, the excise stamp is paid, and the file reaches the register before 4:30. Afterward, ask for your lender's cancellation to be recorded, since that costs nothing, and keep the recorded copy with your closing papers.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Lee County Register of Deeds stop recording documents?

4:30 p.m. every day. Staff are there until five on weekdays, but recording has ended half an hour sooner since January 1, 2017.

What will a Lee County deed cost at the register's counter?

$26.00 buys 15 pages, and every further page is $4.00. Mortgage paperwork is $64.00 for 35 pages. The excise stamp is extra.

Does Lee County charge to cancel a deed of trust?

No. No. Recording a cancellation of an old loan is free, so it adds nothing to what you pay at closing.

Who is charged the transfer stamp on a Lee County deed?

The seller. The transferor settles it with the register before recording, at one dollar per $500 of price, with any remainder counted as another unit.

Is there a free alert for new filings under my name in Lee County?

Yes. The register offers a free property notification service that emails you when a document with your registered name is filed in the Lee County office.
