Office address and contact

The Register of Deeds is at 101 North Queen Street, Kinston, ZIP 28501. Mail goes to PO Box 3289, Kinston, 28502. The front desk is 252-559-6420, and email goes to lcrod@lenoircountync.gov.

Counter and recording hours are weekdays, 8:30am to 5:00pm. The same desk files maps, assumed names, notary oaths and military discharges, and issues birth, death and marriage records, so a seller who also needs a certified family record can ask for it on the same trip.

The office applies state recording law, so a Lenoir County deed follows the same ground rules as one filed anywhere else in North Carolina.

From signed deed to recorded deed

After the grantor signs before a notary, the paper goes to the Kinston office with payment. The deputy stamps the date and time, indexes the grantor and grantee names, and assigns the book and page that title searchers will use.

  1. Have your closing attorney prepare and notarize the deed.
  2. Send it with the page fee and excise tax, by hand, by mail to the PO box, or electronically.
  3. Collect the receipt and note the book and page.
  4. Check the index a few days later to confirm your name shows as grantor.

E-recording is available, and filers who want to enroll can call Simplifile at (801) 223-1046. At the counter a debit or credit card works, though the county adds a small usage fee. Vital records ordered by mail are different: the office wants cash or a money order, never a personal check, along with a stamped return envelope and a photocopy of the requester's picture ID.

Recording fees

Recording charges are set by the state, and the office posts its own fee sheet as a link on its Register of Deeds page. Call the office to confirm the current sheet before you file.

Selected statewide recording charges under G.S. 161-10
DocumentCharge
Standard instrument$26 buys the first 15 pages; each page beyond adds $4
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 runs through page 35; each page beyond adds $4
Paid-off loan releaseNo charge
Map or plat$21 a sheet
Certified copy$5 on page one plus $2 per added page
Nonstandard paper$25 on top of the usual fee

Clearing an old loan before a Kinston sale adds a little delay but no filing charge.

Excise tax on a Lenoir County deed

Expect $1 for every $500 of price or value, with any leftover piece billed as a full block. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay, which means the seller, and the money is owed in Kinston before the deed is entered.

Half stays in the county general fund. The rest is sent to the state every month, once refunds and the county's retained allowance are taken out.

A separate check is rarely needed. Your closing attorney subtracts the tax at settlement and submits it with the deed, so it appears as a seller-side line on the closing statement.

Why the recording time matters

In North Carolina, G.S. 47-18 ranks competing claims by the moment they reach the county books. A buyer who holds only a signed deed can lose to a creditor or later purchaser whose paper was registered first.

That is why lenders want recording on closing day. A deed that sits in a briefcase over a weekend leaves a gap during which a new judgment or lien could attach ahead of it.

Options, leases longer than three years and first-refusal rights fall under the same rule. If your Kinston-area property has any such document, ask for a title search that looks for them before a closing date is set.

Property tax and the sale

The Lenoir County Tax Department shares the building at 101 North Queen Street and answers at 252-527-7174. It lists, appraises and bills property, and it maintains the records that follow transfers. Real estate sits on a permanent listing system, so owners file only when something about the property changes. Mobile homes, boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles must be listed in January or draw a 10 percent late penalty.

September 1 is the due date, and January 6 starts a 2 percent charge followed by monthly interest of three-fourths of one percent. Under G.S. 105-355 the tax lien dates from the listing date, which keeps old balances on the parcel. Ask the tax office for a payoff number and have the attorney pay it out of proceeds at settlement.

What to confirm before selling

Begin with the index itself. Ask the Register of Deeds what appears under your surname and under the seller before you, then follow up on any loan, easement or plat you did not expect.

  • Names on the latest recorded deed, including heirs if a prior owner has died.
  • A recorded release for every paid-off loan.
  • Any unpaid county bill or present-use deferral.
  • Whether you will file by paper or sign up for e-recording.
  • Excise tax and filing charges, so your net number is realistic.

For an inherited house, call the clerk of superior court about the estate steps before anyone signs, and order a certified death certificate from the Register of Deeds, which keeps those records.

Packing the envelope for a mailed deed

Some sellers in outlying parts of the county mail the deed rather than driving to Kinston. If you do, address it to PO Box 3289 and include the notarized original, a check for the page fee and the excise tax, and a note with a phone number in case the deputy has a question. A deed that comes back for a formatting problem costs you days, and the nonstandard paper fee of $25 applies if the pages do not meet state layout rules.

Electronic filing avoids most of this. Your attorney or title company submits the file, the office reviews it, and the recorded copy returns the same way.

Lenoir County market context

The county seat is Kinston, with a population of 55,837 and 27,402 housing units. Owners live in 59.2 percent of homes, and the typical owner-held home is worth $120,500. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025. With values near $120,500, a fixed recording fee takes a bigger bite out of a modest sale, so figure your net with it in mind.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A cash sale at the Kinston counter

A cash buyer can shorten the path to closing, but the recording steps are the same as for any other sale. The deed is still signed before a notary, the seller's excise tax is still paid, and the file still goes to 101 North Queen Street by hand, by mail or electronically. What a cash sale removes is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which often cause the delays.

If liens or back taxes sit on the house, the payoff letters are what you need to gather. A release of a paid-off mortgage costs nothing to record, so the cost of clearing the title is mostly the time it takes the lender to send the paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

What are the office hours at the Lenoir County Register of Deeds?

The doors are open Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 101 North Queen Street. The phone is 252-559-6420, and the mailing address is PO Box 3289, Kinston, NC 28502.

Is e-recording available through Lenoir County?

Yes. To enroll, call Simplifile at (801) 223-1046. Your closing attorney may already use it, so ask before you sign up.

Who owes the excise tax on a Lenoir County deed?

You do, as the seller. It is $1 for each $500 of value, a partial block counts as a whole one, and it is paid before the deed is recorded. The attorney typically deducts it at settlement.

Do I pay to record a mortgage release in Lenoir County?

No. G.S. 161-10 makes a release of a mortgage or deed of trust free to record. After payoff, ask your lender to send it to the Kinston office.

How do I learn what property tax is due on a Lenoir County house?

Call the tax department at 252-527-7174. Bills are due September 1 and interest starts January 6, and your attorney can pay what is owed from the sale proceeds.

Office location and hours

The Lincoln County Register of Deeds is at 206 Gamble Drive, 2nd Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092. The phone is (704) 736-1744, the fax is (704) 736-8830, and email goes to register@lincolncountync.gov.

The office is open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday, except county holidays. Real estate recordings and notary oaths stop at 4:30pm every day, so a deed that arrives at 4:45pm waits for the next business day. If you are driving in from Denver or Maiden on a closing day, plan to arrive well before that cutoff.

Payment is by cash, certified or business check, money order, or debit and credit card. Personal checks are not taken, and cards are not accepted for a recording that contains excise tax. That covers most deed filings, since most sales carry that tax.

Records the office holds

The office holds real estate records back to 1769, birth and death records from 1913, and marriage records from 1868. Real estate records and the birth, death and marriage indexes are also searchable online.

For a seller, the useful pieces are the grantor and grantee indexes, recorded deeds of trust, plats and maps, powers of attorney and assumed names. The office also keeps military records and notary public records. Since January 1, 2022 it no longer issues birth certificates for people born outside Lincoln County, so heirs closing out an estate should request those certificates from the county of birth.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust recorded against the parcel.
  • Plats and maps that show boundaries and lot numbers.
  • Powers of attorney used by a signer who is not present.
  • Death records for owners who have died.

Deed formatting rules

A paper deed must follow the state formatting standards in G.S. 161-14, which the office posts on its site. An instrument that misses them is still recorded, but the register collects a $25 fee for a nonstandard document.

Paper formatting standards for recorded instruments
Page elementStandard
Sheet size8 1/2 x 11 or 8 1/2 x 14
Top margin, first pageAt least 3 inches
Other margins, first pageAt least 1/2 inch on three sides
Margins, later pagesAt least 1/2 inch on all sides
Ink and paperBlack on white
Smallest typeNo smaller than 9 points
Sides printedFront only
Instrument typeNamed at the head of page one, under the margin

Pen is allowed for filling blanks or making corrections. If the only defect is print smaller than 9 points, the register may waive the $25 charge when the page is still legible, but the office advises 9 point type to avoid rejection. The standards cover instruments in general, deeds of trust and mortgages, UCC filings, Torrens registration and master forms.

Recording fees and excise tax

State law fixes the fees. G.S. 161-10 sets a base of $26 for an ordinary instrument of up to 15 pages and $64 for a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages, with $4 for every page past those limits. Bundling a second instrument into the same document adds $10. Lenders pay nothing when they record a cancellation.

The excise tax is separate. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the rate is $1 per $500 of the price or value, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the seller must deliver it to the register ahead of recording.

Because card payments are barred for recordings with excise tax, the closing attorney usually brings a firm or trust account check.

How recording protects a seller

Recording fixes the order of claims. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or sales contract has no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until the register of deeds in the land's county has it on file, and the timing of that filing sets who comes first.

Two practical points follow for a Lincoln County seller. First, confirm that old mortgages show a recorded cancellation before closing, since a lender's payoff letter alone does not clear the index. Second, options, long leases and first-refusal rights are governed by that statute too, so have the closing attorney look for them.

Property taxes are ordinarily prorated at closing by the closing attorney, so ask to see the proration on the settlement statement.

Lincoln County market context

Lincoln County has 98,654 residents, up 13.7 percent since 2020, and 41,865 housing units. Owners occupy 78.9 percent of homes, and the typical home is worth $321,000. With 785 building permits in 2025, new construction competes with resales. Fire district rates differ across the county, including Alexis, Crouse, Denver, East Lincoln, High Shoals and North Brook, so read the tax rate sheet before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lincoln County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to bring to the Lincolnton counter

Bring the signed, notarized deed, the excise tax, the page fee and a plan for the receipt. If a lender is paying off a loan, line up the cancellation so the old deed of trust comes off the index promptly.

  • A deed that meets the margin and type size standards, with the instrument type printed at the top.
  • Payment in an accepted form, remembering that cards are not taken when excise tax is due.
  • Arrival before 4:30pm, the daily cutoff for real estate recordings.
  • The full list of owners, spouses and heirs who must sign.
  • A look at the tax rate sheet: the county rate is 0.499 per $100 for 2026/2027, and the City of Lincolnton adds 0.5000 for a total of 0.9990.

Tax matters live in a different office. Collections are handled by the Lincoln County Tax Department, and the 2027 revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, so ask that department about current-year balances.

A cash sale and the recording step

Selling for cash does not change what the register needs. The deed still has to be signed, notarized and formatted correctly, the excise tax still has to be paid, and the closing attorney still delivers it before 4:30pm. What a cash sale can remove is the wait for a lender, which helps if the house has liens, tenants or repairs you would rather not tackle.

If a prior loan is paid off at closing, the cancellation recorded afterward is what clears the index. Ask the attorney to confirm it has been recorded, and keep a copy with your closing papers.

A rough order for closing day in Lincolnton: the attorney reviews the deed against the formatting table, you sign before a notary, the buyer funds, and the attorney brings the deed and a firm or trust account check for the excise tax and page fees to Gamble Drive. After recording, the old lender's cancellation follows, and recording it costs nothing.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Lincoln County Register of Deeds stop recording?

Real estate recordings and notary oaths stop at 4:30pm every day, even though the office stays open until 5:00pm. Arrive before 4:30pm on closing day.

Can I pay the Lincoln County recording fee with a credit card?

A card works for most services but not for a recording that contains excise tax. Use cash, a certified or business check, or a money order, and do not bring a personal check.

How far back do Lincoln County real estate records go?

Real estate records go back to 1769, and the same years are searchable online. Birth and death indexes start in 1913 and marriage indexes in 1868.

What happens if my deed is not formatted correctly in Lincoln County?

The register will still record it, but it collects a $25 nonstandard document fee. Black ink on white paper, correct margins and 9 point type avoid the charge.

Where do I get my Lincoln County property tax balance before I sell?

Call the Lincoln County Tax Department or use its online payment page. Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5, and the closing attorney normally prorates the current year.

Where Macon County deeds are filed

Deeds are recorded at the Macon County Register of Deeds in Franklin. County government works from 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734, and the switchboard at (828) 349-2000 can connect you to the office.

Call ahead for the recording hours and the same-day cutoff before you plan a closing around them.

The register is elected by county voters for a two-year term under G.S. 161-1. Recording follows statewide rules, so a Macon County deed uses the same format, fee and tax rules as a deed filed in any other North Carolina county.

Recording fees and excise tax

Fees come from G.S. 161-10, and the excise tax comes from G.S. 105-228.30. The register collects both before a deed is recorded.

  • Ordinary instruments: a $26 base for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page past that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: a $64 base for up to 35 pages, again $4 for each extra page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust: no fee.
  • A second instrument in the same document: $10.
  • Excise tax: $1 per $500 of value, rounded up for any partial block.

The seller is the transferor and owes the excise tax. The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to state revenue officials monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Closing attorneys in Franklin normally deduct the tax from the seller's proceeds and deliver it with the deed.

Why filing order matters

Filing sets priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from deeds, sale contracts, options and leases over three years until they are registered where the land lies, and whoever registers first comes first.

A parcel that has changed hands through several families can carry old rights of way or boundary agreements. Your closing attorney should search the Macon County index under every prior owner. Pick up the parcel map from Land Records as well, so the new deed's legal description lines up with the tax parcel.

Filing a deed does not itself clear the tax bill. The county assesses property as of January 1, so ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and plan the proration with your closing attorney.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Macon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The Land Records (Mapping) office

The Land Records office, also called the Mapping Office, is on the main level of the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in downtown Franklin. It is the place to get property cards, parcel maps and county maps, and it has public terminals for document searches, property searches, collection information and assessment data.

The tax office website links an address change form, property tax forms and a land records search, so many owners can pull a map or a parcel record before they visit. A seller preparing a listing can print the parcel map to check the lot lines against the deed.

The Tax Department itself sits in the annex at 5 West Main Street. It posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the county scroll.

Tax dates after a sale

The county tax calendar drives most of what follows a sale. The Macon County Tax Department lists these dates.

Macon County tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; personal property ownership and place of taxation are set as of this date
January 1 to 31Listing period for personal property, except tagged motor vehicles, and for exemption and exclusion filing
January 5Last day to pay property taxes without interest
January 6Interest begins
AprilReview board hears appeals
April 15Last date to file listings with a prior approved extension
AugustCurrent-year tax bills processed and mailed

Appeals must be received or postmarked by the day the review board adjourns each April. A 2027 reappraisal is coming, and the tax office runs an online appeal portal, so use it after new values are mailed.

Paying a bill and avoiding scams

Bill payment runs on a newer platform, so owners need to register their accounts again and re-enroll in paperless billing. The portal is open around the clock and includes AutoPay, text alerts with pay-by-text, and an automated pay-by-phone line. Collections answers at (828) 349-2142.

The tax office also warns about lookalike government scams. The Macon County Tax Office does not contact taxpayers asking to come to their homes to collect a debt. If a caller does, share no personal information and hang up at once. Sellers who owe back taxes are a likely target, so route any demand through the official office and your closing attorney.

Businesses must list business personal property each January under G.S. 105-308, which covers furniture, fixtures, machinery and similar equipment. A rental owner who keeps furnishings in an income-producing unit should ask the Personal Property desk at (828) 349-2144 whether those items need listing.

Macon County at a glance

Macon County includes Franklin, Highlands and Nantahala, and has 39,232 residents, up 6.0 percent from 2020. It has 27,700 housing units but only 18,406 households, and owners occupy 77.6 percent of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $251,900. A buyer planning a second home or a rental will want to see the recorded deed and any restrictions on file with the register.

If the owner has died

Call the clerk of superior court before the register of deeds. The Estates and Special Proceedings line is (828) 349-7204, and that office can explain whether a small estate affidavit fits or whether the estate needs a personal representative.

For intestate estates, G.S. 28A-25-1 permits an affidavit filed with the clerk in the county of domicile when personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, any time after 30 days from death. A surviving spouse who is the only heir may reach a limit up to $30,000 after the spousal allowance. The affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

When someone has authority to sign, the deed then goes to the Register of Deeds. Bring the certified death record if the register or the title company asks for it.

Getting a Macon County deed recorded, step by step

  1. Confirm who must sign, including spouses and any heirs, and get the deed notarized.
  2. Ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and settle the proration with your closing attorney.
  3. Match the legal description to the parcel map from Land Records.
  4. Pay the page fee and the excise tax, normally deducted from the seller's proceeds by the closing attorney.
  5. Have a lender's satisfaction recorded for any old mortgage or deed of trust, which carries no fee.
  6. Keep the recorded copy with your closing papers.

A cash sale follows the same steps. What it skips is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so liens, back taxes and estate paperwork are the items to line up first.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Macon County Register of Deeds?

The office is part of Macon County government in Franklin, whose main address is 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734. Call (828) 349-2000 and ask for the Register of Deeds to confirm hours.

What do Macon County deed filings cost?

An ordinary instrument starts at $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 per page after that, and the excise tax adds $1 per $500 of value. The office collects both before it records the deed.

Does Macon County have a separate tax scroll for Highlands?

Yes. The Macon County Tax Department posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the main county scroll. Ask the tax office which scroll applies to your parcel.

When do Macon County property taxes become late?

January 5 is the last day to pay clear of interest, which starts January 6. Current-year bills are processed and mailed in August.

Where can I get a parcel map in Macon County?

Visit the Land Records office in the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in Franklin, or use the land records search linked from the tax office page. Property cards, parcel maps and county maps are available there.

What the Madison County Register of Deeds does

The office files your signed deed in the county's permanent index. That filing is the moment the transfer becomes visible to everyone else. The phone number is 828-649-3131.

The register checks the document, collects the fixed state fees and the seller's stamp tax, and notes the time of filing. Valuation and yearly billing happen down the road at Tax Administration in Marshall, which is open weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25.

Call the register before you travel and ask about current counter hours, or let your closing attorney handle the office from a distance. Plan a second call to Tax Administration too. A deed that is filed cleanly but never reaches the tax roll keeps sending the old owner a bill.

Why filing time matters

North Carolina ranks competing claims by when each was registered. Under G.S. 47-18, deeds, options, leases running beyond three years and rights of first refusal gain force against lien creditors and paying purchasers only once registered in the county where the land sits.

For a Madison County parcel, the Madison County office is the only one that counts, wherever the seller lives. Excise tax on a parcel spanning two counties is paid where more of the value lies.

  • A buyer whose deed waits unfiled can lose out to a creditor who files first.
  • A new lender's deed of trust filed late may rank behind liens that were never meant to come first.
  • A deed filed in a neighboring county leaves the Madison County record unchanged.

That is why closings end with the deed and the loan documents going in on the same day, in the order the attorney planned.

Recording fees at the Madison County counter

One statute, G.S. 161-10, sets the fees for every North Carolina county, so Madison County has no schedule of its own. A plain deed costs $26.00 up to 15 pages, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 up to 35 pages.

Madison County recording charges under G.S. 161-10
Document or serviceCharge
General instrument, up to 15 pages$26.00
General instrument, each extra page$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, up to 35 pages$64.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, each extra page$4.00
Plat, each sheet$21.00
Certified copy, page one$5.00
Certified copy, later pages$2.00 each
Release or cancellation of a mortgageFree

Two surcharges can apply: $25.00 for a document in nonstandard format and $10.00 for every extra instrument bundled into one filing. Payment is due before filing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Madison County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Does a land split need a recorded plat first?

Usually yes, when the split counts as a subdivision. The county's subdivision ordinance, revised June 28, 2022, bars the sale or transfer of any lot on a required subdivision plat until the final plat is recorded by the Register of Deeds.

The register is told not to file a subdivision plat that has not been approved under the ordinance. A building permit or septic permit also has to wait until the Planning Board approves the final plat and the register records it. Buyers of a back lot get caught here, since a lender will not close on a parcel that cannot be permitted.

  • Combining or recombining recorded lots without adding lots is carved out, as long as the results meet county standards.
  • A family subdivision has its own approval, and the final plat carries a title block that says so.
  • Plats must comply with G.S. 47-30 to be suitable for recording.

An owner may sign contracts to sell by reference to an approved preliminary plat before the final plat exists, though the lot itself cannot transfer until that plat is recorded. If you plan to carve a lot off a Madison County tract, ask the county's subdivision administrator whether your split needs a plat, and settle it before you list.

Who pays the deed stamp tax

The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 sets a levy of $1.00 per $500 of price, counting any fraction of $500 as a full unit, on whoever transfers the land. The register takes the money before the deed is entered.

Half stays with the county. Monthly remittances carry the other half to the Department of Revenue, less a 2 percent county share of it.

The exact figure appears on your settlement statement, next to the loan payoff and any tax balance. A cash purchase works the same way.

Email alerts when a document is filed

The register has offered an email notice whenever a recorded document matches a name an owner signed up to watch. Sign-up asks for your name, your email and the names to monitor, followed by a confirmation email that may land in a junk folder.

If you own land you rarely visit, or you are settling an estate, an alert like this can catch a forged deed or a stray lien the day it reaches the index. Call 828-649-3131 to confirm the service is running.

Electronic filing is a separate question for the same counter. Your closing attorney knows which vendors the office accepts.

After the sale: the two Marshall offices

Filing the deed hands the assessor the new owner. That office tracks ownership changes and keeps the property maps.

  • After recording, call Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 and confirm the owner name.
  • Have the year's September 1 bill paid or credited at closing so the lien does not follow the house.
  • Where a circuit breaker deferral exists, give the tax office 10 days to prepare deferred bills.
  • Take the parcel number from the tax bill and put it on the deed paperwork.

The county counted 11,874 housing units in 2025, with 77.5 percent owner-occupied across 2020 to 2024. Ordinary sales and family transfers make up most of what the register sees.

What to have ready before closing

A title agent or attorney files the paperwork. Gather these items so nothing stalls.

  • The old deed, so names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff statements for each deed of trust on the parcel. Lenders then file cancellations, and those carry no fee.
  • The parcel number, plus a survey if the acreage is uncertain.
  • For an inherited house, estate paperwork. Small estate affidavits go to the superior court clerk, and G.S. 28A-25-1 sets the dollar limits.

A cash buyer can take a house with a tangled history, yet every link in the chain still has to be recorded properly. Running the title early gives you time to chase down a missing release before the closing date.

If the closing is by mail or through a remote attorney, ask who carries the deed to the office and who confirms the recording afterward. Keep the book and page reference once the office gives it to you, because the next buyer's title search will start from it.

Frequently asked questions

What number reaches the Madison County Register of Deeds?

Call 828-649-3131. Ask about counter hours and recording options before you send anything.

What does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?

A deed of 15 pages or fewer costs $26.00, then $4.00 per added page. Mortgages and deeds of trust cost $64.00 through page 35. State law fixes both amounts.

Who pays the Madison County excise tax?

The seller pays, at $1.00 per $500 of price, and the register collects it before recording.

Does Madison County charge to file a mortgage release?

No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for filing a satisfaction or cancellation.

After recording, who updates the tax bill owner?

The assessor tracks ownership changes, so confirm the new name with Tax Administration and settle the September 1 bill at closing.

What the Williamston office handles

The Register of Deeds sits on the ground-level floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston. Land records there start in 1771. Easements, agreements, assignments, releases, plats, deeds and deeds of trust are all recorded at this counter, with an index for each kind and a separate index for plats.

Uniform commercial code statements join the real estate books too, a practice dating to July 1, 2001. The office also files military discharge papers (DD-214), assumed business name, partnership and incorporation instruments, and gives oaths to notaries.

A title searcher will find whatever sits in these books, so look first. If something odd turns up, such as an easement or an unreleased lien, ask the office about it before you list.

Searching Martin County deeds online

Deeds are searchable at martinrod.org, with records back to 1771. A separate online service takes vital record orders.

If you inherited the house or have owned it for decades, an hour in the index is time well spent.

  • Search under your name and under the previous owner's name.
  • Match the legal description on the latest deed to the tax record.
  • Flag any old deed of trust that has no release recorded behind it.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

Recording charges

The county's fee sheet follows the statewide schedule, and amounts can change. Call about the total before you mail a payment, and write money orders to Martin County Register of Deeds.

Deed formatting rules

Any paper signed on or after July 1, 2002 must follow the layout rules in G.S. 161-10, or the office tacks $25.00 onto the recording charge.

  • Letter or legal paper, 8 1/2 inches wide.
  • A blank three-inch band across the top of page one and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black on white, type no smaller than 9 points, printed on one face.
  • The words naming the instrument type, printed above everything else on page one.

Hand-inked blanks and corrections are allowed, and exhibits follow the same rules. The signing date decides which standard applies, not the arrival date.

Who pays the excise tax

This one is the seller's. Martin County's sheet words the rate as $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price; the statute words it as $1.00 per $500, with a partial block rounded up.

Payment comes at filing. The money is divided between the county general fund and the state, and the county can keep 2 percent of the state's share.

Your settlement statement shows the exact dollars in the seller's column. Staff hold the deed until the tax is in.

Why filing order matters on a Williamston sale

A deed, an option, a lease longer than three years or a right of first refusal protects its holder against lien creditors and paying purchasers only after it is registered (G.S. 47-18). For land in this county, registration happens in Williamston no matter where the owner lives.

Suppose a creditor files a judgment an hour before your buyer's deed goes in. The buyer can end up second in line. Attorneys head this off by filing the moment funds are confirmed.

  • Mail or deliver the signed deed with any lender release in a single packet.
  • Include a check covering fee and tax.
  • Get the book and page reference after recording.

Steps from signed deed to recorded deed

Nearly every Martin County sale moves along this short path, cash sales included.

  • The attorney or title company checks the old deed, the legal description and the payoff letters for any loan on the house.
  • The seller signs in front of a notary.
  • The packet, with a check for the fee and the tax, goes to Williamston. Page count sets the fee, so ask the office to total it when a deed runs long.
  • Staff stamp the time, index the deed and hand back the book and page reference.
  • Any lender release follows. It costs nothing to record, but someone has to make sure the lender actually sends it.

With no lender underwriting in the way, a cash sale often leaves the records as the one thing to clear. If an old deed of trust shows up with no release after it, start that request with the lender right away, since the lender's response time sets the pace.

Vital records for heirs

The same counter issues marriage licenses and certified vital records, and heirs selling an inherited house often need the latter. A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage record costs $10.00, and the county limits who may request one: the person named, close family members, an authorized agent or attorney, or anyone who can prove a legal need tied to a personal or property right.

An executor or heir usually brings proof of the relationship or a document showing legal authority. Uncertified copies are open to the public at $0.25 a page.

Tax bills, due dates and interest

Recording a deed does not change the tax bill. Real and personal property bills are mailed in July or August and fall due September 1. You can pay with no interest through January 5. When that day lands on a weekend or holiday, the cutoff slides to the next business day.

On January 6 a 2 percent penalty kicks in, and three-fourths of one percent more is added each month afterward. Between March 1 and June 30 the collector must run unpaid real estate tax in the local newspaper, and the delinquent owner is charged for the notice.

Visit the collector at 305 East Main Street, Room 125 (8 AM to 5 PM on weekdays) or phone 252-789-4360. A written payoff figure lets the attorney deduct the bill from your proceeds at the table.

Housing in Martin County

Population was about 21,601 in mid-2025, a 2.0 percent drop from April 2020, spread across 11,071 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied rate was 66.8 percent and the median home value $109,700.

With values this modest, deferred repairs can make a traditional lender balk. A cash buyer will take the house in its present state, repairs untouched, and close as soon as title is clear. Have your attorney run the land records early so any uncancelled deed of trust gets released before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Martin County register of deeds?

In the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, on the first floor. The county prints (252) 789-4320 for record questions.

How far back do Martin County land records go?

To 1771. The index of recorded instruments starts that year, and deeds are searchable at martinrod.org.

What is the Martin County fee for a deed of trust?

$64 through page 35, plus $4 per additional page or fraction. A plain deed costs $26 through page 15.

Does Martin County charge for recording a mortgage satisfaction?

No. Cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction all carry no fee.

Who pays Martin County's deed excise tax?

The seller, at $2.00 per $1000 of price, collected as the deed is filed.

Office address and hours

The McDowell County registrar is at 35 West Fort Street in Marion. Call 828-652-4727. Weekday hours are 8:30am to 5:00pm. Online services live at McDowellDeeds.com.

Staff record, index and store real estate and business paper. Marriage licenses, notary oaths, military discharge records and certified birth and death copies come through the same door. For a seller, the land side is what counts: the goal is a public record that is complete, accurate and safe.

Can a McDowell County deed be filed electronically?

Filing fees

G.S. 161-10 governs, and the county adds nothing of its own. Typical line items:

  • Ordinary deed: a $26.00 base for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page.
  • Mortgage or deed of trust: a $64.00 base for 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page.

Who pays the stamp tax?

Sellers carry this tax in McDowell County. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the rate is one dollar for each $500 of price, and a leftover amount under $500 is rounded up. The registrar will not record until it is paid.

The county's general fund keeps one share. The state gets the other share each month, minus refunds and the county's allowance.

Find the figure in the seller column of the closing statement, below the loan payoff line.

Parcel maps and the assessor after recording

GIS mapping in the assessor's office processes deed transfers and updates the maps, and it also serves as plat review officer. Deed transfers and parcel maps are handled by the same people, so check the map once your deed is recorded.

Find the assessor at 60 E. Court Street on the same weekday schedule. Real property, mapping and land records each have their own extension. A 2027 real property reappraisal is coming, and the new values will fall on whoever owns the house then.

  • Ask mapping whether your parcel shows the shape and acreage you expect.
  • Ask real property staff what the reappraisal could do to your assessment.
  • A link on the assessor's page lets you report storm damage.

Tax Collections is in the same County Services Building and keeps the same 8:30am to 5:00pm hours. Email taxcollections@mcdowellnc.gov or call (828) 652-0701 for a payoff on the current bill. With both offices under one roof, you can settle the value question and the payoff question in a single trip.

Property tax relief that affects a buyer

Find out early if your parcel sits in a relief program, because several end or come due when the house transfers. Applications go to 60 East Court Street between January 1 and May 31, with all paperwork back by June 1. No one may combine programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the home and one acre lose the greater of $25,000 or half of their assessed value. No lien is created. The owner must be 65 by January 1 or totally disabled. Phone the office for the yearly income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 comes off the assessed value after one application. Age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: you must have owned and lived in the home five years and reapply each June 1. Three years of deferred tax sit as a lien that comes due on a death, a transfer or a move.
  • Present-use value: for farm, forest or horticultural land, requested in January. Forest land needs a sound management plan.

Tax foreclosure auctions

When the county sues over unpaid tax under G.S. 105-374, the sale itself happens at the courthouse, 21 S. Main St. in Marion. Whoever bids highest must give the commissioner $1,000.00 in cash right away.

Ten days follow for upset bids, filed with the clerk. Any new bid must exceed the last by 5 percent, and by at least $750.00. Each raised bid restarts the ten-day clock. The clerk's number is (828) 655-4100.

  • Upcoming sales are posted through the county's foreclosure page.
  • Look up map, assessed value, acreage and deed reference in the GIS by parcel number.
  • Wells and septic are left for the bidder to research.

An owner who has fallen behind can skip the auction by selling first. Ask the tax collector for a payoff number while no sale date is set.

Why filing order matters

Priority goes to whoever registers first. G.S. 47-18 says a deed does nothing against lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is filed where the land sits, and for McDowell land that means Marion.

For that reason attorneys file the deed and the buyer's loan papers as a set. They also pursue stale releases, which cost only the time a lender takes to respond. When the title search shows a lien that was never cancelled, ask the attorney to request the release at once.

What to bring to a McDowell County closing

Your attorney does the filing, but a few items on your side save days.

  • Your vesting deed, so the legal description and owner names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff letters for every loan secured by the house, with a note on which lender will file the release.
  • The parcel number from your tax bill, for checking the GIS map after recording.
  • The assessor's reply on any relief program or deferred circuit breaker tax.
  • For an inherited house, estate papers that show who has authority to sign.

Once the deed is filed, confirm the new owner's name with the assessor and the collector, so the following bill reaches the right person. A call to the registrar at 828-652-4727 confirms the filing date and gives you the reference you need for your records.

Inherited houses, probate sales and homes that need work often lead owners to ask for cash offers. That kind of buyer can close the day the deed is ready to file.

Whichever route you choose, a clean record makes the closing quick. Pull your deed from McDowellDeeds.com, confirm every old loan has a recorded release, and ask mapping to verify the parcel before a buyer's surveyor does.

Frequently asked questions

What days is the McDowell County registrar open?

Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 35 West Fort Street. The number is 828-652-4727.

Which vendors file McDowell County deeds electronically?

Simplifile, EDL (Electronic Document Logistics) and CSC (Corporation Service Company). The county accepts any document this way.

How much does it cost to file a 12-page deed in McDowell County?

The seller, at $1.00 per $500 of price, paid at the counter before filing.

What is the minimum upset bid at a McDowell County tax sale?

Five percent over the last bid, with a floor of $750.00 more. The clerk's office takes it, and the ten-day clock starts over.

What the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds does

This is the county's public archive for land and business filings. Staff accept documents for registration, index them and store them, so anyone can trace who owns a Charlotte lot or a Davidson farmhouse.

On the real estate side the office handles conveyances, deeds of trust, mortgages, powers of attorney, assumed business names, separation agreements and plats. The same counter issues marriage licenses, swears in notaries, records military discharge papers and holds vital records.

The office website posts holiday closings, so check it before planning a trip downtown.

Searching Mecklenburg land records

Two databases cover the full span. The modern one holds real estate documents from March 1990 to the present. The historic one holds land records and images from 1763 through February 1990. Physical records can also be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

Title work on an old parcel often crosses the 1990 line: a recent deed of trust sits in the modern index, while the older chain of conveyances sits in the historic one. If you inherited the house, search under the family name and the previous owner's name to see what is still of record, such as a mortgage that was never released.

Why recording time matters

Registration decides who stands first. G.S. 47-18 provides that a conveyance does not defeat lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies, and rank follows the order of filing.

In practice, a creditor's claim could still beat your buyer until the new deed is indexed. Ask your closing attorney when the package will be submitted, and whether the buyer's deed of trust is going in right behind your deed. Keep the recording confirmation after closing. If a question about the date ever comes up, that proof settles it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mecklenburg County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

Mecklenburg posts a Uniform Fee Schedule that follows G.S. 161-10. The amounts sellers meet most often are below, and every added page beyond the allowance costs $4.

Fees most often paid on a Mecklenburg sale
ServicePosted amount
Deed and other general instruments$26 for 15 pages
Loan security instrument$64 for 35 pages
Document outside format rules$25 extra
Mortgage satisfactionFree

Other charges: a certified copy is $5 for page one and $2 for the rest. Plain copies are 25 cents a page at the counter or $1 by mail. A plat is $21 a sheet, and each extra instrument in one filing is $10. Party names past twenty cost $2 each in index fees.

Format rules for a filing

G.S. 161-14(b) sets the layout. A document that misses it is still accepted, for the $25 surcharge. The county's checklist has five points.

  • Paper: 8.5 inches wide, 11 or 14 inches tall.
  • Margins: three open inches above the text on sheet one, a quarter inch elsewhere.
  • Type: black on white, nine points or larger. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Sides: print on one side only.
  • Heading: a label naming the kind of instrument on the first sheet.

If you drafted a document yourself, run it against this list before you submit it.

The deed tax and who covers it

Sellers carry this cost. G.S. 105-228.30 sets one dollar for each $500 of price, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the office collects it before it records the deed.

The county keeps half and the state receives the other half. Your settlement statement shows the dollar figure for your sale price.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mecklenburg County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to check in the records before listing

Three places answer three different questions. The Register of Deeds shows what is recorded against the parcel. The county's property record card shows how Tax Administration describes the house. The Tax Collector shows what is owed.

  • Recorded deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction. A loan you paid off can still look open if the lender never filed its release.
  • The name on the latest deed. On an inherited property, the last recorded owner is often the person who died.
  • The property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov, which lists bedrooms, bathrooms and other features the county uses to value the house.
  • The county's no-cost alert service, so a later filing under your name reaches you.

A closing attorney will run a full title search regardless. A light version first tells you whether the sale will be quick or whether an old lien, a missing release or an unprobated estate needs to be cleared up.

From signed deed to public record

Four steps carry a deed from signature to the index. The state treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, so payment is due when you file.

  • Match the grantor's name and legal description to the prior deed.
  • Have the seller's side cover the excise tax.
  • Add the page-count fee and any surcharge.
  • Hand in the original and keep proof that it was recorded.

A lender's satisfaction after payoff is recorded free and shows up in the index afterward.

Disabled veteran relief and other offices

Military discharge papers are recorded at this office. A property tax break for a disabled veteran is a separate matter: the applicant completes Form NCDVA-9 with a veteran service officer and files with the county assessor. The exclusion covers $45,000 of value and has no age or income cutoff.

The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years under G.S. 161-1. Questions about deed wording or title for a specific house belong with a closing attorney. Value and exemption questions go to Tax Administration.

For context on the market you are selling into: 1,233,383 residents in mid 2025, a median owner value of $406,800 for 2020 to 2024, and 55.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paying at the counter and guarding your title

The counter takes cash, Mastercard, Visa and Discover, checks, money orders and approved escrow accounts. A check needs a printed name and address and a phone number, made out to the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds. Starter and counter checks are turned away, and a bounced check may cost $35.

The office runs a no-cost Property Fraud Alert that notifies you when any document under your name reaches the records, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses. Anyone buying on a contract for deed should know that Chapter 47H obliges the seller to record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days.

If you own a Mecklenburg house burdened by back taxes, a title snag or a difficult tenant, a cash buyer can set a closing date that works, with a closing attorney handling the recording.

Frequently asked questions

What does Mecklenburg County charge to file a deed?

$26 covers the first fifteen pages, plus $4 for each page past that. A loan instrument costs $64 for thirty-five pages. Documents outside the format rules carry a $25 surcharge.

Which party pays the deed stamp tax in a Mecklenburg sale?

The seller owes it. The rate is one dollar per $500 of price, rounded up for a partial block, and it is due at the counter.

Does recording a mortgage satisfaction cost anything?

No. The fee schedule lists satisfaction instruments as free, so your only task is confirming that your lender files one after payoff.

Can I look up Mecklenburg land records on my own?

Yes. A modern online database covers documents from March 1990 forward, a historic index covers 1763 through February 1990, and records can be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

What happens to a deed that breaks the format rules?

It is still recorded, but you pay $25 on top of the usual fees. Margins, tiny type and two-sided pages cause most of those cases.

Finding the Mitchell County recording counter

The office is Suite 4 at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Bakersville, NC 28705. It is open on weekdays except holidays and records from 8:00 until 4:30. Call 828.688.2139. Extension 1401 handles fee and recording questions, and extension 1402 reaches the register's line. The fax number is 828-688-3666.

Marriage licenses are written until 4:00 and cost $60, payable by check, cash or money order. Recording itself can be paid in cash, by card, check or money order.

Staff act only as a recording office, and state law bars the register and employees from practicing law. Any question about what a deed should say goes to an attorney.

Searching the online records

At mitchelldeeds.com you will find real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. Older material, from 1861 through 1993, sits in the Index Book Viewer under the search menu. The county's services list also covers vital records, an online vital request, document recording standards, index standards and a page for redacting personal information.

The 1994 line matters if your family has held land for generations. A deed of trust from the early nineties, a right-of-way, or a division of a family tract may appear only in the older books.

  • Search the current index under your name and the prior owner's name.
  • Open the Index Book Viewer when the chain of title reaches back before 1994.
  • Write down every deed of trust you find and confirm each has a recorded satisfaction.

Your closing attorney still performs the formal title search. A pass of your own simply tells you whether surprises are likely.

Mitchell County housing snapshot

Mitchell County is small and settled: 15,062 residents and 8,785 housing units as of July 1, 2025, with 6,587 households in the survey ending 2024. Median rent is $813, owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,275 a month in costs, and 90.1 percent of residents lived in the same home a year earlier. Builders pulled 44 permits in 2025.

For an inherited house, gather the death certificate, the prior deed and any recorded deeds of trust before you meet with a closing attorney.

Recording fees

The posted fee schedule cites G.S. 161-10 and took effect October 1, 2016. Amounts:

Mitchell County recording fees
Document or servicePosted amount
Deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, $4.00 each page after
Other instruments, such as a deed$26.00 for 15 pages, $4.00 each page after
Plat$21.00 a page, 18 by 24 inch sheets only
UCC filing$38.00 for 1 to 2 pages, $45.00 for 3 to 10
SatisfactionNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional

A UCC filing over ten pages is $45.00 plus $2.00 for every page past ten. If a figure matters for your closing, call 828-688-2139 extension 1401 before you send a check.

Electronic filing

Yes, the office accepts e-recording through Simplifile or CSC, the two vendors on its e-recording page.

Law firms and title companies commonly submit this way, so ask your closing attorney which route the firm uses. A paper document you file yourself, such as a corrective deed or a gift deed, can go to Suite 4 on any weekday.

Who pays the deed tax

The seller pays it in Bakersville when the deed is submitted. G.S. 105-228.30 sets the rate at one dollar per $500 of price, rounding a partial $500 up.

The county holds half and sends the state half, less refunds and a 2 percent county allowance on the state portion.

The tax depends on your actual deed price, so read the number off your settlement statement rather than estimating.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mitchell County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Vital records and marriage licenses

The office keeps birth, death and marriage records, current and historical, and offers an online vital request. Anyone can obtain a copy of a vital record, but state law restricts who may receive certified copies, so check the vital records page for the list.

A marriage license is $60 and is issued on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Call ahead for the requirements before you drive over.

Why recording order matters

G.S. 47-18 says unrecorded transfers and options give way to lien creditors and paying purchasers, and that rank follows the time of registration. Registration happens in the county where the land sits, so Mitchell parcels are registered in Bakersville.

Ask when the buyer's deed is expected to appear in the index. County voters choose the register every two years under G.S. 161-1.

Getting ready to record

Most of the work happens before anyone visits Suite 4.

  • Pull your current deed and confirm that the names and legal description are right.
  • List each loan against the house and ask each lender when it will file its satisfaction. Filing is free, but the lender has to send it.
  • Decide whether your attorney will submit electronically or whether you will bring paper to Bakersville.
  • Confirm the total with the office at extension 1401 if the document runs long, since extra pages add $4.00 each.

Once the deed is recorded, keep the stamped copy or the confirmation from the e-recording vendor. It is your proof of filing, and the next owner's title search will begin with it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Protecting against deed fraud

Sign up for the office's free Fraud Alert system, which warns you if someone tries to change records tied to your property. It helps most with vacant, rental and inherited houses.

  • Keep copies of every deed, release and satisfaction you receive.
  • Search your name in the index every so often.
  • Record inherited or gifted property promptly.

Anyone buying on an installment land contract should read Chapter 47H, which requires the seller to put the contract, or a short memorandum of it, on record within five business days.

Other county offices in a house sale

Three offices touch the same sale. The register records the deed. The Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle takes payment of the year's bill. The Tax Assessor at Suite 5, next door to the register, handles relief applications. Bills go to the January 1 owner of record in August, so the closing papers need to say who covers the year.

Property tax relief for a disabled veteran or an older owner is applied for through the assessor on Form AV-9, with Form NCDVA-9 added for the disabled veteran exclusion after a visit with a veteran service officer. Neither claim is filed with the Register of Deeds. The register's office handles related paper, such as recorded deeds and discharge records, but the relief decision is the assessor's. Ask that office which documents it wants before the next January listing period.

A cash buyer of an inherited Mitchell County house can close as-is, with the deed filed through a closing attorney at settlement.

Frequently asked questions

Which phone line reaches Mitchell County recording staff?

Call 828-688-2139 and use extension 1401 for fees and recording, or extension 1402 for the register's line. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville.

How old are the Mitchell County records I can search online?

The online index holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. The 1861 through 1993 material is in the Index Book Viewer on the search menu.

Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost money in Mitchell County?

No. Satisfactions carry no fee.

Can my attorney e-record a Mitchell County deed?

Yes, through Simplifile and CSC, the two vendors the office uses for e-recording.

Will the recording staff tell me what my deed should say?

No. The office acts as a recording office only, and state law keeps the register and staff from practicing law. Ask an attorney about wording, title or rights.

Selling in Montgomery County?

What the Montgomery County Register of Deeds handles

This office keeps the paper trail of land ownership in the county: deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats, releases and the index that ties them together. The county's department page calls it the legal custodian of real estate and vital records.

Staff also handle military discharge records (DD 214), assumed name and partnership filings, and UCC fixture filings. Residents come for marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, and newly commissioned notaries take their oath there.

A seller in Troy, Biscoe, Candor, Star or Mount Gilead meets this office at the very end of a sale. A buyer's title examiner searches its index before closing, and the new deed lands in its books afterward. A quick cash sale follows the same route as any other.

Local housing picture

Montgomery County is a small, rural county in the Uwharrie region, with an estimated 26,403 people in mid-2025 spread over 491.54 square miles of land, roughly 52 residents per square mile. Housing units number 15,439. Owners live in 75.0 percent of households, the typical home was valued at $161,700 for 2020 to 2024, and typical rent was $766. Builders took out 176 permits in 2025.

Sellers here include long-time owners, older owners and heirs, and each of them relies on a deed that was recorded correctly.

Who owes the excise tax at closing?

The seller. Under the statute, whoever transfers the property hands the tax to the county's land records office ahead of recording (G.S. 105-228.30).

The levy is $1.00 on each $500 block of value, and a partial block counts as a whole one. Half of every payment stays with the county and the other half goes to the State.

  • Your closing attorney normally carries the payment in with the deed.
  • If a parcel spans two counties, the county with more of its value collects.
  • Ask the attorney for the final amount before signing, since it tracks the value stated on the deed.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Montgomery County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

The county has no price list of its own. G.S. 161-10 sets a single schedule for every register of deeds, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment before filing.

  • An ordinary deed is priced by page count, with a flat charge for the opening pages and a smaller one for each sheet after those.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust costs more than a deed, with a longer first stretch of pages.
  • Plats are priced per sheet and certified copies per page.
  • Filing the lender's release after payoff is free.
  • A page that breaks the state formatting rules picks up its own add-on charge.

Read the statute for the exact dollar figures. When a payoff is part of your sale, the free release means the lender's cleanup step costs you nothing extra.

How the tax office uses what is recorded

The Tax Administrator keeps the ownership and parcel records that begin with recorded deeds, then lists, values and bills each property. The county tax department oversees about 30,000 parcels of real property.

Which office sends your bill depends on the address. The county collects its own tax plus the real estate tax for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead. Troy collects for itself. Lake Tillery, Badin Lake and Wadeville fire district charges ride along on the county bill.

  • The county was last revalued in 2020, with the next reappraisal scheduled for 2028.
  • Commissioners set the rate in June, and the county mails bills in the summer after that.
  • Bills fall due September 1 and are not past due until January 5.
  • The listing window runs from January 2 to January 31, and listing late costs a 10% penalty.
  • To collect unpaid tax the office can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, levy personal property, use debt setoff or foreclose on real estate.

The state tax lien reaches the parcel on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so request a payoff statement from the tax office or Troy before any fall or winter closing.

What if a signed deed is left unrecorded?

A buyer holding an unrecorded deed is exposed. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance, an option or a lease running past three years gives no protection against lien creditors, or buyers who paid value, until it is entered in the land records of the parcel's own county.

Registration order sets priority. If a creditor records a judgment before the deed is filed, the creditor may win. Families sometimes keep a signed deed in a drawer for years, and that habit is the surest way to create the problem.

The cure is quick. Carry the signed, notarized deed in along with the excise payment and filing fee, and keep the recording details the staff hand back.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Montgomery County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Preparing before you record

Most of the effort comes before anyone reaches the counter. Register of deeds staff in North Carolina record documents without drafting them or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares the deed.

  • Look up the parcel number and owner record on the county's real estate and GIS search so the deed's description matches the tax record.
  • Gather payoff letters for each mortgage or lien, and confirm each lender will file its release.
  • Find out whether the county or the Town of Troy collects the tax on your parcel.
  • Have the excise payment and the recording fee ready as separate amounts.
  • Keep the notarized original with the recording stamp once the deed is filed.

Call the Montgomery County Register of Deeds for current hours and ask how it accepts documents before you make the trip. If your attorney is filing for you, ask who will bring the paper in and who will confirm the recording afterward, so nothing sits on a desk over a weekend.

Other county offices that touch a home sale

The register of deeds is one stop among several. Each office below can come up during a sale.

Montgomery County offices and what they answer
OfficeTypical question
InspectionsUnpermitted work a buyer may spot
PlanningLot size and setbacks outside town limits
Environmental HealthWell and septic questions on rural lots
Public UtilitiesMoving the water account to the buyer
Tax DepartmentParcel records, values, bills and payoffs

The county also runs a program to enroll farmland in a voluntary agricultural district, and an enrolled parcel carries that status into the sale. Its website has a how-do-I menu with a real estate and GIS search, a permit link and an occupancy tax payment link. Starting there often saves a phone call.

Frequently asked questions

Which party owes the Montgomery County excise tax?

The seller owes it. The transferor pays the county office ahead of filing, at $1.00 per $500 block of value.

Where is the price list for recording in Montgomery County?

G.S. 161-10 is the one price list every North Carolina register of deeds follows. Pages drive the charge for a deed, a mortgage costs more, and a release after payoff is free.

Will the office draft my deed for me?

No. Staff file deeds but do not write them or offer legal advice. A closing attorney or other lawyer prepares the deed, and the office records it after it is signed and notarized.

When is a Montgomery County tax bill late?

September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the point where a bill is past due. Interest then starts at 2%, and each month from February adds another 3/4 of 1%.

Does the county collect tax on a house inside Troy?

Troy collects its own real estate tax. The county office handles the county bill plus the bills for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead, so a Troy owner can expect a town bill and a county bill.

Finding the Moore County land records office

Go to 26 Courthouse Square, Carthage, NC 28327. The office opens each weekday at 8 am and closes at 5 pm. Mail goes to Post Office Box 1210 in Carthage, and the phone line is 910-947-6370.

The county's office page describes a mission of protecting the public records, preserving them and keeping them open to everyone. Marriage licenses are by appointment: complete the application, then call and press option 1.

One research tip. Staff are still back-filling the index for records dated January 1, 1888 through June 30, 1988, adding parties as they go, so a name can be missing from the online search for those years. Confirm any early search in the paper index books at the office.

What a deed needs on its first page

A deed arrives finished, signed and notarized, either on paper at the Carthage counter or electronically through a filer. Staff are barred by statute from drafting deeds or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares it first.

The recording requirements page lists what page one of a North Carolina deed or deed of trust must carry.

  • The name of the person who drafted the document.
  • A return name and address, with a stamped envelope addressed to the filer.
  • The grantee's mailing address, which the Tax Department needs for the next bill.
  • The excise tax stamp on the front of the deed.
  • The instrument type, printed across the head of page one.

The stamp is paid along with the filing fee. The county states the math as $2 for every $1,000 of price, which equals $1 per $500 block. The seller carries that cost as the transferor (G.S. 105-228.30).

Formatting slips that add a charge

A paper that misses the state formatting standards still gets recorded, with a $25 non-standard charge added to the usual fee. The standards trace to G.S. 161-14(b), and Moore County repeats them on its site.

Moore County formatting checklist
Document featureRequirement
PaperLetter or legal size sheets
Top of page one3 blank inches
Remaining marginsHalf an inch on the other sides of page one and on every side of later pages
TypeBlack on white, no smaller than 9 points
PagesSingle-sided only
LabelInstrument type named at the head of page one

UCC filings on the national form and satisfactions are exempt. The register may also waive the charge for small type when the scanned image is legible, and an acknowledgment dated before July 1, 2002 carries no extra charge.

Can a law firm or lender e-record?

Yes, once the firm enrolls with an approved vendor. The county names three: Epen (eRecording Partners), CSC and Simplifile.

The firm then emails the county a completed Memorandum of Understanding for approval. A homeowner does not need to do any of this, because the firm handling the closing usually holds the account.

  • Electronic filers need the vendor account and the approved agreement on file before the first submission.
  • Paper filings come to the Carthage counter, or arrive by post with a check covering the stamp and fee.
  • Paper or electronic, the same page-one and margin rules apply.

Recording fees and the free alert service

The fee schedule is the statewide one in G.S. 161-10: a base price for the first pages of an ordinary instrument, a larger base for a deed of trust, and a per-page charge after that. Paying off a mortgage and filing the satisfaction costs nothing.

Moore County also runs a free Real Estate Recording Notification Service. Once you subscribe, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name you listed. One address can watch up to 10 names or spellings, and the alert covers only filings made after you subscribe.

For a homeowner it works as an early warning against a surprise lien, or a deed filed in your name that you never signed. Heirs settling a parent's estate can watch the parent's name and their own.

Before you list, a short checklist helps.

  • Confirm every deed of trust on the house has a recorded satisfaction.
  • Check that the last deed names the owner you expect, which matters most for an inherited house.
  • Ask your attorney whether the buyer's lender will file the new deed of trust the same day as your deed.

Moore County housing figures

The mid-2025 estimate is 110,619 people, up 10.9% since 2020, on 697.68 square miles of land. For 2020-2024, half of owner-occupied homes were valued above $351,400, owners lived in 76.4% of households, and typical rent was $1,254 a month. Builders took out 1,077 permits in 2025.

With estate transfers and new construction both passing through Carthage, a clean chain of recorded documents keeps a sale moving, especially when a house changed hands within a family.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Moore County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The Tax Department after recording

Once the deed is recorded, the Land Records Section at the county Tax Department updates ownership from what the Register of Deeds or the Clerk of Court received. The Tax page lists 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, 910-947-2255, with weekday service from 8 am to 5 pm.

The latest revaluation became effective January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027, followed by four-year rounds. A recorded sale does not reset the assessed value, though a price far outside the assessment can bring an appraiser to the property.

Request the current bill and any past-due balance before closing so the settlement statement shows the payoff.

How appraisers learn about changes to a house

The Tax Department learns about new work mostly through permits. The Appraisal page explains that the Commercial and Residential Section receives permit data from the county and from Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines, then schedules a site visit to record what was added.

Anything that adds heated floor area counts, and so do decks, porches, patios, sheds, pools and barns. The county still expects owners to report improvements themselves. A seller who finished a garage conversion without telling anyone may find the buyer's inspection and the tax record disagree.

  • Every parcel has an ID, sometimes called the PARID or land record key, that appears on the GIS site and on the bill.
  • The GIS site also shows the field review document and a condensed property record card for each parcel.
  • Customer service at 910-947-2255 can walk an owner through the record.

Checking that card before listing the house catches errors in square footage or features that a buyer's agent will notice.

Frequently asked questions

What are the visiting hours in Carthage?

Weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm, at 26 Courthouse Square in Carthage. Call 910-947-6370. Marriage licenses are by appointment once the application is complete.

Which items belong on the first sheet of a Moore County deed?

Page one needs the drafter's name, a return name and address with an envelope, the grantee's mailing address, the excise stamp and the instrument type. It also needs 3 blank inches at the top.

How much is the non-standard document fee in Moore County?

It is $25, added to the recording fee when a document misses the state formatting standards. The register may waive it for small type when the scanned image reads clearly.

Can I be alerted when something is recorded under my name?

Yes. The county's free Real Estate Recording Notification Service sends an email when a document is filed under a name you list, up to 10 names per address, for filings made after you subscribe.

Who handles my tax bill after the sale?

The Moore County Tax Department in Carthage lists, values and collects, and its Land Records Section updates the owner record from recorded deeds. Call 910-947-2255.

Records on file

Land records in Nash County reach back to 1777, when the county was carved out of western Edgecombe County. Marriage records begin in 1862, and birth and death records start in October 1913.

Deeds dated 1777 through 1969 can be searched online. Newer ones come as paper copies, so a seller chasing down an older deed of trust or a plat should phone the office at (252) 459-9836. Anything recorded before 1970 can often be found from your kitchen table.

Is a house in Rocky Mount recorded in Nash County?

Sometimes, and sometimes in Edgecombe County, because the city of Rocky Mount straddles the line between the two. Check the tax parcel record for your lot before anyone drafts a deed.

Every other Nash County town sits wholly inside the county and records at the same office: Nashville (the county seat), Sharpsburg, Dortches, Castalia, Red Oak, Whitakers, Middlesex, Bailey, Momeyer and Spring Hope. A Spring Hope seller and a Sharpsburg seller file at the same counter, though their towns are at opposite ends of the county.

Deed formatting rules

Documents recorded on or after July 1, 2002 must meet state paper rules, which the county's filing standards page boils down to a checklist. A deed that misses the mark still gets recorded, but the office adds a $25.00 nonstandard fee.

  • Letter (8 1/2 x 11) or legal (8 1/2 x 14) paper.
  • A clear 3 inch blank band across the top of page one.
  • Black type on white paper, at least 10 point.
  • Print on one side of each sheet.
  • The document type written directly beneath the blank band.

Blank spaces may be filled in with pen. Since October 1, 2011 the other margins on page one have been one quarter inch. If type is under 10 points yet still easy to read, the Register may waive the extra charge.

Recording fees

The 2025-2026 fee schedule sets the real estate charges below. The first four match the statewide amounts in G.S. 161-10, and the rest are items a seller or closing attorney may meet along the way.

Nash County Register of Deeds real estate fees, 2025-2026
Document or serviceFee

Excise stamps are priced at $1.00 per $500, covered in the next section.

Who pays the excise stamps when a Nash County house sells?

The seller does. Stamps run $1.00 per $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor owe the tax at the register before the deed goes on record. A leftover amount under $500 counts as a full unit.

Look for the stamp among the seller's charges on the closing statement. It has nothing to do with income tax on any gain, and its size follows the price stated in the deed.

E-recording a deed

Filers sign a Memorandum of Understanding and then receive a filing number. Call (252) 459-9836 to start that step.

Electronic filings are received on weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm, holidays excepted. Closing attorneys and title firms usually do the filing. Your part is to sign on time and ask which day the deed was submitted.
