Splitting a lot before a sale

County planning fees show what a split adds. A recombination or exempt plat costs $25. A minor final plat of two lots or fewer with no road, water, sewer or drainage work costs $50 plus $10 per lot, and a zoning permit is $10. Recording fees for plats are paid to the Register of Deeds once the plat is approved.

New construction or additions inside Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope or Whitakers need a zoning permit from that town's office before the county issues construction permits. A buyer hoping to add a room should hear that before closing.

Filing a plat sheet costs $21.00. The county's tax office sells copies of recorded plats at $4.00 for a full-size sheet and $1.00 for a reduced one.

Other services for estate and relocation sellers

Someone settling an estate or moving away often needs a few small items from the same counter.

  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10.00 each.
  • Marriage license: $60.00, and a certified marriage copy is $10.00.
  • Notary oath: $10.00, and authentication of a notary: $5.00.
  • Genealogy copy: $1.00 by mail or $0.10 in the office.

Ask the office which of these your sale needs, since the right papers depend on how title passed to you.

Steps for a seller at the register

Most of the work is done by your closing attorney, but knowing the order helps. The deed is prepared and signed, checked against the paper rules above, and then submitted either in person or electronically. The excise stamp is paid before it is accepted, and the recording fee follows the schedule by page count. Once the deed is on record, the office indexes it, and that date is your proof of who owns the house.

If a mortgage is being paid off in the same closing, the lender's release goes in as a satisfaction instrument, which carries no fee. Ask your attorney for recorded copies afterward, and keep a certified copy with your sale papers. A certified copy costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Why record a deed promptly?

Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option or long lease that never reached the register cannot be used against lien creditors or buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first wins. A parent's old deed that was signed but never filed is the classic example.

Recording a release of a paid-off deed of trust carries no fee. If a lender has merged or vanished, ask a North Carolina attorney to guide the cleanup before the listing goes live.

Before you list, pull your own deed and any open deed of trust from the office, and confirm that the names and legal description match what your agent will put in the contract. A cash buyer will want the same documents, though the closing skips lender paperwork.

Nash County housing snapshot

Nash County had about 99,365 people in mid-2025, 4.6% above 2020. Owners lived in 63.6% of its 45,068 housing units across 2020 to 2024. The middle owner-occupied house was worth $191,000, and renters paid a median of $953 a month. Builders pulled 483 permits in 2025.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about Nash County land records?

Call (252) 459-9836, the Register of Deeds number on the county filing standards page. Staff can explain e-recording sign-up and where older books are held.

What will the Register charge to file my Nash County deed?

Expect $26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 more per page. Add $25.00 if the paper breaks the printing rules.

Is there a charge to file a loan payoff release in Nash County?

No. Satisfaction instruments carry no fee on the county schedule.

Which Nash County town offices issue zoning permits before building?

Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope and Whitakers. The county issues its construction permits only after the town permit.

What are Nash County excise stamps on a deed?

They are the transfer tax receipt, priced at $1.00 per $500 of value and owed by the seller.

Where to record a deed in Wilmington

Real estate recording is handled in Land Records, Suite 102, at 320 Chestnut Street in Wilmington. A second counter on Government Center Drive accepts recordings in the afternoon only.

  • Land Records, Suite 102 (main office), 320 Chestnut Street, Wilmington, NC 28401: Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Vital Services, Suite 120 (same building): Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Satellite office, 230 Government Center Drive, Wilmington, NC 28403: recording from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays, vital records from 8 am to 5 pm.

The office number is 910-798-4530. Anything sent by mail must go to the Suite 102 address, never the satellite site.

What the county wants on page one

Quite a bit. On top of the statewide format rules, Wilmington's office requires these items on recordings:

  • A return name and address for the original document.
  • The drafter's name, on every deed and deed of trust.
  • The parcel's tax ID number, on any document that conveys land.
  • The grantee's address, again on conveyances of land.

Tax ID numbers come from Land Records in the county Tax Department, at 910-798-7300. Get the number early, since it has to be typed onto the deed before anyone signs.

Nonstandard paper

The county will still record a deed that breaks the format rules, for an extra $25.00 under G.S. 161-10(a)(19) on top of ordinary fees. To avoid it, follow this list when you file in Wilmington.

  • Page sizes: 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • Margins: three inches blank at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere on that page, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Ink and font: black on white, with 9 points counted as the smallest legible size.
  • Sides: text on the front of the sheet only.
  • Label: the instrument type at the top of page one, outside the blank margin.

Blanks may be inked in by hand, and corrections must use black ink. Releases of deeds of trust or mortgages, in every form, and UCC filings are exempt from these standards.

Register of Deeds real estate fees, fiscal year 2026-27

Excise stamps

The rate is $1.00 per $500.00 of price, which works out to $2.00 per $1,000.00. State law makes the seller pay, and G.S. 105-228.30 requires payment at the register before recording.

If you call and ask what a house sold for, you will be told only the stamp amount. The Register does not search titles or report on liens.

The schedule also shows the rate by era: $2 per $1,000 from 1991 to the present, $1 per $1,000 from 1968 to 1991, and $1.10 per $1,000 before 1968. That helps if you read an old deed and wonder what its stamp meant.

What the register can and cannot do

The office keeps the public record but cannot advise you on it.

  • Off limits: legal advice, attorney referrals and title searches.
  • Public: every filed record except DD-214 discharges, open to viewing and copying at the office.
  • Name changes on title: a new deed is needed to add or drop a name.
  • Wills: filed with the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Maps: subdivision and condominium plats only, not lot surveys.
  • House size and age: ask the Tax Department.

A free fraud alert is available too. Once you enroll, any document recorded under your name triggers an email with a copy. Owners of a vacant or inherited house may want it.

Why does the order of recording matter?

Under G.S. 47-18, the first instrument registered takes priority, and a deed that was never registered gives no protection against lien creditors or buyers who paid value. A deed signed on Friday but filed the following week can lose to something registered in between.

Because the office does not run title searches, ask an attorney or title company to check for open liens before anything is signed.

Other services at the Wilmington office

Besides land records, staff issue certified vital records, passport services and military discharge filings, and they take e-filed assumed business name certificates. Marriage licenses need an appointment, while notary oaths do not.

The county's page also links a public records search and a guide called "Don't Overpay for a Copy of Your House Deed," useful when a closing needs a copy of the vesting deed. First-time adult passport books are $165 and passport cards $65. Certified birth, death and marriage copies are $10 each, a marriage license is $60, and a minor's passport book is $135. Mailed requests for uncertified vital record copies carry a $1.25 fee. For a business-name form, the office keeps printed copies of the Secretary of State form as a courtesy.

Preparing to sell

Before listing, get a copy of your vesting deed and note the tax ID, the drafter and the grantee address that the county expects on page one. Ask your closing attorney whether a release of your current deed of trust is queued, since satisfactions record without a fee. If you are selling to a cash buyer, the same recording steps apply to the deed, but there will be no new deed of trust to file.

New Hanover County has 128,402 housing units, and owners live in 61.4% of occupied homes, so a large share of buyers and sellers are landlords or investors who file frequently. Arriving with a correct deed saves a second trip downtown. Bring a pen with black ink for any fill-ins, and confirm the hours for the counter you plan to visit, since the satellite office records only in the afternoon. Mail goes to Suite 102 on Chestnut Street, so allow a few days for delivery before a closing deadline.

What is the street address for recording a deed in Wilmington?

Go to 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102, in Wilmington (ZIP 28401). A satellite counter at 230 Government Center Drive takes recordings from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays.

Will New Hanover County accept a deed by mail?

Yes, but only at the Suite 102 address on Chestnut Street. Mailed recordings should not go to the satellite office.

Who owes the New Hanover County excise tax?

The seller. The rate is $1.00 per $500.00, and the register can later tell you only the stamp amount on the recorded deed.

Where can I find my parcel's tax ID for a New Hanover County deed?

Ask Land Records at the county Tax Department, 910-798-7300. The number belongs on page one next to the grantee's address.

No. They go to the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court. The register handles deeds and other property records.

What the Northampton Register of Deeds does

The office holds the county's permanent records: land instruments, plats, UCC filings and vital records. Sellers meet it because the deed to the buyer, and the security for the buyer's loan, are filed here.

Land books begin in 1741, marriage entries in 1863, and birth and death entries in December 1913. Older entries are found through paper indexes. Staff also issue marriage licenses and certified vital records, so say up front that you are calling about a deed.

Phone 252-534-2511 with questions, and ask there for the street address, hours and holiday closings.

Searching land records online

A free search is available at northamptonrod.org. The computerized index starts January 1, 1991, and it was the first time these records appeared on the internet.

  • From 1991 forward, search the website for deeds, deeds of trust and releases.
  • For older records, plan on the hard-copy indexes at the office.
  • Search under the owner's name exactly as the latest recorded deed spells it, because the index follows document names.

The title history of a family farm or inherited lot may begin before 1991. If your parcel passed through several generations, phone the office before assuming the website shows everything.

Northampton County housing market

The county is sparsely populated: an estimated 16,491 people on 536.70 square miles of land in mid-2025, which is 5.6 percent fewer than in 2020. Of 7,857 households, 74.6 percent own, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued around $114,500. Rents sit near $758. Builders took out 15 permits in 2025.

For a long-held house, a clean recorded chain of title matters most, and a gap in the index is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it. Modest values and a shrinking population also mean that an inherited or repair-heavy house can take a while to sell on the open market. A cash sale closes quickly and skips lender inspections and appraisals, which suits some owners of that kind of property.

Filing fees

Fees are uniform statewide, so Northampton charges what neighboring counties charge. G.S. 161-10 is the legal basis, calling the fees complete and exclusive and collectible before filing.

Real estate filing fees at the register of deeds
FilingFee
Ordinary instrument, including a deed$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per extra page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 covers 35 pages; $4 per extra page
Plat$21 a sheet

Who covers the deed tax at a sale?

The seller. Each deed carries a tax of $1 per $500 of consideration, with a leftover under $500 counted as a full $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor deliver it to the register ahead of filing. The county general fund keeps half. The other half goes to the state revenue department in a monthly remittance.

The office page also links a Deed Tax Certification form, a deed of trust fee change notice and a public records redaction request. Ask which, if any, your closing needs.

Other filings that touch a sale

The office also files loan security instruments, releases and plats. Satisfactions cost nothing, so an old paid-off loan can be released for free, and the buyer's lender will expect that.

  • A plat is $21 a sheet, which applies if a lot is split before sale.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.
  • Assignments add $10 for each extra index reference, and a party beyond the twentieth adds $2 a name.
  • A UCC record runs $38 for one or two pages.

Owners of several parcels, or of older estate property, can ask the office to look through the index for liens, releases and earlier deeds ahead of closing. Anything older than 1991 requires a phone call.

Checklist before listing

A sale touches the register, the tax department and, with an estate, the clerk of court. Work through this list before closing.

  • Locate the latest recorded deed and compare its names to the people signing.
  • Search 1991 forward for any deed of trust never released, and call about older ones.
  • Ask the tax department what is owed for every open year, including bills from earlier years.
  • Download the parcel's property tax card and GIS map from the tax page so the acreage and description agree with the deed.
  • After an owner's death, confirm with the clerk of court who may sign and whether a will has been probated.

The tax page also links a room occupancy tax return, so if a lodging operator runs out of the property, ask the tax department about closing that account.

How to submit a deed

Send every filing with a self-addressed stamped envelope, the signed deed and payment.

  • Compare the deed against the recording standards published by the state association of registers.
  • Enclose the filing fee and the seller's deed tax.
  • Phone to learn whether mail, couriers or drop-off are accepted.
  • Keep the confirmation, because under G.S. 47-18 a deed binds creditors and later buyers only after it is registered.

Filing order sets priority, so a deed that arrives late can rank behind an earlier lien. In a typical sale the closing attorney handles all of this, and the seller's job is to sign, supply the payoff letters and ask for a recorded copy afterward.

Timeline from signing to recorded deed

Think of the recording as the last step of a short chain. Before closing, your attorney or title firm gathers the deed, the payoff for any old loan, and proof that property taxes are handled. At closing you sign, and the seller's deed tax is collected with the fee. The deed then goes to the register, and the date it is registered is the date that counts against anyone else claiming the house. Afterward the office indexes it, and from 1991 forward you can find it on the free website under the owner's name.

If a buyer is paying cash, there is no lender waiting on a new deed of trust, so the packet is smaller and the filing is simpler. Whatever the route, ask for the recording date in writing and keep it with your sale papers.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax bills

The Tax Department, at 126 E. Jefferson St. in Jackson, bills Northampton parcels. Bills for 2026 are due September 1, 2026, and interest holds off until after January 5, 2027. Numbers: 252-534-4461 (main), 252-534-5941 (land records) and 252-534-3431 (listing).

The tax page links appeal forms and a list of county property for sale. Before fixing a closing date, ask what balance clears the parcel. An owner who prefers no repairs or showings can ask Cash Home Buyers for a cash offer and set it beside the payoff and recording costs.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records deeds for Northampton parcels?

The Northampton County Register of Deeds. A deed takes effect against creditors and later buyers once registered in the county where the parcel lies, under G.S. 47-18. Phone 252-534-2511 for the street address and hours.

What is the filing fee for a deed here?

A deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages with $4 added per extra page, and a deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. The seller's deed tax, $1 per $500 of price, is a separate payment.

Is there a free online index?

Yes, from 1991 forward at northamptonrod.org. Older records are searched in paper indexes at the office.

Is the seller or buyer responsible for deed tax?

The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment on the transferor, due at the register of deeds before filing, at $1 per $500 of consideration.

When is the property tax deadline?

September 1. Interest on 2026 bills starts only after January 5, 2027. State law then adds 2 percent through January and 0.75 percent per month afterward.

Location and hours

The counter is at 602 Anne Street in Jacksonville. Mail goes to a different spot, 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the main number is 910-347-3451.

Recording opens at 8 in the morning and the last item goes in at 5:30 in the afternoon, Monday to Friday. Marriage licenses stop a quarter hour earlier. Call before a long drive if weather or a holiday could change the schedule.

  • Walk-in address: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville
  • Mailing address: 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville
  • Phone 910-347-3451, fax 910-347-3340
  • Weekdays only, 8 a.m. until 5:30 p.m.

How far back do Onslow County real estate records go?

Land records reach back to 1734. The office files conveyances, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements.

Anything filed there is open to view at the counter. Staff will not fill in forms or search a title for you, because doing so would amount to practicing law without a license. Owners who want a title check should hire a closing attorney or order one through a title company.

You can also ask in writing to have a Social Security, bank or card number blacked out of an image on the county website. There is no charge for that request.

What to put on a deed before filing

Three things matter most: an excise tax statement, a tax certification form and clean personal data. Check each one before you present a deed.

  • Page one must show the excise tax, including a line for zero when nothing is due.
  • A tax-exempt transfer needs the legal reason for the exemption on page one.
  • A Tax Certification Form must be attached to the back of the original deed. That rule dates from July 1, 2013 and came from a decision of the Onslow County Tax Office.
  • Identity and account numbers stay out of the document unless the law or a court order requires them, or unless only the last four digits show.

Closing attorneys know these rules. A seller who prepares paperwork alone should phone 910-347-3451 first.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Onslow County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Fees and payment rules

Beyond the state's uniform fees, Onslow County charges a few amounts of its own and accepts payment in specific forms.

Onslow County recording and payment rules
TopicRule or amount
Extra instruments in one document$10 for each additional instrument
Credit cardsAccepted for $5 or more, with a 3% processing fee added
Business checksPhysical address and phone number required
Personal checksAddress, phone, and driver license number with issuing state
Vital recordsCash or money order only
Plats18 by 24 inches, mylar or paper

The base fee for a general instrument under G.S. 161-10 is $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page. A deed of trust or mortgage runs $64.00 for up to 35 pages. Satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no fee. The latest fee schedule is linked from the county's Recording Information page.

When one package counts as several instruments

The office treats a package as several instruments when it holds two or more papers with different legal consequences or intent, each signed and acknowledged on its own and able to be recorded alone. The charge is $10 for each instrument after the first.

A seller sees this when a deed arrives bundled with a separate easement, a right-of-way agreement or a power of attorney in one stack. Each paper that could stand by itself is its own instrument. If you are unsure how many your package holds, ask the closing attorney or call 910-347-3451 before presenting it, because the extra charge is collected at the counter along with the base fee.

Who pays the excise tax on an Onslow County house sale?

The seller does. The tax is $1 per $500, or part of $500, of the price or value conveyed, as set out in G.S. 105-228.

Payment goes to the register of deeds ahead of filing, and page one of the paper has to state the figure. Ask your closing attorney to add this tax to your payoff and other seller charges so your net sheet matches the check you receive.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Onslow County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Why filing time matters

Priority follows the clock. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, mortgage, option or lease longer than three years has no force against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered where the land lies.

A deed in a desk drawer protects nobody. In Onslow County, a judgment filed against a seller on Monday can beat a buyer whose deed reaches the office on Tuesday. Ask the closing agent for the recording time plus the book and page, and keep that confirmation with your sale papers.

Mail-in and plat recordings

Include an addressed, stamped return envelope with any mailed package so the original comes back to you. Make checks out to Onslow County Register of Deeds for the full amount.

Electronic plat submission through approved vendors began May 1, 2021, and plats can still be brought in. The county keeps the 18 by 24 inch statutory size. Sticky notes over wet-ink seals confuse the scanner, and residue gets a plat rejected. Anyone dividing a lot ahead of a sale should hand over a clean original.

Onslow County housing context

Onslow grew 6.2% between the 2020 count and July 2025, reaching 217,175 people, with 91,470 housing units. Owners hold 63.7% of homes, the typical owner-occupied value is $236,400, and typical rent is $1,265. The county issued 1,372 building permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale houses in many parts of the county. A seller near a new subdivision should expect buyers to compare the two.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Clearing liens before the deed goes in

Clear them first. Filing a lender's release costs nothing at this counter, so the only variable is how fast the lender sends it.

Property tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, so an unpaid bill follows the house to the buyer's closing. Ask the Onslow County Tax Office for the balance owed and have it paid from your proceeds. A seller whose debts exceed the likely price should talk to a closing attorney before choosing a date, since a recorded lien blocks a clean transfer. A cash buyer can still close quickly, but the same payoffs and releases are needed first. Collect the lender's payoff letter, the tax balance and a copy of your current deed, then hand them to the closing agent together so nothing waits on a missing paper. If your deed was recorded long ago, ask the office for a copy at the counter, where the records are open to view.

Frequently asked questions

What is the street address of the Onslow County Register of Deeds?

602 Anne Street, Jacksonville, NC. Mail is sent to 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the phone is 910-347-3451.

What time does the Onslow County Register of Deeds close?

Weekday recordings are accepted until half past five. The marriage license desk shuts 15 minutes sooner.

Does Onslow County add a card fee when recording?

Yes. Credit cards are accepted for payments of $5 or more, and a 3% processing fee is added to the total.

Will the Onslow County office help me fill in a deed?

No. Staff cannot complete forms or run title searches, since they may not practice law. They can show you the public record.

What has to be attached to an Onslow County deed?

A Tax Certification Form goes on the back of the original deed. Page one must also show the excise tax amount, or the reason for any exemption.

Where to file a deed in Orange County

Go to Suite 300 of the Gateway Center, 228 S Churton Street, Hillsborough, NC 27278. Weekday hours run from 8 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon.

A seller in Chapel Hill, Carrboro or Efland files at the same Hillsborough counter as everyone else in the county. Park in the deck directly behind the Gateway Center. E-recording is also available, which lets a title office send documents without a drive across town.

  • Place: Gateway Center, Suite 300, on S Churton Street
  • Open: Monday to Friday until 5 p.m., closed on holidays
  • Parking: the deck behind the building
  • Records search: the county's document inquiry website

Fees beyond the basic filing charge

The schedule dated October 1, 2026 starts with the familiar statewide amounts, then adds a long list of smaller charges. These are the ones most likely to turn up in a home sale or an estate.

Selected Register of Deeds charges, October 1, 2026 schedule
ServiceCharge
Non-standard document$25 per document
Each party name past the twentieth$2
Certified plat copy$5 per page
Uncertified plat copy$3 per page
Right of way plans or highway maps$21 first page, $5 each added page
Notary public oath of office$10
Notice of satisfactionNo charge

Deeds themselves are $26 for 15 pages and mortgages $64 for 35 pages. Recording payments can be made by cash, certified check, money order, personal or business check or card, with American Express and Apple Pay excluded.

What stamp tax applies to an Orange County deed?

The stamp is $1 per $500 of the value conveyed, counting any leftover fraction as a full $500. The fee table prints the same idea as $2 per thousand for deeds from August 1, 1991 on.

Older rates are listed only for history: $1 per thousand from January 1, 1968 through July 31, 1991, and $1.10 per thousand earlier. The seller owes the tax at the counter before filing. For the exact stamp amount on your price, ask your closing attorney rather than guessing.

What staff can and cannot do

Staff issue certified copies of deeds recorded in the county and help owners find a plat by book and page. Title searches go to attorneys.

A title search must come from an attorney, or a paralegal under an attorney's supervision. Changing a name on a recorded deed takes a new deed, and legal counsel is a good idea for anyone not used to drafting one. That fits an inherited house or a divorce, where a closing attorney can draft the right instrument ahead of a sale.

  • Certified copies of recorded deeds: yes, at the scheduled fee
  • Plat copies: certified $5 a page, uncertified $3 a page
  • Title search: attorney or supervised paralegal
  • Changing names on a deed: a new deed is needed

Which county gets the deed near a county line?

Whichever county holds the land. Registration there fixes the deed's rank against rival claims, whatever city the buyer or lender calls home.

Orange County's rate codes include city entries for Durham and Mebane, a reminder that those towns reach into the county. If part of a parcel is in another county, ask the closing attorney which office takes the deed and the excise tax. A deed is not safe against later claims until the register of deeds has stamped it.

Other filings at the office

Besides deeds, the office takes plats, notices of satisfaction, assumed business names and Uniform Commercial Code filings. The county's recording page links to document standards, an inquiry tool for submitting and searching document questions, and a guide to registering an assumed name.

UCC filings fall under Chapter 25, Article 9 of the General Statutes. The fee is $38 for an initial filing, correction, amendment or termination of up to two pages, $45 for three to ten pages and $2 for each page beyond ten. An owner who financed fixtures or equipment tied to a property should ask the office whether a filing exists before listing. Marriage licenses cost $60 and are valid at once for sixty days.

What to settle before the deed is filed

Settle the mortgage payoff, the tax bill and the stamp tax. Each one changes what the closing attorney sends to Hillsborough.

  • A lender's satisfaction of a deed of trust is recorded free, so ask the lender how long it takes to send one.
  • The yearly property tax is a lien from its listing date and the bill is due September 1. Ask Orange County Tax Administration for the balance.
  • The stamp tax comes out of the seller's proceeds at closing.

Sellers who want to skip repairs and showings sometimes pick a cash buyer. The filing steps look the same either way, though there is no lender payoff to coordinate on the buyer's side.

Other counter services

The same Gateway Center office issues marriage licenses, certified vital records and notary oaths, and it runs a passport service. Those lines can mean a wait on a busy day, so schedule a deed filing for a time when you can wait.

A marriage license costs $60. Applications are taken daily between eight and four except on holidays, and card payments carry a 2.5% convenience fee with a $2 minimum. A passport execution fee is $35 and a passport photo is $17. Certified copies of births, deaths and marriages are $10 each. Military discharge copies carry no charge. Some of these services take only certain forms of payment, so read the payment list on the fee page before you go.

Orange County housing context

From 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied home was worth $459,500, and owners occupy 63.8% of homes. Median rent is $1,496, and owners with a mortgage report monthly costs near $2,221. Builders took out 666 permits in 2025. A seller pricing a house here should lean on recent nearby sales rather than a county-wide median.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring to the office

Bring the signed, notarized original deed and payment for the recording fee and the stamp tax. For vital records, a photo ID is needed: a driver license with photograph, a state identification card or a passport.

Someone collecting a certificate for another person, such as an agent or attorney, must show papers proving authority. For deeds that run long, list many parties or use an odd page size, phone the office first. Added-page, non-standard document and extra-name charges can apply to those. A good habit is to call a day ahead, describe the package, and ask what total to expect, so the check you bring matches the bill at the counter. Closing attorneys and title firms often do this for you, but a seller filing alone will want the same answer.

Frequently asked questions

What is the address of the Orange County NC Register of Deeds?

228 S Churton Street, Suite 300, in the Gateway Center, Hillsborough, NC 27278. The office is open weekdays until 5 p.m.

What does recording a deed cost in Orange County?

$26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for every page after that. Add $25 if the document is non-standard, and $2 for each party name past 20.

How much is the deed stamp tax in Orange County?

$1 per $500 conveyed, with leftover fractions rounded up, which the fee table shows as $2 per thousand. The seller pays it at the counter before filing.

Does the Orange County office run title searches?

No. An attorney, or a paralegal working under one, must do a title search. Staff can point you to the recorded documents.

Does Orange County accept e-recording?

Yes. E-recording is listed on the county's recording page. Call the Hillsborough office to confirm how to set it up before you plan around it.

Where Roxboro files its deeds

The Register of Deeds is at 21 Abbitt Street in Roxboro (ZIP 27573), phone (336) 597-1733. The Tax Office, which you will also need, is at 13 Abbitt.

The department is the custodian of Person County's most important records. Visitors come for:

  • searches of land records
  • vital records, meaning births, deaths and marriages
  • marriage licenses and notary oaths
  • plats, cemetery records, grave removals, military discharges and genealogy files

Sellers mostly want the first item and the filing of the deed. Phone before you go to learn counter hours and whether electronic filing is offered.

The Person County market

About 19,000 homes and apartments (19,023 housing units) sit on 392.34 square miles, and owners occupy 77.3% of them. The median owner-occupied home is worth $213,900. Most deeds therefore record a resale of an existing house rather than a new build.

On a house in that range, a flat filing fee and a stamp tax of $1.00 per $500.00 are small pieces of the closing statement. Your title and tax payoff matter far more.

The register and filing order

The register is an elected officer with a two-year term (G.S. 161-1). The office takes in conveyances, applies the uniform charges, and collects excise tax before anything goes on record (G.S. 161-10).

Priority is set by time stamp. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or a lease of more than three years does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies.

Clerks will not draft a deed or settle who owns what. An unfiled deed gives you no protection, which is why your attorney should file it the moment funds are released.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Person County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Person County recording fees

The legislature fixes every charge, so the Roxboro counter has no discretion.

Recording charges under G.S. 161-10
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument, 15 pages$26.00
Page 16 onward, general instruments$4.00 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage, 35 pages$64.00
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Map or plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per page after
Document in nonstandard form$25.00 extra
Additional instrument within one document$10.00 each

Pay before filing. Recording the release when you pay off an old loan costs nothing at this counter.

Excise stamp tax on a Roxboro deed

The person giving up title pays, which in a sale is the seller. The tax is due before the deed is filed, and G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at $1.00 for each $500.00 or part of it in price or value.

The county keeps half. The state gets the rest monthly, after refunds and an allowance. A tract that spans counties pays where more of its value lies.

  • Put it on your net sheet, since it reduces what you take home.
  • It tracks the price in your contract.
  • For a gift or family transfer with little stated value, ask the office how it handles that.

Get the figure from your attorney in writing before closing day.

Checking land records before you list

Spend an hour in the index, or pay an attorney to, and hunt for anything that blocks a clean transfer. Old unreleased loans, judgments and forgotten options are the usual finds.

  • Seller names should match the last recorded deed.
  • The contract's legal description should match that deed's.
  • Every earlier deed of trust needs a recorded release.
  • Ask the Tax Office for the balance so the lien clears at closing.

If you financed a buyer yourself, Chapter 47H has you record the contract or a brief memorandum within five business days.

One call to the old lender usually fixes a missing release. Title held by a deceased owner is a bigger job. A cash buyer can move fast, though insurable title still comes first.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Person County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to prepare a deed for filing

Bring the signed, notarized original with the tax payment and fee, and check the page count, since each extra page adds four dollars.

Order of events counts. The buyer's lender normally files its deed of trust right after the deed, and your own payoff releases should already be in motion.

  • Look over the notary block for a full date and signature.
  • Add the parcel number to page one if your attorney does.
  • Keep a copy with the registration time on it.

Ask whether the office takes electronic filing, and confirm counter hours before driving over.

Certified copies of old deeds and plats

The office searches and copies land records, and the statewide schedule sets the price for certified copies and for filing a plat.

An older deed helps when you plan a sale, for three reasons:

  • It shows the exact words used for the boundary, which a buyer's surveyor will compare against the ground.
  • It names the people who held title before you, which confirms the chain.
  • It may refer to an easement, a road right, or a restriction that survives to the new owner.

Copies are priced per page (see the table), and a plat is filed per sheet. If you ordered a new survey as part of dividing land, the plat is recorded here before lots are sold separately.

Bring the tax parcel number and the names of recent owners to speed up the search, and ask staff which index years cover the period you need. Staff cannot interpret what a deed means, so take any unclear wording to an attorney or surveyor.

If the owner of record has died

A deed signed by someone who has died cannot be treated as a normal conveyance, so an estate attorney should say who may sign for the owner. State law lets small estates collect personal property by affidavit, with a cap of $20,000 in G.S. 28A-25-1, and that affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

  • Gather a death certificate, which the deed office keeps among its vital records.
  • Search the land records for the last recorded deed to confirm what the person actually owned.
  • Speak with an estate attorney before anyone signs a deed.

An heir who wants a quick sale should know that title company and lender requirements usually decide the timeline, not the filing counter.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Closing day sequence for a Person County sale

Here is how the paperwork usually runs once you have a signed contract. The buyer's attorney searches the land records and orders your tax payoff from the Tax Office. At the table you sign the notarized deed, and the stamp tax comes out of your proceeds. The deed is then filed at the Abbitt Street counter, followed by the buyer's lender's deed of trust. Any release for your old loan goes in as well, and it costs nothing to record.

A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust and its underwriting, so the filing step is shorter. Title work, the tax payoff and the stamp tax stay exactly the same. Ask your attorney to send you the recorded copy with its registration time once the office returns it.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the deed office?

21 Abbitt Street, Roxboro, NC 27573, phone (336) 597-1733. Call for counter hours.

What does a deed filing cost?

A deed runs $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page. The table above covers loans, plats and copies.

Who pays the stamp tax when a home sells?

The seller does, to the register, before filing. The rate is $1.00 per $500.00 or part of the value.

Do I pay to record the release of my old mortgage?

No. Releases of deeds of trust or mortgages carry no fee.

Why does the filing time matter?

Priority follows the time of registration, and an unfiled conveyance loses to lien creditors and paying buyers.

Deeds for Pitt County land are recorded at the Pitt County Register of Deeds, 100 E. 1st Street in Greenville. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 5:00, the phone is 252-902-1650 and the fax is 252-830-4132.

The same office keeps deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and the other land papers that make up the chain of title. For a seller, the office matters at one moment above all: the deed that moves the house to a buyer has to land in these books before it protects anyone.

Why filing order matters in a sale

The first paper on file wins. Under the state recording statute, an unfiled deed or option has no force against creditors with liens or buyers who paid value, and ranking among claims follows filing time.

Greenville is where that time stamp gets set, which is why every closing ends with a filing step. A signed deed left in a drawer protects nobody. If you hold an old deed from a family transfer that never reached the office, file it, or talk to an attorney, before you advertise the house.

Pitt County recording fees

The General Assembly sets the fees, and they are the same in every county.

Pitt County recording charges
FilingCharge
General instrument (deed, easement)$26 through page 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 with a 35-page allowance
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25 extra
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 per extra page
Mortgage releaseNo charge
PhotocopiesTypically $0.25 per page

The lender figure comes from G.S. 161-10. Call before sending a lender document so the check matches. The office accepts cash, check, money order and card.

The deed stamp tax

The excise tax runs a dollar for every $500 of price, with a leftover part of $500 counting as a full one. It follows the sale price.

The seller carries the duty under the excise tax statute, and it has to be paid before the register will accept the deed. Pitt keeps half the money and the State receives the other half. Look for the line on your settlement statement.

Electronic filing

Yes, Pitt County takes electronic filings through several vendors, and filers should call each one to compare prices. Four vendors are listed on the county FAQ, each with its own phone number.

Most sellers never touch this step, since the closing office sends the deed and the buyer's loan papers together. A family transfer with no lender is different: ask whoever prepared the deed whether they file electronically or in person, and who covers the vendor charge.

Watching for deed fraud and checking records

Pitt County has an alert sign-up that notifies owners whenever a filing matches their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Do this before listing, especially with an inherited house. A loan that was never released, or a missing link in the ownership record, takes less effort to fix while no buyer is waiting.

Other papers in a Pitt County sale

Besides the deed, a closing can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: Chapter 47H calls for recording the contract within five business days.

The office also records agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps.

Other services at the register's office

The office is more than a deed counter. It holds birth and death certificates for events in the county, issues marriage licenses, files notary commissions and gives the oath to every notary public. A veteran can file military discharge records here, and the charge for filing or copying them is waived.

It also takes Uniform Commercial Code financing statements on personal property, listed at $38 for one or two pages. The overlap that helps sellers is notary service. A $10 notarial act fee is tied to a filing, so someone who has not yet signed a deed can ask about doing it at the counter. Call 252-902-1650 first, and bring photo identification.

Old deeds and the chain of title

Pitt County was formed in 1760, and its oldest records include land grants, indentures and property agreements from the 1700s. Online search reaches back to September 1762, and index books for older records are kept on site. Look up the grantor or grantee in the alphabetical index, note the book and page, then pull the full document with that reference.

An old farm or family tract can have a chain of deeds that runs back generations. If a deed in that chain was never filed, or a name is spelled differently from one deed to the next, a buyer's title search will flag it. Start the search early, and keep every book and page number you find.

What a Pitt County seller should do before closing

Begin with a title check. Pull the deed that put the house in your name, confirm each old loan has a filed release, and ask the tax office what is owed.

Property tax lives in a different office. Under the collection statute, each bill falls due on September 1, and interest begins after January 5. Pitt County Tax Administration gives the balance on your parcel.

Repairs, tenants and estate delays do not block a quick sale to a direct cash buyer. The filing steps stay the same: the deed goes to Greenville.

Closing day paperwork in Pitt County

Once a contract is signed, the buyer's attorney searches the land records and requests your tax payoff. At closing you sign the deed, the stamp tax comes out of your proceeds, and the closing office sends the deed to the register in Greenville. The buyer's lender then files its deed of trust, and the release of your old loan is recorded if the lender has not already done so.

With a cash buyer there is no new deed of trust, so fewer papers go to the counter. Title work, the stamp tax and the tax payoff stay the same. Ask your attorney for the recorded copy showing the filing time, and keep it with your sale papers.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Pitt County Register of Deeds?

At 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834. Weekdays only, 8:00 to 5:00, and the phone is 252-902-1650.

Who covers the deed stamp tax in a Pitt County sale?

Sellers do. The statute names the transferor, and the office takes the payment at the counter. Your settlement statement should show the line.

Is there a charge to file a mortgage release in Pitt County?

No. Satisfactions and cancellations are free. The lender files the release, so ask yours to do it.

Is there an online deed search for Pitt County?

Yes. Documents recorded from September 1762 forward can be searched online by name, type, book and page, or dates.

What is the base fee for a Pitt County deed?

$26 buys a general instrument of up to 15 pages, then each extra page adds $4. Plats are $21 a sheet. Get the final total for your own document by phone.

Where Polk County deeds are recorded

Deeds go to the Register of Deeds in the Polk County courthouse complex at 40 Courthouse St., Columbus, NC 28722. Postal mail uses PO Box 308. Weekday hours are 8:30 to 5:00, and the phone is (828) 894-8450.

The office files deeds, powers of attorney, cancellations of deeds of trust and plats. It also keeps marriage, birth and death records, issues marriage licenses by appointment only, and handles assumed business name certificates. A home sale reaches this counter at the very end, once the deed is signed.

How a recorded deed reaches the tax records

The county updates its tax records after a deed is recorded. A recorded plat also prompts an update, with the tax side working alongside the GIS department on mapping.

Sellers often miss the January 1 rule. Polk County treats whoever held title on that date as the taxpayer for the year, even if the house sells in March. Splitting the bill with a buyer is a private agreement, so take that question to the closing attorney or the agent. Give the tax office a correct mailing address so notices find the right person.

When the GIS map still shows the old owner

Give it time. Parcel data refreshes every one to two months, so a name can lag behind a fresh deed.

  • Recording comes first, and the map follows.
  • If a sale closed in the last two months, wait before worrying.
  • Past two months, call the tax office at (828) 894-8954.
  • For general ownership and transfer questions, call (828) 894-8500.

Write down the book and page of your recorded deed. The tax office may want it if a name needs correcting.

Polk County recording fees

One fee schedule applies to every register of deeds in the state, printed in G.S. 161-10. Phone Columbus for the final amount before mailing anything. The statute's figures are below.

Statewide recording fees as they apply in Polk County
DocumentFee
General instrument such as a deed$26.00 to start, $4.00 per page past page 15
Home loan security instrument$64.00 to start, $4.00 per page past page 35
Lender's release of a loanNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 per further page

The office collects fees before it files anything. A non-standard document adds $25.00, and each extra instrument in one packet adds $10.00.

Deed excise tax

The seller pays. The rate is a dollar for each $500 of price or value, rounding any remainder up (see the excise tax statute). It is handed over before the deed gets recorded.

Polk County and the State split the money in equal halves. Check the excise tax line on your settlement statement against the sale price.

Why record a Polk County deed right away

The state recording statute ranks competing claims by who registered first. Until the paper is on file in Columbus, an unrecorded deed or option offers no protection against lien creditors or purchasers who paid value.

Two practical points follow. A deed from an earlier family transfer that never reached the office should be recorded before the house is sold. And a paid-off loan clears title only when the lender files its release. The county's Property Check sign-up emails an alert if anything new is filed against your name, which suits a house nobody lives in.

Contract for deed recording

Chapter 47H governs seller-financed deals on homes of up to four families. Within five business days the seller must file the contract itself or a brief memorandum describing it. The buyer may back out until midnight on the third business day.

If either side of a Polk County deal works this way, record promptly and have an attorney read the papers. A forfeiture needs a written notice that gives at least 30 days to cure.

Who else touches a Polk County home sale?

Beyond the register, a sale usually involves the county tax office, which values the parcel and prints the bill, and the settlement agent, who runs the title search and the closing. The register's office coordinates with the tax department, the health department, inspections and the court.

A house tied up in probate or foreclosure goes through the court clerk first. The deed that finally transfers the land still comes back to the Columbus office to be recorded.

Other services at the Polk County register's office

Marriage licenses are by appointment only. Applicants complete a form online and bring it to the appointment, scheduled by phone at (828) 894-8450 or by email.

  • Vital records: births, deaths and marriages recorded in Polk County can be bought online. Records from elsewhere cannot.
  • Assumed business names: owners must refile at the local register's office to stay on the statewide registry.
  • Property Check: a sign-up that warns you about new filings under your name.
  • Powers of attorney: the register records them along with deeds.

A seller who runs a small business from the house or who holds a recorded power of attorney for a parent should ask about these items before closing, so the paperwork lines up with the deed.

What to bring or send to the Columbus office

Phone first at (828) 894-8450 to confirm payment and mail-in details. Then gather the items below so the clerk has everything in one visit.

  • The signed deed, or the plat if you are splitting a parcel.
  • Payment for the excise tax, plus the recording fee quoted by the office.
  • The parcel number printed on your last tax bill.
  • The buyer's mailing address, so later notices arrive.

A month or two after recording, check the parcel on the county GIS site. A plat is the one paper that also reshapes the map, since the tax office and GIS department work together to update mapping after a plat is filed.

Handling the tax bill when you sell

Get the current balance from the Polk County tax office, then tell the closing attorney who owes that year's bill. Tax is due September 1 and can be paid at face value through January 5 (see the collection statute).

A direct cash purchase can shorten the timeline for an inherited, vacant, rented or run-down house. The recording work described above stays the same either way: the signed deed, the excise tax and the filing fee still go through the Columbus counter, and the buyer or the closing office usually handles the trip.

Steps from signed deed to recorded deed

The path is short but the order matters. First, the closing office collects the excise tax and the recording fee. Second, the signed and notarized deed goes to the Columbus counter, where it receives a time stamp. Third, the tax office updates its records, and the GIS parcel map follows within a month or two. Fourth, you or your attorney keep the book and page number for your files.

If anything is missing, such as a payment or a page, the clerk cannot file the deed, and the time stamp slips. For that reason many closings send the packet the same day the funds are released.

Frequently asked questions

What hours does the Polk County Register of Deeds keep?

The Columbus office at 40 Courthouse St. is open weekdays, 8:30 to 5:00. Phone (828) 894-8450 to confirm, especially around holidays.

If I sell in spring, who owes that year's Polk County tax?

The January 1 owner carries the liability. Whether the buyer reimburses you is settled privately at closing.

How big is the state's deed excise tax?

A dollar for each $500 of price or value. The selling side pays it at the register's counter.

Can I buy Polk County birth and death records online?

Yes, with one limit. Only vital records recorded in Polk County can be bought online, so a certificate from another county must be requested there.

Is there a fee to record a loan release in Polk County?

No. A lender's release of a loan carries no fee. The lender is the one that files it, so ask yours to do so at payoff.

What happens at the Register of Deeds after you sign

Your signed and notarized deed goes to the Shaw Building office in Asheboro, where it is indexed and added to the county land record. From that point a title examiner for any later buyer can find it. The office handles real estate recording (deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, releases and real property UCCs), plats and condominium maps, partnerships and assumed names, military discharges, and the satisfaction of deeds of trust.

Staff there also issue marriage licenses, hold certified birth, death and marriage records for events in Randolph County, and swear in notaries. Only the real estate side touches a sale, but a notary oath or a certified copy you need for closing paperwork may be handled at the same counter.

Recording matters because of the recording statute: a conveyance carries no weight against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is on the record where the land sits.

The 4:30 recording cutoff and holidays

Staff are on hand from eight in the morning until five on weekdays, yet real estate recording ends at 4:30 pm. County commissioners passed a resolution letting the office stop taking real estate documents, notary oaths and marriage licenses at that hour every day.

Closing attorneys know to send deeds before the cutoff. If a signing runs long, expect the filing to slide to the following business day. The register follows the holiday schedule used by Randolph County government, and the county posts the list each year, so check it before setting a signing date near a holiday. Offices closed that day cannot file anything, and a deed handed over the next business morning takes that morning's time stamp.

Getting to the Randolph County Register of Deeds

Aim for the Shaw Building in Asheboro. From Highway 64, turn north on Cox Street between the Dunkin and Hardee's, follow it to Worth Street, and turn left at the stop light. The building stands on the left.

If you arrive on the Highway 220 bypass, leave at the Asheboro (Highway 42) exit, which sits to your left, and turn east on Salisbury Street. Northbound drivers go straight over the ramp crest to the next light. Turn right at North Fayetteville Street, move into the left lane, and turn left on Worth Street. This time the building is on the right.

Parking, a map and an email link to the office sit on the county website. Questions about records can be sent there, which saves a trip when you only need to know whether something was recorded.

Who pays the excise tax on a Randolph County sale

The seller pays the register just before the deed is filed. The levy is a dollar per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $500 step (the excise tax statute).

Receipts are split between the county and the state. A parcel that lies in two counties is taxed through the one with more of the value. On a Randolph County closing the attorney's settlement statement shows the number, and the firm brings payment with the deed.

Looking up or correcting a recorded deed

The online system lets you search by name, book and page, subdivision or date range, and filter by document type. Another route is the county GIS map: search an address and follow its deed link.

  • For 1986 to 1993, first names such as Charles, Robert, Thomas and William may be shortened to Chas, Robt, Thos and Wm.

A book and page ending in E means the record is with the Clerk of Court, not this office. To add or drop a name, someone must prepare and record a new deed. The office offers no deed forms and no drafting help.

Other documents in a Randolph County sale

A deed is the headline filing, but the buyer's lender files a deed of trust, and your old loan is cleared by a certificate of satisfaction. That certificate is how an owner who paid off a mortgage confirms the lien is gone, and you can check it online by name.

Options, contracts to convey, leases over three years and rights of first refusal also need registration to bind later buyers. A seller-financed contract for deed under Chapter 47H must be recorded, or a short memorandum of it recorded, within five business days.

Mobile homes are a separate matter. Owners are sent to the state motor vehicle office for those titles.

Estates and tax liens

Wills are filed with the Randolph County Clerk of Court, and probate proceeds there. For a small estate, a statutory affidavit may suffice when personal property after liens is $20,000 or less, and it lists each tract of real estate owned.

Property tax runs on its own track. The lien attaches on the listing date and can be enforced by a foreclosure action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure, with a courthouse-door sale. Before drafting a deed for an inherited or tax-troubled house, ask the Randolph County tax office what is owed.

What a seller should do before closing day

Confirm your payoff will produce a recorded satisfaction, then search the online index afterward by name. Nobody holds your deed but you, unless the closing attorney kept it.

Tell the attorney to use a return address where the recorded original will reach you, and ask for a list of every document to be filed so nothing lands after 4:30. If something goes missing, email the register through the county website. A cash sale skips the buyer's lender, so there may be no deed of trust to file, but the deed, the excise tax and the cutoff stay the same.

Frequently asked questions

What time does Randolph County stop recording deeds?

4:30 pm every day. The office stays open until 5 pm on weekdays, but a commissioners' resolution ends real estate recording at the earlier hour. Plan the deed delivery for the morning of closing.

Does the Randolph County office hand out deed forms?

No. It supplies only assumed business name forms. Staff will not advise on wording, so lean on your closing attorney for the document itself.

Where do I take a will in Randolph County?

To the Randolph County Clerk of Court, not the register of deeds. The register's FAQ page lists the clerk's phone number for questions about wills and estate filings.

How can I see a copy of my Randolph County deed?

Search the register's website by name, or use the county GIS map by address and click the deed link. A deed recorded before 1986 may sit in the older books, so ask the office if the online index shows nothing.

Who covers the excise tax on a deed in Randolph County?

The seller. Payment goes in with the filing, at a dollar per $500 of value, and the closing attorney normally brings the check with the deed.

What the Richmond County Register of Deeds does

The office in Rockingham holds the deeds, deeds of trust, plats, marriage records and birth and death certificates for Richmond County, and it records new ones as they come in. When you sell, it is the stop where your deed to the buyer joins the permanent record.

Everything on file is public. A buyer, a title examiner or a curious neighbor can all ask for copies by paying the usual fees, so assume any deed you sign will be read by others.

The date of recording is what counts, because G.S. 47-18 ranks a deed against lien holders and later purchasers by when it was registered, not when it was signed.

Excise tax on a Richmond County deed

Sellers settle this tax when the deed is filed. The rate is a dollar per $500 of value, with a partial $500 rounded up, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment ahead of recording.

Half stays in Richmond County's general fund, and half is passed up to Raleigh. Look for the line on your settlement statement and check it against the contract price.

Fixing the names on a deed

The staff will record a corrected deed but will not draft it. The fix is a fresh deed that an attorney drafts, the owner signs, a notary acknowledges and the office then records.

Situations where this comes up before a sale include:

  • A spouse added or removed after a marriage or divorce.
  • An heir who needs to appear on title after a death.
  • Co-owners who want to sell to one buyer together.

Each case needs the right signatures on the new deed, and signatures take time to gather. Settle it early so the closing date holds. Once the corrected deed is signed and notarized, bring it to the Rockingham counter with the recording fee, and ask your attorney to confirm which names must appear on the sale deed.

Deed and plat copies and notary oaths

For a copy, give staff your name and about when you acquired the land, in person or by mail. A plat can be requested as long as it was surveyed and recorded.

Other papers filed with a Richmond County sale

Ask your attorney to list each document that will be filed, so none is held back. Each one is recorded in the order it arrives, so the deed to the buyer should go in before the buyer's deed of trust.

Foreclosure and inherited estates

These go through the Richmond clerk of superior court instead. In a power-of-sale case the clerk holds the hearing, and notice must be served 10 or more days beforehand (G.S. 45-21.16).

Once a foreclosure sale is reported, anyone can submit an upset bid during the next ten days. It needs to beat the last figure by 5 percent and at least $750, and every new bid starts the ten days over.

For a modest estate, an affidavit can replace full administration when personal property net of liens stays at $20,000 or under. The deed that follows is recorded in Rockingham.

Questions to ask the Rockingham office before closing

A short call to 910-997-8250 can head off delays. The staff are used to questions from attorneys, title searchers and owners, and everything they hold is public.

  • Has the deed been indexed yet, and what book and page does it carry?
  • Did the cancellation of my old deed of trust record?
  • What is the total of fees for the page count of my filing?
  • Can my attorney's e-Recording submission still go in before the deadline?

Write down the answers with the date and the name of the person who gave them. Staff cannot interpret a document, but they can confirm what has been recorded and when.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Before recording, what a Richmond County seller should do

Get from the closing attorney the day the deed should be recorded and proof that your old loan was cancelled. After closing, search the county records for both and keep the recorded copies.

Property tax becomes a lien on the listing date, so the current bill stays with the parcel until paid. Ask the Richmond County tax office for the balance. Fees and excise tax are paid at the filing, and the return address you give should be one where the recorded original will reach you.

A cash buyer can shorten the wait for loan approval. The recording steps do not change: the deed still goes to Rockingham before 4:30, and your payoff and tax balance still come from the closing proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What hours does the Richmond County Register of Deeds record documents?

Staff remain until 5:00 PM, yet counter recording ends half an hour sooner and electronic filing ends at 4:00. Papers that come after 4:30 are recorded first the next morning, so a late closing can push your recording date back.

Where is the Richmond County Register of Deeds?

At 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379, which is also its mailing address. Call 910-997-8250 during business hours with questions.

How much is a photocopy of a recorded deed in Rockingham?

35 cents a copy when you ask in person. Certified copies are priced under the state table instead, starting at $5 for page one.

Do I need an appointment to record a deed in Richmond County?

No appointment is required. Bring the signed, notarized deed during recording hours, or have an eligible submitter e-record it before 4:00 PM.

Can staff draft my deed for me?

No. An attorney or the owner has to prepare the deed, and it must be signed and notarized before it is brought in. The office records the paper and gives no advice on its wording.

What the Register of Deeds records in Lumberton

Anything that transfers or encumbers land in Robeson County ends up here: the deed to your buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, the cancellation of your old loan, plats and similar papers. Call 910-671-3040 with questions about a recording.

State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it keeps no forms. Its recording page tells filers to see an attorney for any legal question and for drafting.

Recording matters because of G.S. 47-18, which works like a queue. A deed protects its holder against outside claims from the moment it is registered locally, and earlier registration wins.

Tax certification before recording

Every deed needs tax certification before recording, unless it comes with the delinquent tax statement under G.S. 161-31. A deed mailed without either one is returned to the sender.

The certification comes from the county tax department, not the register. That makes the tax office the first stop for a Robeson deed, and it is the step sellers most often forget.

Ways to get a Robeson County deed certified by the tax office
MethodHow to do it
EmailSend the documents to deeds@robesoncountync.gov
MailRobeson County Tax Department, 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton NC 28358
PhoneCall the tax office at 910-671-3060 for instructions

Ask your closing attorney whether the firm already requests certification for every deed it sends. Many firms do, but a seller handling a family transfer or a sale without an attorney has to do it personally.

Recording a deed in person

Every document recorded in person must show a return name and mailing address. If you bring no stamped, self-addressed envelope, a $1.00 mailing fee is added.

The paper must be drafted, signed and notarized before it arrives. Staff can't repair a bad acknowledgment or write in missing terms. If the notary left out a seal or a date, the document has to go back to be fixed before you return. Bring this:

  • Tax certification or the delinquent tax statement attached.
  • A return name and address on the document.
  • An envelope addressed to you with postage, or a dollar for the office to mail it.
  • The signed, notarized original.

Mailed packages follow the same rules, so include the certification from the start. A call to 910-671-3040 can settle questions about a specific filing, and the county also hosts online deed search tools through its records page.

Recording fees

These are statewide figures from G.S. 161-10, the same across North Carolina. Fifteen pages of an ordinary instrument cost $26, and each added page is $4. Loan documents get 35 pages for $64. Recording a loan cancellation is free.

Plats cost $21 per sheet. A certified copy starts at $5, with $2 for each added page. A document in nonstandard form adds $25, and each extra instrument in the same packet adds $10. Fees are paid before filing, so budget for them at closing, along with the mailing fee if it applies.

Who pays the deed excise tax?

The seller pays it, under G.S. 105-228.30. The transferor pays the register before filing, at a dollar for each $500 of value, with any fraction counted as a whole $500.

Half stays with Robeson County. The rest goes to the state revenue department every month after refunds, and the county may keep 2 percent of that state half. A parcel split between counties is taxed where more of its value sits.

Your closing attorney should print the amount on your settlement statement. If you want a figure early, give the register's staff the sale price.

Property taxes and your sale

Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 owes for the year, and a later sale does not clear the seller's liability. Proration is a private agreement between buyer and seller, and the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer.

To be safe, ask for payment to the tax collector at closing. If the new bill isn't due yet, the collector takes a prepayment based on the previous year's rate. A past-due bill on a property that sold during the year can result in both names being advertised.

The tax office that issues the certification is the same one to ask about your balance, so a single call can cover both.

Parcel numbers and online payments

The tax administrator's Land Records and Mapping section assigns each tract a parcel identification number. Other county departments use it for owner, acreage, value and zoning. The GIS and Addressing section sits in the same division. Quote the parcel number when you contact the tax office about certification, so staff can pull the right record.

The tax office also accepts online and phone payments. The phone line is 1-866-249-0705, and a convenience fee applies.

  • Parcel number: ask the mapping section or find it on your tax bill.
  • Real property: listed permanently, so no annual listing is needed.
  • Bills: mailed in August and due September 1.

Before closing, make sure the tax figure the buyer's attorney requests matches what the collector tells you. Keep the payment confirmation with your closing file, along with the certification the tax office gave for the deed.

Other filings that can accompany a sale

A satisfaction clears your mortgage, and the office charges nothing to record it. Under G.S. 47-18, options, contracts to convey, leases past three years and rights of first refusal bind later buyers only when registered. Under Chapter 47H, an owner-financed contract for deed or a memorandum of it must be recorded within five business days.

  • Check that your payoff results in a recorded satisfaction.
  • Keep copies of every recorded paper.
  • Ask whether a plat or easement affects the lot.

A closing attorney can list every document headed to the register before the day arrives. If you're selling without one, write your own list and check each item off as it is recorded.

Speeding up recording

Contact the tax office for certification as soon as the deed is drafted, not on closing day. The certification has to be in hand before the register will accept the paper. Confirm that the deed carries a return address and that an envelope or postage is ready.

After filing, follow up with the register to confirm the book and page, and ask the title company or attorney for a copy of the recorded deed. Keep the receipt for fees and the excise tax with your closing papers. If anything comes back to you, read the reason first. The usual causes are missing tax certification or a missing return address.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can Robeson County register of deeds staff advise me on a deed?

No. State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it has no forms. Take drafting questions to an attorney before the signing.

What if a deed is mailed to Robeson County without certification?

The office returns it to the sender. Every deed needs tax certification or the delinquent tax statement before it can be recorded.

How do I get tax certification for a Robeson deed?

Email deeds@robesoncountync.gov, mail the document to the Tax Department at 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton, or phone 910-671-3060 for instructions.

Does Robeson County charge for mailing back a recorded deed?

Yes, $1.00, when you record in person and bring no addressed, stamped return envelope. The document must also carry a return name and mailing address.

Does the seller or the buyer owe the excise tax in Robeson County?

The seller does. The tax is $1.00 per $500 of value and is paid to the register before the deed is recorded.
