Where the Register of Deeds is and what it does

The office is at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, Reidsville, NC 27320. Phone 336-342-8820, fax 336-342-6209. It is open weekdays, and it takes documents for recording until 4:30 p.m. on days the county is open.

Staff describe the office as a recording agency. They do not draft documents, fill in forms or search title, so a Rockingham County seller normally relies on a closing attorney to prepare the deed and carry it to the counter. For any question about legal forms, consult an attorney.

What a deed needs before it will be recorded

The office posts a checklist, and a deed that skips an item can be refused or hit with an added fee. These items matter most in a house sale:

  • Page one names whoever drafted the deed, a person or a law firm.
  • Page one also carries the buyer's mailing address, because the tax office uses it for billing.
  • Notarized papers show the acknowledgment, the notary's official seal and the date that commission ends.
  • Conveyances show the excise stamp amount on their face. If nothing is owed, the signer writes NTC, short for no taxable consideration.
  • No Social Security, bank account, card, passport or license numbers may appear, except the final four digits where the law demands an identifier.
  • Mail-ins need a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a return envelope with a stamp. A bounced check costs $25.

Your attorney usually handles all of this, but check it yourself on a family deed, a deed into a trust, or a sale with no attorney.

Formatting rules

Rockingham County enforces the statewide standard in G.S. 161-14, and a document that misses it picks up a $25 surcharge. The standards call for letter or legal paper, black ink on white, a clear three-inch strip across the top of the first sheet and a quarter inch of white space around everything else.

Beneath that strip, page one states what kind of instrument it is. Print must be nine points or larger and appear on a single side. Pen may fill blanks or make corrections. Satisfactions, cancellations, military discharges and separately recorded plats (governed by G.S. 47-30) are exempt. The register may overlook a slightly small font if it copies cleanly, but stay above nine points.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Rockingham County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

The county's fee page tracks the state statute and adds practical items such as copies. These lines matter to a house seller:

Selected Rockingham County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceFee
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 per page or fraction
Multiple instruments in one document$10.00 for each added instrument
Parties above 20 in one instrument$2.00 for each extra party
SatisfactionsNo fee
State excise tax on conveyances$2.00 per thousand ($1.00 up to $500.00)
Certified land record copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 later pages
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

The same schedule prices passports, marriage licenses and vital records, which have no bearing on a sale. Plat copies of 18 by 24 inches or larger run $3.00 a page uncertified.

How the deed excise tax is figured

Divide the sale price into $500 slices and charge $1 per slice, counting a partial slice as a whole one. A price that lands between two $500 marks is rounded up to the next one before the math.

The grantor reports and pays the tax at the register before the deed is accepted, so it normally appears among the seller's charges at settlement. The county keeps half of the revenue in its general fund and passes the rest to the state. Ask your closing attorney for the figure before the closing date, so there are no surprises on the settlement statement. If the deed carries NTC, no stamp amount is owed.

Processing order and the 4:30 cutoff

The office processes in-person filings first, then e-recordings, then priority mail such as UPS or FedEx, then regular mail. Each item has to be opened, reviewed and found acceptable before it is recorded.

The 4:30 p.m. cutoff applies to paper and electronic filings alike. Anyone already in line at 4:30 is served that day. Later arrivals wait until another day. If the exact recording date carries real weight, hand the instrument over at the counter and stay until it is recorded.

E-recording is accepted during business hours. It has three benefits: the recorded document comes back right away, nobody has to travel, and a rejection is flagged immediately. Ask the office for its list of approved e-recording vendors.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Rockingham County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Looking up land records and mortgage releases

The E-Vault is the county's public search site for land records. For 1789 through 1995 the official index is the paper index inside the office, with scanned copies under an Old Index Books tab. From 1996 on, the electronic database in the office is the official index. Vital records are not in the E-Vault, and website records are unofficial, so the office holds the official set.

Fresh filings appear first in a temporary index shown in red entries and move to the permanent index, in blue, after full indexing. Use fewer characters in the search fields for better results.

When a loan is paid off, the lender must file a satisfaction. Recording a satisfaction is free, but reference only one original instrument per satisfaction to avoid a $25 charge for each extra reference. A payoff does not create a new deed. You can pull a copy of the satisfaction from the E-Vault or at the office.

Checklist before closing

Confirm that every old loan shows a recorded satisfaction and that the vesting deed matches the name on the contract. A missing release is the most common snag, and a buyer's title insurer will ask for it.

  • Search the E-Vault for the last deed and any deed of trust on the parcel.
  • Ask the lender about any loan paid off years ago with no release showing.
  • Confirm that the grantee's mailing address and the drafter's name are on the deed.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed goes by e-recording or in person at Reidsville.

Under North Carolina law a deed carries no weight against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on the record of the county holding the parcel, and rank follows registration time. That is why buyers push for same-day recording after funds move.

Frequently asked questions

When should I arrive to record a deed in Rockingham County?

Arrive before 4:30 p.m. on a weekday. That is when the office stops taking documents for recording, and a later arrival is not recorded that day.

Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Rockingham County?

No, recording a satisfaction is free. The county charges $25 for each extra reference when one satisfaction document points to more than one original instrument, so list only one.

Does Rockingham County accept recording by mail?

Yes. Send the original with a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds plus a stamped return envelope, never cash. Regular mail is handled after in-person, electronic and priority-mail items.

How is the deed excise tax calculated in Rockingham County?

The seller pays $1 per $500 of price, rounding up to the next $500. It is paid at the register before the deed is accepted.

Does the Rockingham County register of deeds search title for me?

No. The office is a recording agency and cannot help complete forms or run a title search. Hire an attorney or title agent for that, and use the E-Vault for your own look at the record.

What the Register of Deeds does

The register is responsible for the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of every public record recorded in the office. For a house seller, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the deed of trust that secures a loan both live there.

The office offers more than land records. You can order certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates online, where identity is verified through an online system and a vendor adds a small convenience fee. It is also a passport acceptance facility. Families settling an estate often need death certificates to support a deed or probate filing, and the same counter serves buyers, lenders and heirs.

E-recording

Rowan County started electronic recording in August 2010 and accepts electronically submitted documents, maps included. It helps banks, title companies, law firms and other businesses in real estate deals.

E-recording offers these benefits:

  • No travel time or travel cost to reach the counter
  • No check writing, since fees are handled electronically
  • Document security
  • Real-time tracking of document status
  • A quick return of the recording information and a stamped image
  • An easy start for new users

An individual seller does not usually sign up for this. The closing attorney or title company handling your sale will already use a vendor from the county's vendor list.

Property Check fraud alerts

Property Check emails or texts you when a filing appears under a name or parcel number you register. The register does not decide whether a document is genuine, so a fraudulent paper that meets statutory recording requirements and has the fees paid can still enter the record.

The service is free, runs around the clock and sends alerts through the contact method you pick. It can't block a bad filing, only warn you quickly. If you suspect fraud, call local law enforcement. Owners of vacant or inherited houses gain the most, because nobody is otherwise looking at the record. Questions on the system go to 704-216-8636. Register every name you have used on the title and every parcel number you own, and pick the contact method you actually check each day.

Recording a map or survey

Have the Rowan County Review Officer sign the map first, then bring it to the register on one of three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches or 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers work in the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

You get the original back after recording, and the office keeps a digital copy. Ask about electronic map recording. If your lot sits in a recorded subdivision or you hold a recorded survey, a copy costs $2 at the register's counter. Sellers sometimes order one to settle a boundary question before a buyer orders a survey. Bring the recorded map's book and page reference if you have it, and the counter staff can find the copy faster.

Recording fees and excise tax

The state sets one fee schedule for every county, so these amounts apply in Rowan County as they do elsewhere, and the seller covers the excise tax.

Statutory charges at the Rowan County register
ChargeAmount
General instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages
Added pages$4.00 each

Excise tax$1.00 for each $500 or fractional part

The tax is collected up front, before recording. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and a parcel that spans two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value. The statute makes the recording fees complete and exclusive.

Why recording order matters

A conveyance, option or long lease has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it reaches the public record of the county that holds the parcel. Time of registration sets the ranking between competing instruments.

Closing attorneys therefore hold funds until the deed is ready to go on the record. Ask yours to confirm that earlier mortgages were released and that any transfer from an heir or ex-spouse already appears in the Rowan County record. If a release or transfer is missing, fix it before the closing date, because the buyer's lender will not fund against a gap in the chain of title.

Selling an inherited house

A death transfer starts with the court clerk, not the register. Plan on extra time for this step, because the buyer cannot close until the authority to sign is in order. When a small estate has no will, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk of the person's home county after waiting 30 days. The limit is $20,000 of personal property, or up to $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the sole heir, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property owned.

Estates above those limits need a personal representative named by the court. After that, the paper that shows who can sign the deed is what the register records, so ask a probate attorney before listing. A buyer's title insurer will want the right authority on record, and Property Check can watch the parcel while the house sits empty.

After the deed is recorded

The Tax Assessor's office updates ownership for billing, and the register's office keeps the recorded image. The Tax Assessor page lists a separate land records contact, so a new owner who doesn't get a tax bill should reach out there. Rowan County Tax Administration also publishes a parcel map tool for checking boundaries and parcel numbers.

Recording is the moment the deed becomes public. After that, the real work is the tax proration at closing and any bill for the year that arrives in the buyer's name. The register and the assessor each handle half of the paper trail.

What to check at the register before listing

Pull the recorded deed that put the property in your name, then confirm that the names, the legal description and the parcel number match your sale contract. Rowan County offers an online document search for land records, so you can check this before you call anyone.

  • Search for the vesting deed and read the names exactly as recorded.
  • Look for each deed of trust and confirm a satisfaction was recorded after payoff.
  • Check for easements, rights of way or an old recorded map that affects the lot.
  • Sign up for Property Check if the house will sit empty during the sale.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed will go in by e-recording or by hand.

Fix problems early. A gap such as a deed from a deceased owner or an unreleased lien can add weeks to a closing, and cash buyers value a clean record as much as any other buyer.

When did Rowan County start electronic recording?

The Rowan County Register of Deeds began electronic recording in August 2010, and the office accepts electronically submitted documents including maps.

Yes. You create an account, list a name or parcel number and choose how to be alerted when a filing is recorded.

Which map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?

The register accepts 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches. The Rowan County Review Officer must sign before the map goes to the register.

Who pays the excise tax on a Rowan County deed?

The seller, as transferor, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price.

A copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.

Where the office is and when it's open

The Rutherford County Register of Deeds works from 229 North Main Street in Rutherfordton. Postal mail goes to Post Office Box 551, Rutherfordton, NC 28139. The counter is staffed from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted.

Two phone lines are published: 828-287-6155 for the main desk and 828-287-6195 for the record room. Holdings reach back into the 1700s, which helps anyone selling a family tract that has changed hands many times.

Most sellers never visit in person, because the attorney or title agent delivers the deed. If you do go, bring the original signed and notarized deed, the tax clearance and a way to pay the fee. Still, a rejected deed delays the closing and the payout, so the rules are worth knowing.

Records the office keeps

The register's collection covers a wide range of public records:

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust, with their cancellations
  • Assumed names and powers of attorney
  • Road maintenance agreements and plats
  • Separation agreements and similar filings

An online index lets you search by name. A separate alert tool named Property Check emails you when something new is filed against a name or parcel you choose. Heirs watching a house that sits empty can use it to spot an unexpected lien or a forged transfer early. It costs nothing to set up, and it is worth doing as soon as you decide to sell a house nobody lives in.

Deed formatting rules

Section 161-14 sets layout rules that a deed must meet on the page. Hold your draft up against each one:

  • Page one of a deed or deed of trust carries the preparer's name.
  • Paper is 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Page one keeps its upper three inches empty, and every other edge needs at least half an inch of white space.
  • Text prints black on white, at 9 points or larger, on one side of each sheet.
  • The kind of instrument is spelled out across the head of page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked in by hand. Having your attorney read the draft before signing is the cheapest way to dodge a rejected filing.

Delinquent taxes and recording

Late property tax will stop a deed from recording. Section 161-10(a)(19), effective October 1, 2011, makes payment of delinquent taxes a condition of recording.

A tax lien explains the rule. Under section 105-355 it fastens to the property on the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs fasten with it. If the debt goes unpaid, a foreclosure auction can follow, and a person who redeems before confirmation must pay all of it (section 105-374).

Request a written balance for every parcel from the Rutherford County revenue office before you sign a contract, so your attorney can clear it from the sale money. Do it early, since a balance you learn about on closing day can postpone the recording and the payout.

Recording fees

The statewide schedule in section 161-10 governs. On top of that, military discharges are recorded free and satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no charge.

Recording charges at the Rutherford County desk
DocumentFee
Standard instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00 flat
Standard instrument, each page after 15$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64.00 flat
Mortgage or deed of trust, each page after 35$4.00
Deed of trust satisfactionNone
Military dischargeNone
Plat sheet$21.00

These are the only charges, and they are due before anything is filed.

Deed excise tax

The charge is one dollar per $500 of price or value, with leftover dollars rounded up to the next $500 block. The seller settles it before the deed is filed (section 105-228.30). The county keeps one half and the state receives the other.

A sale for cash is a transfer for value, so the tax is owed. Your attorney can show it as a separate line item.

Land that spans two counties is taxed in whichever county holds more of the value. If your Rutherford tract crosses a county line, raise it with your attorney early.

The statute also lets the county retain a small slice of the state half as an allowance, which is bookkeeping between governments.

Getting a tax balance

The county revenue department answers tax bill questions at 828-287-6000. It sits at 145 College Avenue, Suite A, Rutherfordton, NC 28139, with counter hours of half past eight to five. A collections email address is posted on the department page.

All tax bills are due September 1 each year, and payment by January 5 avoids interest and enforced collection. Mailed payments are honored by postmark through that date. Cash or check payments are taken at the tax office. Online payment runs through a third-party service that adds its own fees.

The department page also offers a search for tax bill information, a link to registered vehicle tax receipts, and a list of delinquent tax bills. Pull your parcel's bill and ask for a payoff before your closing attorney orders the deed. Keep the payoff letter and the paid receipt together, because the title company will ask for both.

A tax rate document is posted too. Because the total bill depends on the fire district and town where the house sits, ask the office which rates apply to your parcel instead of assuming a countywide figure. Have the parcel number ready when you call.

Assumed business names for landlords

The register of deeds records assumed business name certificates, the doing-business-as forms that tell the public a person or firm trades under a particular name in one county or in all 100 North Carolina counties. The recording fee is $26.00.

An online option exists for businesses located in Rutherford County, with a $15.00 service fee added to the recording fee. Landlords with rentals should make sure the business name used on their leases is still on file.

Electronic filing and why timing matters

E-recording through Simplifile began in the office on April 24, 2018, with plats added on February 1, 2022. Microfilming began January 1, 2017.

Speed matters because registration time sets rank. A deed or long lease binds lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the moment it is registered, and the earlier filing wins (section 47-18). When a buyer's lender and a seller's lender both file on closing day, a same-day electronic filing keeps your deal clean.

Anyone unsure about a particular document can call the main desk at 828-287-6155 before sending it. Ask your attorney or title agent which method they will use, and when you can expect the recorded copy back, so you know when the buyer officially holds title.

Frequently asked questions

What days is the Rutherford County recorder open?

Half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. The main line is 828-287-6155. Calling first avoids a wasted trip on a holiday week.

Is filing a deed of trust satisfaction free in Rutherford County?

Yes. No charge applies to satisfactions, and state law agrees. Make sure your lender files one after payoff.

Who owes deed excise tax when a Rutherford County house sells?

The seller does. Section 105-228.30 sets one dollar per $500, collected ahead of filing, and the settlement statement should show it as its own entry.

Can overdue taxes hold up my Rutherford County deed?

Yes. Under section 161-10(a)(19), back taxes come first. Obtain the balance from the revenue office and pay it at closing.

Does Rutherford County take electronic recordings?

Yes. E-recording via Simplifile started April 24, 2018, and plat e-recording started February 1, 2022. Title companies and attorneys generally use it.

What the Register of Deeds keeps

Sampson County's Register of Deeds is the official custodian of records for county residents, keeping a permanent, standardized record of who owns real estate and how it changed hands. The office files deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and miscellaneous real estate papers.

Vital records share the same counter: birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges, and the commission records of notaries public. The office also swears in notaries.

The county site points to online access for these records. Start there for the index search before you phone anyone, and write down the book and page of each deed you find. A homeowner who inherited a Sampson County house can trace each recorded deed back through the chain of owners and confirm every name is spelled the same way, which saves trouble when a title company runs its search.

Legal advice and deed drafting

The office can't explain how to fill out a deed. It is a recording office alone, and state law forbids the register of deeds and staff from practicing law. They will not provide legal forms, walk you through completing one, or comment on what a filed paper does legally.

The work divides like this on a Sampson County sale:

  • An attorney drafts the deed and answers wording questions.
  • A title agent or closing attorney searches the chain of title and arranges loan payoffs.
  • The register of deeds checks each paper against recording rules, takes the charge, and indexes it.

When a house came to you through a family arrangement, see an attorney first. A recorder can't repair a deed that was written wrongly, and a rejected filing means a delay at the closing table.

Errors an attorney tends to catch include a misspelled seller name, a missing preparer line on page one, and a land description at odds with the mapped parcel. Sorting those out before closing costs far less than a corrective deed afterward, and it keeps your buyer's lender from pausing the funding.

Filing charges

Section 161-10 sets the schedule the register applies, and the statute treats it as the whole list. Payment comes first, so request a combined total when several papers go in together.

Statewide filing charges applied in Sampson County
Document or serviceCharge
Most instruments, pages 1 through 15$26.00 flat
Most instruments, page 16 onward$4.00 each
Deed of trust or mortgage, pages 1 through 35$64.00 flat
Deed of trust or mortgage, page 36 onward$4.00 each
Cancelling a deed of trustFree

Certified copy, later pages$2.00 each
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra

After closing, request a certified copy of the recorded deed, because lenders, heirs and later buyers tend to ask for it. Keep it with your closing papers, along with the receipt for the filing charge and the excise tax.

Who pays the excise tax

Sellers pay. A deed conveying an interest in land carries a levy of $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 block counted whole. The transferor remits it to the recorder before filing (section 105-228.30).

One half goes to Sampson County's general fund. The rest flows to the state, after refunds and a small collection allowance. For land in more than one county, the county with the greater value collects.

Check that the tax shows on its own line of your closing statement, so your net proceeds are no surprise. If you split costs with the buyer by contract, put the allocation in writing, since the statute assigns the tax to the transferor by default.

Recording order and buyer protection

Section 47-18 ties a deed, option, first refusal right or lease over three years to the moment of registration. Until then it does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value. Order of registration sets rank. That is why closing instructions usually call for same-day filing, and why delay can cost a buyer first position.

Filing the buyer's deed and the new lender's deed of trust together gives that buyer first position. For the seller, a recorded cancellation of the old mortgage clears the index. Forgotten, uncancelled liens can resurface and slow a later sale. Ask your lender to confirm in writing that the cancellation has been sent for recording, then check the index a few days later.

Unpaid property tax on a parcel

Section 105-355 makes unpaid tax a lien as of the listing date, together with penalties, interest and costs. The county may pursue it through a court action patterned on a mortgage foreclosure (section 105-374).

If it comes to that, the parcel is auctioned at the courthouse door. The sale is reported within three days, exceptions or a raised bid can be filed for ten days after that, and anyone redeeming before confirmation pays the tax along with penalties, interest and costs.

Online tools for sellers

The county runs several web tools next to the recorder's index, each useful before listing:

  • The GIS Data Viewer searches by owner name, address or parcel ID and shows property layers, maps and reports.
  • The Property Record Search draws on the Tax Department's database for the parcel.
  • The Tax Bills site lets you search, view and pay a bill.
  • The Development Services Portal covers building inspection, planning and zoning and environmental health, with permit applications and status checks.

Use the GIS viewer to confirm the parcel ID and acreage match your deed. Check the permit portal for open permits or unfinished work tied to the address, which an inspector for the buyer could uncover.

Public record requests are handled under Chapter 132 of the General Statutes. Anything the register keeps is public, so assume anyone, a title examiner included, can read what you recorded.

Tax bills and town levies on a sale

The county tax office collects for the county, fire and school districts and, at present, for Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland. The address is PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, and the phone is (910) 592-8146.

County bills fall due on September 1, with a 2 percent discount for payment by August 31. Parcels still unpaid are listed in a newspaper notice, normally early in April. Your closing attorney needs the current balance for the parcel before anything is sent to the recorder, so request it as soon as you have a contract. A balance that is paid or prorated at the table keeps the recording from stalling.

Frequently asked questions

Can the Sampson County Register of Deeds give legal advice about a deed?

No. The office exists to record documents, and the law bars staff from practicing law. They cannot supply forms, explain how to complete them or discuss what a filing means.

What excise tax applies to a Sampson County deed?

It is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, paid by the transferor before filing under section 105-228.30. The county general fund gets half, and the state gets the rest.

What is the standard filing charge in Sampson County?

Under section 161-10, $26.00 covers an ordinary instrument through page 15, with $4.00 for every page past that. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through page 35. Cancelling one costs nothing.

What else does the Sampson County office handle?

Birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges and notary records, plus notary oaths.

Why file a deed promptly after closing in Sampson County?

Registration fixes priority. Under section 47-18, a conveyance binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from registration, so quick filing protects the buyer's position.

Where Scotland County land records are kept

Land records for Scotland County sit with its Register of Deeds, the custodian of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats and other legal papers. The same staff issue birth and death certificates and marriage licenses, and they file military discharges.

A home sale there ends with the buyer's deed landing in this office. The department's page keeps the research tools in one spot, so a seller can read the public trail on a parcel before any offer arrives. Reading it first helps you spot an old easement, an unreleased loan or a misspelled name while there is still time to fix it.

Search tools for deeds and plats

The county splits its tools by era and by purpose:

  • One index covers 1978 to the present together with every plat, and you enter it by signing in as a guest.
  • A second search holds pre-1978 documents at a new web address.
  • The Laurinburg and Scotland County GIS map often shows an owner's name and usually a book and page cite for the deed.
  • A tax foreclosure listing is reachable from the department page, where you scroll to the Scotland County entries.
  • PropertyCheck lets you save names and receive a notice when a filing appears.

For rights of way from before 1978, email the references to the office. Bring book and page numbers if you are chasing an old easement across a lot.

What the recorder checks before accepting a deed

The recorder reviews each instrument against statutory prerequisites and the state's Document Standards. The usual ones:

  • Papers are normally originals bearing original signatures and proof of notarization.
  • A North Carolina deed or deed of trust names its drafter, a person or a law firm, on page one.
  • Fees are collected before filing, unless a statute lets the paper be recorded free.
  • A transfer of real property, other than a mortgage or deed of trust, must state the excise tax owed by the grantor.

Staff may not practice law, so they can't help prepare a deed or discuss its legal meaning. Take drafting questions to an attorney. This matters most when a house passed through a family transfer, since the wording of an older deed can affect who is able to sign now.

Unpaid taxes and recording

Unpaid taxes can keep a deed out of the records. Since July 1, 2020, a deed moving real property is turned away unless the Scotland County tax collector has certified that no delinquent county, municipal or other collector-charged taxes are a lien on the land.

An alternative wording is allowed. The deed may carry a line saying a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the collector by the closing attorney when closing money is disbursed. That clause is why local closings tend to route through an attorney's trust account.

Before listing, ask the collector for a payoff on each parcel. Get it in writing and hand a copy to your closing attorney, so the certificate or the attorney's statement can be handled without a last-minute scramble. Tax foreclosures for the county appear in the listing the register of deeds links to.

Recording and excise tax costs

Several transfers owe no excise tax: gifts, intestacy, a lease for a term of years, a merger or consolidation, operation of law, and transfers under a will. State statute states the rate as one dollar per $500, which works out to the same $2 per $1000 (section 105-228.30).

Privacy of recorded documents

Once a paper is recorded in the real property books it becomes a public record that anyone may inspect and copy. Because the county posts images online, filers should leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver license, passport, bank account or card numbers, and PIN codes, unless a law or court order requires it or all but the last four digits are redacted.

Anyone can ask in writing to have such data removed from an online image. The request must name the information, identify the document, and say where in the document it appears. No fee is charged for a redaction request, and a person who requests a redaction without authority commits an infraction punishable by a fine up to $500 per violation.

If you spot your own account number on an old filing, send that written request through the register of deeds.

Why recording order matters in a sale

A deed or lease running more than three years binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land sits, and priority follows the order of registration (section 47-18).

That makes same-day filing of the buyer's deed and the lender's deed of trust the normal practice. On the seller's side, a payoff should be followed by a recorded satisfaction, which carries no fee. Keep the recorded deed's book and page numbers with your files, and ask the office to correct the index if a number looks wrong. A buyer's title examiner will use those same numbers to confirm that your deed is the one in the chain of title.

What to bring when you contact the office

Staff can prepare records faster when you call before visiting. A short checklist keeps the call productive:

  • The owner's name as it appears on the deed, and the book and page if the GIS map gave you one.
  • The street address or parcel, if you are tracing a boundary or easement.
  • For a filing, the original signed instrument with proof of notarization and the preparer's name on page one.
  • A way to pay the recording fee, since fees are due before the paper is filed.

Questions about what a document means or whether it is valid go to an attorney, because the office can't give legal advice. The staff can still tell you whether a paper meets the recording prerequisites and which index holds it.

Marriage licenses and vital records

Applicants complete a county form and then call 910-277-2575 to schedule an appointment. A license isn't valid until signed by the applicants and by staff in the office, lasts 60 days, and covers marriages in North Carolina only.

Birth and death certificates and marriage licenses can be picked up after a call ahead, or ordered by mail through an online request that is processed the day it is received.

$2 per $1000, owed by the grantor, which matches the state rate of one dollar per $500. Gifts, intestacy and transfers under a will are among the exempt transfers.

Yes. Since July 1, 2020, a real property deed needs the tax collector's certificate of no delinquent taxes, or an attorney's statement that back taxes will be paid from closing funds.

No. The office is barred from practicing law and cannot help prepare documents. An attorney should draft it and be named on the first page as preparer.

Where to find the Register of Deeds in Albemarle

Albemarle is the seat of a county of roughly 395 square miles with over 42,000 parcels and ten municipalities. Whether your house stands in Oakboro, Norwood, Locust or Badin, its deed lands in this one set of books.

What must happen before a deed is accepted for recording?

A Tax Certification Form has to travel with the deed, and the collector's stamp reading "Checked By Tax Collector" must be on the deed before the register can take it. The form moves through three stages, shown below.

Who covers the deed tax when a Stanly County house sells?

The seller. The rate is one dollar for each $500.00 of price, rounding a remainder up, and the register collects it before filing. The county keeps half and sends half to the state.

Closing attorneys subtract it from proceeds, so it appears as a single line on your settlement statement.

Why filing order matters

Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, or a lease longer than three years, cannot bind lien creditors or paying buyers until it is registered where the land sits. The first to file generally ranks first.

  • Obtain a recorded release from your lender after payoff.

How the tax bill affects a closing

An unpaid balance holds up the collector's stamp, so the tax position of the parcel comes first. Stanly bills mail in late July or early August, a 1% discount applies to payment before September 1, and January 5 is the last day to pay without interest. How to challenge a value

Call 704-986-3631 and ask for an informal review by a certified appraiser, which can raise, lower or keep your value. Still unhappy? File with the five-member review board the commissioners appoint, which normally sits in April.

That board starts from the view that the county's number is right, so bring proof: an appraisal dated to the last reappraisal, a broker's market analysis, nearby comparable sales, photos of serious defects, or a sketch if the dimensions on file are wrong. Because a sale triggers repayment, request the payoff in writing.

Permits and map records tied to a sale

The mapping office keeps the county base map and ownership data, drawn from deeds and plats filed with the register. Property search runs through the county GIS site.

If you made repairs or additions before listing, Central Permitting handles building inspections, planning and zoning, and environmental health from one place. Permit requests and inspections go through an online platform, and no application is processed without a street address. Inside the City of Albemarle, Richfield or Oakboro, the town issues the address, so call the town first.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Zoning and housing rules a buyer may ask about

Planning and Zoning sits at Stanly County Commons, 1000 North First Street, Suite 20, Albemarle, phone 704-986-3660. Its ordinances cover zoning, subdivisions, watershed protection and floodplain management, plus a minimum housing ordinance with a complaint form. It also offers a short term rental application, home occupation permits, rezoning and variance forms, and an abandoned manufactured home program.

A free review committee meets on the first and third Wednesdays so owners can talk a project through with several departments before applying. A buyer planning a rental, a home business or a split of the lot will ask about these rules, so having answers ready helps a sale move.

Farm and forest land: present use value

Present use value taxes qualifying land on its productive use. Agriculture needs ten acres in crops or livestock for commercial sale and an average gross income of $1,000 over the prior three years. Horticulture needs five acres with the same income test, and forestry needs twenty acres under a written management plan. Wildlife land must be twenty to one hundred acres under a conservation plan.

All tracts on one application must have identical ownership. Call 704-986-3630 with questions, and ask how a sale changes enrollment before you list rural acreage.

A short checklist for recording day

Bring the signed deed, the Tax Certification Form with the top section filled in, and payoff paperwork for any loan being retired. Have the closer confirm that the grantor name matches the prior deed, that the deed tax line is on the settlement statement and that a release will be recorded for the old mortgage.

If you are selling an inherited house, ask your attorney which estate papers the register will expect with the deed.

Frequently asked questions

Does Albemarle charge more than other North Carolina counties?

No. The base amounts are set by statute for every county: $26.00 covering 15 pages of an ordinary instrument, then $4.00 per extra page.

What has to be stamped on a Stanly County deed first?

The Tax Collector must stamp it "Checked By Tax Collector" after confirming no delinquent tax, using the county's Tax Certification Form.

Who writes the check for the deed tax in Stanly County?

The seller, at the register's counter before recording. The charge is one dollar per $500.00 of price, with any remainder counted as another block.

Where do I request a birth or death certificate copy in Albemarle?

At the Register of Deeds window in the Courthouse, 201 South Second Street, weekdays from 8:30 until 5.

When does Stanly tax start accruing interest?

January 6. The charge is 2% for that month and 0.75% for every month afterward.

How to reach the Stokes County Register of Deeds

Walk in at 1014 Main Street, Danbury, ZIP 27016, or write to P.O. Box 67. The office line is (336) 593-2414 and the fax is (336) 593-9360.

Stokes County Register of Deeds service windows

Recording documents8:30 to 4:45
Marriage license applicationsUntil 4:30

The recording window closes a quarter hour before the office does, so a deed delivered at ten to five likely waits until the next business day.

What this office does in a home sale

This office keeps, indexes and preserves land and vital records for the county. A typical sale produces three filings: the seller's deed, a deed of trust for the buyer's loan if there is one, and a release of the seller's old loan.

Stokes County was split off in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry County, so a title chain for land near the line may run into Surry's books, which go back to 1771.

Does a Stokes County deed need tax clearance first?

It does. Tax Administration requires that every deed offered for recording include its certification that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property being transferred (G.S. 161-31).

An unpaid bill therefore holds the deed back. The tax office shares the building and street address, so the errand is short, and it keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00. Ask for the current-year balance at the same visit, so you know what the closing attorney must pay from your proceeds before the register takes the deed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Stokes County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording costs in Danbury

The statute fixes the prices. A standard instrument is $26.00 for its first 15 pages, then $4.00 per page after that. Mortgages and deeds of trust begin at $64.00 and cover 35 pages. Recording a loan release is free.

A document that breaks the formatting rules adds $25.00, and each extra instrument in one filing adds $10.00. No other fees apply, and payment comes before filing. The seller's deed tax is a separate charge, also paid at this counter.

Why fast filing helps both sides

North Carolina ranks competing claims by the order of registration. Until a deed is registered where the property sits, it does not defeat lien creditors or paying buyers (G.S. 47-18).

The buyer wants priority. The seller wants a clean break, because claims against the buyer that arise afterward cannot reach back. Keep a copy showing the date and time of filing. If a late afternoon closing runs past 4:45, ask your attorney whether the deed can be filed first thing the next business day, and make sure no new liens or judgments are likely to land in the gap.

Installment land contracts

Yes, record them. Chapter 47H covers sales where the seller keeps title to a home of up to four units and the buyer makes at least five installments. The contract itself, or a memorandum of it, goes on file within five business days of signing, and the buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day.

  • A default notice must leave a cure period of at least 30 days.
  • Late charges stop at 4% and start only after 15 days.

If you sold this way years ago, check that the memorandum is indexed in Danbury.

What a seller can do before recording day

Go over this list with your closing attorney.

  • Verify the parcel on the county GIS site and the property record card.
  • Pick up the tax certification from the office down the hall.
  • Figure the deed tax from the sale price at $1.00 per $500.00.
  • Make sure an old mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Arrive before 4:45 on a weekday.

For title questions about an inherited or vacant house, speak with a North Carolina attorney, and call the register about document form.

When the owner has died

Small estates can skip full administration. An heir can wait 30 days and then file an affidavit with the superior court clerk in the decedent's home county, if personal property net of liens is under $20,000 (under $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the only heir). Every tract of land the person owned must be described in it.

Larger estates take the longer route. Either way, the deed that finally conveys the house is filed in Danbury with the tax certification, so bring the court papers.

What happens to a recorded deed of trust in a foreclosure?

A lender or trustee starts by filing a notice of hearing with the clerk of superior court. The clerk has to find a valid debt, a default and a right to foreclose. An owner can appeal that finding in 10 days by posting a bond of 1% of principal unless the judge lowers it.

After the sale is reported, upset bids must top the last one by 5% or $750 added, whichever is greater, with a deposit. A borrower who sells before the hearing usually keeps more equity, and the payoff ends with a release filed in Danbury.

The tax calendar and your deed

Stokes bills come due by January 5, with interest from January 6. The tax certification a deed needs reflects what the county's books show owed on the parcel at that moment, so a house sold in autumn, after bills go out, usually has an open current-year balance.

Plan to settle it at the closing table. Tax Administration can quote a figure, and the tax website lists property record cards and land and home values that confirm what the county has on file for your parcel.

Other offices at the Danbury address

The Administration Building at 1014 Main Street houses more than one office a seller will visit. Tax Administration is there, along with Planning and Inspections at (336) 593-2444, and the Finance Department, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 20.

  • Planning and Inspections keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and asks that permit applications arrive by 4:30 in the afternoon to be processed the same day.
  • The Finance Department takes calls at (336) 914-9188.
  • The Register of Deeds answers at (336) 593-2414.

One trip to Danbury can therefore cover the tax certification, a permit question and the recording itself.

A sample recording day

Do the errands in this order. Tax Administration comes first, because the certification must be in hand and any balance settled. Then go to the register with the signed deed, the filing fee and the deed tax payment, and ask for the stamp showing date and time. Hold on to the receipt.

A paid-off lender's release costs nothing to file, yet someone has to file it, so ask who will. The location of the house in the county affects permits and utilities, but every deed records in Danbury. Check the parcel on the county GIS site before you advertise the property, and keep the book and page reference once the deed is indexed.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds recording hours?

Recording runs from 8:30 to 4:45 on weekdays, with the general office open 8:30 to 5:00.

What is the mailing address for Stokes County deeds?

P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

Does a Stokes deed need tax clearance first?

Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property before the deed is offered for recording.

Who pays the deed tax in Danbury?

The seller pays at the register's window ahead of recording. The rate is one dollar for every $500.00 of price, and a leftover amount counts as another block.

Is a loan release free to record in Danbury?

Yes. State law sets no fee for filing a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.

Which office files deeds for Surry County land?

The Register of Deeds in Dobson. The office is at 201 East Kapp Street, with P.O. Box 303 for mail, and answers at (336) 401-8150. Every parcel in the county is recorded in this one office.

Walk-in hours differ by task. Counter service runs from 8:15 am to 5:00 pm, except Tuesday, when doors open at 9:00 am. Real estate filings stop at 4:30 pm, half an hour before closing time, so a late-afternoon courier run can slip to the following day. Faxed real estate paperwork has its own line, (336) 401-8149, distinct from the vital records fax.

Electronic recording

Surry County accepts it. The office takes e-recorded documents from two companies: Simplifile and Corporation Service Company.

Most title companies and closing attorneys already hold an account with one of them, so a closing can be recorded without anyone driving to Dobson. If you are selling without an attorney, ask the person handling your closing how the deed will be submitted. Simplifile's number is (800) 460-5657, and Corporation Service Company has a web address on the county's real estate page.

  • Electronic submission goes through an approved vendor, not directly through the county website.
  • Paper deeds can be delivered in person or mailed to the P.O. Box.
  • The real estate fax line is separate from the vital records fax line, so use (336) 401-8149 only for real estate matters.

Filing fees at the Dobson desk

Fees come from state law and are the same in every county. G.S. 161-10 sets the price of an ordinary instrument by page count and makes its fee list exclusive. Open the statute for the current schedule, and ask the Dobson office about any add-on for an oversized or nonstandard document.

A seller seldom writes this check, because the buyer's closing costs usually absorb recording. Your contract controls that point, so read it before closing day.

Who pays the excise tax when a Surry County house sells?

You do, as the seller. The deed stamp tax, found in G.S. 105-228.30, falls on the person transferring title and must reach the register before the deed is filed.

The amount rises with the price, so ask your closer for the exact line on the settlement statement instead of working it out yourself. Receipts are shared between the county and the State. If your acreage straddles a county line, the tax goes to the county holding the larger share of the value.

Why filing order protects a seller

Filing is what protects the buyer's title, and your clean exit with it. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, long lease, option or right of first refusal carries no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered, and the earlier filing wins.

So a signing is only half of a closing. Until the clerk stamps the deed into the record, someone with a claim against you could be placed ahead of your buyer. A same-day e-recording avoids the Tuesday late opening and the 4:30 pm cutoff entirely.

Once the deed is filed, request the book and page or instrument number from your title company. You or a future owner can use that reference in the online search.

Land records and how far back they go

The records start in 1771, the year Surry County was formed from Rowan County. The early collection includes deeds from agents of Lord Granville, state land grants, sheriff's deeds, mortgages and property divisions. Original books can be viewed or copied through the imaging system, and they also exist on microfilm and in book form. The oldest index covers 1771 to 1870, and a second index runs from 1870 to 1937.

Land that now sits in Stokes, Forsyth or Yadkin may appear in early Surry volumes. Online search and recording standards are linked from the real estate page.

If a title problem surfaces during a sale, a title examiner usually does this research. A seller can still look up the chain of ownership to find a missing release or an old easement.

Can personal information be removed from records online?

Yes, within limits. G.S. 132-1.10(f) allows certain personal identifiers to be redacted from the website copy of a record, and the county publishes a redaction request form.

The request must be in writing, signed by the requester or an agent with power of attorney, and must name the information and the document. Items that can be covered include Social Security numbers, driver's license and passport numbers, bank account numbers and card numbers or PINs. Only the website image changes. The official record kept in the deed vault stays as it was recorded.

This matters if you recorded an old deed that contains a number you would rather not have online. Call (336) 401-8150 before sending a request.

Housing context for a Surry County sale

The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $177,600, and owners live in 73.4% of homes. Median gross rent is $761 and median household income is $55,656. The county had 34,405 housing units in mid-2025, and builders pulled 244 permits during 2025.

Because stamp tax follows price, a sale at these values typically carries a modest tax line on the settlement statement.

What to bring to a Surry County closing

Bring identification, the signed deed, and payoff statements for any loan on the property. When a lender is paid off, its release is filed as a cancellation of the deed of trust, and state law charges nothing for that filing.

  • A deed that follows the recording standards linked on the county page.
  • Money or instructions covering the stamp tax.
  • Notarized authority if someone signs for you under a power of attorney.
  • The name of whoever will file the deed, by e-recording or over the counter.

Inherited homes add one step: ask the superior court clerk which estate papers must be on file before a buyer's attorney will accept the deed.

Timing a Surry County recording

Plan the day around the office clock. A deed that reaches the counter after 4:30 pm will wait for the next business day, and Tuesday mornings begin at 9:00 am. If your closing is late in the day, ask the closer to e-record through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company so the filing does not depend on a courier.

The property tax bill is a separate matter. Recording a deed does not change it, so settle the current year with your closer and ask the Surry County tax office for the amount.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Surry County deed office?

It is 201 East Kapp Street, Dobson, NC 27017, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 303 and a main phone of (336) 401-8150. Real estate filings are taken until 4:30 pm on weekdays.

Can my closing company e-record a deed in Surry County?

Yes, through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company, the two vendors the office accepts. Ask your closer which one they use.

Which party owes the stamp tax on a Surry County sale?

The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the deed stamp tax on whoever transfers title, payable ahead of recording.

How much does the register charge to record an ordinary deed?

The schedule is statewide and printed in G.S. 161-10. Ask the Dobson office for the figure that fits your page count.

Does recording a deed change the property tax bill?

No. The bill follows the parcel, not the recording. Settle the current year with your closer and ask the Surry County tax office for the amount.

Where is the Swain County Register of Deeds?

Staff are at the counter weekdays, 8:30 am until 5:00 pm. Marriage licenses stop half an hour sooner, at 4:30 pm. The office also has an email address, RegisterofDeeds@swaincountync.gov, for questions before you travel.

Swain County has 14,024 residents. Everyone with a deed to record, whether the parcel is in town or on a mountain road, uses this one counter.

What documents does the Swain County register take in?

The office records real property documents and also keeps the county's vital records. These categories cover nearly everything a seller will meet:

  • Deeds, contracts, leases, mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Cancellations of deeds of trust, maps and plats, and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed names, UCC filings, articles of incorporation and corporate mergers.
  • Bankruptcy orders, judgments, marriage settlements and military discharges.

The same office collects the revenue stamps, meaning the excise tax, on deeds being recorded. It also issues certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates. Certified vital record copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each. Those fees apply to vital records, so they are separate from the schedule for recording a deed.

Recording costs in Bryson City

Deed recording prices come from a single state schedule, G.S. 161-10, with a short list of per-page and per-document items. Swain County links a recording fee sheet and a document standards sheet from its register page, and both are worth reading before you send a paper deed.

Payment comes before filing. Sellers rarely write this check, because recording of the deed and the lender's security instrument normally sits with the buyer. Your purchase contract decides who bears it.

Who pays the deed stamps in a Swain County sale?

The amount appears on your settlement statement, and the closer carries it to Bryson City with the deed. It scales with the price, so request the exact number instead of estimating.

Swain County home values

The typical owner-occupied home in Swain County is valued at $207,000. Owners live in 72.7% of homes, and median rent is $742. The county had 8,951 housing units in July 2025, and permits totaled 94 for 2025. Households earn a median $52,349.

About 30.6% of residents identify as American Indian and Alaska Native alone. If a parcel has an unusual ownership history, ask your title company early what it needs to see. A clean chain of title at the register speeds up any closing.

Vital records and notary help for sellers

A seller settling an estate often needs a death certificate, and the register issues them. The county lists four ways to ask: upload a photo of your ID on its premium site, email a photo, fax a request, or mail it with a copy of your ID. In person, bring a state ID, driver license, military ID or passport.

Under G.S. 130A-93, those entitled to a certified copy include yourself, a spouse, a sibling, a child or step-child, a parent or step-parent, a grandparent or grandchild, and an authorized agent or attorney with proof. Requesting a record by fraud is a felony under G.S. 130A-26A.

The county tax office, in the same building, offers notary service for cash only, at $8.00 for the first signature, $9.00 for a second signer and $10.00 for more than two. The tax department closes for lunch from 1:30 to 2:00 and shuts at 4:30 pm. Call ahead before a signing trip.

Can I search Swain County land records online?

Yes. The county provides a remote access site for land records with two modes. The full system lets you search by grantor or grantee name, instrument number, or book and page. The imaging system only retrieves deed book images when you enter a book and page.

Online records are unofficial, and the official records are kept at the register's office. For a certified copy that a court or lender will accept, ask the office itself.

  • Search by name when you do not know the book and page.
  • Use book and page for a direct image of a known deed.
  • Take any reference from the online index to the counter if you need an official copy.

How the Swain County tax office ties in with a sale

The tax office sits in the same Courthouse Building, with a separate mailing address of P.O. Box 2321. It splits into an assessor side, which handles values and reappraisal, and a collections side, which handles payment and enforcement. Phone numbers run through (828) 488-9273.

Bills go out in July, fall due September 1, and begin collecting interest after January 5. G.S. 105-360 holds the interest schedule.

Swain County's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2021, on an eight-year cycle, and a revaluation contractor has been working in the Alarka community. Call the assessor to learn which year applies to you. The county tax page carries a disabled veteran exclusion form and a property tax relief application.

What your closer should confirm

Three things matter most: that the deed matches the legal description, that the excise tax amount is on the statement, and that outstanding property tax is settled. A buyer will expect unpaid property tax to be paid off, since G.S. 105-355 makes it a charge against the parcel.

  • Ask whether the buyer's lender needs a payoff letter from a prior mortgage.
  • Ask who will carry the signed deed to the register and by what date.
  • Request the recording book and page once the deed is filed.

If the house came through an estate, start with the court clerk. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes an affidavit route for small estates, and land questions belong with an attorney.

A quick plan for a Swain County sale

Call the register's office before you travel and confirm the counter hours. Pull the recording fee sheet and the document standards sheet from the county page, then have your closer prepare the deed to match. On closing day the closer brings the deed, the stamp tax and the filing fee to Bryson City, and the buyer's lender instrument goes in at the same visit. Afterward, ask for the book and page so you can find the deed in the online index.

Frequently asked questions

When can I visit the Swain County deed office?

Come between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm on a weekday to 101 Mitchell Street in Bryson City. License issuing ends 30 minutes earlier.

How do I search Swain County deeds online?

Use the county's remote access site, which offers a full system search by name, instrument number or book and page, plus an imaging-only mode. Those results are unofficial, so use the office for certified copies.

Which party covers the deed stamps in Swain County?

The seller does, ahead of recording, under G.S. 105-228.30. Your closer will show the figure on the statement.

What does a certified vital record copy cost in Swain County?

When are Swain County property taxes due?

September 1, with interest starting after January 5. Ask the Courthouse Building tax office for your bill.

Contacting the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds

The office is at 403 Main Street in Columbia, NC 27925. The mailing address is P.O. Box 449. Call (252) 796-2901 or fax (252) 796-0148.

Hours are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, closed on holidays. Time any visit inside those hours. If you plan to mail a deed, use the post office box and phone first, so the staff can tell you what else the package needs. A call before you drive or mail anything saves a second trip.

Tyrrell County is small and rural: 3,537 residents in mid-2025 on 390.78 square miles of land, about 8.3 people per square mile. The median owned home is valued at $164,500 and 77.8% of homes are owner-occupied. With so few sales in a year, a buyer's lender or a title company will look hard at the paperwork on any parcel, so a clean record helps your sale move.

What the office does

The Register of Deeds lets a property owner put the public on notice of an ownership interest. That public record protects later buyers and lenders from unknown transactions and hidden liens.

The records run from old land grants to modern deeds, maps, leases and agreements. The same counter also issues vital certificates and marriage licenses.

The office runs a Fraud Alert Notification Service. Register an email address and you get an automatic message whenever a recording looks possibly fraudulent. It is worth a few minutes if you own vacant land or a house you do not live in, since you are not at the parcel to notice anything odd.

Who pays the conveyance tax

The seller does. State law names the person transferring title as the one who pays the excise tax at the register's office, before the deed is recorded.

The statute sets a flat charge for each $500 of price or value, and any leftover amount counts as a full block. The county and the State share what comes in.

Do not estimate the dollar figure yourself. The attorney or title agent running your closing reads it off the settlement statement. If you are filing without one, the Columbia counter can help.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tyrrell County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

Fees for recording come from the General Statutes, so Tyrrell County has no local schedule of its own. If your paperwork is out of the ordinary, check with the Columbia staff before mailing. Pay when you hand the document over.

Charges that can apply to a Tyrrell County recording
Recording itemFee
Basic instrument, first 15 pages$26.00
Each added page$4.00
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each after
Release of a mortgage lienFree of charge
Deed excise taxPer $500 block of value

A mortgage payoff produces a release, and that filing costs nothing. Ask your closer to confirm the release is recorded so the old lien clears from the public record.

Inherited or long-distance property

Owners who inherit land here sometimes live far away. If the property came to you from a relative, ask a title company to review the chain of title before you list it or accept an offer, and keep any estate paperwork together with the deed.

A few steps make a distance sale easier: sign up for the register's fraud alert, get a clear title review, and line up a local contact who can handle the closing details. Paper mail and phone calls still work well in this county, so you do not have to depend on e-recording alone.

Why recording matters after you sell

G.S. 47-18 leaves an unregistered deed exposed to creditors and to later purchasers who paid value. Whichever deed gets filed at the county office first generally wins priority.

If your deed is not recorded, a creditor with a claim against you, or a second buyer, could end up ahead of the purchaser. Make sure the deed is on its way to Columbia on closing day, whether through your closer or by your own delivery.

  • Ask when the recording will happen and how it will be submitted.
  • Keep proof of delivery if you mail the deed to P.O. Box 449.
  • Request the recording information once the register has filed it.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tyrrell County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property taxes and a sale

Interest rules sit in G.S. 105-360, and G.S. 105-355 explains the lien that follows the parcel. Unpaid taxes stay attached to the property, so they need to be settled at or before closing.

Tyrrell County offers six ways to pay: web portal, phone, mail, the tax office counter, a drop box in the hallway before the tax department door, and a bank's bill pay. Card payments carry a $2.50 fee or a 2.95% fee, whichever is greater, and e-check payments an added $2.00 fee. A bank's bill pay can lag by as much as seven business days, so start early.

For the current bill, tax rate and any prepayment discount, ask the Tyrrell County tax office. The Register of Deeds does not collect property taxes.

Selling an inherited house without a full estate

Sometimes, yes. Small estates may use the affidavit procedure in G.S. 28A-25-1. The ceiling is $20,000 of personal property net of liens, or $30,000 when the sole heir is a surviving spouse, after any spousal allowance. Nobody can have a personal representative petition pending, and 30 days must be up since the death.

File it with the superior court clerk where the person lived. The affidavit describes every tract of land the person owned. Whether you can then deed the land is a question for an attorney. Ask the clerk of court about the forms, and ask the register what must be recorded to show the heirs' authority to convey.

If you sell for cash and as-is, you skip repairs and showings, but the deed still gets recorded and the title still has to be clear.

Closing day in Columbia, step by step

Typically the title agent or attorney collects your signed deed, confirms the payoff of any mortgage, and pays the excise tax out of your proceeds. The deed then goes to the register for filing. After the filing, ask for the book and page information so you hold proof that the transfer is on record. If a mortgage is being paid off, watch for the release as well: it costs nothing to file, and the old lender is responsible for sending it, so a quick check a few weeks later keeps the record tidy.

Handing over the keys and the proceeds does not wait on the recording in most closings, but your protection as seller depends on the deed reaching the Columbia office promptly.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring when you record a deed

Bring the signed, notarized deed, the payment for the recording fee, and the excise tax if you are filing yourself. Most sellers never do this personally, because the attorney or title agent handles it at closing. If you are sending the package yourself, call (252) 796-2901 first and ask what else the office needs for your document type.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds hours?

Nine to five on weekdays that are not holidays. Find the office at 403 Main Street in Columbia or call (252) 796-2901.

Is there a fraud alert for Tyrrell County property records?

Yes. The register offers a Fraud Alert Notification Service that emails you if a possibly fraudulent recording is made. Sign up through the register's website.

Who owes the conveyance tax in Tyrrell County?

The seller, before recording. Look for the figure on the settlement statement.

What does a basic recording cost in Tyrrell County?

The base charge covers the first 15 pages, with a per-page charge after that. Ask the office whether your document triggers extra charges.

Does the Tyrrell County register collect property taxes?

No. The tax office takes property tax payments and lists the ways to pay. Ask that office for your bill before closing.

Why a Monroe-area seller deals with this office

A sale is not finished in the public record until the deed lands at the Union County Register of Deeds. That office holds the lasting record of who owns land in the county and how it changed hands: deeds, plats, powers of attorney and more.

Vital records, marriage licenses, notary oaths and passport applications are handled at the same counter. A house seller only cares about the land side. Whoever runs your closing delivers the signed deed, and its time stamp decides who ranks first if two claims collide.

The office dates to the county's formation in 1842, and the register is an elected position. Even a quick cash sale of a Union County house ends at this counter.

What the office can and cannot do

Think of this as a filing counter, not a legal help desk. State law bars the register and staff from practicing law, which means no blank legal forms and no coaching on completing one. Staff send people to an attorney.

Changing the names on a house means recording a fresh deed. An old deed is never edited.

  • Liens and judgments against a person or property: the Clerk of Court, 704-698-3100.
  • Who owns a given street address: the tax assessor, 704-283-3746, since the register indexes by name.
  • Drafting or correcting a deed: a North Carolina attorney.

Where to file a deed in Monroe

The office is in the Union County Government Center, 500 North Main Street, Monroe. Recording hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. You can bring a document in or send it through an e-recording vendor. Neighborhood covenant files are kept on the second floor.

Simplifile, CSC and ePN are the vendors in use now. You arrange setup with the vendor directly, but most sellers never touch it, because the firm running a closing usually already has an account. Ask which vendor your firm uses and when the stamped copy comes back.

Paper filers bring the signed original and a check for the fee. Payment is expected at the time you hand the document over, so a package without it will not get filed. If your closing firm is handling all of this, you only need to ask for confirmation once the filing is done.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Union County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording costs

The first fifteen pages of an instrument cost $26.00, and each further page is $4.00. State law uses the same pair of numbers for instruments generally. The excise tax on deeds is $2 per thousand dollars for deeds since August 1, 1991.

Union County recording charges
Recording itemAmount
Instrument, first fifteen pages$26.00, then $4.00 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 per page
Satisfaction of a deed of trustNo charge
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Assumed name$26
Deed excise tax since August 1, 1991$2 per thousand

A nonstandard document adds $25.00. Ask the office for its current fee sheet before you mail a check.

Excise tax on a Union County deed

The transferor owes this tax. As written by the legislature the rate is a dollar for each $500 of value, the same as $2 per thousand, and it has to be paid ahead of recording.

In a typical sale that is the seller, shown as a line at settlement. Half the tax stays in the county general fund and half goes to the state.

The amount follows the value stated in the deed, so take the figure from your closing office.

Searching records online

The register's website carries deeds starting in 1973 and maps starting in 1842. Older deeds, plus every other kind of record, mean a visit in person.

Two limits catch people. The deed look-up covers deeds and plats only, so mortgage information is not there. And the index is built on names, so typing a street address into it gets you nowhere.

  • Know the owner's name as it appears on the last deed.
  • Call the assessor for the owner of a street address.
  • Go to the office for mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Look in the same office for filed HOA covenants, if the county holds them.

A seller can use the search to confirm that the signers match the names on title and that no old deed of trust is still open.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Union County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Union County housing at a glance

The 2025 population estimate is 267,674, up 12.4 percent from the April 2020 base of 238,179, with 95,683 housing units. About 81.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so most sales here involve a single-family owner rather than a landlord.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $417,300, and median household income is $102,900. Median rent is $1,496, and builders took out 2,707 permits in 2025. Median monthly owner cost is $1,940 with a mortgage and $553 without one. Steady new construction shapes who buys, and the register's index shows every deed that moves between them.

Mail, phone and suite numbers

For land records, use 500 North Main Street, Suite 239, Monroe, NC 28112, telephone 704-283-3843. Mail goes to PO Box 248, Monroe, NC 28111-0248. If you deliver a deed by hand, go to Suite 239.

Most sellers skip the mail and let the closing firm file electronically.

The county also posts older excise tax rates for tracing past transfers: $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968. They only matter if you are working through an old deed in the family chain of title.

Does filing order change who wins a dispute?

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value before it is registered, and rank follows registration time.

A gap between signing and filing therefore carries risk. An uncancelled deed of trust on an inherited house also deserves a look before you sign a contract. Releases record free. Keep the recorded copy with your sale papers.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Useful phone numbers

Three numbers cover most questions: assessor 704-283-3746, Clerk of Court 704-698-3100 and the register's vital records line 704-283-3610.

Notary commissions are also kept here. A notary who is renewing takes the oath in person for a $10.00 fee. Have your closing office confirm that the notary witnessing your signature holds a current commission.

Probate, divorce and tax matters run through the courts and the tax office. The register files the paper they produce.

What happens at closing

Your attorney or title firm prepares the deed, you sign it before a notary, and the firm pays the excise tax out of your proceeds. The firm then files the deed, usually electronically, and the office stamps it with the date and time. Ask for the stamped copy and keep it. If you paid off a mortgage, the satisfaction of the deed of trust records free, so confirm it is filed. For a cash sale the steps are the same, just without a lender's paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Union County deed office open on weekends?

No. Hours are weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. E-filers use Simplifile, CSC or ePN; ask the vendor about its cutoff time.

Will Union County staff fix a mistake in my deed?

No. Staff cannot advise on drafting, so the attorney who prepared the deed has to correct it.

How was the deed tax set before 1991?

It was $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968. The rate is $2 per thousand now.

Why can't I type my address into the deed search?

The index runs on names, not addresses. Call the assessor at 704-283-3746 for an owner. Online deeds begin in 1973.

Do payoff releases cost extra in Union County?

No. G.S. 161-10 exempts satisfactions and cancellations from the fee.
