Visiting the Wake County Register of Deeds

The office is in the Wake County Justice Center, 300 S. Salisbury St., Suite 1700, Raleigh, NC 27601. It is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. Call 919-856-5460 or write to rodinfo@wake.gov.

Land documents share the counter with marriage licenses, birth and death certificate copies, business name filings, nuptial agreements and restrictive covenants.

A seller with a Raleigh-area house rarely goes in person. Your closing firm files the deed, and that filing is the step that publishes the sale.

Recording fees

An ordinary deed starts at $26 and a deed of trust at $64, with $4 for each page past the included count.

Wake County fees a home sale may touch
Document or serviceWake County price
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 covers 35 pages; $4 per page after
Amendment to a deed of trust$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per page after
Other instruments, including assumed names$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per page after
Non-standard layout$25 on top of the recording fee
Each additional instrument bundled in a document$10 each
Satisfaction of a security instrumentFree
Plat or condominium map$21 a page
Certified copy$5 for page one; $2 for each later page
Deed excise tax from August 1, 1991$2 per thousand

Large filings pay $2 for each party name beyond twenty, and an assignment's first added deed of trust reference is free.

What counts as a standard deed

Missing any one item on the standard-document list triggers the $25 surcharge. The list covers layout only.

  • Paper sized 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches at the top of the first page, with half-inch margins everywhere else.
  • Black print on white paper in at least 9 point.
  • One side only, with the instrument type centered on page one.

Pen is fine for filling blanks and making corrections. Documents from a title firm pass as a matter of course. A form downloaded and printed double-sided, or a scan that crowds the edge, is the kind of file that draws the extra $25.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wake County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The deed transfer tax

The rate is $2 per thousand for deeds since August 1, 1991. State law words it as a dollar per $500 and makes the transferor pay first, so the seller sees it at settlement. Ask the closing office for the number on your deed.

Older rates matter when you read an old transfer: $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1969.

Searching the index

Wake County public records start in 1785, and the Consolidated Real Property Index lets a seller or a buyer's lawyer follow title from a desk.

Start with your own deed and compare its legal description and owner names against the contract. Next, look for the deed of trust you are paying off. After closing, look for its satisfaction, which is recorded at no charge.

A fraud alert service emails you when a monitored name appears on a recorded document, handy for heirs, landlords and owners of empty houses.

What to have ready before a deed goes in

The package is a signed, acknowledged deed that meets the layout rules, plus payment. Firms handle it for most sellers, but someone recording a family transfer may do it alone.

  • Names written as on the previous deed, since the index is searched by name.
  • Recording fee, plus excise tax if the transfer is a sale.
  • Any added instrument, which carries its own $10 charge when bundled.

For any drafting question, see an attorney. A wrong legal description or missing signature goes back to whoever prepared the deed, and adding or removing an owner means recording a new deed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wake County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The register and the tax office

Two county departments touch the house. The register records the ownership paper, while Tax Administration appraises and bills. Settle the tax bill through closing.

The tax help line is 919-856-5400. Wake also bills towns and special districts, so one bill can carry several charges. The county rate is 53.71 cents after a 2-cent increase for Fiscal Year 2027.

Values reset on January 1, 2027, the effective date of the next revaluation, which sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods.

Seller checklist

None of this needs a trip downtown if a closing firm is involved.

  • Your recorded deed, pulled from the online index.
  • The payoff letter for any deed of trust, followed by a recorded release at no charge.
  • A tax figure from Tax Administration, which matters most for owners who pay by escrow and never see a bill.
  • A deed laid out to the standard list.

Heirs unsure what is recorded can search the index, then phone 919-856-5460. An attorney can answer questions about the deed itself.

Services for heirs selling an inherited house

The register sells certified death certificates, which heirs often need for estate paperwork. Certified copies are $10 each, with a $10 amendment charge. For out-of-county death certificates, expect a $14 search fee, a $10 certified copy and $15 for each additional copy. Ordering online adds a county charge of $10 per copy plus a vendor convenience fee that varies.

Certified copies of recorded documents cost $5 for page one and $2 for each page after, with no charge for the trailer page. A certified copy of a map is $5.

  • Get a certified deed copy to show how the decedent held title.
  • Check the index for any open deed of trust before listing the house.
  • Ask an attorney whether probate steps must come before a deed is recorded.

The register does not decide who may sign a deed for an estate. That question belongs to the probate side and to your attorney.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Maps, covenants and other filings

Plats and condominium maps are $21 per page. Right-of-way plans and highway maps are $21 for the first page and $5 for each page after. UCC filings are $38 each for the UCC-1 and UCC-3, rising to $45 above two pages, so a 13-page UCC filing comes to $51.

For a seller, the useful items are the maps and restrictive covenants, since both can describe limits on the parcel. They are recorded here, and the index reaches back to 1785. Ask your title or closing firm to pull any plat and covenant that applies to your subdivision.

Business owners operating from home may also file an assumed name here, at the $26 instrument rate.

E-recording and paper filing

Ask the office or your closing firm how a deed will be sent and what cutoff applies. Paper goes to the Justice Center on weekdays. For any question tied to a particular filing, call 919-856-5460 before you go.

Why recording matters after a sale

Until a conveyance is registered in the county where the land lies, it carries no weight against lien creditors or purchasers for value. For a Raleigh-area house, that makes the filing the buyer's protection.

Keep the stamped copy with your closing papers and confirm the old lender's release is recorded. If you sell for cash, the same recording steps apply, only without a lender's paperwork.

Closing-day steps for a Wake County seller

Typically the attorney or title firm collects your signed deed, confirms the payoff of any deed of trust, and deducts the excise tax and recording costs from your proceeds. The firm submits the deed, and once it is recorded the index shows the transfer. A week or two later, look the property up and confirm both the new deed and the release of your old loan appear. If either is missing, call 919-856-5460 with the document details.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Wake County deed office open on Saturdays?

No. The Justice Center office keeps weekday hours only. Call 919-856-5460 about holidays.

How is Wake County's deed excise tax stated?

As $2 per thousand on deeds since August 1, 1991. The transferor pays.

Does Wake County charge to record a payoff release?

No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are free.

How do I change the names on a Wake County deed?

With a new deed. The register suggests an attorney unless you are used to preparing legal papers.

How far back do Wake County deeds go online?

To 1785.

Office address and hours

The Warren County Register of Deeds is at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton. It serves the public Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. Call (252) 257-3265, or mail to P.O. Box 506, Warrenton, NC 27589. The register is an elected position, filled every second year under G.S. 161-1.

Warren is a rural county of about 20,000 people spread over 443 square miles, and one counter covers all of it. A quick call can save you a drive.

Anyone may read what the office holds. Lookups run on names, so a person hunting for a parcel's owner should have a name. With only a street address, call the tax office at (252) 257-4158.

What recording a deed does

Recording protects the buyer. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded transfer, or a lease longer than three years, cannot beat a lien creditor or a paying purchaser. Whoever registers first stands first.

The office exists so owners can publish their interest in real estate. It also files births that happened in Warren County, marriage licenses and notary oaths, and it files DD-214 papers for retired service members at no cost.

  • The land side takes deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and powers of attorney.
  • Wills live elsewhere, with the courthouse clerk.
  • Liens and judgments: call the clerk at (252) 257-6300.

Filing costs

Warren County follows the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. Twenty-six dollars buys the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed and every page after costs four. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages, with the same four-dollar overage. Filing a release costs nothing.

What each Warren County filing costs
FilingAmount
Ordinary deed$26 plus $4 per page beyond 15
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 plus $4 per page beyond 35
Release of a mortgageNone
Plat$21 a sheet
Certified vital record by mail$10
DD-214 filingNone

Call the office before mailing a package and confirm the figures for your document.

Deed stamp tax

Sellers pay. For each $500 of value, or any leftover part of $500, the stamp is one dollar, handed to the register before the deed is entered.

The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to the state monthly, less a small allowance. That is the same as $2 per $1,000. The settlement statement shows the exact stamp.

What to line up before you list

Three items come first: matching names, a current tax account and a document that fits the office's format. The register's website carries a recording checklist and a fee page, and staff answer by phone.

  • Changing who is named takes a fresh deed. Use an attorney, then pay the normal filing fee, plus stamp tax where a price is involved.
  • Check the tax account. Each bill is due on September 1 and starts drawing interest after January 5, under G.S. 105-360.
  • Ask the clerk if a lien or judgment sits on the file.
  • Pay with cash, check or money order, since the office does not take cards.

Make two short calls, one to each office, before listing. Ask the register what format your deed needs, and ask the tax office for the current balance and whether any back years are open. Having both answers early means the closing attorney can work from real numbers instead of guesses, and it keeps a surprise from stalling the sale.

Selling rural land and farm tracts

Farm tracts and family land come up often in a county of this size, and such sales may add a survey, plat or easement, each filed separately. A plat is $21 a sheet. Splitting acreage? Learn the register's plat format before the surveyor starts.

A copy of a recorded map is five cents a page (fifty for large maps) and a deed copy is also five cents. The online search shows scanned deeds. Tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial photos come from tax mapping, not here.

Heirs who want to sell should see whether a deed was ever recorded in their names. Estate papers may start at the clerk.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Warren County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How far back vital records reach

Birth and death certificates run from 1914 to the present. Delayed birth certificates reach back to the late 1800s. Marriage indexes begin in 1867, and marriage bonds and licenses go back to the late 1800s.

  • Certificates, bonds and licenses are filed only for events that took place in Warren County.
  • NC Vital Records in Raleigh holds records for every county in the state and is the place to ask about events elsewhere. Its line is 919.733.3526.
  • Wills are not here. The Warren County clerk of court keeps them.

Heirs selling a Warren County house will find the register useful for the marriage and death side of the family story, while the will itself sits with the clerk. If an owner died in another county, the record will not be in Warren County's files.

Other business at the counter

Many visitors come for reasons besides land. A marriage license costs sixty dollars, lasts sixty days and is booked by phone. A certified marriage certificate is ten dollars and can be had starting ten days after the ceremony.

A certified vital record goes only to a short list: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, a legal representative, or someone with proof of a legal need. Plain copies are open to all.

New notaries swear in at the counter without an appointment, bringing the notice from the Secretary of State, for a $10 fee. Births outside the county are recorded by NC Vital Records.

Selling a house with liens or repairs

It can be done. Liens and back taxes come out of the price at closing and the releases get recorded. A house that needs work can find a buyer who takes it as it stands, and a cash sale skips lender repair demands.

Start the title work early so both the register's index and the clerk's judgments are checked.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Looking up and paying a tax bill online

The county's property page for the register of deeds links to a combined tool for paying tax bills and searching property record cards. Questions about assessments still go to the tax office.

Keep the bill and the recorded deed together. When a closing is scheduled, the person handling it will want the account number and the book and page of the last recorded deed, and both come from those two lookups.

What happens on closing day

Your closing attorney collects the signed deed, confirms the payoff of your loan, and files the deed with the register. The stamp tax is paid out of your proceeds before the deed goes on record. Afterward, ask for the recording details, and watch for the release of your old mortgage, which costs nothing to file. If either looks late, phone the office at (252) 257-3265 with the names on the deed.

Frequently asked questions

Is releasing a Warren County mortgage free?

Yes. No fee applies to recording a satisfaction of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Can Warren County staff name a parcel's owner from an address?

No. Staff search by name only, so address-only callers are sent to the tax office.

Does the Warren County deeds office file wills?

No. The clerk of superior court takes wills and estates. The register takes deeds, mortgages, plats, releases, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

Does Warren County charge to record a DD-214?

No. The office files discharge papers for retired military free.

Who answers deed questions in Warren County?

Phone (252) 257-3265, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. The office is at 109 South Main Street, Warrenton.

Washington County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Where Washington County keeps its deed records

The Register of Deeds is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth. Mail goes to Box 1007, Plymouth, NC 27962. Hours are 8:30 to 5 on weekdays. Call (252) 793-2325 or fax (252) 793-6982.

Voters fill the register's seat for a four-year term. The office exists so that owners can put their interest in land on public notice, which in turn shields later buyers from unknown transactions and secret liens. It also issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses.

The county is rural, with Plymouth, Roper and Creswell as its towns. One counter handles every filing, so a phone call before you visit is wise.

How old the land records are

The oldest go back to 1799, the year Washington County was carved out of Tyrrell County. Marriage records start in 1851 and the licenses themselves in 1881.

The shelves hold old land grants, deeds, deeds of trust, maps, leases, agreements and powers of attorney. Anyone selling farmland or shoreline here should expect a long chain of title, and a title searcher will walk it back through those early books. A link on the county page opens deeds online.

North Carolina began statewide birth and death registration in 1913. Some earlier births appear in the county's files as delayed registrations filed by the person later. Send older vital record requests in writing, with names and dates.

Steps before a deed can be filed

Two local checkpoints apply. First, every deed passes through the GIS (mapping) office to receive a parcel identifier number. Second, the county tax collector must certify that no delinquent taxes exist, or the deed itself must carry a statement from the closing lawyer promising to send any back taxes to the collector out of the closing funds. The statement route is the usual one.

  • Name the person who prepared the deed on page one.
  • Choose letter or legal size paper, with a three-inch blank band across the top of the first page and quarter-inch margins on the remaining edges.
  • Print in black on white, nothing smaller than nine point, on one side only.
  • Label the type of instrument at the top of page one.

A paper that misses those standards is still accepted, but the register adds a $25 non-standard charge to the normal fee. Cancellations and satisfactions can be sent through Simplifile.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Filing costs

Fees follow the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at twenty-six dollars, which covers fifteen pages, with four dollars for each page beyond. A deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages and takes the same four-dollar surcharge per added page.

Washington County register charges
FilingCharge
Ordinary deed$26, plus $4 per page past 15
Indexing over twenty names$2 per extra name
Deed of trust$64, plus $4 per page past 35
Extra reference on an assignment$10 each
Map, sized 18 by 24$21
Cancellation or satisfactionFree
Stamp tax$1 per $500 or part
Certified vital record$10

Maps are routed through GIS for a parcel number and through the county review officer for approval, unless the map carries one of three stock statements: no new street, an existing building or natural feature, or a control survey.

Stamp tax on a Plymouth-area sale

The person transferring the property pays it. The register collects it before the deed goes on record, at one dollar per $500 or fraction of the price or value.

G.S. 105-228.30 divides the money between county and state. The settlement statement will show the stamp, so no one has to calculate it in advance. If a deed has no ordinary sale price, ask the register how the stamp applies before you bring it in.

Contracts for deed

The office files any instrument touching land, and seller financing is a common case. Under Chapter 47H, a contract for deed on a one to four family home must be written, signed and acknowledged, and the seller has five business days to record the contract or a memorandum of it.

The buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day. If the seller later seeks forfeiture, the written default notice must give a cure date at least thirty days after service.

Other things a Washington County seller may bring to the counter:

  • A power of attorney, if someone signs the deed for the owner.
  • A map or plat in the 18 by 24 format, after GIS review.
  • A lease or agreement, both among the record types the office keeps.

Because the preparer must be named on page one, line up whoever drafts the deed before you go.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Marriage licenses and vital records

Marriage licenses are a regular errand. Any North Carolina register will issue one, and the ceremony can be held in any county, but the signed license must come back to the county that sold it. Each applicant needs a driver's license and a Social Security card, or a W-2, pay stub, insurance card or Social Security printout as proof of the number. Blood tests and physicals are no longer required.

Applicants aged 16 to 17 bring a certified birth certificate, and anyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's consent. Those under 16 must call the office first.

Certified vital record copies go only to the applicant or immediate family, and in-person requests need identification. The same counter that handles those errands files your deed, so allow time on busy days.

Why filing order matters

The earliest registration wins. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until registered in the county where the land lies.

  • For a deed naming more than twenty parties, call (252) 793-2325 first.
  • Ask the tax collector about open bills, since the deed needs the certification or the lawyer's statement.
  • Check whether an old loan still lacks a recorded satisfaction.

Shoreline and farm parcels often carry surveys, and any plat that comes with the sale follows the map rules above.

Selling with title or tax problems

It can be done. A closing lawyer clears unpaid taxes and liens from the price, and a buyer can take the house in its present condition. Searching the register's index is the first move for any title searcher.

A cash sale can shorten the timeline, since no lender is waiting on repairs or an appraisal, but the parcel number step and the tax certification still happen before the deed is filed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A closing-day walk-through

On the day of closing, the lawyer collects your signed deed, pays off any lien from the proceeds, and sends the deed to Plymouth with the stamp tax and fee. The deed gets its parcel number from GIS, the tax statement or certification is attached, and the register records it. Afterward, keep the recorded copy, and ask whether a payoff satisfaction has been filed. Call (252) 793-2325 if you need the status of a filing.

Frequently asked questions

Does Washington County charge to record a satisfaction?

No. Cancellations and certificates of satisfaction are free, and the non-standard document fee never applies to a cancellation.

Is a parcel number needed before a Washington County deed is filed?

Yes. Every deed goes to GIS first so a parcel identifier number can be assigned.

What does a certified birth, death or marriage copy cost in Washington County?

Ten dollars certified and twenty-five cents uncertified. Certified copies go only to the applicant or immediate family, and faxed requests are refused.

How long does a Washington County marriage license last?

Sixty days, at a cost of sixty dollars. Arrive before 4:30 p.m., because the visit takes fifteen to twenty minutes.

Whom do I phone about filing a Washington County deed?

The register of deeds at (252) 793-2325. The office is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5.

Finding the Watauga County deeds office

The office is inside the courthouse, Room 119, at 842 West King Street in Boone. Mail goes to the same street, Suite 9, Boone, NC 28607. Call 828-265-8052 for land records, 828-265-8034 for vital records, or send a fax to 828-265-7632.

Hours are weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00 except holidays. Marriage licenses are by appointment, with applicants in the door by 4:30.

Voters elect the register under G.S. 161-1. Wills are filed with the clerk of court, and liens and judgments on real property are checked with the clerk of superior court.

Searching the land records

The website carries indexes and images from 1872 forward, searchable by name or by book and page. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 lives under the old index books tab, because on that date deeds and deeds of trust were folded into one series, the Book of Records, restarting at Book 1.

Plats can be searched by book and page, subdivision, or the owner as grantor, no matter when they were recorded. North Carolina's indexing standards began in 1995, and the office keeps copies.

Nearly everything filed is public. The one exception is military discharges on file under 80 years. For the owner of a given parcel, call tax mapping at 828-265-8030.

Tax mapping, not the register, answers parcel ownership questions. The register's index runs on names and recorded documents, while tax mapping runs on parcels and maps. Bring the book and page of your deed to either call.

Fees at the register

The schedule tracks G.S. 161-10. A deed opens at twenty-six dollars for fifteen pages. A deed of trust opens at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five. Each added page is four dollars in both cases.

Watauga County register fees
FilingFee
Deeds and instruments$26.00, then $4.00 a page after 15
Mortgages and deeds of trust$64.00, then $4.00 a page after 35
Records of satisfactionNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 on top of the filing fee
Parties beyond twenty$2.00 each
Multiple instruments$10.00 per extra instrument
Plats$21.00 a sheet
Excise stamps$1.00 per $500.00 or fraction

Plats offered for registration must measure 18 by 24 inches. Records supplied to help someone claim military benefits are free, and so are copies of a service discharge.

Fees apply per instrument, so a closing that records a deed and a new deed of trust is billed on two lines. Releases of an old loan add nothing. Compare the schedule with your closing statement.

Electronic recording

Yes, for all land record document types. More than 1,500 submitters, such as banks, law offices and mortgage companies, already send documents this way.

Three vendors are in use:

  • Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657.
  • Corporation Service Company, 1-866-652-0111.
  • eRecording Partners Network, 1-888-325-3365.

Most home sales arrive electronically through the lawyer handling the closing, so sellers seldom carry paper in. Deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, easements and powers of attorney can all be filed electronically.

What staff cannot do for a seller

Staff can point you to the right book and tell you whether a document is a real estate record or a vital record. They cannot run a title search, offer a legal opinion, or change a deed already recorded. Adding or deleting a name would count as practicing law, so that job goes to an attorney.

Address searches are also off the table. This office indexes documents by legal description, with boundary, lot, block and acreage details, so a street address has to go to the Tax Mapping Department at (828) 265-8030.

  • A lost deed is replaceable: a copy can be certified with the office seal, because the recording matters more than the paper.
  • Copies cost five cents a page, and a recorded subdivision plat copy is one dollar.
  • If no money changes hands, no excise stamp applies.
  • A person with private data in online records can ask in writing, at no charge, for it to be removed from the online copy under the Identity Theft Protection Act of 2005.

The excise stamp on a Boone-area deed

The seller pays. The stamp is a dollar for each $500 or fraction of the consideration, paid to the register before the instrument is entered. The county gets half and the Department of Revenue gets half under G.S. 105-228.30.

The settlement statement carries the final amount. North Carolina repealed its estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, so an inherited Watauga County house adds no estate tax step before recording.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Watauga County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other services at the counter

Besides land, the register issues marriage licenses at $60 and certified birth, death and marriage copies at $10. Notary oaths are $10, with $2 for verifying a commission. Military discharge records are kept, and a certified copy of an armed forces discharge costs nothing.

The office also offers an assumed business name certificate, a redaction request form, a fraud notification system and an identity theft page. Because deeds and deeds of trust are public, the fraud notice and the redaction form are the two a homeowner is most likely to use.

  • Uncertified copies cost whatever is posted at the office.
  • Comparing a copy for certification is $5.00.
  • For birth and death certificates, call 828-265-8034.

Must a deed be recorded, and can I write my own?

Record soon after drafting, since an unrecorded deed can make a later sale or mortgage impossible to prove. G.S. 47-18 denies a conveyance force against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies.

An owner may write a deed, though an attorney is strongly advised. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, and the register has no blank forms.

A search of the index shows how the present owner took title, which matters when property passed through heirs or a trust.

Fixing loose ends in the title

Begin with the index. Look up the owner, note the book and page of the last deed, and watch for old deeds of trust with no recorded release. Releases cost nothing to file.

Next, phone the clerk of superior court about liens and judgments and the tax office about the account. A house with flaws can still sell as it is, and a cash sale skips the lender's repair and appraisal requirements.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Closing day in Boone, step by step

Your closing attorney collects the signed deed, confirms the payoff of your loan, and files the deed electronically in most cases. The excise stamp comes out of your proceeds. Afterward, search the index by your name or by book and page to confirm the deed and the release of your old deed of trust both appear. If something is missing, call 828-265-8052 and have your names and the closing date ready.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Watauga County Register of Deeds?

In the courthouse, Room 119, 842 West King Street, Boone. Dial 828-265-8052 for land records and 828-265-8034 for vital records.

How far back do the online land records in Watauga County go?

To 1872. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 is under the old index books tab.

Does Watauga County charge to file a release of a deed of trust?

No. Records of satisfaction carry no fee.

Does the Watauga County register keep wills?

No. Wills go to the clerk of courts. Separation agreements can come from the register, while divorces are filed with the clerk.

Can a Watauga County deed be recorded online?

Yes, through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. Most sellers let the closing lawyer handle it.

Office location and hours

The Wayne County Register of Deeds is at 224-226 E Walnut Street, Suite 100, Goldsboro, NC 27533. The phone is 919-731-1449 and the fax is 919-731-1441. The office page gives general hours of 8:00 to 5:00.

Real estate filings are taken from 8:00 to 4:45 without an appointment, and nothing should be walked in after 4:45 p.m. If a closing runs into the evening, send the documents by wire or electronic filing instead.

  • Real estate filings: 8:00 to 4:45
  • Vital records and notary oaths: 8:15 to 4:45
  • Marriage licenses: 8:00 to 4:00

Land records and vital records share the building, but each window keeps its own hours. Call 919-731-1449 before you drive over with anything time sensitive, so you know the right window is open.

What the office keeps

The office is the custodian of county land and business records: deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions and cancellations, powers of attorney, assumed business names and separation agreements. Marriage licenses, notary commissions and DD-214 discharge recordings come from the same counter.

The archive reaches back to 1913. The online index covers most real estate papers from 1971 onward, so an older tract usually means a visit in person.

Funeral homes can email registerofdeeds@waynegov.com or drop off a request, and staff call when the order is ready. Wills are not recorded here. They go to the Clerk of Courts at 919-722-6100.

Staff cannot give legal help

The office records what is handed over. North Carolina law bars its staff from practicing law, so they will not draft a deed, explain what a form does or help fill in blanks.

Most Wayne County sales therefore run through a lawyer or title firm that prepares the deed, searches title, collects the tax and delivers the filing.

If you sell without an agent, you can still hire an attorney just for the paperwork. Ask whether the attorney will handle the recording and who pays the fees.

If you plan to skip a lawyer, call the office first and ask what the counter will and will not check. Staff can say whether a packet is in proper form to file, though they will not say whether the document does what you want.

Electronic recording

Wayne County accepts every document type by eRecording, and its eRecording page notes that plats can now be sent this way too. Firms must pick from a list of approved vendors.

The vendor helps the firm complete a submitter agreement. Within two business days of processing it, the Register of Deeds emails an identification number, and every electronic filing needs that number.

  1. Choose an authorized vendor.
  2. Complete the submitter agreement.
  3. Receive the ID number by email.
  4. Submit deeds and deeds of trust electronically.

Vendors must hold approval under G.S. 47-14(a1). Individual sellers rarely sign up themselves, because their title company already has an account.

Recording fees

Recording charges under G.S. 161-10, collected at the Wayne County office
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages; $4.00 for every page past that
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages; $4.00 each page after
Release of a loan (satisfaction)Free
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy$5.00 plus $2.00 a further page

The statute makes this schedule exclusive and requires payment before filing. Phone the office for the exact amount due on your packet.

Seller's transfer tax

The seller owes the state deed excise tax, paid at the Goldsboro counter before recording. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars (or part) of value conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

You will see it on the settlement statement. Check the figure against your contract, and ask about it if the transfer is a gift or sells below market.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wayne County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Why record right after closing

A deed that sits unregistered gives the buyer no protection against lien creditors or later purchasers for value (G.S. 47-18). The earlier registration wins.

You can help by clearing old liens beforehand. A paid off mortgage with no recorded satisfaction clouds the title, and lenders file releases at no charge.

  • Search the grantor index for open deeds of trust
  • Ask any lender you paid off for a satisfaction
  • Confirm the legal description matches your own vesting deed

How to check your title before listing

Run three checks before you sign a listing or an offer. They take little time and head off most closing surprises.

  • Search the online index, which covers most real estate documents from 1971, for your name as grantee and grantor.
  • Look for deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction.
  • Match your own vesting deed against the parcel shown in the county's real estate search on the tax site.

For anything before 1971, go to the Goldsboro office and ask how the older books are indexed. Staff can show you where records are kept, though they cannot interpret them.

If a plat is involved, check with the Planning Department about plats and signatures before presenting them.

What goes in a recording packet

Your closing attorney normally assembles the packet, so use this list to check their work.

  • The signed and notarized deed, with a legal description that matches the prior deed
  • A check or account for the recording charge
  • The excise tax payment, collected on the seller's side
  • A deed of trust for the buyer's lender, recorded after the deed
  • Any satisfactions for loans paid at closing

Electronic filings follow the same order, and the vendor's system carries the fee and tax figures. If something is rejected, call 919-731-1449.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Other Goldsboro offices in a sale

Three county offices come into play. The Register of Deeds records the paper. The Tax Collector, at P.O. Box 1495, supplies the tax payoff. The Clerk of Courts, at 919-722-6100, holds wills for an estate sale.

If the house belongs to an estate, call the clerk and an attorney before looking for a buyer, because the right person to sign the deed depends on what the court has done. The register of deeds will record the deed once it is signed and acknowledged, but cannot tell you whether the signer has authority.

Death certificates and other vital records come from the same Walnut Street counter, which helps an heir completing an estate file. Funeral homes are served by email, so an heir rarely needs to make a separate trip for that part.

Old loans and long ownership

Owners in Wayne tend to stay put, so a house may carry decades of deed history, and a buyer's title search reads all of it. An old loan that was never released is a common loose end. Median gross rent of $965 also means many sellers are landlords with rental properties to clear.

If the owner has died, the register of deeds holds the recorded chain, and the estate's attorney works from the clerk of court for the will.

Frequently asked questions

Until what hour are real estate filings taken?

4:45 p.m. The office asks people not to bring recording packages after that time, and general hours are 8:00 to 5:00.

Will staff draft my deed?

No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft a deed or explain its effect. Hire an attorney or use a closing office.

How far back are real estate records online?

Most real estate records are searchable from 1971 forward, while the archive itself goes back to 1913.

Is recording a loan release free?

Yes. State law sets no fee to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Which Wayne County office takes a will?

The Clerk of Courts, which the Register of Deeds lists at 919-722-6100.

Address and hours

The Wilkes County Register of Deeds is at 500 Court House Drive, Suite 1000, Wilkesboro, NC 28697. Phone 336-651-7351 or fax 336-990-0041. The county page shows hours of Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:55 p.m., closed on holidays.

Tax Administration is in a different building, the Wilkes County Offices at 110 North Street. A seller may need both, or can have an attorney handle the recording while phoning the tax office for figures.

  • Land records: Court House Drive, Suite 1000
  • Tax bills and appeals: North Street
  • Recording deadline for the day: 4:55 p.m.

On a closing day, call ahead if the packet runs long, since pages past the first fifteen of a deed add to the charge.

How far back the records go

Land records begin with the formation of the county in 1778. Birth and death records start in 1913, with a few earlier delayed birth entries, and marriage licenses go back to 1882.

The register takes in deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, separation agreements, foreclosures, notary oaths and military discharges. Digitizing is ongoing, so ask how far back a given book is indexed.

On a parcel with deep family ownership, older deeds can describe land by landmarks instead of lot numbers. A survey tied to the current deed saves arguments with a buyer's title examiner.

Heirs sorting an estate often start here, since births, deaths and marriages are on file alongside land records. A short visit with the death certificate and the last recorded deed can show who held title and whether a loan was ever released.

Searching deeds online

Use wilkesncrod.org, which the register of deeds opened on July 1, 2017. It is the authoritative site for recorded documents.

The tax office runs a second, narrower tool. Its Deed Search holds face pages and legal descriptions of certain deeds scanned for the mapping staff. Signature and notary pages are usually left off, and deeds of trust, satisfactions and wills are not included.

Attorneys and title examiners are told not to rely on it. Treat it as a quick way to find a legal description by book and page, and use the register for the real record.

Once you have the book and page from a prior deed or from the register's own site, you can pull the scanned face page and compare its legal description with your survey. Keep a printout for your attorney.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wilkes County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording charges

Recording charges collected in Wilkes County
FilingCharge
Deed, general instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 a page
Loan releaseNo charge
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

These are the only fees, and they are payable before filing. Ask at the counter what your packet will cost.

Who pays the deed tax

The seller does, at the register of deeds, before recording. The state rate is one dollar per five hundred dollars or part of the value of the interest conveyed.

The county general fund keeps half. The balance goes to the state monthly, less refunds and an allowance.

Why recording matters to the buyer

A deed that is never registered loses to lien creditors and to later buyers who paid value, and priority follows the time of registration. That is why lawyers record on the day funds move.

  • Locate paid off loans and confirm releases are on record
  • Get the tax balance from North Street
  • Bring the excise tax with the deed
  • Record the deed ahead of the buyer's loan

The register is chosen by county voters in an election.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wilkes County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Boundary questions on older tracts

North Carolina lets a person gain title by 20 years of possession under known and visible lines and boundaries, adverse to others. On older rural tracts, fences and farm roads may sit off the deed line.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed from the register, order a survey if lines are unclear, and tell your attorney about any neighbor who uses part of the land. A buyer's examiner will find recorded claims, so surprises cost more late.

Preparing before closing day

Work backward from the recording desk. It closes at 4:55 p.m., so a closing that wraps up at four leaves little room for a corrected page.

  • Ask your attorney who will carry the package to Court House Drive, or whether it goes electronically.
  • Check that every signature and notary stamp is complete.
  • Have a check ready for the filing charge if the closing office does not cover it.
  • Keep the recorded copy, with its book and page, for your files.

The tax office's deed search asks for those book and page numbers, so they also help later when you need a legal description for a survey or an insurance form.

Excise tax and the tax value

The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall as of January 1, 2025. For recording, though, the price in your contract is what drives the excise tax. The county's tax value does not set it. If your contract price and the county's value differ widely, your attorney can explain why before the deed is drafted.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens after closing

Once funds move, your attorney carries the signed deed to the register. Staff check that the packet is in proper form and that the fee and excise tax are paid, then index the deed by book and page. The buyer's deed of trust follows it. If you paid off a loan, watch for the lender's release to appear on record, and call the register at 336-651-7351 if it has not shown up after a reasonable wait.

A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, so the packet is shorter, but the deed, the excise tax and any release of your old loan still have to be recorded in the same order.

Which office handles which paper

A short map prevents trips to the wrong building.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, plats, powers of attorney, foreclosure papers: Register of Deeds, Court House Drive
  • Tax balances, appeals, relief applications, parcel and GIS look-ups: Tax Administration, North Street
  • Court files, estates and wills: Clerk of Superior Court

For any official use of land records, go to the register and the clerk of superior court. Keep the three straight and a sale usually moves without a second visit.

Checking the tax record against the deed

Besides deeds, the register takes foreclosure papers and powers of attorney, which matter when an owner signs by proxy or the lender has begun sale proceedings. The tax office offers a real property search and GIS maps.

To confirm who is on the tax record, search the parcel there, then match it to the recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org. Mismatches usually trace to an unrecorded transfer or a name change.

  • Real property search on the tax site
  • GIS parcel maps
  • Recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org

Frequently asked questions

When does the Wilkes County Register of Deeds close?

At 4:55 p.m., Monday through Friday. The doors open at 8:30 a.m. and close for holidays.

How can I search Wilkes County deeds from home?

Use wilkesncrod.org, the register's site that has been online since July 1, 2017. The tax office also has a limited deed copy tool for finding legal descriptions.

What year do Wilkes County land records start?

1778, when the county was formed. Births and deaths begin in 1913, and marriage licenses in 1882.

Do I pay to record a loan release in Wilkes County?

No. The statewide fee schedule sets no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Who owes the excise tax on a Wilkes County deed?

The seller. It is paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

What the office does

The Register of Deeds keeps Wilson County's real property and vital records. The county page lists deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney, maps and many other documents among the papers it records.

The same office issues marriage licenses and holds the county's birth, death and marriage files, plus military discharges and notary oaths. For a house sale, only the real property side matters: the deed that moves title and the deed of trust that secures a buyer's loan both end up here. The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years by the county's voters.

The office phone is 252-399-2935, and it is the number to use for most questions about a recording that is already in progress or a document you cannot find in the index. Marriage license visits and vital record amendments are scheduled by phone through that number.

Searching records online

The online search holds Wilson County's real estate indexes back to 1974, and older documents are still being scanned so their images can be viewed online. For an older chain of title, expect to ask the office for images that are not yet online.

Useful lookups before a sale include:

  • The current deed, to confirm how the owners' names appear.
  • Any deed of trust, to see whether a lender still has a lien.
  • Recorded cancellations, which show that an old loan was released.
  • Maps and plats that describe the lot lines.

Title searches for a closing are normally ordered by the closing attorney, but a quick index search lets an owner spot a stale lien early.

The delinquent tax statement on deeds

A deed has to carry a statement about delinquent property tax before the register accepts it. The county's deed requirements page explains that the rule dates from October 1, 2014 and rests on G.S. 161-31, which names Wilson County and which the commissioners implemented by resolution on December 6, 2004.

There are two routes. In the first, the paper is taken to the tax department's Collections Division, where a clerk confirms that no delinquent tax is owed. The attorney should have the parcel number printed on the deed or on hand. In the second, the attorney fills in the statement personally, and the deed can go straight to the register.

The county asks for separate checks, one for taxes owed and one for the Register of Deeds' recording fees. The tax department takes questions at 252-399-2900, option 2.

Filing charges

Every register in the state charges the same amounts, Wilson County included. An ordinary document costs $26.00 with 15 pages included. A loan security document starts at $64.00 and includes 35 pages. Extra pages on either are $4.00 apiece.

Recording fees at the Wilson County counter
DocumentFee
Ordinary instrument, 15 pages included$26.00 base, $4.00 for each page beyond

Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee

Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per later page

These fees are complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Nonstandard documents add $25.00, and each extra instrument in one document adds $10.00.

Who pays the deed stamp tax

The seller does. The state levy runs $1.00 for each $500 or fraction of value passing, and it is due to the register before filing.

One half is retained by the county and the other half is sent to the state monthly. Your closing attorney calculates it and deducts it at settlement, so ask for the exact number.

Why recording order matters

Protection against outside claims starts at registration in the land's home county. Contracts to convey, options, leases over three years and conveyances are not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time of registration, and priority follows the order of registration.

A seller who signs on Friday and a buyer who records the following week are both better off if the closing office records the same day. A seller who also owes tax should note that a deed without the tax statement cannot be filed in Wilson County.

Vital records at the same office

Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records can be ordered online, with pickup orders confirmed by a phone call, or requested by mail.

Adopted people born in Wilson County can now request new birth certificates directly from the register, in person only, under Senate Bill 248. Marriage license applicants print and fill out the application first, then call to book a visit, and only the couple attends. None of this affects a sale, but it explains why the front counter can be busy.

Ordering a certified copy of a deed

Search the online index first, since it lists real estate documents back to 1974, then request an image or a certified copy from the office. A certified copy runs $5.00 for its first page and $2.00 for each page that follows.

Deeds from before the online coverage may be missing from the images. A call to 252-399-2935 gets a clerk looking for the book and page. Heirs often need the deed that put title in the decedent's name, so order early to avoid delay during the contract period. A closing attorney or title company can also request the copy for you, which saves a trip to the counter in Wilson.

Common reasons a deed gets held up

Most delays come from the tax statement, not the recording itself. A deed brought to the register without either of the two tax options will not be accepted for recording, so the attorney has to go back to the tax department first.

Other frequent snags:

  • One check covering both taxes and recording fees, when the county asks for separate ones.
  • A missing parcel number, which slows the clerk's delinquent tax check.
  • A deed of trust left open after payoff, which keeps showing as a lien in the index.

If you hold a house inherited from a relative, the names on the last recorded deed may differ from the heirs. Sort that out with an attorney before a buyer's lender asks.

What to do before closing

Gather the paperwork in the order the office will ask for it, starting with the tax statement since it is the item most likely to hold things up.

  • Find the parcel number in the county tax records.
  • Confirm the delinquent tax statement route with the closing attorney.
  • Bring two checks, one to the tax department and one to the register.
  • Ask whether any old deed of trust still needs a recorded cancellation.

A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, so the packet is shorter, but the tax statement and the recording fees still apply. Deeds move through this office steadily, with 411 building permits issued in 2025 across a county of 38,463 housing units.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a Wilson County deed filed?

With the county Register of Deeds, reachable at 252-399-2935. For a sale, the closing attorney usually files it.

Does Wilson County require a tax statement on the deed?

Yes. The county accepts a deed only if it carries one of its two delinquent tax options, either verified by a tax department clerk or completed by the attorney.

What fee applies to a general deed in Wilson County?

An ordinary document costs $26.00 with 15 pages included, and each page past that adds $4.00. Loan security papers start at $64.00.

Who owes the excise tax on a Wilson County sale?

The seller, who pays the register before the deed is filed.

Can I search Wilson County deeds online?

Yes, for real estate indexes back to 1974. Older documents may not have images online yet, so ask the office about them.

Selling in Yadkin County?
We buy Yadkin County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What the office handles

In Yadkinville, the register of deeds is the keeper of land records for the whole county, including deeds, deeds of trust and maps. Anyone may inspect them. Staff also certify copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, issues marriage licenses and swears in notaries.

Until the deed is on the books, a sale is not fully protected. An unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

Electronic recording is encouraged for every document. Appointments for marriage licenses and notary oaths go through 336-849-7904. Voters elect the register, and the deed excise tax is paid at this same counter, so a seller's money and the buyer's paperwork meet here.

How a deed gets recorded after a sale

In most sales the attorney or title company sends the deed in electronically from the closing table. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. A firm that wants to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The county's tax office points owners to an attorney for deed work. As a result, a seller in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or anywhere between rarely visits the recording desk personally.

  • Ask if your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement here.
  • Learn who is writing the check for the excise tax. The seller owes it.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive over.

Recording fees

The fee schedule is the same in every North Carolina county. It is complete and exclusive, and payment is due up front.

Charges that apply to a Yadkin County house sale
DocumentAmount
Deed, first 15 pages$26.00
Mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00
Overflow pages on either$4.00 each
Paying off a mortgage (satisfaction)Free
Certified copy of a recorded deed$5.00 plus $2.00 per added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Tally the pages of the deed plus exhibits ahead of time. The $4.00 charge begins on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Yadkin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays the excise stamp

The transferring owner pays this tax. The rate is one dollar per five hundred dollars of value, due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

The proceeds are split evenly: the county keeps half, and the other half is sent to the state each month, minus up to 2 percent the county may hold back. The settlement statement shows the dollar amount for your sale price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

Tax office versus Register of Deeds

Think of them as two counters with different jobs. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. A 2027 revaluation is underway at the tax office.

Billing and payment questions go to the tax office at 336-849-7903. That office gives a 2 percent discount for August payment and bills a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household ($38.00 with the elderly exemption). Taxes are due September 1, with interest beginning January 6.

Other documents recorded here

The recording desk takes more than deeds. Options, leases beyond three years and rights of first refusal must be registered before they bind a later buyer. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Yadkin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Sales of inherited and older houses

Of Yadkin County's 17,697 housing units, owners occupy 76.9 percent, and plenty of sales involve inherited or aging houses. Builders pulled only 116 permits in 2025, so resale homes dominate. An older house often has a longer chain of deeds, and a buyer's title examiner will read every link, from the first conveyance to your own vesting deed.

When an estate owns the house, ask the clerk of superior court who may sign the deed. The register takes it once it is signed and acknowledged, yet staff will not rule on the signer's authority.

If the owner has a tax lien

An owner facing a tax lien can look at the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page to see how auctions are listed. Redemption remains possible before a sale is confirmed.

Any lien will turn up in the buyer's title exam. Clear it before you list, because a late discovery can delay closing or shrink your proceeds. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure that includes the solid waste fee, and give it to the closing attorney.

Setting up electronic recording

You will rarely do this yourself, but it helps to know what your closing firm needs. Yadkin County takes every document type except maps by e-recording, and the firm must work through Simplifile, CSC or ePN.

  1. The firm picks one of the three providers.
  2. It completes a submitter agreement, which the provider passes to the county.
  3. It sends the signed deed and the deed of trust electronically.
  4. It keeps the confirmation showing the date and time of recording.

If your attorney does not already have an agreement with Yadkin County, ask whether paper recording will be used and how long the office will need. A plat or map always goes in on paper.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Questions to ask your closing attorney

A short conversation with your attorney saves surprises at the register's counter. Ask who is responsible for the recording fee, whether any exhibits will push the deed past 15 pages, and whether the deed of trust for the buyer's loan will be filed the same day. Ask too whether an old option or lease in your chain of title has been recorded, and whether any seller-financed terms would fall under Chapter 47H.

If you live outside Yadkin County while the house is in it, the attorney can handle everything by e-recording, and you will only need to sign.

Steps before closing

  1. Learn whether your attorney will record electronically or on paper.
  2. Estimate the recording fee from the page count of the deed and exhibits.
  3. Decide who writes the excise tax check.
  4. Verify a satisfaction is on record for any mortgage you paid off.
  5. File the recording confirmation with your closing papers.

A cash sale skips the buyer's lender and its deed of trust, so the packet is smaller, but the deed and the excise tax are still recorded in the same way. Ask your attorney for the recording date and time, because that timestamp, not the signing date, fixes who ranks first.

Frequently asked questions

Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?

Yes. The seller owes a deed excise tax, paid to the register at filing. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage?

No. State law sets no charge for a satisfaction, so the payoff paperwork is free to file.

How long does a buyer under a contract for deed have to cancel?

Through midnight of the third business day. After that, the seller has a five-business-day window to record.

Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?

Yes, a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
